tokens.name: Tenochtitlan
tokens.title: Lacustrine Imperial City
tokens.description: Tenochtitlan was a large Mexican altepetl built on an island in Lake Texcoco, in the Valley of Mexico. The city stood in what is now the historic centre of Mexico City.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Largest city in pre-Columbian Americas at its peak
tokens.fun_fact_2: Founded circa 1325 (traditional date)
tokens.fun_fact_3: Located in present-day Mexico City
tokens.rare_fact: The Templo Mayor was rediscovered in 1978 when electricity workers found a huge stone disc of the goddess Coyolxauhqui.

tokens.name: K2
tokens.title: Extreme High-Altitude Summit
tokens.description: K2, also known as Mount Godwin-Austen, is the second-highest mountain on Earth at 8,611 metres. It lies in the Karakoram range, partly in Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan and partly in China.

tokens.name: Stonehenge

tokens.fun_fact_2: Aligned with summer solstice sunrise
tokens.fun_fact_3: UNESCO World Heritage Site

tokens.aliases: Auckland War Memorial Museum, Sky Tower (Auckland)
tokens.image_credit: elpinto007 · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Avenue of the Baobabs
tokens.description: Avenue lined with Grandidier's baobabs along Road No. 8 between Morondava and Belon'i Tsiribihina in western Madagascar. Granted temporary protected status in 2007, it draws travellers from around the world.
tokens.fun_fact_1: These are technically upside-down trees (roots up)
tokens.image_credit: Hanay · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Awash National Park
tokens.description: National park in eastern Ethiopia, about 225 km east of Addis Ababa, on the border of the Oromia and Afar regions. It covers 827 square km, most of it at about 900 m altitude.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Lucy (Australopithecus) found 60km away
tokens.image_credit: Ji-Elle · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ayaz-Kala
tokens.description: Archaeological site of an ancient Khorezm fortress on a hilltop in Karakalpakstan, northern Uzbekistan. Built between the 4th century BCE and the 7th century CE, it overlooks the Kyzylkum Desert.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Builders carved into desert — no water within 100km
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ayutthaya Historical Park
tokens.description: Ruins of the old city of Ayutthaya in Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya province, Thailand. The city was founded by King Ramathibodi I in 1351, and the park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bank for International Settlements
tokens.description: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is an international financial institution owned by member central banks. Founded in 1930, it is the oldest international financial institution and serves as a bank for central banks.
tokens.fun_fact_1: The most powerful bank nobody talks about
tokens.image_credit: Taxiarchos228 · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bahrain Financial Harbour
tokens.description: Bahrain Financial Harbour is a waterfront commercial development on the northern shore of Manama, Bahrain. Its two Harbour Towers opened in May 2007 as part of a project costing $1.5 billion.
tokens.image_credit: Droodkin · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Ignacio Lagoon
tokens.description: San Ignacio Lagoon, in Mulegé Municipality, Baja California Sur, is one of the winter sanctuaries of the eastern Pacific gray whale. It lies about 59 km from the town of San Ignacio.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Whales approach boats for petting — only place wild animals seek human contact

tokens.name: Bale Mountains National Park
tokens.description: Bale Mountains National Park in Ethiopia covers about 2,150 km2 of the Bale Mountains and Sanetti Plateau. Its Afromontane habitats have one of the highest rates of animal endemism of any terrestrial habitat in the world.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Ethiopian wolf eats only giant mole rats
tokens.image_credit: Indrik myneur · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Banaue Rice Terraces
tokens.description: The Banaue Rice Terraces are terraces carved into the mountains of Banaue, Ifugao, in the Philippines, by the ancestors of the Igorot people. They were built largely by hand with minimal equipment, about 1,500 metres above sea level.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Carved by hand with no machinery — took 2000 years
tokens.aliases: Batad Rice Terraces, Banaue Ifugao Terraces
tokens.image_credit: User: (WT-shared) Roundtheworld at wts wikivoyage · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bengaluru
tokens.description: Bengaluru, known as Bangalore until 2014, is the capital and largest city of the southern Indian state of Karnataka. The 2011 census counted 8.4 million inhabitants in the city.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Time zone advantage — Indian engineers fix code while US sleeps
tokens.image_credit: Gpkp · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bangui
tokens.description: Bangui is the capital and largest city of the Central African Republic. It was founded as a French outpost in 1889 on the northern bank of the Ubangi River.
tokens.fun_fact_1: CAR has 80% of diamond reserves but is among world poorest countries
tokens.image_credit: Alllexxxis · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Basra
tokens.description: Basra is a port city in southern Iraq and the capital of Basra Governorate. It is the third largest city in Iraq and lies on the Shatt al-Arab, which empties into the Persian Gulf.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Legend says Sinbad sailed from here on his seven voyages

tokens.name: Batu Caves
tokens.title: Hindu cave shrine
tokens.description: Limestone cave complex about 13 km north of Kuala Lumpur, home to Hindu temples and a shrine to Murugan. It is the focal point of the Thaipusam festival in Malaysia.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bay of Islands
tokens.description: Area on the east coast of the Far North District of New Zealand's North Island, with many islands. It is one of the country's most popular sailing, fishing and tourist destinations.
tokens.image_credit: JamesNZguy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golden Eagle Festival
tokens.description: Annual festival of Kazakh eagle hunters held each autumn near Olgii in Bayan-Olgii Province, western Mongolia. Hunters on horseback compete with trained golden eagles in speed and agility contests.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Only place on Earth where people still hunt with golden eagles on horseback

tokens.name: Beirut Central District
tokens.description: Historical and geographical core of Beirut, the capital of Lebanon, also called downtown Beirut. It is described as the country's vibrant financial, commercial and administrative hub.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Has been destroyed and rebuilt 7 times in history
tokens.image_credit: UggBoy UggGirl · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kingdom of Benin
tokens.description: Traditional kingdom in southern Nigeria, also known as Great Benin, with its capital at Edo, now Benin City. It has no historical relation to the modern Republic of Benin.

tokens.name: Białowieża Forest
tokens.description: Large forest complex and UNESCO World Heritage Area straddling the border of Poland and Belarus. It is one of the last large remains of the primeval forest of the European Plain and is home to more than 800 European bison.
tokens.image_credit: Jacek Karczmarz · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bissau
tokens.description: Capital and largest city of Guinea-Bissau, on the Geba River estuary off the Atlantic Ocean. It is the country's major port and its administrative and military centre.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Country controlled by drug lords — cocaine transshipment center
tokens.image_credit: August Dominus · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bombay Stock Exchange
tokens.description: BSE Limited, known as the Bombay Stock Exchange, is an Indian stock exchange based in Mumbai. Established in 1875, it is the oldest stock exchange in Asia.
tokens.fun_fact_1: World's largest by number of listed companies
tokens.image_credit: Niyantha Shekhar · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: East Siberian taiga
tokens.description: The East Siberian taiga is a very large biogeographic ecoregion in eastern Russia. It belongs to the taiga and boreal forests biome.

tokens.name: Heart of Borneo
tokens.description: The Heart of Borneo is a conservation agreement to protect a 220,000 km² forested region on Borneo island. It was signed by Brunei, Indonesia and Malaysia in Bali in 2007.

tokens.name: Buckingham Palace
tokens.title: Residence of the British Monarch
tokens.description: Buckingham Palace is the official London residence and administrative headquarters of the British monarch. It is located in the City of Westminster.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Became the monarch's official residence in 1837 under Queen Victoria
tokens.fun_fact_2: Bought by George III in 1761 as Buckingham House
tokens.fun_fact_3: The Changing of the Guard takes place in front of it
tokens.aliases: Buckingham, Marlborough House, Party at the Palace, Rolls-Royce Holdings

curation.notes: Reviewer fame override. Was common. "GBP 2B value" removed (unverified). IMAGE TO SOURCE (network blocked).

tokens.image_credit: Julian Herzog (Website) · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ark of Bukhara
tokens.description: The Ark of Bukhara is a massive fortress in the city of Bukhara, Uzbekistan, first built around the 5th century AD. It was used as a fortress until it fell to the Soviet Union in 1920.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Emir executed foreigners by throwing them into Bug Pit with insects
tokens.image_credit: ほっきー · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park
tokens.title: Mountain gorillas
tokens.description: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park is a forest national park in southwestern Uganda, on the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994.

tokens.name: ByteDance
tokens.description: ByteDance is a Chinese internet technology company based in Haidian, Beijing. It developed the video-sharing app TikTok, known in China as Douyin.
tokens.image_credit: N509FZ · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Camargue
tokens.description: The Camargue is a coastal region in southern France, between the Mediterranean Sea and the two arms of the Rhône river delta. It lies south of the city of Arles.
tokens.image_credit: Norbert Nagel, Mörfelden-Walldorf, Germany · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bafut Palace
tokens.description: Royal palace of the Fon of Bafut, seat of a traditional fondom in Mezam Department, northwest Cameroon. The palace is on UNESCO's Tentative List.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Chief has hundreds of wives by royal custom
tokens.image_credit: Abu Shawka · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cango Caves
tokens.description: Show caves in limestone at the foothills of the Swartberg range near Oudtshoorn, South Africa. The principal cave is one of the country's best-known tourist caves.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Accessible but claustrophobic cave passage called Devil Chimney
tokens.image_credit: Rute Martins of Leoa's Photography (www.leoa.co.za) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cardamom Mountains
tokens.description: Mountain range in southwest Cambodia and eastern Thailand, also called the Phnom Kravanh or Banthat Mountains. Its silhouette appears on the provincial seal of Trat.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Khmer Rouge hid here for decades after regime fell

tokens.name: Cedars of God
tokens.title: Ancient cedar grove
tokens.description: Ancient forest of Lebanon cedar in the Kadisha Valley of Bsharre, Lebanon, a remnant of the forests that once covered Mount Lebanon. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Ouadi Qadisha and the Forest of the Cedars of God.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Mentioned in Bible 70+ times. Solomon built Temple from these trees
tokens.image_credit: BlingBling10 at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chapada Diamantina
tokens.description: Mountain region of Bahia state in northeast Brazil, forming the northern part of the Espinhaço Mountains. Its name means Diamond Plateau in Portuguese.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Mosquito Falls has underwater chamber that glows blue — no artificial light
tokens.image_credit: Cleide Isabel · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chefchaouen
tokens.title: Blue city
tokens.description: City in northwest Morocco, chief town of Chefchaouen Province, noted for its buildings in shades of blue. It lies in the mountains between Tétouan and Ouazzane.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Blue paint was introduced by Jewish refugees in 1930s
tokens.image_credit: Badr Rachadi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wat Rong Khun
tokens.description: Contemporary privately owned art temple outside Chiang Rai, Thailand, known as the White Temple. Designed and built by national artist Chalermchai Kositpipat, opened to visitors in 1997.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Still being built by one artist since 1997 — donation funded
tokens.image_credit: JJ Harrison (https://www.jjharrison.com.au/) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chittor Fort
tokens.description: Chittor Fort is one of the largest forts in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was the capital of Mewar and stands in the present-day city of Chittorgarh.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Jauhar — mass suicide to avoid capture — done three times here
tokens.image_credit: Ssjoshi111 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chitwan National Park
tokens.description: Chitwan National Park is the first national park of Nepal, established in 1973 in the Terai region. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.
tokens.image_credit: Vadim Tolbatov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chobe National Park
tokens.description: Chobe National Park is Botswana's first national park and its most biologically diverse. It lies in the north of the country along the Chobe River.

tokens.name: Congo Basin
tokens.description: The Congo Basin is the sedimentary basin of the Congo River, in the Central African region known as west equatorial Africa.
tokens.image_credit: MONUSCO Photos · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Conkouati-Douli National Park
tokens.description: Conkouati-Douli National Park is a coastal national park in the Republic of the Congo. Its work includes biological research, community outreach and tourism development.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Orphan gorillas rehabilitated and released here

tokens.name: Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba
tokens.description: The Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba is a former mosque in Andalusia, Spain, now the Roman Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Córdoba. It is also known as the Mezquita.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Cathedral hammered into center of mosque — UNESCO calls it architectural vandalism
tokens.image_credit: Toni Castillo Quero · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Daintree National Park
tokens.description: Daintree National Park is in Far North Queensland, Australia, about 100 km northwest of Cairns. It has been a World Heritage Site since 1988 as part of the Wet Tropics of Queensland.
tokens.image_credit: User:Diliff · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Autonomous Port of Dakar
tokens.title: West African port
tokens.description: The Autonomous Port of Dakar is a Senegalese public enterprise with a sheltered harbour. It is the third largest port in West Africa.
tokens.image_credit: KaBa (KaaBaa) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dambulla Cave Temple
tokens.description: Sri Lanka's largest and best-preserved cave temple complex, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991. It lies about 72 km north of Kandy.
tokens.fun_fact_1: King hid in cave during invasion — created temple in gratitude
tokens.image_credit: Lankapic · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Danum Valley Conservation Area
tokens.description: Danum Valley Conservation Area is a 438 square kilometre tract of relatively undisturbed lowland dipterocarp forest in Sabah, Malaysia. It is home to the Bornean orangutan, gibbons, clouded leopards and over 270 bird species.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Orangutans share 96.9% DNA with us — watching them is watching cousins
tokens.image_credit: Christopher Michel · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dar es Salaam
tokens.description: Dar es Salaam is the largest city and financial hub of Tanzania, on the Swahili coast. With over 7 million people, it is the largest city in East Africa by population.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Named Haven of Peace in Arabic — though no longer capital
tokens.image_credit: Vijay8808 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dili
tokens.description: Dili is the capital and largest city of Timor-Leste. It lies on the northern coast of Timor island, in a small area of flat land between mountains.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Youngest country to join UN — independence 2002 after 24 year occupation
tokens.image_credit: Bahnfrend · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dinder National Park
tokens.description: Dinder National Park is a national park and biosphere reserve in eastern Sudan. It is connected to Ethiopia's Alitash National Park.
tokens.fun_fact_1: One of Africa largest and least visited parks

tokens.name: Diriyah
tokens.description: Diriyah was the original home of the House of Saud and capital of the first Saudi state from 1727 to 1818. Its At-Turaif District has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2010.
tokens.image_credit: Matti&Keti · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Port of Doraleh
tokens.title: Horn of Africa trade gate
tokens.description: The Port of Doraleh is a multipurpose port 5 km west of Djibouti City, with terminals for oil, bulk cargo, containers and livestock. Its container facility was seized by the Djibouti government in February 2018.
tokens.fun_fact_1: China has military base next to US base here

tokens.name: Dogon country
tokens.description: Homeland of the Dogon people in eastern Mali and northwestern Burkina Faso. The Bandiagara Escarpment within it has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1989.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Knew Sirius had a companion star 700 years before Europeans discovered it

tokens.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
tokens.description: Three distinctive battlement-like peaks in the Sexten Dolomites of northeastern Italy. One of the best-known mountain groups in the Alps.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Three Peaks — face three different compass directions exactly
tokens.image_credit: Tiia Monto · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Darvaza gas crater
tokens.description: A burning natural gas field that collapsed into a cavern near Darvaza, Turkmenistan, also known as the Door to Hell. It has been on fire since 1971.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Never intentionally lit — it was an accident
tokens.image_credit: Tormod Sandtorv · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Draa River
tokens.description: Morocco's longest river, about 1,100 km, flowing from the High Atlas toward the Atlantic. Its valley holds long strings of palm oases and kasbahs.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Supplied gold and slaves across Sahara for millennia
tokens.image_credit: Theoliane · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dubai Gold Souk
tokens.description: A traditional gold market in the Deira district of Dubai, UAE, with over 380 retailers, most of them jewellery traders.

tokens.name: Port of Durban
tokens.title: Africa's busiest container port
tokens.description: The largest and busiest shipping terminal in sub-Saharan Africa, handling up to 31.4 million tons of cargo a year. It is a major container port in South Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Planet Labs, Inc. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: ECOWAS
tokens.title: West African Economic Bloc
tokens.description: A regional political and economic union of twelve West African countries. Its headquarters are in Abuja, Nigeria.

tokens.name: Eden Gardens
tokens.title: Kolkata's cricket colosseum
tokens.description: Cricket stadium in Kolkata, India, established in 1864 with a capacity of 68,000. It is the oldest cricket stadium in India.
tokens.image_credit: Nahid Sultan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Edinburgh Castle
tokens.description: Historic castle on Castle Rock in Edinburgh, Scotland, occupied since at least the Iron Age. It was a royal residence until 1633.
tokens.image_credit: Enric · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Elephant Trunk Hill
tokens.description: Karst hill in Guilin, Guangxi, China, known for its natural rock arch. It is a landmark and tourist attraction of the city.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus
tokens.description: Ancient Greek theatre of the 4th century BC in the Sanctuary of Asklepios at Epidaurus, in the Argolid. It is still used for performances and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Pin drop audible from back row — acoustics not fully scientifically explained
tokens.image_credit: DieBuche · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mari
tokens.description: Ancient Semitic city-state on the western bank of the Euphrates in Syria, today the ruins of Tell Hariri. It flourished as a trade centre between 2900 BC and 1759 BC.
tokens.image_credit: Heretiq · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Euronext Amsterdam
tokens.description: Stock exchange in Amsterdam, Netherlands, formerly the Amsterdam Stock Exchange. It merged in 2000 with the Brussels and Paris exchanges to form Euronext.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Founded by Dutch East India Company
tokens.aliases: AMS-IX Amsterdam, Amsterdam Canal Ring, Euronext
tokens.image_credit: Bybbisch94, Christian Gebhardt · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Everglades National Park
tokens.description: United States national park protecting the southern 20% of the original Everglades ecosystem in Florida. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: River of grass flows slowly south — wide shallow sheet impossible to see from ground
tokens.image_credit: Everglades NPS from Homestead, Florida, United States · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Doubtful Sound
tokens.description: Doubtful Sound / Patea is a fiord in Fiordland, in the far south west of New Zealand. It is New Zealand's second most famous tourism destination after Milford Sound.
tokens.image_credit: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Frankfurt Stock Exchange
tokens.description: The Frankfurt Stock Exchange (Börse Frankfurt) is the world's 3rd oldest stock exchange and the 12th largest by market capitalization. It operates from 08:00 to 22:00 German time.
tokens.fun_fact_1: More internet traffic than most countries
tokens.image_credit: Mylius · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Garden Route
tokens.description: The Garden Route is a 300 km stretch of the south-eastern coast of South Africa, from Witsand in the Western Cape to the Tsitsikamma Storms River border in the Eastern Cape. Its name comes from its verdant, ecologically diverse vegetation and numerous estuaries and lakes.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Highest commercial bungy jump in world at Bloukrans Bridge
tokens.image_credit: Original uploader was Conrad88 at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Flaming Cliffs
tokens.description: The Flaming Cliffs (Bayanzag) are a region of the Gobi Desert in Ömnögovi Province, Mongolia. The area is famous for yielding the first discovery of dinosaur eggs.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Roy Chapman Andrews — Indiana Jones inspiration — found eggs here
tokens.image_credit: Christopher Michel · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gobustan Rock Art Cultural Landscape
tokens.description: The Gobustan Rock Art Cultural Landscape in Azerbaijan is a UNESCO World Heritage site with a large collection of petroglyphs. The engravings are estimated to date back 5,000 to 20,000 years.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Roman soldier carved graffiti here — most surprising inscription in Caucasus
tokens.image_credit: Walter Callens · CC BY 1.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gombe National Park
tokens.description: Gombe National Park is a national park in Tanzania, in the Kigoma District of the Kigoma Region. It was formerly called Gombe Stream National Park.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Goodall arrived with no degree — just curiosity. Changed primatology

tokens.name: Greenland ice sheet
tokens.description: The Greenland ice sheet is the second-largest body of ice in the world. It is on average 1,673 m thick and over 3,488 m thick at its maximum.
tokens.fun_fact_1: If melted, would slow Earth's rotation
tokens.image_credit: Hannes Grobe 20:10, 16 December 2007 (UTC) · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gur-e-Amir
tokens.title: Tamerlane's tomb
tokens.description: The Gur-e-Amir is a mausoleum of the conqueror Timur (Tamerlane) in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It influenced later Mughal tombs, including the Taj Mahal in Agra.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Legend: do not open his tomb or great conqueror will come. Opened June 19 1941. Germany invaded June 22
tokens.image_credit: Willard84 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gyeongbokgung
tokens.title: Joseon royal palace
tokens.description: Former royal palace of the Joseon dynasty in Seoul, established in 1395 as the first royal palace of that dynasty. It is one of the most significant tourist attractions in South Korea.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Has fastest internet in world — 1 Gbps available everywhere for $25/month
tokens.image_credit: Basile Morin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Daereungwon
tokens.description: Complex of Silla-era royal tumulus tombs in Gyeongju, South Korea. It has been a designated Historic Site since 2011 and is a popular tourist attraction.
tokens.image_credit: Heera7 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haʻamonga ʻa Maui
tokens.description: Stone trilithon of coral limestone on Tongatapu, Tonga, built in the 13th century by King Tuʻitātui for his two sons. It is sometimes called the Stonehenge of the Pacific.
tokens.image_credit: Tauʻolunga · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kīlauea
tokens.description: Active shield volcano on the southeastern shore of Hawaii Island. Since the islands were settled it has been the most active of the five volcanoes that form the island, and among the most active on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: USGS/K. Lynn · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hell's Gate National Park
tokens.description: National park near Lake Naivasha in Kenya, named after a narrow break in the cliffs that was once a tributary of a prehistoric lake. It was established in 1984.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Inspired the African setting of Disney Lion King
tokens.image_credit: Alexandra Cadet · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nokia
tokens.description: Nokia Corporation's main headquarters, in Espoo in the Helsinki metropolitan area. The Finnish telecommunications and technology company was originally established as a pulp mill in 1865.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Nokia market cap was 40% of Finland GDP — then iPhone destroyed them
tokens.image_credit: pikkuanna · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hermitage Museum
tokens.description: Museum of art and culture in Saint Petersburg, Russia, founded in 1764 when Catherine the Great acquired a collection of paintings. It holds the largest collection of paintings in the world.
tokens.image_credit: GAlexandrova · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hierapolis
tokens.description: Ancient Hellenistic Greek city in southwestern Anatolia, Turkey, founded in the 3rd century BC on the site of a Phrygian cult centre. It was famous for its hot springs and as the birthplace of the Stoic philosopher Epictetus.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Cleopatra allegedly bathed in the sacred pool
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Himeji Castle
tokens.title: White Heron castle
tokens.description: Himeji Castle is a hilltop Japanese castle complex in Himeji, Hyogo Prefecture, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is regarded as the finest surviving example of prototypical Japanese castle architecture.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Painted white specifically to prevent cannon fire — white = no heat absorption
tokens.aliases: Himeji White Heron Castle, Himeji Castle
tokens.image_credit: Nikos Kitsakis · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hollywood Walk of Fame
tokens.description: The Hollywood Walk of Fame is a sidewalk along Hollywood Boulevard and Vine Street in Los Angeles, California. It contains more than 2,800 terrazzo-and-brass stars honoring achievement in the entertainment industry.

tokens.name: Hong Kong Stock Exchange
tokens.description: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong is a stock exchange based in Hong Kong and one of the largest in Asia. It connects international investors with mainland Chinese companies and is a major platform for capital raising.
tokens.fun_fact_1: World's largest IPO market in 2022
tokens.image_credit: WiNG · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Victoria Peak
tokens.description: Victoria Peak is a 552-metre hill on the western half of Hong Kong Island, the tallest hill on the island. It is also known as The Peak.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Case · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Honiara
tokens.description: Honiara is the capital and largest city of the Solomon Islands, on the northwestern coast of Guadalcanal. It is served by Honiara International Airport and the seaport of Point Cruz.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Battle of Guadalcanal — turning point of Pacific War — fought here
tokens.image_credit: Kahunapule Michael Johnson from Pukalani, Hawaii, United States of America · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Honolulu
tokens.description: Honolulu is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of Hawaii. It lies on the southeast coast of the island of Oahu, in the Pacific Ocean.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Pearl Harbor attack December 7 1941 brought US into WWII
tokens.image_credit: Farragutful · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Imperial City of Huế
tokens.description: The Imperial City of Huế is a royal enclosure within the walled city of Huế, the former imperial capital of Vietnam under the Nguyễn dynasty. It contains the palaces that housed the imperial family, along with shrines, gardens and offices.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Heavily damaged in 1968 Tet Offensive — still being restored
tokens.image_credit: NguyenThanhBac123 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hunza Valley
tokens.description: The Hunza Valley, also known as the Hunza-Nagar Valley, is a mountainous river valley traversed by the Hunza River. It lies in Gilgit-Baltistan, in the Pakistan-administered part of Kashmir.
tokens.fun_fact_1: James Hilton based Lost Horizon on traveler accounts of this valley
tokens.image_credit: FaizanAhmad · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hustai National Park
tokens.description: Hustai National Park is a protected steppe and mountain area in Töv Province, Mongolia, covering 506 km2. Przewalski's horses were reintroduced there in 1992.
tokens.fun_fact_1: These are the only truly wild horses — all others descended from domesticated
tokens.image_credit: Eddy23 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: International Atomic Energy Agency
tokens.title: UN Nuclear Watchdog
tokens.description: The International Atomic Energy Agency, founded in 1957, is headquartered in Vienna at the Vienna International Center. It promotes the peaceful use of nuclear energy and works to inhibit its military use.

curation.notes: Legacy opinionated stats removed. Facts generic. IMAGE TO SOURCE (network blocked).

tokens.image_credit: IAEA Imagebank · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: International Criminal Court
tokens.title: Permanent War Crimes Court
tokens.description: The International Criminal Court is seated in The Hague, Netherlands. Established in 2002 under the Rome Statute, it prosecutes individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression.

curation.notes: Legacy opinionated stats removed. Facts generic. IMAGE TO SOURCE (network blocked).

tokens.image_credit: OSeveno · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jabal al-Lawz
tokens.description: Jabal al-Lawz is a 2,580 metre mountain in northwest Saudi Arabia, near the Jordanian border above the Gulf of Aqaba. Some researchers have proposed it as the biblical Mount Sinai, a view not accepted by mainstream scholars.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Some believe Moses received Ten Commandments here not Egypt Sinai
tokens.image_credit: وكالة الأنباء السعودية · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jaisalmer Fort
tokens.title: Living golden fort
tokens.description: Jaisalmer Fort is a sandstone fort in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, India, where nearly a quarter of the old city's population still lives. It is one of six forts in the UNESCO World Heritage site Hill Forts of Rajasthan.
tokens.image_credit: Shitha Valsan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tokyo Stock Exchange
tokens.description: The Tokyo Stock Exchange is a stock exchange located in Tokyo, Japan. It is owned by Japan Exchange Group, a holding company that is itself listed on the exchange.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Merged Tokyo + Osaka exchanges in 2013
tokens.image_credit: Kakidai · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hallasan
tokens.title: Volcanic island
tokens.description: Hallasan is a shield volcano and the highest peak in South Korea, at 1,947 m. It forms most of Jeju Island and lies within Hallasan National Park and the UNESCO World Heritage property Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes.
tokens.image_credit: LG전자 · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Manjanggul
tokens.description: Manjanggul is a lava tube in Gimnyeong on Jeju Island, about 8.9 km long. It is part of the Geomunoreum Lava Tube System, inscribed by UNESCO in 2007 as part of Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes.
tokens.fun_fact_1: 160km of lava tubes — most connected in world
tokens.image_credit: AhmadElq · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kakadu National Park
tokens.description: Kakadu National Park is a protected area in the Northern Territory of Australia, about 171 km southeast of Darwin. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Andrea Schaffer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Karakorum
tokens.description: Karakorum was the capital of the Mongol Empire from 1235 to 1260, and later of the Northern Yuan dynasty. It was founded in 1220 and probably fell into dereliction at the start of the 15th century.
tokens.fun_fact_1: First capital of world largest empire ever — now sheep graze over ruins
tokens.image_credit: Brücke-Osteuropa · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Karakoram Highway
tokens.description: The Karakoram Highway is a 1,300 km national highway from Hasan Abdal in Pakistan to the Khunjerab Pass on the Chinese border. At 4,714 m near the pass, it is one of the highest paved roads in the world.
tokens.fun_fact_1: 810 Pakistani and 82 Chinese workers died building it
tokens.image_credit: SHAKEEL GILGITY · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kashgar Sunday Market
tokens.description: Kashgar Sunday Market, also called Yekshenbe Bazaar, is a traditional bazaar in Kashgar in Xinjiang, China. The full-scale market runs on Sundays and sells livestock, carpets, textiles and spices.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Marco Polo described same market — it looks identical today

tokens.name: Kerala backwaters
tokens.description: The Kerala backwaters are a network of brackish lagoons, lakes and canals along the Malabar Coast of India, with more than 900 km of waterways. Five large lakes are linked by canals and fed by 38 rivers.
tokens.image_credit: RndmCrs · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kilwa Kisiwani
tokens.description: UNESCO World Heritage ruins of the Kilwa Sultanate, a medieval Swahili state whose authority stretched along the Swahili Coast in the 13th to 15th centuries. The island was a major center of Indian Ocean trade.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Traded gold from Zimbabwe to Arabia and India
tokens.image_credit: Halidtz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kingstown
tokens.description: Capital and largest city of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, on the main island of Saint Vincent. It has the country's main port and its biggest commercial center.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Disney Pirates of Caribbean filmed on its beaches — Jack Sparrow territory
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kinkaku-ji
tokens.title: Golden Pavilion of Kyoto
tokens.description: Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan, officially named Rokuon-ji. Its Golden Pavilion has its top two floors coated in gold leaf, and the temple is a World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Nacaru · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Koh Ker
tokens.description: Remote archaeological site in northern Cambodia, about 120 km from Siem Reap and the Angkor site. More than 180 sanctuaries lie in a protected area of 81 square kilometres.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Jungle reclaimed it for 900 years — discovered by accident
tokens.image_credit: PsamatheM · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Komodo Island
tokens.title: Home of the Komodo dragon
tokens.description: Komodo is an Indonesian island named after the Komodo dragon, the largest lizard on Earth. It covers 291 square kilometres and had about 1,800 residents in 2020.

tokens.name: Konark Sun Temple
tokens.description: 13th-century Hindu temple dedicated to the sun god Surya, at Konark in Odisha, India, attributed to about 1250 CE. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and much of its tall tower is now in ruins.
tokens.image_credit: Subham9423 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kruger National Park
tokens.description: National park in the northeast of South Africa, in the provinces of Limpopo and Mpumalanga. It covers 19,623 square kilometres and extends 360 km from north to south.

tokens.name: Apapa Port Complex
tokens.description: Nigeria's largest and busiest port complex, with quays, wharves and container terminals in Apapa, Lagos. It became the busiest port for exporting agricultural produce in the late 1920s.

tokens.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
tokens.description: A 71-metre stone Buddha carved into a cliff where the Min and Dadu rivers meet near Leshan, Sichuan. Built between 712 and 804 AD in the Tang dynasty, it is part of a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lewa Wildlife Conservancy
tokens.description: Wildlife conservancy of over 250 square kilometres in northern Kenya, formed in 1995. It protects black rhinos, Grevy's zebras and sitatungas, with the adjacent Ngare Ndare Forest.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Prince William proposed to Kate Middleton here

tokens.name: Lilongwe
tokens.description: Capital and largest city of Malawi, with about 1.1 million inhabitants in 2020. Its population grew from 674,448 in 2008 to 989,318 at the 2018 census.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Lake Malawi has more fish species than any lake — 1000+ cichlid species
tokens.image_credit: Felixfeld · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lomé
tokens.description: Capital and largest city of Togo, on the Gulf of Guinea at the country's southwest corner. It is Togo's administrative and industrial centre and has an oil refinery.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Lomé accords 1975 — first major EU-Africa trade agreement signed here
tokens.image_credit: Reich geck · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: London Stock Exchange
tokens.title: London meat market
tokens.description: Global stock exchange based in Paternoster Square in the City of London. Founded in 1801, it is one of the world's oldest continuously operating stock exchanges.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Founded 1801. Lost world #1 to NYSE after WW1
tokens.image_credit: London Stock Exchange · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Longsheng Rice Terraces
tokens.description: Rice terraces climbing from the riverside to 600 to 800 metres above sea level near Longji, in Longsheng County, about 100 km from Guilin. The fields show water, green shoots, ripe rice and frost through the seasons.
tokens.image_credit: severin.stalder · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lopé National Park
tokens.description: National park of 4,912 square kilometres in central Gabon, where rainforest meets relict savannah along the Ogooué River. Part of the Lopé-Okanda UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2007.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Unique mosaic of savanna and rainforest
tokens.image_credit: Ngangorica · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Madaba Map
tokens.description: Byzantine floor mosaic in the church of Saint George in Madaba, Jordan. It is the oldest surviving original cartographic depiction of the Holy Land, especially Jerusalem.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Oldest surviving map of Jerusalem — still in church floor
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Disdero assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Madagascar lowland forests
tokens.description: Tropical moist broadleaf forest ecoregion on the eastern coast of Madagascar. Its plants and animals are 80 to 90 percent endemic, and the eastern plain is a key centre of this endemism.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Vassen from Brussels, Belgium · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Majuro
tokens.description: Capital and largest city of the Marshall Islands. It lies on a large coral atoll of 64 islands in the Pacific Ocean.
tokens.fun_fact_1: US tested 67 nuclear bombs here 1946-1958 — residents still contaminated

tokens.name: Baa Atoll
tokens.description: Administrative atoll in the western Maldives, with 75 islands of which 13 are inhabited. It was designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2011.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Will be completely submerged within 50 years

tokens.name: Maracanã Stadium
tokens.description: Football stadium in the Maracanã neighborhood of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is managed by the clubs Flamengo and Fluminense and forms a complex with the Maracanãzinho arena.
tokens.fun_fact_1: 1950 WC final: 199,854 people in stadium
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taputapuatea marae
tokens.description: Large marae complex at Opoa on the east coast of Raiatea, French Polynesia. Once the central temple and religious center of Eastern Polynesia, it was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2017.
tokens.image_credit: Michel-georges bernard · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gonur Depe
tokens.description: Early Bronze Age settlement about 60 km north of Mary (ancient Merv) in Turkmenistan, dated 2400 to 1600 BCE. It is the major settlement of the Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Contemporary of early Egypt and Mesopotamia — unknown civilization
tokens.image_credit: David Stanley · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Masada
tokens.description: Mountain-top fortress complex in the Judaean Desert, overlooking the western shore of the Dead Sea in southeastern Israel. Its most significant remains date to the reign of Herod the Great, c. 37 to 4 BC.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Masada shall not fall again — Israeli army oath
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Imam Reza Shrine
tokens.description: Mausoleum of Imam Reza, the eighth Imam of Shia Islam, in Mashhad, Iran. Nearly 30 million pilgrims visit it each year, the most visited pilgrimage site in Islam.
tokens.image_credit: AmirVarastehAhmadi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mayon
tokens.title: Perfect cone
tokens.description: Active stratovolcano in Albay province, Bicol, Philippines, known for its near-perfect symmetric cone. Declared a national park in 1938, the first in the Philippines.
tokens.image_credit: Patrickroque01 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: McLeod Ganj
tokens.description: Suburb of Dharamshala in Himachal Pradesh, India, known as 'Little Lhasa'. The Tibetan government-in-exile is headquartered there.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Tibet in India — entire culture preserved here after Chinese invasion
tokens.image_credit: Derek Blackadder · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Medellín
tokens.description: Capital of Antioquia department and the second-largest city in Colombia, located in the Aburrá Valley of the Andes. Population 2,427,129 at the 2018 census.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Most transformed city in world — murder capital to Innovation City of Year 2013
tokens.image_credit: Juan Gómez · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
tokens.description: Multi-purpose stadium in East Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, home ground of AFL and cricket teams. It frequently hosts the Australian national cricket team.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Ranked most liveable city 7 years in a row — perfect urban life balance
tokens.image_credit: Flickerd · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Merapi
tokens.description: Active stratovolcano on the border of Central Java and the Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia, and the most active volcano in Indonesia. It has erupted regularly since 1548.
tokens.image_credit: Fahmi Widayat · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mesa Verde National Park
tokens.description: UNESCO World Heritage national park in Montezuma County, Colorado, protecting some of the best-preserved Ancestral Puebloan sites in the United States. Established in 1906.
tokens.image_credit: Tobi 87 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Meta Menlo Park
tokens.description: Headquarters campus of Meta Platforms at 1 Hacker Way in Menlo Park, California. Meta owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads.

tokens.name: Mgahinga Gorilla National Park
tokens.description: National park in southwestern Uganda, created in 1991 and covering 33.9 km2. It protects mountain gorillas.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Sits on Rwanda-Uganda-DRC triple border point

tokens.name: Microsoft campus
tokens.description: Corporate headquarters of Microsoft in Redmond, Washington, part of the Seattle metropolitan area. The campus is estimated at over 8 million square feet of office space with more than 50,000 employees.
tokens.image_credit: Atomic Taco · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mirissa
tokens.description: Small town on the south coast of Sri Lanka in the Matara District, about 150 km south of Colombo. Its beach and nightlife make it a popular tourist destination.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Best place in world to see blue whales — can see 4-5 at once
tokens.image_credit: Ji-Elle · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monrovia
tokens.description: Capital and largest city of Liberia, founded in 1822 on Cape Mesurado on the Atlantic coast. It had 1,761,032 residents at the 2022 census.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Founded by freed US slaves — only African country named after US president
tokens.image_credit: blk24ga · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve
tokens.description: Costa Rican cloud forest reserve along the Cordillera de Tilarán, founded in 1972. It covers over 10,500 hectares and draws roughly 70,000 visitors a year.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Quakers from Alabama settled here 1951 — no roads — to refuse military service
tokens.image_credit: Haakon S. Krohn · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santa Maria de Montserrat Abbey
tokens.description: Benedictine abbey on the Montserrat mountain in Catalonia, Spain, founded in 1025. It enshrines the image of the Virgin of Montserrat, patroness of Catalonia.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Legend: Golden Globe hidden here by monks 1936 to save from Franco
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moroni, Comoros
tokens.description: Largest city and national capital of the Union of the Comoros, an archipelago in the Indian Ocean. It is also the capital of Ngazidja, the largest of the three main islands.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Has had 20 coups since independence — most coup-prone nation on Earth
tokens.image_credit: Woodlouse · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Bromo
tokens.description: Active somma volcano in East Java, Indonesia, rising to 2,329 m in the Tengger mountains. It is a Hindu pilgrimage site and one of the most visited destinations in East Java.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Hirsch (= user Ravn) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Musandam Peninsula
tokens.description: Mountainous peninsula at the northeastern tip of Arabia, where deep inlets cut into the coast. It lies between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, and its control is divided between Oman and the UAE.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Oman territory completely separated from rest of country by UAE
tokens.image_credit: Photo by Rita Willaert (Belgium) · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nvidia
tokens.description: Headquarters campus of Nvidia in Santa Clara, California, a maker of GPUs for graphics, data centres and artificial intelligence. The company was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Jensen Huang started in a Denny's booth
tokens.image_credit: Coolcaesar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Naoshima
tokens.title: Art island
tokens.description: Island in Japan's Seto Inland Sea, part of Kagawa Prefecture. It is best known for its many contemporary art installations and museums.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nara Park
tokens.description: Public park at the foot of Mount Wakakusa in Nara, Japan, established in 1880 and one of the country's oldest. Its free-roaming deer are considered sacred.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Deer are considered divine messengers — protected by law since 768 AD
tokens.image_credit: Ian G Shingler · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tōdai-ji
tokens.description: Tōdai-ji is a Buddhist temple complex in Nara, Japan, founded in 738 CE. Its Great Buddha Hall houses a giant bronze statue of Vairocana Buddha and is one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
tokens.description: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill in the Alps of southern Bavaria, Germany. King Ludwig II of Bavaria commissioned it, and construction began in 1869.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Basis for Sleeping Beauty Castle in Disneyland
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ngorongoro Crater
tokens.description: Ngorongoro Crater is a large volcanic caldera in northern Tanzania, inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. The conservation area is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Jantjeerkamp at Dutch Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Niamey
tokens.description: Niamey is the capital and largest city of Niger. It lies on the left bank of the Niger River in the west of the country.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Niger controls 7% of world uranium — France dependent on it for nuclear power
tokens.image_credit: Roland Huziaker · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nikkō Tōshō-gū
tokens.description: Nikkō Tōshō-gū is a Shinto shrine in Nikkō, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan. It forms part of the Shrines and Temples of Nikkō UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Deliberately left one pillar inverted — perfection angers gods
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nizwa Fort
tokens.description: Nizwa Fort is a 17th-century fortification in Nizwa, Oman, built in the 1650s under Imam Sultan bin Saif. It is known for its large circular tower.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Largest fort in Oman — had boiling oil channel for attackers
tokens.image_credit: Francisco Anzola · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Noravank
tokens.description: Noravank is a 13th-century Armenian monastery in a narrow gorge near Yeghegnadzor, Armenia. It is best known for its two-storey Surb Astvatsatsin church, whose upper floor is reached by a staircase jutting out from the facade.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Armenia has 4000 monasteries — highest density per km² of any religion
tokens.image_credit: Eupator · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monte Albán
tokens.description: Monte Albán is a large pre-Columbian archaeological site on a low mountain range in the Valley of Oaxaca, Mexico. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Historic Centre of Oaxaca and Archaeological Site of Monte Albán.
tokens.image_credit: nsaum75 !Dígame¡‎ · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shuri Castle
tokens.description: Ryukyuan gusuku castle in Naha, Okinawa, and palace of the Ryukyu Kingdom from 1429 to 1879. Almost completely destroyed in the 1945 Battle of Okinawa, it is part of the UNESCO Gusuku Sites World Heritage listing.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Burned to ground twice — 1945 WWII and 2019 fire — rebuilt both times
tokens.image_credit: CEphoto, Uwe Aranas · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ancient Olympia
tokens.description: Panhellenic sanctuary of ancient Greece in Elis, Peloponnese, where the ancient Olympic Games were held every four years. The archaeological site, mainly dedicated to Zeus, has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Winners received olive wreath — but also lifetime stipends and front row seats
tokens.image_credit: John Karakatsanis from Athens, Greece · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khazaen Economic City
tokens.description: Planned economic city and logistics hub in Barka, Al Batinah, Oman, developed by the state-owned ASYAD Group as an inland port linked to Sohar Port. It has no English Wikipedia article.

tokens.name: Orvieto Cathedral
tokens.description: 14th-century Roman Catholic cathedral in Orvieto, Umbria, built to house the Corporal of Bolsena relic. Its San Brizio Chapel holds Luca Signorelli's Last Judgment frescoes.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Built on volcanic tufa rock — underground city of Etruscan tunnels beneath
tokens.image_credit: Justinawind · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ouarzazate
tokens.description: City in south-central Morocco and capital of Ouarzazate Province in the Drâa-Tafilalet region. It is a primary tourist base and the starting point for excursions into the Draa Valley and the desert.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jellyfish Lake
tokens.description: Marine lake on Eil Malk island in Palau's Rock Islands, known for its population of stingless jellyfish. It is one of about 70 marine lakes in the Rock Islands.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Jellyfish evolved to lose their sting — no predators in lake
tokens.image_credit: Lukas from Munich, Germany · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River
tokens.description: Subterranean river flowing through a limestone karst mountain on Palawan, Philippines, with tidal influence where it reaches the sea. It lies in Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1999.
tokens.image_credit: lumoplank · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pamir Highway
tokens.description: The M41, known as the Pamir Highway, is a road of over 1,200 km across the Pamir Mountains. It is the main supply route to Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region and also runs through Afghanistan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan.
tokens.image_credit: lee hughes · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pamir Mountains
tokens.description: The Pamir Mountains are a mountain range in Central Asia at the junction of the Tian Shan, Karakoram, Kunlun, Hindu Kush and Himalayas. They are among the world's highest mountains.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Where Silk Road crossed — merchants rested before deadly passes
tokens.image_credit: Irene2005 · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pampas
tokens.description: Fertile low grasslands in southern South America, covering much of Argentina as well as Uruguay and southern Brazil. The plains have been heavily changed by humans since cattle, sheep and pigs were introduced.

tokens.name: Darién Gap
tokens.description: A remote, roadless rainforest on the Colombia and Panama border, stretching across Panama's Darién Province. It acts as a natural barrier between North America and South America.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Only gap in 30,000km road from Alaska to Argentina — intentionally kept roadless

tokens.name: Highlands Region
tokens.description: One of the four regions of Papua New Guinea, made up of seven provinces in the mountainous interior of the mainland. Mount Hagen is its largest city.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Most linguistically diverse place on Earth

tokens.name: Park Güell
tokens.description: Park complex with architectural elements in Barcelona's Gràcia district, on the southern slope of the Turó del Carmel hill. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Works of Antoni Gaudí, inscribed in 1984.
tokens.image_credit: Canaan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pashupatinath Temple
tokens.description: Pashupatinath Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Pashupati, a form of Shiva, on the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Nepal. It is part of the Kathmandu Valley UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1979.
tokens.image_credit: Bijay Chaurasia · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fjords and channels of Chile
tokens.description: The southern coast of Chile has a large number of fjords and fjord-like channels, from Cape Horn at 55 degrees south to the Reloncavi Estuary at 42 degrees south. Some are navigable channels giving access to ports such as Punta Arenas and Puerto Natales.
tokens.image_credit: Redfive · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marble Caves
tokens.description: Marble Caves are a group of caverns, columns and tunnels in marble on the shore of General Carrera Lake in Chile. Wave action has carved them over roughly 6,200 years.
tokens.image_credit: Dentren at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Torres del Paine National Park
tokens.description: Torres del Paine National Park covers mountains, glaciers, lakes and rivers in southern Chilean Patagonia. The Cordillera del Paine group of mountains is its centerpiece.
tokens.image_credit: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hương Temple
tokens.description: Hương Temple is a complex of Buddhist temples and shrines built into the limestone Hương Tích mountains, now in Hanoi, Vietnam. It is the site of a religious festival that draws large numbers of pilgrims from across Vietnam.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Millions of pilgrims hike here during spring festival

tokens.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
tokens.description: Perito Moreno is a glacier in Los Glaciares National Park, Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. It is one of the most important tourist attractions in Argentine Patagonia.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Advances 2m per day and calves in dramatic crashes
tokens.image_credit: Gedankenstuecke@VicunaUploader · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piton de la Fournaise
tokens.description: Piton de la Fournaise is a shield volcano on the eastern side of Réunion island in the Indian Ocean. It is one of the most active volcanoes in the world and lies within Réunion National Park, a World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Brian Iannone · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Port Moresby
tokens.description: Port Moresby is the capital and largest city of Papua New Guinea. It lies on the Coral Sea coast of the Papuan Peninsula of the island of New Guinea.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Papua New Guinea has 840 languages — 12% of all languages on Earth
tokens.image_credit: Brian ireland · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Port of Rotterdam
tokens.description: The Port of Rotterdam is the largest seaport in Europe, located in and near Rotterdam in the Netherlands. From 1962 until 2004 it was the world's busiest port by annual cargo tonnage.
tokens.image_credit: Dicklyon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Potala Palace
tokens.title: Palace of the Dalai Lamas
tokens.description: Potala Palace is a palace and museum complex in Lhasa, Tibet. It was the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas from 1649 until 1959 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Rises 13 storeys above the city
tokens.fun_fact_2: Construction began in 1645 under the 5th Dalai Lama
tokens.fun_fact_3: The 14th Dalai Lama fled from it in 1959

curation.notes: Reviewer fame override. Was common. "1,000 rooms" not carried over (TO VERIFY). IMAGE TO SOURCE (network blocked).

tokens.image_credit: Ondřej Žváček · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Preikestolen
tokens.title: Pulpit Rock
tokens.description: Preikestolen is a steep cliff rising 604 metres above Lysefjorden in Strand Municipality, Rogaland, Norway. Its flat top is a popular tourist destination and hiking goal.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Krause, Germany · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Punjab, India
tokens.description: Punjab is a state in northwestern India, bordering Pakistan's Punjab province to the west. Its farmland was central to India's Green Revolution in wheat and rice.

tokens.name: Rani ki Vav
tokens.title: Stepwell of Patan
tokens.description: Rani ki Vav is a stepwell in the town of Patan, Gujarat, India, on the banks of the Saraswati River. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 2014.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Stepwells built for water storage but became art galleries
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ranthambore Fort
tokens.description: Ranthambore Fort is a hill fort within Ranthambore National Park near Sawai Madhopur in Rajasthan, India. It is one of the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2013.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Tiger photographed in front of fort gate — most iconic wildlife photo
tokens.image_credit: Manojmeena · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Reed Flute Cave
tokens.description: Reed Flute Cave is a show cave in Guilin, Guangxi, China, filled with stalactites, stalagmites and other rock formations. It takes its name from the reeds growing outside, which can be made into flutes.
tokens.image_credit: Dariusz Jemielniak · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: NEOM
tokens.description: NEOM is a planned megaproject and smart city in Tabuk Province, Saudi Arabia, launched in 2017 under Saudi Vision 2030. Its flagship, The Line, is planned as a 170 km linear city with no cars or streets.
tokens.fun_fact_1: The Line will house 9M people in 34 sq km

tokens.name: Rock-hewn churches of Tigray
tokens.description: Monolithic churches hewn into cliffs and hillsides in Tigray, northern Ethiopia, with more than 120 known in the region. Abuna Yemata Guh, one of them, sits about 200 metres above the surrounding terrain and has to be climbed on foot.

tokens.name: Rungrado 1st of May Stadium
tokens.title: Pyongyang mega-stadium
tokens.description: Multi-purpose stadium on Rungrado Island in Pyongyang, North Korea, opened on 1 May 1989. Wikipedia describes it as the second largest stadium in the world by seating capacity, after Narendra Modi Stadium.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Capacity larger than most cities
tokens.image_credit: Nicor · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Safaricom
tokens.description: Safaricom is a listed Kenyan mobile network operator headquartered at Safaricom House in Nairobi. Its M-PESA mobile money service, launched in 2007 by Vodafone and Safaricom, has since expanded to several other countries.
tokens.fun_fact_1: More transactions than Western Union globally

tokens.name: Tassili n'Ajjer
tokens.description: Tassili n'Ajjer is a mountain range and national park in south-eastern Algeria that holds one of the most important groupings of prehistoric cave art in the world. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
tokens.image_credit: Linus Wolf · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Land of Frankincense
tokens.description: The Land of Frankincense is a UNESCO World Heritage site in Oman on the ancient Incense Road, with frankincense trees and the remains of a caravan oasis. It was inscribed in 2000 as the Frankincense Trail and renamed in 2005.
tokens.fun_fact_1: One of three places frankincense has grown for 7000 years
tokens.image_credit: Mauro Raffaelli · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Akrotiri
tokens.description: Akrotiri is a Cycladic Bronze Age settlement on the Greek island of Santorini. It was buried in volcanic ash during the Theran eruption in the 16th century BC, which preserved its fine frescoes.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Most complete Bronze Age city — frozen in time like Pompeii but 1600 years earlier
tokens.image_credit: Rt44 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oia, Greece
tokens.description: Oia, also called Ia, is a small village in the Cyclades on the northwesternmost part of Santorini and the island of Therasia, Greece. Since the 2011 local government reform it has been a municipal unit of the Santorini municipality.
tokens.image_credit: TomasEE · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saudi Exchange
tokens.title: Riyadh stock exchange
tokens.description: Saudi Exchange, also known as Tadawul, is the stock exchange of Saudi Arabia. It was formed in 2007 as a joint stock company and is the only entity authorised to act as a securities exchange in the country.

tokens.name: Glen Coe
tokens.description: Glen Coe is a glen of glacial origin that cuts through volcanic rocks in the Highlands of Scotland. It is regarded as the home of Scottish mountaineering and is popular with hillwalkers and climbers.
tokens.image_credit: Dave souza · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seoraksan National Park
tokens.description: Seoraksan National Park is a national park on the east-central Korean Peninsula, in Gangwon Province. It includes the Dinosaur Ridge and has been listed by the South Korean government as a tentative UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Rock visible from 60km away — largest exposed granite in Korea
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alcázar of Seville
tokens.description: The Alcázar of Seville is a historic royal palace in Seville, Spain, and one of the official residences of the Spanish royal family. It was built on the site of an Islamic-era citadel and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Spanish royal family still use it as official residence — may arrive any time
tokens.image_credit: EmDee · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shah-i-Zinda
tokens.description: Shah-i-Zinda is a necropolis of mausoleums in the north-eastern part of Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Samarkand, Crossroads of Cultures, inscribed in 2001.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Custodian of tomb of Muhammad cousin — pilgrimage site
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Bund
tokens.title: Waterfront of Shanghai
tokens.description: The Bund is a waterfront area and protected historical district in central Shanghai, on the western bank of the Huangpu River. Its colonial-era buildings face the modern skyscrapers of Lujiazui in Pudong across the river.
tokens.image_credit: 钉钉 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palace of Shaki Khans
tokens.description: The Palace of Shaki Khans is a historic monument in Shaki, northwestern Azerbaijan, that served as the summer residence of the Shaki khans. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Historic Centre of Shaki with the Khan's Palace.
tokens.fun_fact_1: 5000 pieces of glass fitted without putty — light show inside
tokens.image_credit: Ludvig14 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shenzhen Stock Exchange
tokens.description: The Shenzhen Stock Exchange is one of the three stock exchanges operating independently in mainland China, alongside the Beijing and Shanghai exchanges. It is based in Shenzhen, in the Futian district.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Had 30,000 people in 1980. Has 13M now. Fastest urban growth in history
tokens.aliases: Shenzhen Tech Hub, Tencent Shenzhen HQ
tokens.image_credit: Jay Sterling Austin · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valle dei Templi
tokens.description: Archaeological site of the ancient Greek city of Akragas, on a ridge outside Agrigento in Sicily. It contains a series of Doric temples and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Better preserved than temples in Greece — isolated location protected them
tokens.image_credit: Wolfgang Pehlemann · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Similan Islands
tokens.description: Continental archipelago in the Andaman Sea off Phang Nga Province, southern Thailand, forming Mu Ko Similan National Park, established in 1982. It is a popular diving destination.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Closed 6 months per year to let coral recover
tokens.image_credit: Mathias Krumbholz · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
tokens.description: Tropical garden on the fringe of the Orchard Road shopping district in Singapore, founded at its present site in 1859. It is the only tropical garden honoured as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: National orchid Vanda Miss Joaquim — first hybrid orchid registered 1893
tokens.image_credit: Velela · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gardens by the Bay
tokens.description: Urban park of 105 hectares in central Singapore, adjacent to the Marina Reservoir. It consists of three waterfront gardens: Bay South, Bay East and Bay Central.
tokens.aliases: Marina Bay Sands Singapore, Gardens by the Bay
tokens.image_credit: Shiny Things. · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sipadan
tokens.description: Oceanic island in the Celebes Sea off the east coast of Sabah, Malaysia, and the only oceanic island in Malaysia. It rises about 600 metres from the seabed and was formed by living corals growing on an extinct volcanic cone.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Jemaah Islamiyah kidnapped divers here 2000 — now military guards
tokens.image_credit: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sixty Dome Mosque
tokens.description: Historical mosque in Bagerhat, Khulna Division, Bangladesh, part of the Mosque City of Bagerhat UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is the largest mosque in Bangladesh from the Bengal Sultanate period (1352 to 1576).
tokens.fun_fact_1: Actually has 77 domes — name comes from 60 interior pillars
tokens.image_credit: মোয়ায মাহমুদ · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Smithsonian Institution
tokens.description: The Smithsonian Institution is a group of museums, education and research centres created by the United States government in 1846. Its headquarters, the Smithsonian Castle, stands on the National Mall in Washington, D.C.
tokens.image_credit: Nate Lee · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dracaena cinnabari
tokens.description: Dracaena cinnabari, the Socotra dragon tree, is an umbrella-shaped tree native to the Socotra archipelago in Yemen. It is the national tree of Yemen, and the archipelago is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Alex38 · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Deadvlei
tokens.description: Deadvlei is a white clay pan in the Namib-Naukluft Park in Namibia, with dead trees standing among red dunes. It lies within the Namib Sand Sea UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Ikiwaner · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: SpaceX headquarters, Starbase
tokens.description: SpaceX is an American aerospace manufacturer headquartered at the Starbase development site in Starbase, Texas. Its headquarters was previously in Hawthorne, California.
tokens.image_credit: Jenny Hautmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sukhothai Historical Park
tokens.description: Sukhothai Historical Park covers the ruins of Sukhothai, capital of the Sukhothai Kingdom in the 13th and 14th centuries, in north central Thailand. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Historic Town of Sukhothai and Associated Historic Towns.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Home of Thai alphabet and first Thai script
tokens.image_credit: Hartmann Linge · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tana Toraja Regency
tokens.description: Tana Toraja Regency is a landlocked regency in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, home to the Toraja ethnic group. It is known for its cliff graves with tau-tau effigies and its traditional tongkonan houses.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Dead kept at home for years until family can afford funeral ceremony
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Franganillo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sumela Monastery
tokens.description: Sumela Monastery is a former Greek Orthodox monastery, now a museum, in the Pontic Mountains of Trabzon province, Turkey. It is built into a steep cliff at about 1,200 metres above sea level.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Monks hung off cliff face to paint frescoes — no scaffold
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sundarbans
tokens.description: The Sundarbans is a mangrove forest in the Ganges Delta on the Bay of Bengal, spanning India and Bangladesh. Both its Indian and Bangladeshi parts are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, and the area is home to Bengal tigers.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Honey collectors wear masks on back of head — tigers attack from behind
tokens.image_credit: Shihabur Rahman · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sundarbans National Park
tokens.description: Sundarbans National Park is a national park in West Bengal, India, and the core of a tiger reserve in the Ganges Delta. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site within the Sundarbans mangrove forest.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Tigers here swim and have learned to fish — unique behavior
tokens.image_credit: Kingshuk Mondal · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Suva
tokens.description: Suva is the capital and most populous settlement of Fiji. It is the main port and centre of the country's largest metropolitan area, on the southeast coast of Viti Levu.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Has experienced 4 coups since 1987 — most in any Pacific island nation
tokens.image_credit: Maksym Kozlenko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ushguli
tokens.description: Ushguli is a community of five medieval villages at the head of the Enguri gorge in Svaneti, Georgia. It is one of the highest continuously inhabited settlements in Europe and part of the UNESCO-listed Upper Svaneti.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Each family had a defensive tower — 200+ still standing
tokens.image_credit: Florian Pinel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: São Tomé
tokens.description: São Tomé is the capital and largest city of the island country of São Tomé and Príncipe. Founded in the 15th century, it is one of Africa's oldest colonial cities.
tokens.fun_fact_1: First large scale sugar plantation in world — model copied across Americas
tokens.image_credit: Helena Van Eykeren from Gent, Belgium · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ta Prohm
tokens.title: Temple swallowed by trees
tokens.description: Ta Prohm is a temple near Siem Reap, Cambodia, built mainly in the late 12th and early 13th centuries in the Bayon style. Trees grow over its ruins, and it is part of the UNESCO Angkor World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images, but please mention me as the author and may send me a message. (สามารถใช้ภาพได้อิสระ แต่กรุณาใส่เครดิตผู้ถ่ายและอาจส่งข · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: South Tarawa
tokens.description: South Tarawa is the capital and main hub of Kiribati, home to more than half of the country's population. The urban area is a chain of small low-lying islets.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Will be first nation to disappear underwater — bought land in Fiji to relocate
tokens.image_credit: Photo taken by Government of Kiribati employee in the course of their work · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tayrona National Natural Park
tokens.description: Tayrona National Natural Park is a protected area on the Caribbean coast of Colombia, near Santa Marta. It covers about 150 square kilometres of land and 30 of sea, with jungle, beaches and mountain slopes.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Ciudad Perdida — Colombian Machu Picchu — discovered only in 1972 by grave robbers
tokens.image_credit: David Shankbone · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of the Tooth
tokens.description: Sri Dalada Maligawa, known in English as the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, is a Buddhist temple in Kandy, Sri Lanka. It houses a relic believed to be the tooth of the Buddha and lies within the UNESCO Sacred City of Kandy.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pyramid of the Sun
tokens.description: The largest building in Teotihuacan and one of the largest in Mesoamerica, believed to date from about 200 AD. It stands on the Avenue of the Dead within the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Pre-Hispanic Teotihuacan.
tokens.aliases: Teotihuacan Pyramids, Teotihuacan, Pyramid of the Sun
tokens.image_credit: Burkhard Mücke · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gorkhi-Terelj National Park
tokens.description: Mountain national park about 37 km from Ulaanbaatar, reached by a paved road from the city. It is known for its tourist ger camps and valley landscapes.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Stay in traditional ger tent — Mongolian hospitality obligatory to share
tokens.image_credit: Chongkian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gigafactory Texas
tokens.description: Tesla automotive manufacturing facility in unincorporated Travis County, Texas, just outside Austin. Limited Model Y production began in late 2021, and the opening event was held in April 2022.
tokens.image_credit: Larry D. Moore · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tierra del Fuego
tokens.description: Archipelago at the southern tip of South America, split between Argentina and Chile across the Strait of Magellan. Its main island is Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego, and Cape Horn lies among its smaller islands.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Darwin described Yahgan people — most isolated humans he ever saw
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tikal
tokens.title: Maya city in the jungle
tokens.description: Ruin of an ancient Maya city in the rainforest of the Petén Basin in northern Guatemala, one of the largest pre-Columbian Maya sites. It lies within Tikal National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
tokens.image_credit: Mundo Maya · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tiwanaku
tokens.description: Pre-Columbian archaeological site in western Bolivia near Lake Titicaca, about 70 km from La Paz, and one of the largest sites in South America. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000, under the name Tiwanaku: Spiritual and Political Centre of the Tiwanaku Culture.
tokens.image_credit: CLAUDIOLD · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tongariro National Park
