tokens.description: Oldest national park in New Zealand, located in the central North Island, with the active volcanoes Ruapehu, Ngauruhoe and Tongariro at its centre. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its mixed cultural and natural values.
tokens.image_credit: Segeo14 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Topkapı Palace
tokens.description: Large museum and library in Istanbul, Turkey, and the administrative centre and main residence of the Ottoman sultans from the 1460s until 1853. It lies within the UNESCO World Heritage Site Historic Areas of Istanbul.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Only city on two continents — the only one ever capital of 3 empires
tokens.image_credit: Carlos Delgado · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trevi Fountain
tokens.description: Baroque fountain in the Trevi district of Rome, designed by Nicola Salvi and completed by Giuseppe Pannini in 1762. At 26.3 metres high and 49.15 metres wide, it is the largest Baroque fountain in the world.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Coins collected by charities weekly
tokens.image_credit: NikonZ7II · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trolltunga
tokens.description: Trolltunga is a rock formation jutting horizontally from a cliff about 700 metres above the north side of Lake Ringedalsvatnet, in Ullensvang Municipality, Norway. Its hike has become very popular in recent years.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Most instagrammed Norway landmark — 1000 people/day in summer
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tsavo East National Park
tokens.description: Tsavo East National Park is a national park in Kenya covering 13,747 square kilometres. Established in 1948, it forms part of the Tsavo area of about 22,000 square kilometres together with Tsavo West.
tokens.fun_fact_1: 28 railway workers eaten by two lions during construction
tokens.image_credit: CT Cooper · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ur
tokens.description: Ur was a major Sumerian city-state in ancient Mesopotamia, at Tell el-Muqayyar in Dhi Qar Governorate, southern Iraq. Its remains include a ziggurat.
tokens.image_credit: M.Lubinski from Iraq,USA. · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valley of Flowers National Park
tokens.description: Valley of Flowers National Park is a national park in Chamoli, Uttarakhand, India, established in 1982, known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers. It is part of the Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Valley of flowers discovered by accident by mountaineer returning from expedition
tokens.image_credit: Original: Rohit Sharma Derivative work: UnpetitproleX · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Yasur
tokens.description: Active stratovolcano on Tanna Island, Vanuatu, rising 361 m above sea level. It has a nearly circular summit crater about 400 m across.
tokens.image_credit: Rolf Cosar · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vardzia
tokens.title: Cave city monastery
tokens.description: Rock-hewn cave monastery complex in southern Georgia, excavated from the slopes of Erusheti Mountain above the Kura River. Its main construction took place in the second half of the 12th century, in up to nineteen tiers.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Queen Tamar built it — Georgia only female ruler — at height of power
tokens.image_credit: Alexkom000 · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vatnajökull
tokens.description: Vatnajökull is the largest and most voluminous ice cap in Iceland, covering about 8% of the country. It is the second largest ice cap in Europe by area, after the Severny Island ice cap on Novaya Zemlya.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Lava erupts under ice causing jökulhlaup — catastrophic ice flood

tokens.name: World Health Organization
tokens.title: UN Health Agency
tokens.description: Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, of the World Health Organization, a specialized agency of the United Nations. The organisation coordinates international responses to public health issues and emergencies.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Declared COVID pandemic from this building
tokens.image_credit: Thorkild Tylleskar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: World Trade Organization
tokens.title: Rulebook of World Trade
tokens.description: Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, of the World Trade Organization, an intergovernmental organization that regulates and facilitates international trade. It was established on 1 January 1995.

curation.notes: Legacy opinionated stats removed. Facts generic. IMAGE TO SOURCE (network blocked).

tokens.name: Wadden Sea
tokens.description: The Wadden Sea is an intertidal zone in the southeastern part of the North Sea, lying between the coast of northwestern continental Europe and the Frisian Islands. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and an important area for breeding and migrating birds.
tokens.image_credit: Ralf Roletschek · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wadi Bani Khalid
tokens.description: Wadi Bani Khalid is a wadi and tourist attraction in Oman, with large pools of water and boulders scattered along its course. The wadi covers a large area of lowland and the Hajar Mountains.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wadi Halfa
tokens.description: City in Sudan's Northern State on the shores of Lake Nubia, near the Egyptian border. It is the rail terminus from Khartoum, where goods are moved from trains to ferries on the lake.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Entire town relocated when dam built
tokens.image_credit: Bertramz · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Waitomo Glowworm Cave
tokens.description: Show cave at Waitomo on New Zealand's North Island, known for Arachnocampa luminosa, a glowworm species found only in New Zealand. In 2013 it was described as the most visited glowworm display in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Willison · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wakhan
tokens.description: Rugged mountainous region in the Pamir, Hindu Kush and Karakoram ranges, shared by Afghanistan and Tajikistan. Most of it is Wakhan District in Afghanistan's Badakhshan Province.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Marco Polo described giant sheep here — still called Marco Polo sheep
tokens.image_credit: Tom Hartley at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Walt Disney World
tokens.description: Entertainment and vacation resort complex about 20 miles southwest of Orlando, Florida, opened on 1 October 1971. It includes four theme parks, two water parks and four golf courses.
tokens.image_credit: TheWanderingTraders · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wellington
tokens.description: Capital city of New Zealand, at the southwestern tip of the North Island between Cook Strait and the Remutaka Range. It is the country's third-largest city and the administrative centre of the Wellington Region.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Per capita more cafes than New York — and they know how to make coffee
tokens.image_credit: Krzysztof Golik · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wembley Stadium
tokens.description: Association football stadium in Wembley, London, opened in 2007 on the site of the original Wembley Stadium. It is England's national football stadium and hosts England home matches and the FA Cup Final.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jōmon Sugi
tokens.description: Jōmon Sugi is a large yakusugi Cryptomeria tree on Yakushima, Japan, estimated to be between 2,170 and 7,200 years old. Yakushima as a whole is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Forest was inspiration for Princess Mononoke after Miyazaki visited
tokens.image_credit: Σ64 · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yala National Park
tokens.description: Yala National Park is a national park in Sri Lanka, bordering the Indian Ocean and covering 979 km2. It is known for its Sri Lankan elephants, Sri Lankan leopards and 44 mammal species.
tokens.fun_fact_1: More leopards per km² than anywhere on Earth
tokens.image_credit: Ranmith Welikala · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yazd
tokens.description: Yazd is a historic desert city in Iran, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017. Its old quarters are known for wind catchers, traditional towers that cool buildings through natural ventilation.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Fire has burned continuously for 1,550 years
tokens.image_credit: Andrehmarouti · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Old Faithful
tokens.description: Old Faithful is a cone geyser in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, United States. It is known for its predictable eruptions, on average about every 92 minutes.
tokens.image_credit: Dietmar Rabich · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Honghe Hani Rice Terraces
tokens.description: The Honghe Hani Rice Terraces are a system of rice terraces in Yuanyang County, Yunnan, China, built by the Hani people over about 1,200 years. They are a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape.
tokens.image_credit: Jialiang Gao, www.peace-on-earth.org · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Song-Köl
tokens.description: Song-Köl is a high-altitude lake in northern Naryn Region, Kyrgyzstan. It lies at 3,016 metres above sea level and covers about 270 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Ondřej Žváček · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zakouma National Park
tokens.description: Zakouma National Park is a 3,000 square kilometre national park in southeastern Chad. It is the country's oldest national park, declared in 1963, and has been managed by African Parks since 2010.
tokens.fun_fact_1: Population crashed from 4000 to 400. Now 700 with protection

tokens.name: Camino de Santiago
tokens.description: The Camino de Santiago is a network of pilgrim routes leading to the shrine of the apostle James in Santiago de Compostela, Spain. The Camino Francés and Routes of Northern Spain were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

tokens.image_credit: HJ.Weinz · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cape of Good Hope
tokens.description: The Cape of Good Hope is a rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of the Cape Peninsula in South Africa. It is not the southernmost point of Africa, which is Cape Agulhas.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tenke Fungurume Mine
tokens.description: Tenke Fungurume Mine is a copper and cobalt mine in Lualaba Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, run by Tenke Fungurume Mining SA. It is one of the largest copper and cobalt producers in the country, with construction starting in 2006.

tokens.name: Old City of Dubrovnik
tokens.description: Walled medieval old town of Dubrovnik on the Adriatic coast of Croatia. UNESCO World Heritage site inscribed in 1979, enclosed by fortified city walls.
tokens.image_credit: Zysko serhii · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malecón, Havana
tokens.description: The Malecón is an 8 km seawall, esplanade and roadway along the coast of Havana, Cuba, from Old Havana to the mouth of the Almendares. It was built to protect the city from the sea.

tokens.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial
tokens.description: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial, also called the Atomic Bomb Dome, is the preserved ruin of the former Hiroshima Prefectural Industrial Promotion Hall. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996 as a memorial to the 1945 atomic bombing.

tokens.aliases: Hiroshima Peace Museum, Hiroshima Peace Park, Hiroshima
tokens.image_credit: Oilstreet · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hoover Dam
tokens.description: Hoover Dam is a concrete arch-gravity dam in the Black Canyon of the Colorado River, on the Nevada and Arizona border. Built between 1931 and 1936, it was dedicated by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1935.

tokens.image_credit: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Las Vegas Strip
tokens.title: Bugsy Siegel's casino

tokens.image_credit: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cotai Strip

tokens.name: Sassi di Matera

tokens.name: Marshall Islands
tokens.description: The Marshall Islands, officially the Republic of the Marshall Islands, is an archipelagic country in Oceania. It consists of 29 coral atolls and five main islands in the northwestern Pacific Ocean.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. SKopp assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kiribati
tokens.description: Kiribati, officially the Republic of Kiribati, is an archipelagic country in the central Pacific Ocean. The state comprises 32 atolls and other islands and one remote raised coral island, Banaba.
tokens.image_credit: User:Hanzlan · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tuvalu
tokens.description: Tuvalu is an archipelagic country in the Polynesian sub-region of Oceania, about midway between Hawaii and Australia. It is composed of three reef islands and six atolls.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nauru
tokens.description: Nauru, officially the Republic of Nauru, is an island country and microstate in the South Pacific Ocean. It lies within the Micronesia subregion of Oceania.
tokens.image_credit: User:Skimel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maldives
tokens.description: The Maldives, officially the Republic of Maldives, is an archipelagic country in South Asia, located in the Indian Ocean. Its chain of 26 atolls stretches across the equator.
tokens.image_credit: See File history, below, for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jamaica
tokens.description: Jamaica is an island country in the Caribbean. It is the third-largest island in the Greater Antilles and the Caribbean, after Cuba and Hispaniola.
tokens.image_credit: The SVG code is valid. This vector image was created with Inkscape by SKopp, and then manually edited by Zscout370, Madden and others. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haiti
tokens.description: Haiti is a country in the Caribbean occupying the western side of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with the Dominican Republic. It is the most populous Caribbean country.
tokens.image_credit: (colours and size changes of the now deleted versions) Madden, Vzb83, Denelson83, Chanheigeorge, Zscout370 and Nightstallion Coat of arms :Lokal_Profil and Myriam Thyes · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Afghanistan
tokens.description: Afghanistan is a landlocked country at the crossroads of Central and South Asia. The country is predominantly mountainous, with plains in the north and southwest separated by the Hindu Kush.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lebanon
tokens.description: Lebanon is a country in the Levant region of West Asia, on the Mediterranean coast. It is bordered by Syria to the north and east and by Israel to the south.
tokens.image_credit: Henri Pharaon · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zimbabwe
tokens.description: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in Southeast Africa, bordered by South Africa, Botswana, Zambia and Mozambique. Its capital and largest city is Harare.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sierra Leone
tokens.description: Sierra Leone is a country on the west coast of West Africa. It is bordered to the southeast by Liberia and to the north by Guinea.
tokens.image_credit: Zscout370 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malawi
tokens.description: Malawi is a landlocked country in Southeast Africa. It is bordered by Zambia to the west, Tanzania to the north and northeast, and Mozambique to the east, south and southwest.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Unknown author Vector: Achim1999 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chad
tokens.description: Chad is a landlocked country in Central Africa. It is bordered by Libya to the north, Sudan to the east, the Central African Republic to the south, and Cameroon, Nigeria and Niger to the west and southwest.
tokens.image_credit: SKopp & others (see upload log) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ethiopia
tokens.description: Ethiopia, officially the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa. It borders Eritrea, Djibouti, Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan and Sudan.
tokens.image_credit: Drawn by User:SKopp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puerto Rico
tokens.description: Puerto Rico is a Caribbean archipelago and unincorporated territory of the United States. Its main island lies between the Dominican Republic and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and its capital is San Juan.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Unknown Vector: Cerejota · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bermuda
tokens.description: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is an archipelago of 181 islands, most of them joined by bridges into one apparent landmass.
tokens.image_credit: Version 1: Made by Caleb Moore from the Open Clip Art website and uploaded by Nightstallion Version 2: Made by Nameneko from version 1 of File:Flag of Bermuda.svg and version 2 of File:Coat of arms of · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: United States Virgin Islands
tokens.description: The United States Virgin Islands is a Caribbean unincorporated territory of the United States. The islands lie in the Leeward Islands of the Lesser Antilles.
tokens.image_credit: Percival Wilson Sparks. sparksfamilyassn.org. Retrieved on 2026-05-26. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guam
tokens.description: Guam is an organized, unincorporated territory of the United States in the western Pacific Ocean. Its capital is Hagatna, and it is the largest island in Micronesia.
tokens.image_credit: Xrmap · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Northern Mariana Islands
tokens.description: The Northern Mariana Islands is a commonwealth and unincorporated territory of the United States in the northwestern Pacific Ocean. It consists of the 14 northern islands of the Mariana Archipelago.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isle of Man
tokens.description: The Isle of Man is a self-governing British Crown Dependency in the Irish Sea, between Great Britain and Ireland. It has its own separate international identity within the British Isles.
tokens.image_credit: Fry1989 eh? · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jersey
tokens.description: Jersey is a British Crown Dependency in the English Channel, about 23 km off the Cotentin Peninsula of north-west France. It is the largest of the Channel Islands and has its own legal, fiscal and governmental systems.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guernsey
tokens.description: Guernsey is the second-largest island in the Channel Islands, lying about 43 km west of the Cotentin Peninsula in Normandy. It is the main island of the Bailiwick of Guernsey, a British Crown Dependency.
tokens.image_credit: User:Nightstallion · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Greenland
tokens.description: Greenland is an autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark and the world's largest island. It lies between the Arctic and Atlantic oceans, east of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago.
tokens.image_credit: Jeffrey Connell (IceKarma) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Faroe Islands
tokens.description: The Faroe Islands are a North Atlantic archipelago and a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark. The 18 islands lie between Iceland, Norway and Scotland.
tokens.image_credit: It was made by User:IceKarma (Jeffrey Connell), who released it to the public domain. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: New Caledonia
tokens.description: New Caledonia is a French territory of islands in the southwest Pacific Ocean, about 1,210 km east of Australia. It holds a sui generis collectivity status within the French Republic.

tokens.name: French Polynesia
tokens.description: French Polynesia is an overseas collectivity of France in the South Pacific Ocean. It comprises 121 islands and atolls spread over more than 2,000 km, including Tahiti and Bora Bora.
tokens.image_credit: Nightstallion · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aruba
tokens.description: Aruba is an island constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, in the southern Caribbean Sea about 29 km north of the Venezuelan peninsula of Paraguana. The island covers 179 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Whitney Smith Vector: Wester · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Curaçao
tokens.description: Curaçao is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, an island country in the southern Caribbean Sea about 65 km north of Venezuela. It includes the main island and the uninhabited Klein Curaçao.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Unknown Vector: David Benbennick · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nigeria
tokens.description: Nigeria, officially the Federal Republic of Nigeria, is a country in West Africa between the Sahel to the north and the Gulf of Guinea to the south. With a population of more than 242 million, it is the most populous country in Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Jon Harald Søby. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kenya
tokens.description: Kenya, officially the Republic of Kenya, is a country in East Africa. Its capital and largest city is Nairobi, and it is the seventh-most populous country in Africa.
tokens.image_credit: User:Pumbaa80 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Egypt
tokens.description: Egypt, officially the Arab Republic of Egypt, is a country spanning the northeast corner of Africa and the Sinai Peninsula in Asia. It is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Red Sea to the east.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Morocco
tokens.description: Morocco, officially the Kingdom of Morocco, is a country in North Africa. It has coastlines on the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.
tokens.image_credit: Denelson83, Zscout370 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: South Africa
tokens.description: South Africa, officially the Republic of South Africa, is the southernmost country in Africa. It borders Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Eswatini, and it almost completely encloses Lesotho.
tokens.image_credit: Flag design by Frederick Brownell, image by Wikimedia Commons users · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tanzania
tokens.description: Tanzania, officially the United Republic of Tanzania, is a country in East Africa within the African Great Lakes region. It borders the Indian Ocean to the east and is the most populous country located entirely south of the equator.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uganda
tokens.description: Uganda, officially the Republic of Uganda, is a landlocked country in East Africa. It is bordered by Kenya, South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and Tanzania.
tokens.image_credit: tobias · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ghana
tokens.description: Ghana, officially the Republic of Ghana, is a country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea. It shares borders with Ivory Coast to the west, Burkina Faso to the north and Togo to the east.
tokens.image_credit: Theodosia Okoh · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
tokens.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a country in Central Africa. By land area it is the second-largest country in Africa and the eleventh-largest in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Nightstallion · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rwanda
tokens.description: Rwanda is a landlocked country in East Africa. Its geography is dominated by mountains in the west and savanna in the southeast.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Unknown Vector: Zscout370 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pakistan
tokens.description: Pakistan is a country in South Asia and the fifth-most populous country in the world. Islamabad is the capital and Karachi is the largest city.
tokens.image_credit: User:Zscout370 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Indonesia
tokens.description: Indonesia is a country in Southeast Asia and Oceania, made up of between 13,000 and 17,000 islands. It is the world's largest archipelagic state and the 14th-largest country by area.
tokens.image_credit: Jayakatwang · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Myanmar
tokens.description: Myanmar, also referred to as Burma, is a country in northwest Southeast Asia. It is the largest country by area in Mainland Southeast Asia, with a population of about 55 million.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sri Lanka
tokens.description: Sri Lanka, formerly known as Ceylon, is an island country in South Asia. It is located in the Indian Ocean, southwest of the Bay of Bengal.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Sri Lanka Vectorization: Zscout370, Mike Rohsopht · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cambodia
tokens.description: Cambodia, officially the Kingdom of Cambodia, is a country in Mainland Southeast Asia. It is bordered by Thailand, Laos and Vietnam, and has a coastline along the Gulf of Thailand.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Laos
tokens.description: Laos, officially the Lao People's Democratic Republic, is a country in Mainland Southeast Asia and the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia. Its capital and most populous city is Vientiane.
tokens.image_credit: SKopp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mongolia
tokens.description: Mongolia is a landlocked country in East Asia, bordered by Russia to the north and China to the south. It is the world's most sparsely populated sovereign state, with about 3.5 million people.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kazakhstan
tokens.description: Kazakhstan is a landlocked country in Central Asia with a small part of its territory in Eastern Europe, and it has a coastline on the Caspian Sea. Its capital is Astana, and its largest city is Almaty.
tokens.image_credit: Shaken Niyazbekop · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uzbekistan
tokens.description: Uzbekistan is a doubly landlocked country in Central Asia, bordered by Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan and Turkmenistan. It is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Farhod Yoʻldoshev · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Argentina
tokens.description: Argentina is a country in the far south of South America, sharing the Southern Cone with Chile. It is the eighth-largest country in the world and the second-largest in South America.
tokens.image_credit: Manuel Belgrano · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Colombia
tokens.description: Colombia is a country in north-western South America, with insular regions in North America. It borders the Caribbean Sea, the Pacific Ocean, Venezuela, Brazil, Peru, Ecuador and Panama.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chile
tokens.description: Chile is a country in the Southern Cone of south-western South America. It is the southernmost country in the world and extends along a narrow strip of land between the Andes and the Pacific Ocean.
tokens.image_credit: See file history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peru
tokens.description: Peru is a megadiverse country in western South America, with the Pacific Ocean to the west and the Amazon basin to the east. It borders Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Bolivia and Chile.
tokens.image_credit: David Benbennick · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ecuador
tokens.description: Ecuador is a country in north-western South America, bordered by Colombia, Peru and the Pacific Ocean. It includes the Galapagos Islands, about 1,000 kilometres west of the mainland.
tokens.image_credit: President of the Republic of Ecuador, first uploaded by Denelson83 as Flag of Ecuador.svg, modifications by Husunqu, Zscout370 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venezuela
tokens.description: Venezuela is a country on the northern coast of South America, with a continental landmass and islands in the Caribbean Sea. Its capital and largest city is Caracas.
tokens.image_credit: Various, see File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bolivia
tokens.description: Bolivia is a landlocked country in central South America, with an Andean region in the west and tropical lowlands in the east and north. Its terrain includes the Altiplano plateau, the Amazonian plain and the Gran Chaco.
tokens.image_credit: See file history' below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paraguay
tokens.description: Paraguay is a landlocked country in the central region of South America, bordering Bolivia, Brazil and Argentina. It reaches the Atlantic Ocean through the Parana and Paraguay river waterway.
tokens.image_credit: Republica del Paraguay · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uruguay
tokens.description: Uruguay is a country in southeastern South America, bordering Argentina and Brazil. It lies on the Rio de la Plata to the south and the Atlantic Ocean to the southeast.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guatemala
tokens.description: Guatemala is a country in northern Central America, bordered by Mexico, Belize, Honduras and El Salvador. It is bounded by the Pacific Ocean to the south and the Gulf of Honduras to the northeast.
tokens.image_credit: K21edgo · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Honduras
tokens.description: Honduras is a country in Central America, bordered by Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua. Its capital and largest city is Tegucigalpa.
tokens.image_credit: Kes47 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Salvador
tokens.description: El Salvador is a country in Central America with a Pacific coast, bordered by Guatemala and Honduras. Its capital and largest municipality is San Salvador.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuba
tokens.description: Cuba is an island country in the Caribbean, comprising the main island and 4,195 islands, islets and cays. It lies south of Florida and the Bahamas, and west of Hispaniola.
tokens.image_credit: Miguel Teurbe Tolón and Narciso López · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dominican Republic
tokens.description: The Dominican Republic is an island country occupying the eastern five-eighths of Hispaniola in the Greater Antilles. It shares a land border with Haiti to the west and a maritime border with Puerto Rico to the east.
tokens.image_credit: Juan Pablo Duarte · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Turkey
tokens.description: Turkey, officially the Republic of Türkiye, is a transcontinental country mainly located in Anatolia in West Asia, with a smaller part in Southeast Europe. It is home to over 86 million people.
tokens.image_credit: David Benbennick (original author) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iran
tokens.description: Iran, officially the Islamic Republic of Iran, is a country in West Asia, historically known as Persia. With a population of over 92 million, it ranks 17th globally in both size and population.
tokens.image_credit: SVG file: SiBr4Designer: Hamid NadimiConstruction: ISIRI · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iraq
tokens.description: Iraq, officially the Republic of Iraq, is a country in West Asia. It covers an area of 438,317 square kilometres and has a population of over 46 million.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jordan
tokens.description: Jordan, officially the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, is a country in the Southern Levant region of West Asia. The Jordan River flows into the Dead Sea along its western border.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Syria
tokens.description: Syria, officially the Syrian Arab Republic, is a country in West Asia located in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Levant. It borders the Mediterranean Sea to the west and comprises 14 governorates.
tokens.image_credit: Modification by AnonMoos of PD image File:Flag of Syria (1930–1958, 1961–1963).svg (previous non-vector versions were by Coup de crayon 2011) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yemen
tokens.description: Yemen, officially the Republic of Yemen, is a country in southern Arabia. Its territory includes the Socotra Archipelago in the Indian Ocean.
tokens.image_credit: Nightstallion et al., see File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oman
tokens.description: Oman, officially the Sultanate of Oman, is a country in the southeastern Arabian Peninsula in West Asia. It borders Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Yemen.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · OGL-om 1.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Qatar
tokens.description: Qatar is a country in West Asia that occupies the Qatar Peninsula on the northeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula. Its only land border is with Saudi Arabia, and the rest of its territory is surrounded by the Persian Gulf.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bahrain
tokens.description: Bahrain is an island country in West Asia, made up of a small archipelago centred on Bahrain Island near the western shore of the Persian Gulf. It is linked to Saudi Arabia by the King Fahd Causeway.
tokens.image_credit: Source: Drawn by SKopp, rewritten by Zscout370 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Russia
tokens.description: Russia, officially the Russian Federation, is a country in Eastern Europe and North Asia. It is the largest country in the world, spanning eleven time zones and sharing land borders with fourteen countries.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ukraine
tokens.description: Ukraine is a country in Eastern Europe. It is the second-largest country in Europe after Russia, and borders Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Moldova and the Black Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Government of Ukraine · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Romania
tokens.description: Romania is a country in Central and Southeastern Europe, lying on the lower course of the Danube and the northwestern shore of the Black Sea. It borders Ukraine, Hungary, Serbia, Bulgaria and Moldova.
tokens.image_credit: AdiJapan · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Czech Republic
tokens.description: The Czech Republic, also known as Czechia, is a landlocked country in Central Europe. It is bordered by Austria, Germany, Poland and Slovakia.
tokens.image_credit: Jaroslav Kursa · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hungary
tokens.description: Hungary is a landlocked country in Central Europe, spanning much of the Carpathian Basin. It is bordered by Slovakia, Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia and Austria.
tokens.image_credit: SKopp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bulgaria
tokens.description: Bulgaria, officially the Republic of Bulgaria, is a country in Southeastern Europe on the eastern Balkans. It lies south of the Danube and west of the Black Sea.
tokens.image_credit: SKopp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Slovakia
tokens.description: Slovakia, officially the Slovak Republic, is a landlocked country in Central Europe. It borders Poland, Ukraine, Hungary, Austria and the Czech Republic.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Ladislav Čisárik and Ladislav Vrtel Vector: SKopp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belarus
tokens.description: Belarus, officially the Republic of Belarus, is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe. It borders Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.
tokens.image_credit: See File history below for details. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moldova
tokens.description: Moldova, officially the Republic of Moldova, is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe. It is bordered by Romania to the west and Ukraine to the north, east and south.
tokens.image_credit: Gheorghe Vrabie · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Estonia
tokens.description: Estonia, officially the Republic of Estonia, is a country in the Baltic region of Northern Europe. It borders Latvia to the south and Russia to the east.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Unknown author Vector: SKopp, PeepP and ‍others · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Latvia
tokens.description: Latvia, officially the Republic of Latvia, is a country in the Baltic region of northern Europe. It is one of the three Baltic states, with Estonia to the north and Lithuania to the south.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Ansis Cīrulis Vector: SKopp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lithuania
tokens.description: Lithuania, officially the Republic of Lithuania, is a country in the Baltic region of Europe. It lies on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea and borders Latvia, Belarus and Poland.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Jonas Basanavičius, Tadas Daugirdas and Antanas Žmuidzinavičius Vector: SKopp The SVG code is valid. This flag was created with a text editor.Previous version had been created with Inkscape  · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belgium
tokens.description: Belgium, officially the Kingdom of Belgium, is a country in Northwestern Europe. It is bordered by the Netherlands, Germany, Luxembourg and France, and by the North Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Dbenbenn · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Portugal
tokens.description: Portugal, officially the Portuguese Republic, is a country in Southwestern Europe on the Iberian Peninsula. It also includes the Atlantic archipelagos of Madeira and the Azores.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro Vector: Vítor Luís Rodrigues, António Martins-Tuválkin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ireland
tokens.description: Ireland is an island in the North Atlantic Ocean, in Northwestern Europe. The Republic of Ireland covers five-sixths of the island, and Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom, covers the remaining sixth.
tokens.image_credit: Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: New Zealand
tokens.description: New Zealand is an island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean. It comprises two main landmasses, the North Island and the South Island, and over 700 smaller islands.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Albert Hastings Markham Vector: Zscout370, Hugh Jass, s. File history · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Papua New Guinea
tokens.description: Papua New Guinea is an island nation in Oceania that comprises the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and offshore islands in Melanesia. Its capital is Port Moresby.
tokens.image_credit: User:Nightstallion · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Solomon Islands
tokens.description: Solomon Islands is an archipelagic country of six major islands and over 1,000 smaller islands in Melanesia, Oceania. It lies to the northeast of Australia.
tokens.image_credit: User:SKopp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: September 11 attacks
tokens.title: Attacks on New York and Washington
tokens.description: The September 11 attacks were coordinated suicide attacks by the al-Qaeda terrorist organization against the United States in 2001. Hijacked airliners struck the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City and the Pentagon in Virginia.
tokens.image_credit: Flickr user Michael Foran · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Apollo 11 launch
tokens.title: First crewed Moon landing mission departs
tokens.description: Apollo 11 was launched atop a Saturn V rocket from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on July 16, 1969, at 13:32 UTC. The mission was the first crewed flight to land humans on the Moon.
tokens.aliases: Apollo 8 launch, Apollo 17 launch, Apollo 12, Apollo 15, Apollo 16, Apollo 9, Apollo 14
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
tokens.title: Border opens after 28 years
tokens.description: The Fall of the Berlin Wall began on 9 November 1989, when crowds gathered at the border crossings after an East German announcement that citizens could travel without restrictions. Television broadcast the events live worldwide.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown photographer, Reproduction by Lear 21 at English Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of the Titanic
tokens.title: Liner lost on maiden voyage
tokens.description: RMS Titanic sank in the North Atlantic on 15 April 1912, four days into her maiden voyage after striking an iceberg. Around 1,500 people died, one of the deadliest peacetime maritime disasters in history.
tokens.image_credit: Willy Stöwer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Live Aid
tokens.title: Global charity concert at Wembley
tokens.description: Live Aid was a benefit concert held on 13 July 1985 to raise funds for famine relief in Ethiopia. The London leg took place at Wembley Stadium, with a simultaneous show at JFK Stadium in Philadelphia.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Waterloo
tokens.title: Napoleon's final defeat
tokens.description: The Battle of Waterloo was fought on 18 June 1815 near Waterloo, now in Belgium. It was the last engagement of Napoleon I, when his French army was defeated by Wellington's British-led force and Blücher's Prussians.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Normandy landings
tokens.title: Allied assault on Normandy
tokens.description: The Normandy landings were Allied amphibious and airborne operations on 6 June 1944, known as D-Day, during Operation Overlord. Described as the largest seaborne invasion in history, they began the liberation of France.
tokens.image_credit: Chief Photographer's Mate (CPHoM) Robert F. Sargent · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
tokens.title: First wartime use of nuclear weapons
tokens.description: The United States detonated atomic bombs over Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, during the final days of World War II. They remain the only uses of nuclear weapons in an armed conflict.
tokens.image_credit: George R. Caron / Charles Levy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre
tokens.title: Student-led demonstrations in Beijing
tokens.description: Student-led protests were held in Tiananmen Square, Beijing, from 15 April to 4 June 1989. Troops moved into the square on the night of 3 June, in what is known as the Tiananmen Square massacre.

tokens.name: First powered flight
tokens.title: Wright Flyer airborne at Kitty Hawk
tokens.description: The Wright Flyer, flown by Orville and Wilbur Wright, made the first sustained, powered and controlled flight by a manned heavier-than-air aircraft on 17 December 1903. The flight took place at Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina.
tokens.image_credit: John T. Daniels · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
tokens.title: Magnitude 9.0 off Japan's coast
tokens.description: A Mw 9.0 to 9.1 undersea megathrust earthquake struck the Pacific Ocean off the Tōhoku region of Japan on 11 March 2011. The quake triggered a tsunami that flooded large parts of the northeastern coast.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Miracle on Ice
tokens.title: US beats USSR at Lake Placid
tokens.description: The Miracle on Ice was an ice hockey game at the 1980 Winter Olympics in Lake Placid, New York. The United States beat the heavily favoured Soviet Union 4 to 3 on February 22, 1980.
tokens.image_credit: Henry Zbyszynski · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sputnik 1 launch
tokens.title: First artificial satellite in orbit
tokens.description: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957 from Site 1 at the Baikonur Cosmodrome, becoming the first artificial Earth satellite. It sent radio signals back to Earth for about three weeks.
tokens.image_credit: Andrey Butko · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Falcon Heavy test flight
tokens.title: Roadster sent into solar orbit
tokens.description: The Falcon Heavy test flight was SpaceX's first launch of the Falcon Heavy rocket, on 6 February 2018 from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center. The payload was Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster, sent into a heliocentric orbit.
tokens.image_credit: SpaceX · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vostok 1
tokens.title: Yuri Gagarin, first human in space
tokens.description: Vostok 1 carried Yuri Gagarin on the first human orbital spaceflight, launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome on 12 April 1961. The flight completed one orbit of the Earth, reaching a maximum altitude of 327 km.
tokens.image_credit: SiefkinDR · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Apollo 13
tokens.title: Mission survives oxygen tank failure
tokens.description: Apollo 13 was the seventh crewed Apollo mission, launched from Kennedy Space Center on 11 April 1970. An oxygen tank failure aborted the planned Moon landing, and the crew returned safely to Earth on 17 April.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Challenger disaster
tokens.title: Shuttle lost 73 seconds after launch
tokens.description: Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch on 28 January 1986, killing all seven crew members. The breakup occurred over the Atlantic Ocean off Cape Canaveral, Florida.
tokens.image_credit: Kennedy Space Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Columbia disaster
tokens.title: Shuttle breaks up on re-entry
tokens.description: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated while re-entering the atmosphere over Texas and Louisiana on 1 February 2003, killing all seven astronauts. It was the second Space Shuttle mission to end in disaster, after Challenger in 1986.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hindenburg disaster
tokens.title: Airship burns at Lakehurst
tokens.description: The Hindenburg disaster was the fire that destroyed the German airship LZ 129 Hindenburg while it attempted to dock at Naval Air Station Lakehurst, New Jersey. The accident occurred on 6 May 1937 in Manchester Township.
tokens.image_credit: Sam Shere · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
tokens.title: President shot in Dealey Plaza
tokens.description: On 22 November 1963, President John F. Kennedy was fatally shot while riding in a motorcade through Dallas, Texas. The shots came from the nearby Texas School Book Depository, according to the article on the event.
tokens.image_credit: Mchristo19 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Storming of the Bastille
tokens.title: Fortress seized in Paris
tokens.description: On 14 July 1789, insurgents stormed the Bastille, the medieval fortress and political prison in Paris. After about four hours of fighting, the insurgents entered and the governor was killed after surrendering.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Hastings
tokens.title: Norman conquest of England
tokens.description: The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066 between the Norman army of William, Duke of Normandy, and an English army under King Harold Godwinson. The Norman victory began the Norman Conquest of England, near the present-day town of Battle, East Sussex.
tokens.image_credit: Ealdgyth · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Marathon
tokens.title: Athenians repel Persian army
tokens.description: The Battle of Marathon took place in 490 BCE during the first Persian invasion of Greece. It was fought between the Athenians, aided by Plataea, and a Persian force commanded by Datis and Artaphernes.
tokens.image_credit: Tomisti · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Thermopylae
tokens.title: Spartans hold the pass
tokens.description: The Battle of Thermopylae was fought in 480 BC between the Achaemenid Persian Empire under Xerxes and a Greek alliance led by Sparta under Leonidas I. It lasted about three days and was one of the most prominent battles of the second Persian invasion of Greece.

tokens.name: Battle of Salamis
tokens.title: Greek fleet defeats Persians
tokens.description: The Battle of Salamis was a naval battle fought in 480 BC between an alliance of Greek city-states under Themistocles and the Achaemenid Empire under Xerxes. The outnumbered Greeks won in the straits between the mainland and Salamis island, near Athens.

tokens.name: Battle of Gaugamela
tokens.title: Alexander defeats Darius III
tokens.description: The Battle of Gaugamela took place in 331 BC between the army of Alexander the Great and the Persian army of King Darius III. Alexander's victory is considered the final blow to the Achaemenid Empire. The fighting took place near the village of Gaugamela, north of Arbela, modern Erbil.

tokens.name: Battle of Cannae
tokens.title: Hannibal's double envelopment
tokens.description: The Battle of Cannae was fought on 2 August 216 BC during the Second Punic War, near the ancient village of Cannae in Apulia, southeast Italy. Hannibal's Carthaginian army surrounded and practically annihilated a larger Roman and Italian army.
tokens.image_credit: Jörg Schulz · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Actium
tokens.title: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra
tokens.description: The Battle of Actium was a naval battle on 2 September 31 BC in the Ionian Sea between Octavian's fleet under Agrippa and the combined fleets of Mark Antony and Cleopatra. It ended the rivalry between Octavian and Antony and led to Octavian becoming sole ruler of Rome.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Landon · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Julius Caesar
tokens.title: Ides of March in Rome
tokens.description: Julius Caesar, the Roman dictator, was stabbed to death on 15 March 44 BC by a group of senators during a Senate session in the Curia of Pompey in Rome. The assassination was led by Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus.
tokens.image_credit: Vincenzo Camuccini · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD
tokens.title: Pompeii and Herculaneum buried
tokens.description: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pyroclastic flows. It is one of the deadliest eruptions in history and gave its name to the Vesuvian type of eruption.
tokens.image_credit: Qfl247 (talk) (Transferred by Citypeek/Original uploaded by Qfl247) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Tours
tokens.title: Franks halt Umayyad advance
tokens.description: The Battle of Tours was fought on 10 October 732 between the Frankish and Aquitanian forces of Charles Martel and the Umayyad army led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi. Many historians credit the Frankish victory with curtailing the spread of Islam in Western Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Charles de Steuben · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Manzikert
tokens.title: Seljuks defeat Byzantines
tokens.description: The Battle of Manzikert was fought on 26 August 1071 between the Byzantine Empire and the Seljuk Empire near modern Malazgirt in eastern Turkey. The capture of Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes weakened Byzantine authority in Anatolia and helped open the region to gradual Turkic settlement.
tokens.image_credit: O.Mustafin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Agincourt
tokens.title: English longbows win in the mud
tokens.description: The Battle of Agincourt was fought on 25 October 1415 near Azincourt in northern France during the Hundred Years' War. The English victory over the much larger French army boosted English morale and began a new period of English dominance in the war.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Constantinople
tokens.title: Ottomans take Byzantine capital
tokens.description: Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire, was captured by the Ottoman Empire on 29 May 1453 after a 53-day siege. Sultan Mehmed II then made the city the new Ottoman capital, replacing Adrianople.
tokens.image_credit: Fausto Zonaro · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Lepanto
tokens.title: Holy League defeats Ottoman fleet
tokens.description: The Battle of Lepanto was a naval engagement on 7 October 1571 in the Gulf of Patras, where a fleet of the Holy League led by Spain and Venice defeated the Ottoman fleet. It was the last major battle fought almost entirely between galleys and galleasses.
tokens.image_credit: Laureys a Castro · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spanish Armada
tokens.title: English Channel campaign
tokens.description: The Spanish Armada was a Spanish fleet that sailed from Lisbon in late May 1588 to escort an invasion force bound for England. It was the largest engagement of the undeclared Anglo-Spanish War.
tokens.image_credit: Philip James de Loutherbourg · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Trafalgar
tokens.title: Nelson's decisive victory at sea
tokens.description: The Battle of Trafalgar was a fleet action on 21 October 1805 between the Royal Navy and a combined French and Spanish fleet. The allied fleet had sailed from Cádiz in southern Spain.
tokens.image_credit: Clarkson Frederick Stanfield · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Austerlitz
tokens.title: Napoleon's masterpiece
tokens.description: The Battle of Austerlitz was fought on 2 December 1805 near Austerlitz, in what is now the Czech Republic. Napoleon's Grande Armee defeated a combined Russo-Austrian army in the decisive engagement of the War of the Third Coalition.
tokens.image_credit: François Gérard · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Borodino
tokens.title: Bloodiest day of the Napoleonic invasion
tokens.description: The Battle of Borodino was fought on 7 September 1812 near the village of Borodino, on the outskirts of Moscow. It was fought during Napoleon's invasion of Russia, when the Grande Armee met the Imperial Russian Army.
tokens.image_credit: Louis Lejeune · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gettysburg Address
tokens.title: Lincoln's 272-word speech
tokens.description: The Gettysburg Address is a dedication speech delivered by Abraham Lincoln on 19 November 1863. He gave it at Soldiers' National Cemetery, now Gettysburg National Cemetery, in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.
tokens.image_credit: Photographer attributions vary from unidentified (William Frassanito) to Mathew Brady (NARA) and David Bachrach (1845-1921) (Center for Civil War Photography). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Stalingrad
tokens.title: Turning point on the Eastern Front
tokens.description: The Battle of Stalingrad was fought between Nazi Germany and its Axis allies and the Soviet Union for control of the city of Stalingrad, now Volgograd, in southern Russia. It is considered the largest and deadliest urban battle in military history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Midway
tokens.title: Carriers decide the Pacific war
tokens.description: The Battle of Midway was a major naval battle of the Pacific Theater of World War II, fought on 4 to 7 June 1942. The Japanese Combined Fleet suffered a decisive defeat by the U.S. Pacific Fleet near Midway Atoll.
tokens.image_credit: National Museum of the U.S. Navy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Britain
tokens.title: RAF defends the skies
tokens.description: The Battle of Britain was a campaign of the Second World War in which the Royal Air Force defended the United Kingdom against attacks by the German Luftwaffe. It was the first major military campaign fought entirely by air forces.
tokens.image_credit: Skyden67 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dunkirk evacuation
tokens.title: Allied troops rescued from the beaches
tokens.description: Operation Dynamo evacuated more than 338,000 Allied soldiers from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk, France, between 26 May and 4 June 1940. The troops had been encircled during the Battle of France.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Berlin
tokens.title: Final major battle in Europe
tokens.description: The Battle of Berlin was one of the last major offensives of the European theatre of World War II, fought by the Red Army against German forces in April and May 1945. It ended with the capture of the German capital.
tokens.image_credit: Yevgeny Khaldei / Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nuremberg trials
tokens.title: Nazi leaders tried for war crimes
tokens.description: The Nuremberg trials were international criminal trials held in Nuremberg by France, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom and the United States. They prosecuted leaders of defeated Nazi Germany for plotting invasions and committing atrocities in the Second World War.
tokens.image_credit: Raymond D'Addario · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuban Missile Crisis
tokens.title: Thirteen days on the nuclear brink
tokens.description: The Cuban Missile Crisis was a 13-day confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union over Soviet nuclear missiles deployed in Cuba. It lasted from 16 to 28 October 1962 and is widely considered the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war.

tokens.name: Bay of Pigs Invasion
tokens.title: Failed exile landing in Cuba
tokens.description: The Bay of Pigs Invasion was a failed landing in April 1961 on the southwestern coast of Cuba by Cuban exiles of the Democratic Revolutionary Front, backed by the United States. It took place at Playa Giron and influenced relations between Cuba, the United States and the Soviet Union.
tokens.image_credit: Rumlin · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuban Revolution
tokens.title: Castro's forces take Havana
tokens.description: The Cuban Revolution was the military and political movement that overthrew the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista, who had ruled Cuba from 1952 to 1959. Castro's forces entered Havana in January 1959.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph: Lester Cole/Corbis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Saigon
tokens.title: North Vietnamese tanks enter Saigon
tokens.description: Saigon, capital of South Vietnam, was captured by North Vietnamese forces on 30 April 1975, ending the Vietnam War. The fall caused the evacuation of thousands of civilians and American personnel.
tokens.image_credit: Hubert van Es · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
tokens.title: French defeat ends colonial rule
tokens.description: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu was a defeat of French Union forces by the Viet Minh in the First Indochina War, fought from 13 March to 7 May 1954. It took place in northwest Tonkin, deep in the Tai Federation area.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Inchon
tokens.title: MacArthur's amphibious reversal
tokens.description: The Battle of Inchon was an amphibious invasion during the Korean War that resulted in a decisive victory and strategic reversal for the United Nations Command. The landings led to the recapture of Seoul two weeks later.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Partition of India
tokens.title: Independence and division
tokens.description: The Partition of India in 1947 divided British India into the Union of India and the Dominion of Pakistan. The division of the provinces of Bengal and the Punjab followed district-wide religious majorities.
tokens.image_credit: Photo Division, Government of India · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
tokens.title: Shot at Birla House, Delhi
tokens.description: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 in the compound of Birla House in central New Delhi, now the Gandhi Smriti museum. His assassin was Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist from Pune.
tokens.image_credit: Wilson Loo Kok Wee · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salt March
tokens.title: Gandhi marches to Dandi
tokens.description: The Salt March was a 24-day nonviolent civil disobedience march led by Mahatma Gandhi in colonial India, from 12 March to 6 April 1930. It protested the British salt monopoly and ended at the coastal village of Dandi.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Long March
tokens.title: Communist retreat across China
tokens.description: The Long March was a military retreat by the Chinese Communist Party and Red Army from October 1934 to October 1935. About 100,000 troops travelled roughly 10,000 kilometres from Jiangxi to a new headquarters in Yan'an, Shaanxi.

tokens.name: Nanjing Massacre
tokens.title: Atrocities in the captured city
tokens.description: The Nanjing Massacre was the mass rape and murder of Chinese civilians and prisoners of war by the Imperial Japanese Army in Nanjing, between December 1937 and March 1938. It followed the Battle of Nanjing during the Second Sino-Japanese War.
tokens.image_credit: 上野特派员(scanned by Sweeper tamonten (talk on December 25, 2008) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cultural Revolution
tokens.title: Mass political upheaval in China
tokens.description: The Cultural Revolution was a sociopolitical movement in the People's Republic of China, launched by Mao Zedong in 1966 and lasting until his death in 1976. Its stated goal was to purge remnants of capitalist and traditional elements from Chinese society and government.
tokens.image_credit: 《人民画报》 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Chinese Famine
tokens.title: Famine following the Great Leap Forward
tokens.description: The Great Chinese Famine was a famine in the People's Republic of China that occurred between 1959 and 1961. Some scholars also include the years 1958 or 1962.

tokens.name: Iranian Revolution
tokens.title: Monarchy falls in Tehran
tokens.description: The Iranian Revolution culminated in 1979 in the overthrow of the Pahlavi dynasty and the creation of the Islamic Republic of Iran. Ruhollah Khomeini became the country's supreme leader.

tokens.name: Iran hostage crisis
tokens.title: US embassy staff held 444 days
tokens.description: The Iran hostage crisis began on 4 November 1979, when students stormed the US Embassy in Tehran and took 66 Americans hostage. 52 of them were held until 20 January 1981.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soviet-Afghan War
tokens.title: Soviet forces enter Kabul
tokens.description: The Soviet Union and the Communist-led Afghan military fought the Afghan mujahideen from December 1979 to February 1989. The war marked the beginning of the 47-year-long Afghan conflict.
tokens.image_credit: erwinlux · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gulf War
tokens.title: Coalition liberates Kuwait
tokens.description: The Gulf War was an armed conflict between Iraq and a 42-country coalition led by the United States, after Iraq invaded Kuwait on 2 August 1990. The American-led coalition liberated Kuwait on 28 February 1991.
tokens.image_credit: US Air Force · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2003 invasion of Iraq
tokens.title: Coalition forces enter Iraq
tokens.description: The 2003 invasion of Iraq was the first stage of the Iraq War and began on 20 March 2003. A United States-led coalition of mainly American, British, Australian and Polish troops conducted it.
tokens.image_credit: Lance Cpl. Brian L. Wickliffe, U.S. Marine Corps · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Baghdad 2003
tokens.title: Saddam statue toppled in Firdos Square
tokens.description: The Battle of Baghdad (2003), also known as the Fall of Baghdad, was a military engagement in early April 2003 as part of the invasion of Iraq. Coalition forces led by the US Army 3rd Infantry Division captured the city.
tokens.image_credit: Marine Lieutenant Tim McLaughlin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capture of Saddam Hussein
tokens.title: Found near Tikrit
tokens.description: Saddam Hussein, the deposed president of Iraq, was captured by United States forces in Ad-Dawr, Iraq, on 13 December 2003. The operation was codenamed Operation Red Dawn.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Killing of Osama bin Laden
tokens.title: Raid on Abbottabad compound
tokens.description: On 2 May 2011 the United States conducted Operation Neptune Spear, in which SEAL Team Six killed Osama bin Laden at his compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
tokens.image_credit: Sajjad Ali Qureshi · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arab Spring
tokens.title: Uprisings begin in Sidi Bouzid
tokens.description: The Arab Spring was a series of pro-democracy protests, uprisings and armed rebellions that spread across much of the Arab world in the early 2010s. It began in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia, after the self-immolation of Mohamed Bouazizi.
tokens.image_credit: cjb · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2011 Egyptian revolution
tokens.title: Tahrir Square uprising
tokens.description: The 2011 Egyptian revolution, also known as the 25 January Revolution, began on 25 January 2011 and spread across Egypt. It consisted of demonstrations, occupations of plazas, civil resistance and strikes against police brutality under Hosni Mubarak.
tokens.image_credit: Mona · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rwandan genocide
tokens.title: One hundred days of mass killing
tokens.description: The Rwandan genocide, also known as the genocide against Tutsi, took place from 7 April to 19 July 1994. Over about 100 days, Hutu militias systematically killed Tutsi and some moderate Hutu and Twa.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Jones, Ph.D. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1994 South African general election
tokens.title: First multiracial elections
tokens.description: The 1994 South African general election was held from 26 to 29 April 1994. It was the first in which citizens of all races could vote, and it marked the end of apartheid.

tokens.name: Sharpeville massacre
tokens.title: Police fire on protesters
tokens.description: The Sharpeville massacre occurred on 21 March 1960, when South African police opened fire on a crowd protesting the apartheid pass laws. It took place outside the police station in the township of Sharpeville.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soweto uprising
tokens.title: Student protest over Afrikaans
tokens.description: The Soweto uprising was a series of protests by black schoolchildren in the Soweto township, South Africa, beginning on 16 June 1976. The students opposed the use of Afrikaans as the medium of instruction in black schools.
tokens.image_credit: Sam Nzima · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Adwa
tokens.title: Ethiopia defeats Italian invasion
tokens.description: The Battle of Adwa was fought on 1 March 1896 near the town of Adwa between Ethiopian forces under Emperor Menelik II and an Italian colonial army. The Ethiopian victory ended the Italian attempt to impose a protectorate over Ethiopia.
tokens.image_credit: Franko Khoury. · PDM-owner · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Isandlwana
tokens.title: Zulu victory over British column
tokens.description: The Battle of Isandlwana was fought on 22 January 1879 in the Anglo-Zulu War. A Zulu force of some 20,000 warriors attacked a British column of about 1,800 troops and won a major victory.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Edwin Fripp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Rorke's Drift
tokens.title: Defence of a mission station
tokens.description: The Battle of Rorke's Drift was an engagement in the Anglo-Zulu War, fought at a Swedish mission station and British supply depot. A vastly outnumbered British force held the post, and the battle holds the record for the most Victoria Crosses awarded for a single battle.
tokens.image_credit: Alphonse de Neuville · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Suez Crisis
tokens.title: Canal nationalisation leads to invasion
tokens.description: The Suez Crisis was a 1956 invasion of Egypt by the United Kingdom, France and Israel, launched after Egypt nationalised the Suez Canal. The invaders aimed to depose President Gamal Abdel Nasser and regain control of the canal.
tokens.image_credit: United States Army Heritage and Education Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Six-Day War
tokens.title: Rapid war reshapes the Middle East
tokens.description: The Six-Day War was fought from 5 to 10 June 1967 between Israel and a coalition of six Arab states, primarily Egypt, Syria and Jordan. Israel occupied the Sinai Peninsula, the Gaza Strip, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights.
tokens.image_credit: Rafi Rogel (רפי רוגל) · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yom Kippur War
tokens.title: Surprise attack on Yom Kippur
tokens.description: The Yom Kippur War was fought from 6 to 25 October 1973 between Israel and a coalition of Arab states led by Egypt and Syria. Most of the fighting took place in the Sinai Peninsula and the Golan Heights.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oslo Accords
tokens.title: Rabin and Arafat shake hands
tokens.description: The Oslo Accords are two interim agreements between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization, Oslo I signed in Washington in 1993 and Oslo II signed in Taba in 1995. They started the Oslo peace process, based on UN Resolutions 242 and 338.
tokens.image_credit: Vince Musi / The White House · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: United States Declaration of Independence
tokens.title: Thirteen colonies declare independence
tokens.description: The founding document of the United States, adopted unanimously by the Second Continental Congress in Philadelphia on 4 July 1776. It was adopted in the Pennsylvania State House, later renamed Independence Hall.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boston Tea Party
tokens.title: Tea thrown into the harbor
tokens.description: The Boston Tea Party was a protest on 16 December 1773, staged by the Sons of Liberty in Boston against British tea policy. Colonists threw a cargo of British tea into Boston Harbor, escalating tensions with Great Britain.
tokens.image_credit: Original uploader was Cornischong at lb.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
tokens.title: Shot heard round the world
tokens.description: The Battles of Lexington and Concord on 19 April 1775 were the first major military actions between British troops and Patriot militias in the American Revolutionary War. The fighting took place in Middlesex County, Massachusetts.
tokens.image_credit: Don Troiani · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Yorktown
tokens.title: Cornwallis surrenders
tokens.description: The Siege of Yorktown, fought in Virginia in 1781, was the final major land engagement of the American Revolutionary War. Continental and French forces defeated the British army commanded by Charles Cornwallis.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Louisiana Purchase
tokens.title: US doubles in size
tokens.description: The Louisiana Purchase was the 1803 acquisition by the United States from the French First Republic of about 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River, for $15 million. The transfer ceremony took place in New Orleans.
tokens.image_credit: Matysik · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Alamo
tokens.title: Texian defenders fall in San Antonio
tokens.description: The Battle of the Alamo, fought from February 23 to March 6, 1836, was a pivotal engagement of the Texas Revolution in San Antonio. Mexican troops under Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna took the Alamo Mission after a 13-day siege.
tokens.image_credit: Loadmaster (David R. Tribble) This image was made by Loadmaster (David R. Tribble). Email the author: David R. Tribble Also see my personal gallery at Google Photos · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
tokens.title: Custer's last stand
tokens.description: The Battle of the Little Bighorn, fought on June 25 and 26, 1876 in southeastern Montana, was a defeat of the United States 7th Cavalry Regiment. It is also known as Custer's Last Stand and was the most significant action of the Great Sioux War.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Marion Russell · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wounded Knee Massacre
tokens.title: Lakota killed in South Dakota
tokens.description: The Wounded Knee Massacre was an 1890 armed conflict in South Dakota between the United States Army and Native Americans, part of the Pine Ridge Campaign. Between 250 and 300 Lakota people were killed.
tokens.image_credit: Frederic Remington · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: California gold rush
tokens.title: Gold found at Sutter's Mill
tokens.description: The California gold rush (1848 to 1855) began when gold was found at Sutter's Mill in Coloma on January 24, 1848. It brought about 300,000 people to California and helped the territory grow rapidly into statehood through the Compromise of 1850.
tokens.image_credit: George H. Johnson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Chicago Fire
tokens.title: City center burns
tokens.description: The Great Chicago Fire burned in Chicago, Illinois, from October 8 to 10, 1871. It killed approximately 300 people and destroyed about 17,000 structures.
tokens.image_credit: Currier and Ives · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1906 San Francisco earthquake
tokens.title: Quake and fires devastate city
tokens.description: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake, a magnitude 7.9 event, struck the coast of Northern California on April 18, 1906. Extensive fires broke out in San Francisco and burned for several days.
tokens.image_credit: Chadwick, H. D · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wall Street crash of 1929
tokens.title: Black Tuesday stock collapse
tokens.description: The Wall Street crash of 1929 was a sharp collapse of US stock prices that began on the New York Stock Exchange in October 1929. It eroded confidence in the American banking system and helped trigger the Great Depression.
tokens.image_credit: US-gov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dust Bowl
tokens.title: Dust storms ravage the Great Plains
tokens.description: The Dust Bowl was a period of severe dust storms in the 1930s that damaged farming and ecology across the American and Canadian prairies. Drought and the loss of topsoil from poor farming methods caused it.
tokens.image_credit: Arthur Rothstein · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Katrina
tokens.title: New Orleans floods after levee failures
tokens.description: Hurricane Katrina was a catastrophic tropical cyclone that struck the US Gulf Coast in late August 2005. It caused its greatest damage in and around New Orleans and killed 1,392 people.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montgomery bus boycott
tokens.title: Year-long protest after Rosa Parks arrest
tokens.description: The Montgomery bus boycott was a campaign against racial segregation on the public buses of Montgomery, Alabama, from 1955 to 1956. It began after Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat, and it was a foundational event of the civil rights movement.
tokens.image_credit: Gene Herrick for the Associated Press; restored by Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: March on Washington
tokens.title: "I Have a Dream" speech
tokens.description: The March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom was held in Washington, D.C., on August 28, 1963, to advocate for the civil and economic rights of African Americans. It is known for Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech.
tokens.image_credit: This photograph was made by Rowland Scherman at the March on Washington. The negatives are in the custody of the National Archives. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Selma to Montgomery marches
tokens.title: Bloody Sunday on Edmund Pettus Bridge
tokens.description: The Selma to Montgomery marches were three protest marches held in 1965 along the 54-mile highway from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama. They demanded voting rights for African Americans and contributed to the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
tokens.image_credit: Abernathy Family · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
tokens.title: Shot at the Lorraine Motel
tokens.description: Martin Luther King Jr., an American civil rights activist, was fatally shot on April 4, 1968, at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee. The shooting took place at about 6:01 p.m. local time.
tokens.image_credit: Bubba73 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Watergate scandal
tokens.title: Break-in that toppled a president
tokens.description: The Watergate scandal was a political scandal involving the administration of President Richard Nixon. It began with the June 17, 1972 break-in at the Democratic National Committee headquarters in the Watergate complex in Washington, D.C., and led to Nixon's resignation in August 1974.
tokens.image_credit: Farragutful · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kent State shootings
tokens.title: National Guard fires on students
tokens.description: The Kent State shootings were the killing of four and wounding of nine students by the Ohio National Guard on the Kent State University campus on May 4, 1970. The shootings occurred during a protest against the expansion of the Vietnam War into Cambodia.
tokens.image_credit: Pacificboyksu · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Plassey
tokens.title: Clive wins Bengal for the East India Company
