tokens.description: The Battle of the Sakarya was fought from 23 August to 13 September 1921 near the Sakarya River and Polatli, in the Greco-Turkish War. It halted the Greek advance towards Ankara.
tokens.image_credit: Sfisek · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Burning of Smyrna
tokens.description: The burning of Smyrna destroyed much of the port city of Smyrna, modern Izmir, in September 1922. The fire started on 13 September and was largely extinguished by 22 September, after the Turkish army captured the city.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2016 Turkish coup attempt
tokens.description: A military coup attempt against the government of Turkey on 15 July 2016. Armed soldiers tried to seize key sites in Ankara, Istanbul and Marmaris but were defeated by loyalist troops and civilians.
tokens.image_credit: Pivox · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gezi Park protests
tokens.description: A wave of nationwide demonstrations in Turkey that began on 28 May 2013 against the redevelopment plan for Istanbul's Gezi Park. The protests spread across the country and concerned press freedom and the government's secularism.
tokens.image_credit: Mstyslav Chernov · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2015 Mina crowd crush
tokens.description: A fatal crowd crush during the Hajj pilgrimage in Mina, near Mecca, Saudi Arabia, on 24 September 2015. More than 2,000 people died, making it the deadliest Hajj disaster in history.
tokens.image_credit: Aiman titi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1983 Beirut barracks bombings
tokens.description: On 23 October 1983, two truck bombs struck buildings in Beirut housing US and French peacekeepers of the Multinational Force in Lebanon. The attacks killed 307 people, including 241 US and 58 French military personnel.
tokens.image_credit: USMC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1982 Hama massacre
tokens.description: In February 1982 Syrian army and paramilitary forces under President Hafez al-Assad besieged the city of Hama for 27 days to crush a Muslim Brotherhood uprising. The campaign killed thousands of civilians and left much of the old city destroyed.

tokens.name: Black September
tokens.description: An armed conflict in Jordan between the army of King Hussein and the Palestine Liberation Organization, also known as the Jordanian Civil War. The main fighting took place between 16 and 27 September 1970 in and around Amman.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Yitzhak Rabin
tokens.description: Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin was assassinated on 4 November 1995 in Tel Aviv, at the end of a rally in support of the Oslo Accords. The assailant, Yigal Amir, was a far-right Israeli law student who opposed the peace initiative.
tokens.image_credit: Israel Press and Photo Agency (I.P.P.A.) photographer · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Egyptian revolution of 1952
tokens.description: On 23 July 1952 the Free Officers Movement, led by Mohamed Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser, toppled King Farouk of Egypt in a coup. It started a wave of revolutionary politics across the Arab world.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Anwar Sadat
tokens.description: On 6 October 1981, Egyptian President Anwar Sadat was shot dead during the annual victory parade in Cairo marking the 1973 war with Israel. The attack was carried out by members of Egyptian Islamic Jihad.
tokens.image_credit: Einsamer Schütze · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kuwaiti oil fires
tokens.description: In January and February 1991, retreating Iraqi forces set fire to between 605 and 732 oil wells in Kuwait during the Gulf War. The last well was capped on 6 November 1991.
tokens.image_credit: Lt. Steve Gozzo, U.S. Navy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Battle of Fallujah
tokens.description: The Second Battle of Fallujah was an American-led offensive of the Iraq War that began on 7 November 2004 and lasted about six weeks. It was the first major engagement fought mainly against the Iraqi insurgency.
tokens.image_credit: Lance Corporal Samantha L. Jones, USMC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse
tokens.description: In 2003 and 2004, United States Army and CIA personnel abused and tortured detainees at Abu Ghraib prison near Baghdad. Photographs published by CBS News in April 2004 caused international outrage.

tokens.name: 2006 Lebanon War
tokens.description: The 2006 Lebanon War was a 34-day armed conflict between Hezbollah and Israel, from 12 July to 14 August 2006. It was the third Israeli invasion of Lebanon since 1978.
tokens.image_credit: Masser · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Kasserine Pass
tokens.description: The Battle of Kasserine Pass was fought from 19 to 24 February 1943 in west central Tunisia during the Tunisian campaign of World War II. Axis forces under Erwin Rommel defeated the U.S. II Corps and British units there.
tokens.image_credit: unknown, WII Signal Corps Photograph Collection · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Annual
tokens.description: The Battle of Annual was fought on 22 July 1921 at Annual in northeastern Morocco, during the Rif War. The Spanish Army suffered a major defeat, known in Spain as the Disaster of Annual.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Capilla · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rif War
tokens.description: The Rif War was an anti-colonial war fought from 1921 to 1926 between Riffian Berber tribes of northern Morocco and Spain, joined by France in 1924. It ended with the surrender of Abd el-Krim after the Al Hoceima landing.
tokens.image_credit: José Moreno Carbonero · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eritrean Ethiopian War
tokens.description: The Eritrean Ethiopian War was a major armed conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea from May 1998 to June 2000. It followed Eritrea's independence in 1993 and a dispute over the new international border.

tokens.name: Ogaden War
tokens.description: The Ogaden War was fought between Somalia and Ethiopia from July 1977 to March 1978 over the Ogaden region. Somalia invaded in support of the Western Somali Liberation Front, which triggered a wider interstate war.

tokens.name: War in Darfur
tokens.description: The War in Darfur was an armed conflict in Sudan's Darfur region that began in February 2003 between rebel groups and the government. It caused hundreds of thousands of civilian deaths and displaced millions of people.
tokens.image_credit: Nite Owl · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Killing of Muammar Gaddafi
tokens.description: Muammar Gaddafi, former leader of Libya, was captured and killed on 20 October 2011 after the Battle of Sirte. The killing was carried out by forces of the National Transitional Council.

tokens.name: Tunisian revolution
tokens.title: Spark of the Arab Spring
tokens.description: The Tunisian revolution was a 28-day campaign of street protests and civil resistance that led to the ousting of Zine El Abidine Ben Ali in January 2011. It is often described as the only successful movement of the Arab Spring.
tokens.image_credit: M.Rais · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Green March
tokens.description: The Green March was a mass demonstration organised by Morocco in November 1975 to press Spain into handing over Spanish Sahara. The marchers crossed into the territory from the Tarfaya area.

tokens.name: 1980 El Asnam earthquake
tokens.description: The 1980 El Asnam earthquake struck northern Algeria on 10 October 1980 with a moment magnitude of 7.1 and a maximum Mercalli intensity of X. The shock hit the town of El Asnam, now Chlef, and was felt more than 550 km away.

tokens.name: War of the Golden Stool
tokens.description: The War of the Golden Stool, also called the Yaa Asantewaa War, was a 1900 uprising of the Ashanti against British occupation in present-day Ghana. It centred on Kumasi and the demand for the Golden Stool.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence
tokens.description: Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence was a statement adopted by the Rhodesian Cabinet at Salisbury on 11 November 1965. It was the first unilateral break from the United Kingdom by a colony since 1776, and the UN imposed the first sanctions in its history in response.
tokens.image_credit: Government of Rhodesia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mozambican Civil War
tokens.description: The Mozambican Civil War was fought from 1977 to 1992 between the FRELIMO government and the RENAMO insurgency. It was shaped by Cold War politics and killed over one million people, mainly through fighting and famine.

tokens.name: Cyclone Idai
tokens.description: Intense Tropical Cyclone Idai hit Mozambique, Zimbabwe and Malawi in March 2019, with more than 1,500 people killed. It is the deadliest tropical cyclone recorded in the South-West Indian Ocean basin.
tokens.image_credit: Rein Skullerud/WFP · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malagasy Uprising
tokens.description: The Malagasy Uprising was a nationalist rebellion against French colonial rule in Madagascar from March 1947 to February 1949. It was triggered by the failure of legal efforts for independence and the harsh French response.
tokens.image_credit: Hardscarf · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Ladysmith
tokens.description: The siege of Ladysmith was fought in the Second Boer War from 2 November 1899 to 28 February 1900 at Ladysmith, Natal. Boer forces surrounded the town until British relief forces broke through.
tokens.image_credit: John Henry Frederick Bacon · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marikana massacre
tokens.description: The Marikana massacre was the killing of 34 striking miners by South African police on 16 August 2012 at the Lonmin platinum mine near Rustenburg. It was the deadliest use of force by South African security forces against civilians since the Soweto uprising in 1976.

tokens.name: Lake Nyos disaster
tokens.title: Lake releases deadly CO2 cloud
tokens.description: On 21 August 1986 a limnic eruption at Lake Nyos in northwestern Cameroon released a cloud of carbon dioxide that killed 1,746 people and 3,500 livestock. The gas flowed down into nearby villages.
tokens.image_credit: United States Geological Survey · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sierra Leone Civil War
tokens.description: The Sierra Leone Civil War (1991 to 2002) was a conflict started by the Revolutionary United Front, backed by Charles Taylor's NPFL from Liberia. It caused an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 deaths and displaced around 2.5 million people.
tokens.image_credit: Laura Lartigue · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mali War
tokens.description: The Mali War is a conflict that began on 16 January 2012 with a Tuareg rebellion in northern Mali. The rebel MNLA was initially allied with the jihadist group Ansar Dine.
tokens.image_credit: Anne Look · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of MV Le Joola
tokens.title: Overloaded ferry capsizes
tokens.description: MV Le Joola was a Senegalese government ferry that capsized off The Gambia on 26 September 2002, with 1,863 deaths and 64 survivors. It is thought to be the third-worst peacetime maritime disaster in history.

tokens.name: Herero and Nama genocide
tokens.description: The Herero and Nama genocide was the extermination of the Herero and Nama peoples in German South West Africa, now Namibia, by the German Empire between 1904 and 1908. Estimates put the Herero deaths at 40,000 to 80,000 and the Nama deaths at about 10,000.
tokens.image_credit: Harald Süpfle · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mahdist War
tokens.description: The Mahdist War from 1881 to 1899 was fought between the Mahdist Sudanese forces of Muhammad Ahmad and the Khedivate of Egypt, later joined by Britain. The Mahdists took Khartoum and gained control of Sudan.
tokens.image_credit: William Barnes Wollen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eddington experiment
tokens.title: Eclipse tests general relativity
tokens.description: The Eddington experiment was a 1919 test of general relativity led by Frank Dyson and Arthur Eddington during the solar eclipse of 29 May 1919. Expeditions to Principe and Sobral measured the bending of starlight passing near the Sun.
tokens.image_credit: C. Davidson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Okehazama
tokens.description: The Battle of Okehazama took place on 12 June 1560 in Owari Province, present-day Aichi Prefecture. Oda Nobunaga's outnumbered forces defeated Imagawa Yoshimoto, establishing Oda as a leading warlord of the Sengoku period.
tokens.image_credit: Utagawa Toyonobu · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Nagashino
tokens.description: The Battle of Nagashino was fought in 1575 at Nagashino in Mikawa Province, present-day Aichi Prefecture, Japan. Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated the Takeda clan, a decisive step in Nobunaga's unification of Japan.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Honnō-ji Incident
tokens.description: The Honnō-ji Incident was the 1582 attack on Oda Nobunaga at the Honnō-ji temple in Kyoto, led by his vassal Akechi Mitsuhide. Nobunaga died there, ending his campaign to unify Japan.
tokens.image_credit: Nobukazu Yōsai · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shimabara Rebellion
tokens.description: The Shimabara Rebellion was an uprising from December 1637 to April 1638 in the Shimabara Domain, led by Amakusa Shiro against heavy taxes and the ban on Christianity. The rebels were crushed at Hara Castle in April 1638.
tokens.image_credit: Saito Shuho (1772-1859), 斎藤 秋圃 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boshin War
tokens.description: The Boshin War was a civil war fought in Japan from 1868 to 1869 between the Tokugawa shogunate and a coalition seeking power in the name of the Imperial Court. It ended the shogunate and opened the way to the Meiji Restoration.
tokens.image_credit: Utagawa Yoshitora (signed as Nagashima Mosai) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Satsuma Rebellion
tokens.description: The Satsuma Rebellion, also called the Seinan War, was a revolt of disaffected samurai against the Meiji government in 1877. It was crushed in September 1877, and its leader Saigo Takamori was mortally wounded.
tokens.image_credit: Sensai Eitaku (Kobayashi Eitaku) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: February 26 incident
tokens.description: The February 26 incident was an attempted coup in the Empire of Japan on 26 February 1936, carried out by young Imperial Japanese Army officers. The rebels killed several senior officials and occupied central Tokyo, but did not take control of the government.
tokens.image_credit: Chosakai (?) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Perry Expedition
tokens.description: The Perry Expedition was a 1852 to 1855 voyage of United States Navy warships under Commodore Matthew Perry to Japan. It forced the opening of Japan to American trade and diplomatic relations after more than two centuries of isolation.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Chosin Reservoir
tokens.description: The Battle of Chosin Reservoir was fought in the winter of 1950 during the Korean War, when Chinese forces attacked United Nations troops in the northeast of North Korea. It is known for the freezing conditions and the withdrawal of the US Marines and Army units to Hungnam.
tokens.image_credit: Photo by Corporal Peter McDonald, USMC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Pusan Perimeter
tokens.description: The Battle of the Pusan Perimeter was fought from August 4 to September 18, 1950, between United Nations Command forces and the North Korean People's Army. The UN defence around Busan held, a turning point of the Korean War.
tokens.image_credit: Pfc. Thomas Nebbia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jeju uprising
tokens.description: The Jeju uprising began on 3 April 1948 when the Workers' Party of South Korea launched an armed revolt on Jeju Island. The military suppressed it by May 1949, with indiscriminate violence against island residents.
tokens.image_credit: Encyclopedia of Korean Culture · KOGL Type 1 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: March First Movement
tokens.description: The March First Movement was a series of protests against Japanese colonial rule held across Korea and by the Korean diaspora from March 1, 1919. It is remembered as a landmark of the Korean independence movement.
tokens.image_credit: Bureau d'information coréen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of ROKS Cheonan
tokens.description: The South Korean corvette ROKS Cheonan sank on 26 March 2010 off Baengnyeong Island in the Yellow Sea, killing 46 sailors. An international investigation concluded that a North Korean torpedo sank the ship, which North Korea rejected.
tokens.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Byron C. Linder · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sampoong Department Store collapse
tokens.description: The Sampoong Department Store in Seoul's Seocho District collapsed on 29 June 1995, killing 502 people and injuring 937. It was the largest peacetime disaster in South Korean history.
tokens.image_credit: 최광모 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seoul Halloween crowd crush
tokens.description: A crowd surge during Halloween celebrations in the Itaewon district of Seoul on 29 October 2022 killed 158 people directly and injured 196. Most victims were young adults, and 27 were foreign nationals.
tokens.image_credit: Watchers Club · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Hansan Island
tokens.description: The Battle of Hansan Island took place on 15 August 1592, when Admiral Yi Sun-sin's Korean fleet destroyed roughly 100 Japanese ships. The victory halted Japanese naval operations along the southern coast.

tokens.name: Huaihai campaign
tokens.description: The Huaihai campaign, fought from 6 November 1948 to 10 January 1949, was a major People's Liberation Army offensive against Kuomintang forces around Xuzhou and the Huai River. It ended with the destruction or surrender of major Kuomintang forces.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Wuhan
tokens.description: The Battle of Wuhan was the largest, longest and bloodiest battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War. It was fought over four and a half months across several central Chinese provinces, with Wuhan as its focus.
tokens.image_credit: 唐古樵 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shanghai massacre
tokens.description: The Shanghai massacre of 12 April 1927 was the violent suppression of Chinese Communist Party organizations and leftist groups by forces backing Chiang Kai-shek. It began a wider anti-communist purge in Nationalist-controlled areas.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boxer Rebellion
tokens.description: The Boxer Rebellion was an uprising in North China from 1899 to 1901, towards the end of the Qing dynasty, by the Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists. It was defeated by the Eight-Nation Alliance of foreign powers.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Opium War
tokens.description: The Second Opium War was fought from 1856 to 1860 between the United Kingdom and France against the Qing dynasty of China. It forced the legalisation of the opium trade and a second defeat for the Qing.
tokens.image_credit: Godefroy Durand · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Sino-Japanese War
tokens.description: The First Sino-Japanese War lasted from July 1894 to April 1895 between the Qing dynasty of China and the Empire of Japan, mainly over influence in Korea. Japanese victory ended with the Treaty of Shimonoseki.
tokens.image_credit: Toshikata Mizuno · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wuchang Uprising
tokens.description: The Wuchang Uprising was an armed rebellion against the Qing dynasty in Wuchang, Hubei, on 10 October 1911. It began the 1911 Revolution that overthrew China's last imperial dynasty.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ping-pong diplomacy
tokens.description: Ping-pong diplomacy was the exchange of table tennis players between the United States and the People's Republic of China in the early 1970s. It began at the 1971 World Table Tennis Championships in Nagoya and is seen as a turning point in US-China relations.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1972 visit by Richard Nixon to China
tokens.description: From 21 to 28 February 1972, US President Richard Nixon visited Beijing, the first visit by a sitting US president to the People's Republic of China. It ended 23 years without official diplomatic ties between the two countries.
tokens.image_credit: President (1969-1974 : Nixon). White House Photo Office. 1969-1974, General Services Administration. National Archives and Records Service. Office of Presidential Libraries. Office of Presidential Pap · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Handover of Macau
tokens.description: The handover of Macau from Portugal to the People's Republic of China took place at midnight on 20 December 1999. It ended 442 years of Portuguese rule that began in 1557.
tokens.image_credit: US Department of State · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2019-2020 Hong Kong protests
tokens.description: From 2019 to 2020, mass protests were held in Hong Kong against a government bill to amend the extradition law. They were the largest series of demonstrations in the city's history.
tokens.image_credit: Studio Incendo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dong Fang Hong 1
tokens.title: China's first satellite
tokens.description: Dong Fang Hong 1 was the first satellite of the People's Republic of China, launched successfully on 24 April 1970. It was part of the Dongfanghong program and the Two Bombs, One Satellite program.
tokens.image_credit: Brücke-Osteuropa · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chang'e 6
tokens.description: Chang'e 6 was the sixth robotic lunar mission of the China National Space Administration and its second sample-return mission. It was the first mission to retrieve samples from the far side of the Moon.
tokens.image_credit: BugWarp · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Guandu
tokens.description: The Battle of Guandu was fought in 200 AD between the warlords Cao Cao and Yuan Shao in the late Eastern Han dynasty. Cao Cao's victory made him the dominant power in northern China.

tokens.name: Tumu Crisis
tokens.description: The Tumu Crisis was a border conflict between the Oirat Mongols and the Ming dynasty that began with Esen Taishi's invasion in July 1449. Emperor Yingzong personally led Ming armies against Esen.

tokens.name: Battle of Guningtou
tokens.description: The Battle of Guningtou was fought in October 1949 on Kinmen (Quemoy) during the final stages of the Chinese Civil War. The Republic of China victory kept Kinmen under its control and halted plans for an immediate Communist invasion of Taiwan.
tokens.image_credit: Getty Images · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mongolian Revolution of 1921
tokens.description: The Mongolian Revolution of 1921 expelled Russian White Guards from Mongolia with help from the Soviet Red Army. It led to the founding of the Mongolian People's Republic in 1924.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Ia Drang
tokens.description: The Battle of Ia Drang in 1965 was the first major battle between the US Army and the People's Army of Vietnam. It was notable for the first large-scale helicopter air assault of the Vietnam War.
tokens.image_credit: United States Army · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Huế
tokens.description: The Battle of Huế, from 31 January to 2 March 1968, was a major battle of the Tet Offensive in the Vietnam War. South Vietnamese and US forces recaptured the city after a little over one month of fighting.
tokens.image_credit: USMC Archives from Quantico, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Linebacker II
tokens.description: Operation Linebacker II was a US strategic bombing campaign against North Vietnam from 18 to 29 December 1972. Its main targets were Hanoi and Haiphong, and it is also known as the Christmas bombing.
tokens.image_credit: USAF · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: August Revolution
tokens.description: The August Revolution was a Viet Minh-led uprising against the Japanese occupation and the Empire of Vietnam from 16 to 30 August 1945. It set the stage for the independence of Vietnam.
tokens.image_credit: Front pour l'indépendance du Việt-Nam · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Long Tan
tokens.description: The Battle of Long Tan, from 18 to 21 August 1966, was fought in a rubber plantation in Phước Tuy Province, South Vietnam. Elements of the 1st Australian Task Force fought Viet Cong and PAVN units there.
tokens.image_credit: Tacintop · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Marawi
tokens.description: The Siege of Marawi was a five-month armed conflict from May 2017 between Philippine government forces and Islamic State-affiliated militants. It was the longest urban battle in modern Philippine history.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Jhomel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Philippine Revolution
tokens.description: The Philippine Revolution was a war of independence waged by the Katipunan against Spain from 1896 to 1898. It ended centuries of Spanish colonial rule in the archipelago.
tokens.image_credit: Manuel Arias Rodríguez · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Philippine Declaration of Independence
tokens.description: The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed by Emilio Aguinaldo on June 12, 1898, at Cavite el Viejo, now Kawit. It asserted the independence of the Philippine islands from three centuries of Spanish colonial rule.
tokens.image_credit: Ralff Nestor Nacor · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Ninoy Aquino
tokens.description: Benigno Ninoy Aquino Jr., a former senator and critic of President Ferdinand Marcos, was shot dead on 21 August 1983 at Manila International Airport. Rolando Galman, accused of the killing, was also killed.

tokens.name: Indonesian National Revolution
tokens.description: The Indonesian National Revolution was the armed and diplomatic struggle between the Republic of Indonesia and the Dutch Empire, from the 1945 proclamation of independence until the Dutch transfer of sovereignty in 1949. It ended with the recognition of the United States of Indonesia.

tokens.name: 30 September Movement
tokens.description: The 30 September Movement was a coup attempt allegedly orchestrated by the Communist Party of Indonesia. In the early hours of 1 October 1965 six Indonesian Army generals were assassinated in Jakarta.
tokens.image_credit: Si Gam · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2002 Bali bombings
tokens.description: Three terrorist attacks on 12 October 2002 in the Kuta tourist district of Bali killed 202 people, including 151 Western tourists. Two suicide bombings hit the Sari Club and Paddy's Pub.
tokens.image_credit: Jonathan Liem · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Suharto
tokens.description: Indonesian President Suharto resigned on 21 May 1998, ending 32 years of New Order rule after nationwide protests and the 1997 Asian financial crisis. Vice President B. J. Habibie succeeded him and launched the Reformasi reforms.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown photographer, attributed to the Office of the Vice President of the Republic of Indonesia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Java Sea
tokens.description: The Battle of the Java Sea, fought from 27 February 1942, was a decisive Imperial Japanese Navy victory over Allied naval forces in the Pacific campaign of World War II. The Allied Combined Striking Force was led by Dutch Rear-Admiral Karel Doorman.
tokens.image_credit: Photo taken from a Japanese aircraft · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 13 May incident
tokens.description: The 13 May incident was a period of violent ethnic conflict between Malay and Chinese communities in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, starting on 13 May 1969 after the general election. A state of emergency was declared and parliament was suspended.
tokens.image_credit: HRH Sultan Ismail Nasiruddin Shah · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sook Ching
tokens.description: Sook Ching was a mass killing of Chinese civilians in Singapore by the Japanese army from 18 February to 4 March 1942, after the city fell. The Civilian War Memorial in Singapore commemorates the civilian victims of the Japanese occupation.
tokens.image_credit: Deoma12 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Assaye
tokens.description: The Battle of Assaye was fought on 23 September 1803 during the Second Anglo-Maratha War. A British army led by Arthur Wellesley defeated a Maratha army under Daulatrao Scindia and Raghoji II Bhonsle near Assaye in western India.
tokens.image_credit: AnonymousUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Saragarhi
tokens.description: The Battle of Saragarhi was a last-stand battle fought on 12 September 1897 between the British Indian Empire and Afghan tribesmen. Orakzai and Afridi tribesmen surrounded the Saragarhi outpost and cut off Fort Gulistan from Fort Lockhart.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Partition of Bengal 1905
tokens.description: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was a territorial reorganisation of the Bengal Presidency by the British Raj, announced by Lord Curzon on 16 October 1905. It separated the largely Muslim eastern areas from the western areas and was undone six years later.

tokens.name: Komagata Maru incident
tokens.description: The Komagata Maru incident was an immigration dispute in which 376 mostly Sikh passengers were denied entry at Vancouver, British Columbia, on 23 May 1914. The ship had sailed from Hong Kong carrying passengers from Punjab, British India.
tokens.image_credit: Vancouver Public Library Historical Photographs · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Indian annexation of Hyderabad
tokens.description: The annexation of Hyderabad, code-named Operation Polo, was a military operation launched in September 1948 by India. It ended the princely state of Hyderabad, which India dubbed a police action.

tokens.name: Indian annexation of Goa
tokens.description: In December 1961 the Republic of India annexed the Portuguese territories of Goa, Daman and Diu after armed action by the Indian Armed Forces. India calls it the Liberation of Goa, while Portugal calls it the Invasion of Goa.

tokens.name: 1984 anti-Sikh riots
tokens.description: The 1984 anti-Sikh riots were organised pogroms against Sikhs across India after Indira Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards. Government estimates put the deaths at about 2,800 in Delhi and 3,350 nationwide.

tokens.name: 2001 Indian Parliament attack
tokens.description: The 2001 Indian Parliament attack was a terrorist attack on the Parliament of India in New Delhi on 13 December 2001. Five Jaish-e-Mohammed militants were killed, and nine security personnel and staff died.
tokens.image_credit: This image was produced by me, David Castor (user:dcastor). The pictures I submit to the Wikipedia Project are released to the public domain. This gives you the right to use them in any way you like,  · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chandrayaan-2
tokens.description: Chandrayaan-2 is the second Indian lunar exploration mission, consisting of an orbiter, the Vikram lander and the Pragyan rover. It was launched in 2019 to study lunar surface composition and water.
tokens.image_credit: Indian Space Research Organisation · GODL-India · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aryabhata satellite launch
tokens.title: India's first satellite
tokens.description: Aryabhata was India's first satellite, built by ISRO. It was launched on 19 April 1975 from Kapustin Yar in the Soviet Union on a Kosmos-3M rocket.
tokens.image_credit: ISRO · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Searchlight
tokens.description: Operation Searchlight was a military operation by the Pakistan Army launched in March 1971 to curb the Bengali nationalist movement in East Pakistan. Its plans included taking control of the major cities, beginning with Dhaka.
tokens.image_credit: Pritam Saha · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bengali language movement
tokens.description: The Bengali language movement was a political movement in East Bengal in 1952 demanding recognition of Bengali as an official language of Pakistan. It is commemorated each year on 21 February, now International Mother Language Day.
tokens.image_credit: Prof. Rafiqul Islam · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
tokens.description: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, founding president of Bangladesh, was killed with most of his family on 15 August 1975 by army personnel in a coup. It was the first direct military intervention in the country's civilian administration.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Department of State from United States · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings
tokens.description: On 21 April 2019, Islamic State-linked suicide bombers attacked three churches and three hotels in Sri Lanka, with further blasts in Dematagoda and Dehiwala. A total of 270 people were killed, most of them Christians.
tokens.image_credit: AntanO · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saur Revolution
tokens.description: The Saur Revolution was a coup and uprising by the People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan on 27 and 28 April 1978. It overthrew President Mohammad Daoud Khan, who was killed with most of his family at the Arg palace in Kabul.
tokens.image_credit: Cleric77 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1935 Quetta earthquake
tokens.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Quetta in Baluchistan on 31 May 1935, killing an estimated 30,000 to 60,000 people. It was the deadliest earthquake to strike South Asia until 2005.

tokens.name: 1966 Tashkent earthquake
tokens.description: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake struck central Tashkent on 26 April 1966, destroying most of the city's buildings. Between 15 and 200 people died, and the historic districts were rebuilt in Soviet style.

tokens.name: 1988 Armenian earthquake
tokens.description: A surface-wave magnitude 6.8 earthquake with maximum MSK intensity X struck northern Armenia, then part of the Soviet Union, on 7 December 1988. The source was a thrust fault just north of Spitak.

tokens.name: Tulip Revolution
tokens.description: The Tulip Revolution, also called the First Kyrgyz Revolution, followed disputed parliamentary elections in February and March 2005. It led to the fall of President Askar Akayev.

tokens.name: Rose Revolution
tokens.description: The Rose Revolution was a nonviolent change of power in Georgia in November 2003, after disputed parliamentary elections. It ended the presidency of Eduard Shevardnadze and the Soviet-era leadership.

tokens.name: Russo-Georgian War
tokens.description: The Russo-Georgian War was fought in August 2008 between Georgia and Russia, with the Russian-backed separatist regions of South Ossetia and Abkhazia. It is regarded as the first European war of the 21st century.
tokens.image_credit: Lt. Jim Hoeft, U.S. Navy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
tokens.description: The Second Nagorno-Karabakh War was a 44-day armed conflict in 2020 over the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh region, involving Azerbaijan and Armenia. It ended with an Azerbaijani victory.
tokens.image_credit: ԶԻՆՈՒԺ MEDIA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Black January
tokens.description: Black January was a violent Soviet military crackdown on anti-Soviet and independence protests in Baku on 19 and 20 January 1990. Official Azerbaijani estimates count 147 civilians killed and 800 injured.
tokens.image_credit: Rəcəb Həsənbəyov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salem witch trials
tokens.description: The Salem witch trials were hearings and prosecutions of people accused of witchcraft in colonial Massachusetts between February 1692 and May 1693. Nineteen people were executed by hanging.
tokens.image_credit: Joseph E., ca. 1837-1914, artist. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Shiloh
tokens.description: The Battle of Shiloh was a major American Civil War battle fought on 6 and 7 April 1862 in southwestern Tennessee. It took place between the Shiloh church and Pittsburg Landing on the Tennessee River.
tokens.image_credit: Thure de Thulstrup / Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Hampton Roads
tokens.title: Ironclads clash
tokens.description: The Battle of Hampton Roads was a naval battle of the American Civil War fought on 8 and 9 March 1862 between the ironclads CSS Virginia and USS Monitor. It was part of the Confederate effort to break the Union blockade.
tokens.image_credit: Kurz and Allison · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sand Creek massacre
tokens.description: The Sand Creek massacre took place on 29 November 1864, when U.S. Army volunteers under John Chivington attacked a Cheyenne and Arapaho village in Colorado Territory. Most sources estimate about 150 people were killed, about two-thirds of them women and children.
tokens.image_credit: Stone Rabbit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haymarket affair
tokens.description: The Haymarket affair was a bombing at a labor demonstration on 4 May 1886 at Haymarket Square in Chicago. The rally supported workers striking for an eight-hour workday, and the event later inspired International Workers' Day.
tokens.image_credit: Thure de Thulstrup · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ludlow Massacre
tokens.description: The Ludlow Massacre was an attack on 20 April 1914 by the Colorado National Guard and mine company guards on a tent colony of striking coal miners and their families in Ludlow, Colorado. About 21 people were killed, mostly miners' wives and children.
tokens.image_credit: Bain News Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Scopes trial
tokens.description: The Scopes trial was a 1925 case in Dayton, Tennessee, in which teacher John T. Scopes was charged under the Butler Act for teaching human evolution. It was widely publicized and is also known as the Scopes Monkey Trial.
tokens.image_credit: Smithsonian Institution from United States; Beyond My Ken (talk) 01:35, 4 August 2017 (UTC) · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tulsa race massacre
tokens.description: The Tulsa race massacre was a two-day attack by white mobs on Black residents of the Greenwood District in Tulsa, Oklahoma, on May 31 and June 1, 1921. More than 35 blocks of the neighborhood, known as Black Wall Street, were burned.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: War of the Worlds broadcast
tokens.title: Radio drama sparks alarm
tokens.description: The War of the Worlds was a Halloween episode of CBS's Mercury Theatre on the Air, broadcast live on October 30, 1938 and directed and narrated by Orson Welles. Its news-bulletin format led some listeners to believe a Martian invasion was under way.
tokens.image_credit: The Cecelia Company, 731 Plymouth Court, Chicago, Illinois; M. L. Annenberg, Publisher · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ivy Mike
tokens.title: First full-scale hydrogen bomb
tokens.description: Ivy Mike was the first full-yield test of a multi-stage thermonuclear device, detonated by the United States on November 1, 1952. The 10.4 megaton blast at Elugelab in Enewetak Atoll vaporized the island.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake
tokens.description: The Loma Prieta earthquake struck the Central Coast of California on October 17, 1989, with its center in the Forest of Nisene Marks State Park near Santa Cruz. Damage included the collapse of a section of the Nimitz Freeway in Oakland.
tokens.image_credit: Flickr photographer sanbeiji / Joe Lewis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Camp Fire 2018
tokens.description: The 2018 Camp Fire in Butte County, Northern California, was the deadliest and most destructive wildfire in California history. It began on November 8, 2018 from a failed PG&E transmission line and mostly destroyed the town of Paradise.
tokens.image_credit: Activist · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Flint water crisis
tokens.description: The Flint water crisis was a public health crisis from 2014 to 2019 in which drinking water in Flint, Michigan, was contaminated with lead. It followed the city's April 2014 switch of its water source to the Flint River.
tokens.image_credit: unknown, United States Environmental Protection Agency · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Saipan
tokens.description: The Battle of Saipan was a United States amphibious assault on Japanese-held Saipan from 15 June to 9 July 1944. The capture of the island put the major Japanese home islands within range of B-29 bombers.
tokens.image_credit: William F. Draper · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Philippine Sea
tokens.description: The Battle of the Philippine Sea was a naval battle on 19 and 20 June 1944 during the American reconquest of the Mariana Islands. It was the last of five major carrier-versus-carrier battles between the US and Japan and crippled Japanese carrier airpower.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1984 Summer Olympics
tokens.description: The 1984 Summer Olympics were held from July 28 to August 12, 1984, in Los Angeles, California, United States. It was the second time Los Angeles hosted the Games, after 1932.
tokens.image_credit: Quintin Soloviev · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2017 Las Vegas shooting
tokens.description: On October 1, 2017, Stephen Paddock fired from a window of the Mandalay Bay hotel on the crowd at the Route 91 Harvest music festival on the Las Vegas Strip. He killed 58 people on site and wounded at least 413 others.
tokens.image_credit: Rmvisuals · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1993 World Trade Center bombing
tokens.description: On February 26, 1993, Ramzi Yousef and associates carried out a van bomb attack below the North Tower of the World Trade Center in New York City. Six people were killed and over a thousand were injured.
tokens.image_credit: DSS Agent in commission of duties (acknowledged in photo caption) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: John Brown's raid on Harpers Ferry
tokens.description: From October 16 to 18, 1859, abolitionist John Brown and a party of 22 raided the federal armory at Harpers Ferry, Virginia, hoping to start a slave revolt. A platoon of U.S. Marines led by Israel Greene defeated the raiders, and the raid is often cited as a cause of the American Civil War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: New Madrid earthquakes
tokens.description: Beginning on December 16, 1811, a series of intense earthquakes struck the New Madrid area of the Mississippi valley, with further major shocks in January and February 1812. They remain the most powerful earthquakes to hit the contiguous United States east of the Rocky Mountains in recorded history.
tokens.image_credit: UnknownUnknown , but published 1851 in a book by Henry Howe (1816–1893) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: I Have a Dream
tokens.title: King speaks at Lincoln Memorial
tokens.description: On August 28, 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the public speech "I Have a Dream" during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom. In it he called for civil and economic rights and an end to legalized racism in the United States.

tokens.name: First inauguration of George Washington
tokens.description: On April 30, 1789, George Washington was inaugurated as the first president of the United States on the balcony of Federal Hall in New York City. Chancellor Robert Livingston administered the presidential oath of office.
tokens.image_credit: Ramon Elorriaga · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mayflower Compact
tokens.description: The Mayflower Compact was the first governing document of Plymouth Colony, written by the men aboard the Mayflower. It contained a pledge of loyalty to the King, and its signers included Separatist Puritans, adventurers and tradesmen.
tokens.image_credit: Jean Leon Gerome Ferris · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Michelson-Morley experiment
tokens.description: The 1887 experiment by Albert Michelson and Edward Morley tried to detect the motion of the Earth through the luminiferous aether by comparing the speed of light in perpendicular directions. Its null result helped lead to the theory of relativity.
tokens.image_credit: Case Western Reserve University · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wow! signal
tokens.description: The Wow! signal was a strong narrowband radio signal detected on 15 August 1977 by the Big Ear radio telescope at Ohio State University. It appeared to come from the direction of Sagittarius and was a candidate extraterrestrial signal that was never repeated.
tokens.image_credit: Credit: Big Ear Radio Observatory and North American AstroPhysical Observatory (NAAPO). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: ThrustSSC
tokens.title: First supersonic land speed record
tokens.description: ThrustSSC is a British jet car that set the world land speed record of 1,228 km/h on 15 October 1997 at the Black Rock Desert in Nevada. It was the first vehicle to officially break the sound barrier on land.
tokens.image_credit: Ikluft · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mariner 4
tokens.description: Mariner 4 was a NASA spacecraft launched on 28 November 1964 that made the first successful flyby of Mars in July 1965. It returned the first close-up pictures of the Martian surface.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cassini-Huygens
tokens.description: Cassini-Huygens was a joint NASA, ESA and ASI mission that studied Saturn and its moons from 2004 to 2017. Its Huygens probe landed on Saturn's largest moon, Titan, in January 2005.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/JPL · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Juno probe
tokens.description: Juno is a NASA space probe launched from Cape Canaveral on 5 August 2011 that entered a polar orbit around Jupiter on 5 July 2016. It studies the planet's atmosphere, magnetic field and interior.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/KSC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spirit rover
tokens.description: Spirit, also known as MER-A, was a NASA Mars rover launched in June 2003 that operated on Mars from 2004 to 2010. It was one of two rovers of the Mars Exploration Rover mission managed by JPL.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parker Solar Probe
tokens.description: The Parker Solar Probe is a NASA space probe launched in 2018 to study the Sun's outer corona. It used repeated Venus gravity assists and reached within 9.86 solar radii of the Sun in 2024.
tokens.image_credit: NASA Kennedy from United States NASA/Glenn Benson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Artemis I
tokens.description: Artemis I was an uncrewed NASA mission that orbited the Moon from November to December 2022. It was the first integrated flight test of the Orion spacecraft and the Space Launch System rocket.
tokens.image_credit: Joel Kowsky · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Inspiration4
tokens.description: Inspiration4 was a 2021 all-civilian crewed spaceflight operated by SpaceX. The Crew Dragon Resilience launched from Kennedy Space Center on September 16, 2021 and orbited the Earth for three days.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Space Force Photo by Staff Sgt. JT Armstrong · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Louisbourg 1758
tokens.description: The siege of Louisbourg took place from 8 June to 26 July 1758 during the Seven Years' War, on Cape Breton Island. The British victory ended French colonial power in Atlantic Canada.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Paton · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Expulsion of the Acadians
tokens.description: The Expulsion of the Acadians was the forced removal of French colonists from Acadia by Great Britain between 1755 and 1764. It affected the present-day Maritime provinces and part of Maine.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Davies · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1988 Winter Olympics
tokens.description: The 1988 Winter Olympics were a multi-sport event held from 13 to 28 February 1988, with Calgary, Canada as the main host city. It was the first Winter Games to last 15 days.
tokens.image_credit: w:en:Colin Keigher (talk | contribs) · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2010 Winter Olympics
tokens.description: The 2010 Winter Olympics were a multi-sport event held from 12 to 28 February 2010 in Vancouver, Canada, with events also in Whistler and nearby suburbs. About 2,600 athletes from 82 nations took part.
tokens.image_credit: Makaristos · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lac-Mégantic rail disaster
tokens.description: On 6 July 2013 an unattended freight train carrying crude oil derailed in downtown Lac-Mégantic, Quebec. The explosions and fires that followed killed 47 people.
tokens.image_credit: Sûreté du Québec · CC BY-SA 1.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Frank Slide
tokens.description: The Frank Slide was a massive rockslide from Turtle Mountain that buried part of the mining town of Frank, Alberta, at 4:10 a.m. on 29 April 1903. About 110 million tonnes of limestone broke off and slid down the mountain.
tokens.image_credit: Keith McClary · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pastry War
tokens.description: The Pastry War began in November 1838 when French naval forces blockaded Mexican ports and captured San Juan de Ulúa at Veracruz. It ended in March 1839 with a British-brokered peace.
tokens.image_credit: Horace Vernet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Camarón
tokens.description: The Battle of Camarón was a last stand fought on 30 April 1863 between a French Foreign Legion detachment and Mexican troops during the French intervention in Mexico. The 65 legionnaires held out for nearly eleven hours at the Hacienda Camarón in Veracruz.
tokens.image_credit: Jean-Adolphe Beaucé · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2017 Puebla earthquake
tokens.description: The 2017 Puebla earthquake struck central Mexico on 19 September 2017 with an estimated magnitude of 7.1. Its epicentre was about 55 km south of Puebla, and more than 40 buildings collapsed in the region, including Mexico City.
tokens.image_credit: AntoFran · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1976 Guatemala earthquake
tokens.description: The 1976 Guatemala earthquake struck on 4 February 1976 with a moment magnitude of 7.5. The shock was centred on the Motagua Fault near Los Amates in Izabal, and the rupture ran about 240 km along the fault.
tokens.image_credit: Photographer not identified · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Mozote massacre
tokens.description: The El Mozote massacre took place on 11 and 12 December 1981 in and around the village of El Mozote, Morazan, during the Salvadoran Civil War. The Salvadoran Army killed more than 800 civilians.
tokens.image_credit: Efrojas · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salvadoran Civil War
tokens.description: The Salvadoran Civil War was a twelve-year conflict between the Salvadoran government, backed by the United States, and the left-wing FMLN guerrilla coalition. A coup on 15 October 1979 is widely seen as its start, and the Chapultepec Peace Accords of 16 January 1992 ended it.
tokens.image_credit: Olivia Isabel Flores · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1972 Nicaragua earthquake
tokens.description: A moment magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck near Managua, the capital of Nicaragua, in the early hours of 23 December 1972. It reached a maximum MSK intensity of IX (Destructive).
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Santa Clara
tokens.description: The Battle of Santa Clara was a series of events in late December 1958 in which rebel forces under Che Guevara captured the Cuban city of Santa Clara. The victory led to Batista fleeing Cuba within 12 hours.

tokens.name: Battle of San Juan Hill
tokens.description: The Battle of San Juan Hill was fought on 1 July 1898 during the Spanish-American War, when American forces attacked the Spanish defenders near Santiago de Cuba. It was a decisive battle of the campaign in Cuba.
tokens.image_credit: Frederic Remington · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mariel boatlift
tokens.description: The Mariel boatlift was a mass emigration of Cubans from Mariel Harbor to the United States between 15 April and 31 October 1980. The refugees were called Marielitos.
tokens.image_credit: Florida Keys--Public Libraries from Key West, Fla., USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Morant Bay rebellion
tokens.description: The Morant Bay Rebellion began on 11 October 1865 with a protest march to the courthouse in Morant Bay, Jamaica, led by preacher Paul Bogle. After seven protesters were shot by the volunteer militia, the courthouse and nearby buildings were attacked and burned.
tokens.image_credit: Author John Cassell Publisher Cassell Petter & Galpin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parsley massacre
tokens.description: The Parsley massacre was a mass killing of Haitians in the Dominican Republic's northwestern frontier and parts of the Cibao region in October 1937. It was ordered by dictator Rafael Trujillo.

tokens.name: Ponce massacre
tokens.description: The Ponce massacre took place on Palm Sunday, 21 March 1937, in Ponce, Puerto Rico, when police fired on a peaceful march organised by the Nationalist Party. Seventeen civilians, one policeman and one National Guardsman were killed.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos Torres Morales of "El Imparcial" · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Junín
tokens.description: The Battle of Junín was a large cavalry engagement of the Peruvian War of Independence, fought on 6 August 1824 on the Plain of Junín in the highlands of Peru. Simón Bolívar led the rebel forces against the Spanish under José de Canterac.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Tovar y Tovar · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Chacabuco
tokens.description: The Battle of Chacabuco was fought on 12 February 1817 during the Chilean War of Independence. The Army of the Andes under José de San Martín defeated the royalist force commanded by Rafael Maroto.
tokens.image_credit: Pedro Subercaseaux · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paraguayan War
tokens.description: The Paraguayan War, also called the War of the Triple Alliance, lasted from 1864 to 1870. Paraguay fought Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay, and it was the deadliest interstate war in Latin American history.

tokens.name: Battle of Curupayty
tokens.description: The Battle of Curupayty was fought on 22 September 1866 during the Paraguayan War. Brazilian, Argentine and Uruguayan armies attacked the fortified Paraguayan trenches led by José Eduvigis Díaz.
tokens.image_credit: Luis Candido Lopez · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thousand Days' War
tokens.description: The Thousand Days' War was a civil war fought in Colombia from 1899 to 1902 between the Liberal Party and the national government. It was rooted in the federalism versus centralism dispute that followed the Constitution of 1886.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos Chahin. Original black and white by D.S. Maduro Jr. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Caracazo
tokens.description: The Caracazo was a wave of protests, riots and looting that began on 27 February 1989 in Guarenas and spread to Caracas after austerity measures under President Carlos Andrés Pérez. Clashes that week caused many deaths, mostly attributed to security forces.

tokens.name: 2016 Ecuador earthquake
tokens.description: The 2016 Ecuador earthquake struck on 16 April 2016 with a moment magnitude of 7.8. Its epicentre lay about 27 km from Muisne and Pedernales, and the Manta, Pedernales and Portoviejo regions accounted for over 75 percent of casualties.
tokens.image_credit: AgenciaAndes · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Japanese embassy hostage crisis
tokens.description: The Japanese embassy hostage crisis began on 17 December 1996, when members of the MRTA seized hundreds of guests at the Japanese ambassador's residence in San Isidro, Lima. The crisis ended with a military rescue operation in April 1997.

tokens.name: 1906 Valparaíso earthquake
tokens.description: The 1906 Valparaíso earthquake struck central Chile on 16 August 1906 with an estimated magnitude of 8.2 Mw. Its epicentre lay offshore of the Valparaíso Region, and the port city suffered severe damage.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1988 Chilean presidential referendum
tokens.description: A referendum held in Chile on 5 October 1988 asked whether Augusto Pinochet should remain president for eight more years. The No side won with about 56% of the vote, ending his rule.
tokens.image_credit: Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional · CC BY 3.0 cl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: AMIA bombing
tokens.description: A suicide van bombing destroyed the AMIA Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires on 18 July 1994. The attack killed 85 people and injured more than 300, the deadliest terrorist attack in Argentine history.

tokens.name: Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571
tokens.title: Andes crash survivors
tokens.description: Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 crashed in the Andes mountains in Argentina on 13 October 1972 while flying from Montevideo to Santiago. The survivors' ordeal became known as the Andes flight disaster.
tokens.image_credit: Wunabbis · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Inconfidência Mineira
tokens.description: The Inconfidência Mineira was an unsuccessful separatist conspiracy in colonial Brazil, centred on the captaincy of Minas Gerais, in 1789. Its leaders were inspired by the independence of the thirteen British colonies in North America.

tokens.name: 1964 Brazilian coup d'état
tokens.description: On 31 March and 1 April 1964 the Brazilian military overthrew President João Goulart, starting a military dictatorship that lasted until 1985. The coup was followed by the installation of a military junta and the exile of the president.
tokens.image_credit: Arquivo Público do Distrito Federal (Public Archive of the Federal District) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mariana dam disaster
tokens.description: On 5 November 2015 the Fundão tailings dam of the Samarco mine near Mariana, Minas Gerais, collapsed and flooded the villages of Bento Rodrigues and Paracatu de Baixo. The disaster killed 19 people and is the largest tailings dam failure on record.
tokens.image_credit: Senado Federal · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brumadinho dam disaster
tokens.description: On 25 January 2019 a tailings dam at the Córrego do Feijão iron ore mine, owned by Vale, collapsed near Brumadinho in Minas Gerais. The mudflow engulfed the mine headquarters, a cafeteria, houses and farms downstream.
tokens.image_credit: Ibama from Brasil · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kiss nightclub fire
tokens.description: On 27 January 2013, a fire started by pyrotechnics igniting acoustic foam killed 242 people at the Kiss nightclub in Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul. At least 630 others were injured in one of Brazil's deadliest nightclub fires.

tokens.name: Earth Summit
tokens.description: The 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development, also called the Earth Summit, was held in Rio de Janeiro from 3 to 14 June 1992. It led to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and helped establish the concept of sustainable development.

tokens.name: Brazil 1-7 Germany
tokens.title: Seven goals in Belo Horizonte
tokens.description: Brazil lost 7-1 to Germany in the first 2014 FIFA World Cup semi-final, played on 8 July 2014 at the Mineirão stadium in Belo Horizonte. It is one of the most widely discussed results in World Cup history.
tokens.image_credit: Marcello Casal Jr/Agência Brasil · CC BY 3.0 br · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Milne Bay
tokens.description: The Battle of Milne Bay, from 25 August to 7 September 1942, saw Japanese naval infantry attack Allied airfields at the eastern tip of New Guinea. The predominantly Australian garrison, reinforced in advance, repulsed the landing, the first Allied land defeat of Japanese forces in the Pacific war.
tokens.image_credit: Bagnall, Frank N · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Attack on Sydney Harbour
tokens.title: Port Jackson
tokens.description: From 31 May to 8 June 1942, Imperial Japanese Navy submarines attacked the Australian cities of Sydney and Newcastle. On the night of 31 May to 1 June, three midget submarines entered Sydney Harbour and tried to sink Allied warships.
tokens.image_credit: Keam, Ronald Noel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ash Wednesday bushfires
tokens.description: The Ash Wednesday bushfires of 16 February 1983 burned across south-eastern Australia, mainly in Victoria and South Australia. More than 180 fires, fanned by winds of up to 110 km/h, caused widespread destruction within twelve hours.
tokens.image_credit: Sydney Oats · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Victorian gold rush
tokens.description: The Victorian gold rush, from about 1851 to the late 1860s, brought extreme prosperity to the Australian colony of Victoria. It drew a large influx of population and financial capital into Melbourne.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Daintree 1832-1878, Antoine Fauchery 1823-1861 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wave Hill walk-off
tokens.description: The Wave Hill walk-off, also called the Gurindji strike, began on 23 August 1966 when about 200 Gurindji workers and their families left the Wave Hill cattle station in the Northern Territory. The strike lasted seven years, and its main demand was the return of traditional Gurindji land.
tokens.image_credit: Mervyn Bishop · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: British nuclear tests at Maralinga
tokens.title: British nuclear test site
tokens.description: Between 1956 and 1963 the United Kingdom conducted seven nuclear tests at Maralinga in South Australia, within the Woomera Prohibited Area. The series comprised Operation Buffalo in 1956 and Operation Antler in 1957.

tokens.name: Battle of Gate Pā
tokens.description: The Battle of Gate Pā was fought on 29 April 1864 at Pukehinahina near Tauranga during the New Zealand Wars. British forces suffered a defeat against a Māori fortified pā.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera
tokens.description: A volcanic eruption at Mount Tarawera near Rotorua on 10 June 1886 reached an estimated VEI 5 and killed around 120 people. It is the deadliest volcanic eruption in New Zealand in the past 500 years.

tokens.name: Tangiwai disaster
tokens.description: The Tangiwai disaster was a railway accident on 24 December 1953, when the Whangaehu River bridge collapsed under an express train. The derailment killed 151 people and is New Zealand's worst rail disaster.
tokens.image_credit: Ron2K · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2016 Kaikōura earthquake
tokens.description: The 2016 Kaikōura earthquake was a Mw 7.8 quake on the South Island of New Zealand on 14 November 2016 NZDT. Ruptures on multiple faults make it one of the most complex earthquakes studied.

tokens.name: Battle of Savo Island
tokens.description: The Battle of Savo Island on 8 to 9 August 1942 was a naval battle between the Imperial Japanese Navy and Allied forces. It was the first major naval engagement of the Guadalcanal campaign in World War II.
tokens.image_credit: Imperial Japanese Navy, copied from the Rear Admiral Samuel Eliot Morison World War II history illustrations file. Originally uploaded to English Wikipedia [1] by user Stan Shebs. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Naval Battle of Guadalcanal
tokens.description: The Naval Battle of Guadalcanal, 12 to 15 November 1942, was a series of air and sea engagements between Allied and Imperial Japanese forces. It was the decisive battle of the Guadalcanal campaign in the Solomon Islands.
tokens.image_credit: Official U.S. Navy photograph · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mutiny on the Bounty
tokens.description: The Mutiny on the Bounty took place in the Pacific Ocean on 28 April 1789, when Fletcher Christian and crewmen seized HMS Bounty from Lieutenant William Bligh. Bligh and 18 loyalists were set adrift in an open launch.
tokens.image_credit: Robert Dodd · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom
tokens.description: On 17 January 1893, a coup led by the Committee of Safety overthrew Queen Liliuokalani of the Hawaiian Kingdom in Honolulu. US Marines landed from USS Boston to support the coup.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2009 Samoa earthquake and tsunami
tokens.description: On 29 September 2009 a magnitude 8.1 undersea earthquake south of Samoa generated a destructive tsunami. The waves caused heavy loss of life and damage on the coasts of Samoa and American Samoa.
tokens.image_credit: Lorn Cramer · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aloha from Hawaii via Satellite
tokens.description: Aloha from Hawaii via Satellite was an Elvis Presley concert held on 14 January 1973 at the Honolulu International Center. It was broadcast live by satellite to audiences in Asia and Oceania.

tokens.name: Nimrod Expedition
tokens.description: The Nimrod Expedition of 1907 to 1909 was Ernest Shackleton's first Antarctic expedition, based at Cape Royds on Ross Island. Its southern march reached 88 degrees 23 minutes south, about 180 km from the South Pole.
tokens.image_credit: J. B. Adams · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Highjump
tokens.description: Operation Highjump was a 1946 to 1947 United States Navy expedition to Antarctica with 13 ships and 33 aircraft. It aimed to establish the Antarctic research base Little America IV.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Navy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Atlantic
tokens.description: The Battle of the Atlantic was the longest continuous military campaign of the Second World War, running from 1939 to 1945. It pitted Allied convoys and navies against German U-boats and aircraft across the Atlantic Ocean.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo 80-G-72409 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the River Plate
tokens.description: The Battle of the River Plate on 13 December 1939 was the first British naval battle of the Second World War. The German cruiser Admiral Graf Spee was damaged and then scuttled off Montevideo.
tokens.image_credit: Royal Navy official photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Falkland Islands
tokens.description: The Battle of the Falkland Islands on 8 December 1914 was a naval action in the South Atlantic. A British squadron destroyed the German cruiser squadron of Admiral von Spee, which had sought to attack the Falklands.
tokens.image_credit: William Lionel Wyllie · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Ten-Go
tokens.description: Operation Ten-Go, also called Operation Kikusui I, was the last major Japanese naval operation of the Pacific War. In April 1945 the battleship Yamato and nine other warships sailed on a suicide attack toward Okinawa, and US carrier aircraft sank Yamato and five others.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle off Samar
tokens.description: The Battle off Samar was the central action of the Battle of Leyte Gulf, fought on 25 October 1944. US escort carriers and destroyers of Taffy 3 fought a much larger Japanese surface force that came through San Bernardino Strait.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Navy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Saintes
tokens.description: The Battle of the Saintes was fought from 9 to 12 April 1782 between the British fleet of Admiral George Rodney and the French fleet of Admiral de Grasse. The British victory forced France and Spain to abandon a planned invasion of Jamaica.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Whitcombe · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1934 FIFA World Cup
tokens.description: The 1934 FIFA World Cup was the second edition of the football championship, held in Italy from 27 May to 10 June 1934. It was the first edition for which national teams had to qualify.
tokens.image_credit: Gino Boccasile · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mike Tyson vs. Buster Douglas
tokens.title: Heavyweight upset in Tokyo
tokens.description: Mike Tyson vs. Buster Douglas was a professional heavyweight boxing match held at the Tokyo Dome on 11 February 1990. Undefeated champion Tyson was knocked out by the 42-1 underdog Douglas.

tokens.name: 1994 San Marino Grand Prix
tokens.description: The 1994 San Marino Grand Prix was a Formula One race held on 1 May 1994 at the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari in Imola, Italy. Michael Schumacher won, but the weekend was marred by the fatal crashes of Roland Ratzenberger and Ayrton Senna.

tokens.name: Superga air disaster
tokens.description: The Superga air disaster on 4 May 1949 killed all 31 people aboard a Fiat G.212 airliner carrying the Torino football team, the Grande Torino. The aircraft hit the retaining wall behind the Basilica of Superga near Turin.
tokens.image_credit: Photo taken by, released into the Public domain by, and uploaded to the Italian Wkipedia by http://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Claude · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kanjuruhan Stadium disaster
tokens.description: The Kanjuruhan Stadium disaster was a fatal crowd crush on 1 October 2022 after a football match at Kanjuruhan Stadium in Malang Regency, East Java, Indonesia. More than 100 people died.
tokens.image_credit: Antara TV: Achmad Syaiful Afandi/Sandy Arizona/Rinto A Navis/Abdal A. Choirozzad · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sikhote-Alin meteorite
tokens.description: The Sikhote-Alin meteorite is an iron meteorite that fell on 12 February 1947 in the Sikhote-Alin Mountains of the Russian Far East. About 23 tonnes of fragments were recovered, making it one of the largest observed iron meteorite falls.
tokens.image_credit: H. Raab (User:Vesta) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Paris 1783
tokens.description: The Treaty of Paris, signed on 3 September 1783, ended the War of American Independence and recognised the Thirteen Colonies as free and independent states. It set the boundaries between the United States and British North America.
tokens.image_credit: Benjamin West · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
tokens.description: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was signed on 3 March 1918 between Soviet Russia and the Central Powers, ending Russia's participation in World War I. It was signed at Brest-Litovsk, now Brest in Belarus.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peace of Augsburg
tokens.description: The Peace of Augsburg was signed on 25 September 1555 between Emperor Charles V and the Schmalkaldic League in Augsburg. It made the legal division of Christianity permanent in the Holy Roman Empire, letting rulers choose Lutheranism or Catholicism.
tokens.image_credit: User:Michail · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaties of Tilsit
tokens.description: The Treaties of Tilsit were two peace treaties signed by Napoleon in July 1807 with Russia and Prussia, at Tilsit, today Sovetsk in Russia. The first was agreed on a raft in the Neman river between Napoleon and Alexander I.
tokens.image_credit: Adolphe Roehn · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Portsmouth
tokens.description: The Treaty of Portsmouth was signed on 5 September 1905 and formally ended the Russo-Japanese War. It was negotiated at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Kittery, Maine, under the mediation of President Theodore Roosevelt.
tokens.image_credit: P. F. Collier & Son · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Berlin Conference
tokens.description: The Berlin Conference of 1884 to 1885 was a meeting of colonial powers that regulated European colonisation and trade in Africa. It was organised by Otto von Bismarck at the Reich Chancellor's palace on Wilhelmstrasse in Berlin.
tokens.image_credit: Adalbert von Roessler · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kyoto Protocol
tokens.description: The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty extending the 1992 UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, with binding greenhouse gas reduction targets for developed countries. It was adopted in Kyoto, Japan, on 11 December 1997 and entered into force on 16 February 2005.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paris Agreement
tokens.description: The Paris Agreement is an international treaty on climate change covering mitigation, adaptation and finance. It was negotiated by 196 parties at the 2015 UN Climate Change Conference near Paris, France.
tokens.image_credit: Presidencia de la República Mexicana · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montreal Protocol
tokens.description: The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of substances that deplete it. It was agreed on 16 September 1987 in Montreal and entered into force on 1 January 1989.

tokens.name: Helsinki Accords
tokens.description: The Helsinki Final Act is the document signed at the closing meeting of the Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe in Helsinki on 1 August 1975. Signed by 35 states from East and West, it aimed to ease Cold War tensions and was not legally binding.
tokens.image_credit: Rabax63 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dayton Agreement
tokens.description: The Dayton Agreement is the peace agreement that ended the Bosnian War. It was signed on 21 November 1995 at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base near Dayton, Ohio, and re-signed ceremonially in Paris on 14 December 1995.
tokens.image_credit: NATO · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty
tokens.description: The Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty was an arms control treaty between the United States and the Soviet Union. Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev signed it on 8 December 1987, and it was ratified on 1 June 1988.
tokens.image_credit: White House Photographic Office · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact
tokens.description: The Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact was a non-aggression pact between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union, signed in Moscow in August 1939. Its secret protocol divided Eastern Europe into German and Soviet spheres of influence.
tokens.image_credit: Template:Helmut Laux · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anglo-Irish Treaty
tokens.description: The Anglo-Irish Treaty was an agreement between the United Kingdom and the Irish Republic, signed at 10 Downing Street, London, on 6 December 1921. It concluded the Irish War of Independence and provided for the Irish Free State as a self-governing dominion.

tokens.name: Abraham Accords
tokens.description: The Abraham Accords are agreements that normalised relations between Israel and several Arab states, starting with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain in 2020. They were signed at the White House in Washington, D.C. on 15 September 2020 under US mediation.
tokens.image_credit: The White House from Washington, DC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Shimonoseki
tokens.description: The Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed on 17 April 1895 at Shimonoseki, Japan, between the Empire of Japan and the Qing dynasty. It ended the First Sino-Japanese War.
tokens.image_credit: Nagatochi Hideta 永地秀太 (1873–1942) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of San Francisco
tokens.description: The Treaty of San Francisco was signed on 8 September 1951 by 49 nations at the War Memorial Opera House in San Francisco. It ended the legal state of war and the Allied occupation of Japan.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Department of State · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
tokens.description: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948 at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris. It was drafted by a committee chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt.
tokens.image_credit: FDR Presidential Library & Museum · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Apollo 7
tokens.title: First crewed Apollo flight
tokens.description: Apollo 7 was flown from 11 to 22 October 1968 as the first crewed flight of NASA's Apollo program. It launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, and resumed US crewed spaceflight after the Apollo 1 fire.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gemini 4
tokens.title: First American spacewalk
tokens.description: Gemini 4 was flown in June 1965 as the second crewed flight of NASA's Project Gemini. During the four-day mission Ed White made the first American spacewalk.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/James McDivitt · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vostok 2
tokens.title: A full day in orbit
tokens.description: Vostok 2 was a Soviet crewed mission that carried Gherman Titov into orbit on 6 August 1961. He spent a full day in space, orbiting the Earth more than 17 times.

tokens.name: Lunokhod 1
tokens.title: First rover on another world
