tokens.description: Lunokhod 1 was the first robotic rover to move across the surface of another world, the Moon, in 1970. The rover was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome, the Earth launch site kept for this lunar mission.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venera 13
tokens.title: Colour images from Venus
tokens.description: Venera 13 was a Soviet Venera probe that landed on Venus in March 1982 and sent back the first colour images of its surface. It was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome in October 1981.
tokens.image_credit: Post of Soviet Union · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mariner 2
tokens.title: First successful planetary flyby
tokens.description: Mariner 2 was an American space probe that became the first robotic spacecraft to report successfully from a planetary encounter, flying past Venus in December 1962. It was launched from Cape Canaveral, the Earth launch site kept for this lunar and planetary mission.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/Jet Propulsion Laboratory · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mariner 9
tokens.title: First spacecraft to orbit Mars
tokens.description: Mariner 9 was a NASA spacecraft that became the first to orbit another planet when it reached Mars in November 1971. It was launched from Cape Canaveral, the Earth launch site kept for this planetary mission.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pioneer 10
tokens.title: First probe to Jupiter
tokens.description: Pioneer 10 is a NASA space probe launched in 1972 that completed the first mission to Jupiter. It was the first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and the first to reach escape velocity from the Solar System.
tokens.image_credit: NASA on The Commons · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Galileo spacecraft
tokens.title: Orbiter of Jupiter
tokens.description: Galileo was an American robotic probe that studied Jupiter and its moons from 1995 to 2003. It was carried into Earth orbit by Space Shuttle Atlantis in October 1989, launched from Kennedy Space Center, the Earth launch site kept for this mission.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Opportunity rover
tokens.title: Long-lived Mars rover
tokens.description: Opportunity was a NASA robotic rover that landed in Meridiani Planum on Mars in January 2004 and was active until 2018. It was launched in July 2003 as part of the Mars Exploration Rover program, from the Earth launch site kept for this mission.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/JPL/Cornell University, Maas Digital LLC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: InSight
tokens.title: Listening to marsquakes
tokens.description: InSight was a NASA robotic lander, managed by JPL, that studied the deep interior of Mars and confirmed marsquakes. It was launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, the Earth launch site kept for this mission.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Lockheed Martin ·  · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: OSIRIS-REx
tokens.title: Asteroid sample return
tokens.description: OSIRIS-REx was a NASA mission that collected samples from the carbonaceous asteroid 101955 Bennu and returned them to Earth in September 2023. The spacecraft was then renamed OSIRIS-APEX for a follow-up mission to Apophis.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kepler space telescope
tokens.title: Planet hunter
tokens.description: The Kepler space telescope was launched by NASA in 2009 to find Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars. It was named after astronomer Johannes Kepler and placed in an Earth-trailing heliocentric orbit.
tokens.image_credit: Photo credit: NASA/Sandra Joseph, Kevin O'Connell · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Double Asteroid Redirection Test
tokens.title: First planetary defence test
tokens.description: The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was a NASA mission that crashed a spacecraft into Dimorphos, the moonlet of the asteroid Didymos, in September 2022. It tested whether an impact can change an asteroid's path, as a planetary defense method.
tokens.image_credit: Bill Ingalls · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Europa Clipper
tokens.title: Mission to Jupiter's icy moon
tokens.description: Europa Clipper is a NASA mission launched on October 14, 2024 by a Falcon Heavy to study Jupiter's icy moon Europa. It is the largest interplanetary spacecraft NASA has launched and will make repeated flybys of Europa.

tokens.name: Polaris Dawn
tokens.title: First commercial spacewalk
tokens.description: Polaris Dawn was a private crewed SpaceX Crew Dragon flight launched on September 10, 2024, led by Jared Isaacman. The crew flew to an elliptical orbit about 1,400 km above Earth and carried out the first commercial spacewalk.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Space Force photo by Joshua Conti · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blue Origin NS-16
tokens.title: Bezos flies to space
tokens.description: Blue Origin NS-16 was a suborbital New Shepard flight on 20 July 2021, the sixteenth flight of the vehicle. It was the first New Shepard flight with people aboard, carrying Jeff Bezos, Mark Bezos, Wally Funk and Oliver Daemen.

tokens.name: Falcon 9 flight 20
tokens.title: First orbital booster landing
tokens.description: Falcon 9 flight 20, also called Orbcomm OG2 M2, was a SpaceX launch on 22 December 2015. It was the first time an orbital rocket's first stage returned and landed vertically, at Landing Zone 1 near the launch site.
tokens.image_credit: SpaceX Photos · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shenzhou 7
tokens.title: First Chinese spacewalk
tokens.description: Shenzhou 7 was China's third crewed spaceflight, launched from Jiuquan on 25 September 2008. It included the first Chinese spacewalk, carried out by Zhai Zhigang and Liu Boming, and landed in Inner Mongolia on 28 September 2008.

tokens.name: Emirates Mars Mission
tokens.title: Hope orbiter to Mars
tokens.description: The Emirates Mars Mission is an uncrewed United Arab Emirates Space Agency mission to Mars. Its Hope probe launched on 20 July 2020 and entered orbit around Mars on 9 February 2021.
tokens.image_credit: BugWarp · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: STS-7
tokens.title: First American woman in space
tokens.description: STS-7 was NASA's seventh Space Shuttle mission and the second flight of Challenger. It launched from Kennedy Space Center on 18 June 1983 and landed at Edwards Air Force Base on 24 June 1983.
tokens.image_credit: NASA image · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: STS-31
tokens.title: Hubble deployed
tokens.description: STS-31 was the Space Shuttle Discovery mission that deployed the Hubble Space Telescope into low Earth orbit on 24 April 1990. It lifted off from Launch Complex 39B at the Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/IMAX · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: STS-61
tokens.title: First Hubble servicing mission
tokens.description: STS-61 was NASA's first servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope, flown by the Space Shuttle Endeavour. It launched from Kennedy Space Center on 2 December 1993 and installed a corrective optics package and a new main camera.
tokens.image_credit: Askeuhd · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: STS-135
tokens.title: Final Space Shuttle mission
tokens.description: STS-135 was the final mission of NASA's Space Shuttle program and the last flight of Atlantis. It launched on 8 July 2011 and landed on 21 July 2011 after a one-day extension.
tokens.image_credit: Bill Ingalls · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: We choose to go to the Moon
tokens.title: Kennedy's speech at Rice Stadium
tokens.description: The Address at Rice University, delivered by John F. Kennedy on 12 September 1962 at Rice Stadium in Houston, contains the line "We choose to go to the Moon". It set the goal of a crewed Moon landing before the end of the decade.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: We shall fight on the beaches
tokens.title: Churchill addresses the Commons
tokens.description: "We shall fight on the beaches" was Winston Churchill's speech to the House of Commons on 4 June 1940, during the Battle of France. It was the second of three major speeches he gave in that period.

tokens.name: This was their finest hour
tokens.title: Churchill speech to Parliament
tokens.description: Winston Churchill's speech to the House of Commons on 18 June 1940, delivered after France had sought an armistice. Its closing phrase became a lasting emblem of Britain's stand in 1940.

tokens.name: Blood, toil, tears and sweat
tokens.title: Churchill's first speech as PM
tokens.description: Winston Churchill's speech to the House of Commons on 13 May 1940, his first as Prime Minister, which gave the phrase 'blood, toil, tears and sweat' to the English language. The speech is set in the Palace of Westminster.

tokens.name: I've Been to the Mountaintop
tokens.title: King's last speech in Memphis
tokens.description: Martin Luther King Jr. gave this final speech on 3 April 1968 at the Mason Temple in Memphis, Tennessee, the night before his assassination. It primarily concerns the Memphis sanitation strike.

tokens.name: Four Freedoms speech
tokens.title: Roosevelt's State of the Union
tokens.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt's 1941 State of the Union address to Congress, in which he named four freedoms that people everywhere should enjoy. He delivered it on 6 January 1941 in the United States Capitol.
tokens.image_credit: Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ain't I a Woman?
tokens.title: Sojourner Truth in Akron
tokens.description: Sojourner Truth's address at the Women's Convention in Akron, Ohio, in 1851, generally considered to have been delivered extemporaneously. The speech did not originally have a title.

tokens.name: Cross of Gold speech
tokens.title: Bryan at the Democratic convention
tokens.description: William Jennings Bryan's address supporting free silver at the Democratic National Convention in Chicago on 9 July 1896. The speech takes its name from its 'cross of gold' passage.
tokens.image_credit: William Robinson Leigh · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atoms for Peace
tokens.title: Eisenhower at the United Nations
tokens.description: Dwight D. Eisenhower's address to the UN General Assembly in New York City on 8 December 1953, on the atomic age and the peaceful use of atomic energy. The speech was given at the United Nations Headquarters.

tokens.name: American University speech
tokens.title: Kennedy's peace speech
tokens.description: John F. Kennedy's commencement address at American University in Washington, D.C., on 10 June 1963, titled A Strategy of Peace. In it he announced negotiations toward a comprehensive test ban treaty.
tokens.image_credit: Cecil Stoughton · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower's farewell address
tokens.title: Warning on the military-industrial complex
tokens.description: Dwight D. Eisenhower's final televised address as president, delivered on 17 January 1961, in which he warned of the military-industrial complex. The broadcast was made from the White House in Washington, D.C.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Ballot or the Bullet
tokens.title: Malcolm X speech in Cleveland
tokens.description: Malcolm X's public speech, first delivered on 3 April 1964 at the Cory Methodist Church in Cleveland, Ohio, urging African Americans to use their vote or be prepared to take up arms. It was repeated in Detroit on 12 April 1964.

tokens.name: Wind of Change speech
tokens.title: Macmillan in Cape Town
tokens.description: Address by British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan to the Parliament of South Africa in Cape Town on 3 February 1960, during his tour of British colonies in Africa. It signalled the end of British colonial rule in Africa.

tokens.name: Rivers of Blood speech
tokens.title: Speech in Birmingham
tokens.description: Speech by Enoch Powell to the Conservative Political Centre in Birmingham on 20 April 1968, criticising Commonwealth immigration and opposing the Race Relations Bill. It is one of the most controversial speeches in postwar British politics.

tokens.name: Vive le Québec libre
tokens.title: De Gaulle on a Montreal balcony
tokens.description: Phrase from a speech by French president Charles de Gaulle from the balcony of Montreal City Hall on 24 July 1967, during his visit to Expo 67. The remark caused a diplomatic incident between France and Canada.

tokens.name: I Am Prepared to Die
tokens.title: Mandela speaks from the dock
tokens.description: Three-hour speech by Nelson Mandela from the dock on 20 April 1964 at the Rivonia Trial in Pretoria, ending with the words that gave it its title. It is widely regarded as one of the most memorable speeches of the 20th century.

tokens.name: Inauguration of John F. Kennedy
tokens.title: Ask not what your country can do
tokens.description: The inauguration of John F. Kennedy as the 35th president of the United States, held on 20 January 1961 at the East Portico of the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C. It was the only term of Kennedy and Lyndon B. Johnson as president and vice president.
tokens.image_credit: Record Group 111, Records of the Office of the Chief Signal Officer (111-SC-578830) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First inauguration of Franklin D. Roosevelt
tokens.title: Nothing to fear but fear itself
tokens.description: The first inauguration of Franklin D. Roosevelt as the 32nd president of the United States, held on 4 March 1933 at the East Portico of the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C. Roosevelt's line that the nation had nothing to fear but fear itself was delivered in his address.
tokens.image_credit: USCapitol · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First inauguration of Abraham Lincoln
tokens.title: Sworn in on the eve of war
tokens.description: Abraham Lincoln was sworn in as the 16th President of the United States on 4 March 1861 at the East Portico of the United States Capitol. The inauguration took place weeks before the American Civil War began.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second inauguration of Abraham Lincoln
tokens.title: With malice toward none
tokens.description: Abraham Lincoln took the oath for his second term as President on 4 March 1865 at the East Portico of the United States Capitol. Lincoln was assassinated six weeks later and Andrew Johnson succeeded him.
tokens.image_credit: Alexander Gardner · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Inauguration of Nelson Mandela
tokens.title: At the Union Buildings
tokens.description: Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as President of South Africa on 10 May 1994 at the Union Buildings in Pretoria. The ceremony followed the country's first non-racial general election and marked the end of apartheid rule.

tokens.name: Wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle
tokens.title: Royal wedding at Windsor
tokens.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle were married on 19 May 2018 in St George's Chapel at Windsor Castle. The wedding was watched by a global audience and followed by a carriage procession through Windsor.
tokens.image_credit: Londisland - YouTube · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Philip Mountbatten
tokens.title: Wedding at Westminster Abbey
tokens.description: Princess Elizabeth, heir presumptive to the British throne, married Philip Mountbatten at Westminster Abbey in London on 20 November 1947. Philip had been born a prince of Greece and Denmark and had taken British nationality before the marriage.
tokens.image_credit: Anefo · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wedding of Rainier III and Grace Kelly
tokens.title: Hollywood star weds a prince
tokens.description: Prince Rainier III of Monaco married the American actress Grace Kelly on 18 and 19 April 1956, with a civil ceremony at the Prince's Palace and a religious ceremony at Saint Nicholas Cathedral. The wedding drew wide international press coverage.
tokens.image_credit: AP · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coronation of George VI and Elizabeth
tokens.title: Coronation at Westminster Abbey
tokens.description: George VI and Queen Elizabeth were crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom at Westminster Abbey in London on 12 May 1937. George VI had become king on the abdication of his brother Edward VIII in December 1936.
tokens.image_credit: Frank O. Salisbury · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coronation of George V and Mary
tokens.title: Coronation at Westminster Abbey
tokens.description: The coronation of George V and Mary as king and queen of the United Kingdom and the British Dominions took place at Westminster Abbey on 22 June 1911. It was the second of four such coronations held in the 20th century.
tokens.image_credit: John Henry Frederick Bacon · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coronation of Nicholas II
tokens.title: Last Russian coronation
tokens.description: The coronation of Nicholas II and Alexandra Feodorovna, the last coronation of the Russian Empire, took place on 26 May 1896 in the Dormition Cathedral of the Moscow Kremlin. Nicholas II was the last emperor of Russia.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY exact title; date given in Old Style 14 May

tokens.image_credit: Laurits Tuxen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Delhi Durbar
tokens.title: Imperial assembly at Coronation Park
tokens.description: The Delhi Durbar was the imperial mass assembly organised by the British Raj at Coronation Park, Delhi, to mark the accession of an Emperor or Empress of India. The ceremonial name comes from the Persian word durbar, meaning royal court.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article covers three durbars

tokens.image_credit: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II
tokens.title: Seventy years on the throne
tokens.description: The Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II was the international celebration in 2022 marking the 70th anniversary of her accession on 6 February 1952. It was the first platinum jubilee celebrated by any British monarch.
tokens.image_credit: Number 10 · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abdication of Edward VIII
tokens.title: A king gives up the throne
tokens.description: In December 1936 King Edward VIII renounced the throne to marry Wallis Simpson, a divorced American socialite opposed by the British government and the Dominions. He signed the Instrument of Abdication at Fort Belvedere on 10 December 1936.

tokens.name: State funeral of Winston Churchill
tokens.title: Farewell at St Paul's
tokens.description: Winston Churchill, Prime Minister during the Second World War, died on 24 January 1965. His state funeral included a service at St Paul's Cathedral and was the first state funeral in the UK for a non-member of the royal family since 1935.

tokens.name: State funeral of John F. Kennedy
tokens.title: Procession to Arlington
tokens.description: The state funeral of President John F. Kennedy took place in Washington, D.C. and Virginia in November 1963, after his assassination in Dallas. He was buried at Arlington National Cemetery on 25 November 1963.
tokens.image_credit: Abbie Rowe · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Funeral of Pope John Paul II
tokens.title: Mass in St. Peter's Square
tokens.description: Pope John Paul II died on 2 April 2005 in the Apostolic Palace in Vatican City. His funeral on 8 April 2005 in St Peter's Square drew about four million mourners to Rome.
tokens.image_credit: Ricardo Stuckert/PR · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Vatican Council
tokens.title: Council opens at St. Peter's
tokens.description: The Second Vatican Council, the 21st ecumenical council of the Catholic Church, met in four sessions at St. Peter's Basilica from 1962 to 1965. It was convoked by Pope John XXIII and closed under Pope Paul VI.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Geymayer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Attempted assassination of Pope John Paul II
tokens.title: Shots in St. Peter's Square
tokens.description: On 13 May 1981 Mehmet Ali Agca shot and wounded Pope John Paul II as he entered St. Peter's Square in Vatican City. The pope survived the attack.

tokens.name: UEFA Euro 1976 final
tokens.title: The Panenka penalty
tokens.description: The UEFA Euro 1976 final was played on 20 June 1976 at the Red Star Stadium in Belgrade between Czechoslovakia and West Germany. Czechoslovakia won 5-3 on penalties after a 2-2 draw, with Antonin Panenka's chipped penalty deciding the shoot-out.

tokens.name: UEFA Euro 1996 final
tokens.title: Golden goal at Wembley
tokens.description: The UEFA Euro 1996 final was played at Wembley Stadium in London on 30 June 1996 between Germany and the Czech Republic. Germany won 2-1 after extra time, with Oliver Bierhoff's golden goal deciding the match.

tokens.name: 1967 European Cup final
tokens.title: The Lisbon Lions
tokens.description: The 1967 European Cup final was played on 25 May 1967 at the Estadio Nacional in Lisbon. Celtic beat Internazionale 2-1, becoming the first British club to win the European Cup.

tokens.name: 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup final
tokens.title: Final in Sydney
tokens.description: The 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup final was played at Stadium Australia in Sydney on 20 August 2023. Spain beat England 1-0, with Olga Carmona scoring the only goal.
tokens.image_credit: Storm machine · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Super Bowl XLII
tokens.title: Giants end a perfect season bid
tokens.description: Super Bowl XLII was played on 3 February 2008 at University of Phoenix Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. The New York Giants beat the New England Patriots 17-14, ending the Patriots' bid for a perfect season.

tokens.name: 1998 NBA Finals
tokens.title: Jordan's last shot as a Bull
tokens.description: The 1998 NBA Finals was the championship series of the 1997-98 NBA season, in which the Chicago Bulls beat the Utah Jazz in six games. The series was decided by Michael Jordan's last shot as a Bull, in Game 6 at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City.

tokens.name: Kobe Bryant's 81-point game
tokens.title: Second-highest single-game total
tokens.description: On 22 January 2006 Kobe Bryant scored 81 points for the Los Angeles Lakers in a 122-104 win over the Toronto Raptors. At the time it was the second-highest single-game total in NBA history.

tokens.name: 2016 World Series
tokens.title: Cubs end a long drought
tokens.description: The 2016 World Series was the championship series of Major League Baseball's 2016 season, between the Chicago Cubs and the Cleveland Indians. The Cubs won in seven games, their first title since 1908.
tokens.image_credit: Arturo Pardavila III from Hoboken, NJ, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Joe Louis vs. Max Schmeling II
tokens.title: Rematch at Yankee Stadium
tokens.description: Joe Louis vs. Max Schmeling II was a professional boxing match held on 22 June 1938 for the undisputed heavyweight championship, at Yankee Stadium in New York City. Louis won by knockout, in a fight of major political significance.
tokens.image_credit: Associated Press · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Long Count Fight
tokens.title: Dempsey v Tunney at Soldier Field
tokens.description: The Long Count Fight was a heavyweight boxing rematch on 22 September 1927 at Soldier Field in Chicago, in which Gene Tunney beat Jack Dempsey by unanimous decision. It is known for a controversial long count after Dempsey's knockdown.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sonny Liston vs. Cassius Clay
tokens.title: Clay takes the heavyweight title
tokens.description: Sonny Liston vs. Cassius Clay was a heavyweight title fight on 25 February 1964 in Miami Beach, Florida. Clay, later known as Muhammad Ali, won by technical knockout and took the world heavyweight title.

tokens.name: Evander Holyfield vs. Mike Tyson II
tokens.title: The bite fight
tokens.description: Evander Holyfield vs. Mike Tyson II was a heavyweight title fight on 28 June 1997 at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas. The fight is infamous because Tyson bit off part of Holyfield's ear.

tokens.name: Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. Manny Pacquiao
tokens.title: Fight of the Century in Las Vegas
tokens.description: Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. Manny Pacquiao was a boxing match held on 2 May 2015 at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, billed as the Fight of the Century. Mayweather won by unanimous decision.

tokens.name: 1980 Wimbledon men's singles final
tokens.title: Borg v McEnroe
tokens.description: Björn Borg beat John McEnroe in five sets in the 1980 Wimbledon men's singles final at the All England Club. McEnroe saved seven championship points, and the match was regarded at the time as the greatest tennis match ever played.

tokens.name: 1997 Masters Tournament
tokens.title: Tiger Woods' first major
tokens.description: Tiger Woods won the 1997 Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club, his first major championship. His winning margin of 12 strokes over runner-up Tom Kite is the largest in the tournament's history.

tokens.name: 2012 Ryder Cup
tokens.title: Miracle at Medinah
tokens.description: The 39th Ryder Cup was held 28 to 30 September 2012 at Medinah Country Club in Medinah, Illinois, a suburb northwest of Chicago. It was the first Ryder Cup held in Illinois and Europe went into it as the cup holders.

tokens.name: Bob Beamon's long jump
tokens.title: Leap at Mexico City
tokens.description: Bob Beamon won the men's long jump at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City with a jump of 8.90 metres. His world record stood for almost 23 years, and the jump is still the Olympic record.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jesse Owens' 100 metres
tokens.title: Owens wins in Berlin
tokens.description: Jesse Owens won the men's 100 metres at the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin, by 0.1 seconds. Ralph Metcalfe took silver and Tinus Osendarp of the Netherlands took bronze.

tokens.name: Ben Johnson's 100 metres
tokens.title: Final later voided for doping
tokens.description: Ben Johnson of Canada won the men's 100 metres at the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul in a world record time of 9.79 seconds. Two days later he was stripped of the gold medal and the record after testing positive for stanozolol.

tokens.name: Michael Johnson's 200 metres
tokens.title: Golden shoes in Atlanta
tokens.description: Michael Johnson won the men's 200 metres at the 1996 Summer Olympics in Atlanta, Georgia, wearing the gold spiked shoes that became famous. The event had 78 athletes from 57 nations.

tokens.name: Abebe Bikila's marathon
tokens.title: Barefoot victory in Rome
tokens.description: Abebe Bikila of Ethiopia won the men's marathon at the 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome, running barefoot. The race had 69 participants from 35 nations and finished at the Arch of Constantine.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dorando Pietri's marathon
tokens.title: Helped across the line in London
tokens.description: The men's marathon of the 1908 London Olympics took place on 24 July 1908. Dorando Pietri was helped across the finish line and later disqualified, and Johnny Hayes won.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Duplantis Olympic pole vault
tokens.title: World record at Saint-Denis
tokens.description: Armand Duplantis won his second consecutive Olympic pole vault gold at the 2024 Paris Games, held at Stade de France. He set a world record of 6.25 metres in the competition.
tokens.image_credit: Aeltegop · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phelps' 100 metre butterfly
tokens.title: Won by one hundredth
tokens.description: Michael Phelps set an Olympic record of 50.58 to win the men's 100 metre butterfly at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. He beat Milorad Čavić by one hundredth of a second.

tokens.name: 1989 Tour de France
tokens.title: Eight-second victory
tokens.description: Greg LeMond won the 1989 Tour de France by eight seconds over Laurent Fignon after the final time trial into Paris. The 76th edition started in Luxembourg on 1 July and finished in Paris on 23 July.

tokens.name: 1976 Japanese Grand Prix
tokens.title: Title decided in the rain at Fuji
tokens.description: The 1976 Japanese Grand Prix was the final race of the 1976 Formula One World Championship, held at Fuji Speedway on 24 October 1976. James Hunt took the title by one point after Niki Lauda withdrew in the rain.

tokens.name: 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
tokens.title: Title decided on the last lap
tokens.description: The 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix was held on 12 December 2021 at Yas Marina Circuit and was the final round of the 2021 Formula One season. Max Verstappen clinched his first Drivers' title on the final lap, against Lewis Hamilton.

tokens.name: 1950 British Grand Prix
tokens.title: First World Championship race
tokens.description: The 1950 British Grand Prix was held at Silverstone on 13 May 1950 and was the first race of the Formula One World Championship. Nino Farina won for Alfa Romeo from pole position.

tokens.name: 1955 Le Mans disaster
tokens.title: Motorsport's deadliest crash
tokens.description: The 1955 Le Mans disaster happened on 11 June 1955 during the 24 Hours of Le Mans at the Circuit de la Sarthe. Pierre Levegh's car went into the spectator area, and an estimated 82 to 84 people died.

tokens.name: 1966 24 Hours of Le Mans
tokens.title: Ford's staged finish
tokens.description: The 1966 24 Hours of Le Mans, the 34th Grand Prix of Endurance, was held on 18 and 19 June 1966 at the Circuit de la Sarthe. It gave the Ford GT40 its first overall win at Le Mans.
tokens.image_credit: ZANTAFIO56 · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1911 Indianapolis 500
tokens.title: First Indianapolis 500
tokens.description: The 1911 International 500-Mile Sweepstakes was the inaugural Indianapolis 500, held at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway on 30 May 1911. Ray Harroun, driving for Marmon, won the race.
tokens.image_credit: Agence de presse Meurisse · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1973 Belmont Stakes
tokens.title: Secretariat wins the Triple Crown
tokens.description: The 1973 Belmont Stakes, the 105th running of the race, was held at Belmont Park in Elmont, New York, on 9 June 1973. Secretariat won by 31 lengths, the largest winning margin in the race's history.

tokens.name: 1983 America's Cup
tokens.title: Australia II ends US streak
tokens.description: The 1983 America's Cup was a 12-metre yacht racing series sailed off Newport, Rhode Island, and won by Australia II four races to three. It ended the New York Yacht Club's 132-year hold on the Cup.

tokens.name: Donald Campbell's Bluebird K7 crash
tokens.title: Record attempt on Coniston Water
tokens.description: Donald Campbell died on 4 January 1967 when his jet hydroplane Bluebird K7 crashed during a water speed record attempt on Coniston Water in the Lake District, England.

tokens.name: 2023 Cricket World Cup final
tokens.title: Final in Ahmedabad
tokens.description: The 2023 Cricket World Cup Final was a One Day International played at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad on 19 November 2023. India played Australia to decide the 2023 Cricket World Cup.
tokens.image_credit: Pantman2 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2024 Men's T20 World Cup final
tokens.title: Final in Bridgetown
tokens.description: The 2024 Men's T20 World Cup final was a Twenty20 International played at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados, on 29 June 2024. India played South Africa to decide the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup.

tokens.name: 2003 Rugby World Cup final
tokens.title: Drop goal in extra time
tokens.description: The 2003 Rugby World Cup final was played at Stadium Australia in Sydney on 22 November 2003 between Australia and England. England won 20-17 after extra time, with Jonny Wilkinson's drop goal deciding the match.

tokens.name: 1900 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Games in Paris
tokens.description: The 1900 Summer Olympics took place in Paris, France, from 14 May to 28 October 1900. The event was also known as Paris 1900 and was held over several months without opening or closing ceremonies.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1908 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Games in London
tokens.description: The 1908 Summer Olympics were held in London, United Kingdom, from 27 April to 31 October 1908. The Games were moved to London after Italy withdrew from hosting on financial grounds.

tokens.name: 1924 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Games in Paris
tokens.description: The 1924 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France, with the opening ceremony on 5 July 1924. They were the second Games hosted by Paris, making it the first city to host the Summer Olympics twice.

tokens.name: 1932 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Games in Los Angeles
tokens.description: The 1932 Summer Olympics were held in Los Angeles, California, United States, from 30 July to 14 August 1932. The Games took place during the Great Depression, and 37 countries competed.
tokens.image_credit: Le Miroir des sports · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1924 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: First Winter Games at Chamonix
tokens.description: The 1924 Winter Olympics were held in Chamonix and Haute-Savoie, France, from 25 January to 5 February 1924. The IOC later recognised these competitions as the first Winter Olympic Games.
tokens.image_credit: Auguste Matisse · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1936 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: Games in Garmisch-Partenkirchen
tokens.description: The 1936 Winter Olympics were held from 6 to 16 February 1936 in Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Germany. It was the last year in which the Summer and Winter Games both took place in the same country.

tokens.name: 1960 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: Games at Squaw Valley
tokens.description: The 1960 Winter Olympics were held from 18 to 28 February 1960 at Squaw Valley, in the Lake Tahoe area of California, United States. The resort's venues were built for the Games between 1956 and 1960.

tokens.name: 1968 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: Games in Grenoble
tokens.description: The 1968 Winter Olympics were held from 6 to 18 February 1968 in Grenoble, France, with thirty-seven countries taking part. They were the first Games in which the IOC allowed East and West Germany to compete separately.

tokens.name: 2006 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: Games in Turin
tokens.description: The 2006 Winter Olympics were held from 10 to 26 February 2006 in Turin, Italy. It was the second Winter Games hosted by Italy, after Cortina d'Ampezzo in 1956.
tokens.image_credit: User Andy Miah of Flickr · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2024 Summer Olympics opening ceremony
tokens.title: Parade on the Seine
tokens.description: The opening ceremony of the 2024 Summer Olympics took place on 26 July 2024 in Paris, with athletes parading on boats along the Seine. French President Emmanuel Macron formally opened the Games.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Army * by Sgt. 1st Class Kulani Lakanaria · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Woodstock '99
tokens.title: Festival at Rome, New York
tokens.description: Woodstock '99 was a music festival held from 22 to 25 July 1999 at the former Griffiss Air Force Base in Rome, New York. It was the second large-scale festival to emulate the 1969 Woodstock festival, after Woodstock '94.

tokens.name: Wattstax
tokens.title: Concert at the LA Coliseum
tokens.description: Wattstax was a benefit concert organized by Stax Records at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on 20 August 1972. It marked the seventh anniversary of the 1965 Watts riots in Los Angeles.

tokens.name: Farm Aid
tokens.title: Benefit concert for farmers
tokens.description: Farm Aid is an American benefit concert and non-profit founded in 1985 by Willie Nelson, Neil Young and John Mellencamp to support family farmers. The first concert was held on 22 September 1985 at Memorial Stadium in Champaign, Illinois.

tokens.name: The Stones in the Park
tokens.title: Free concert in Hyde Park
tokens.description: The Stones in the Park was a free outdoor concert in Hyde Park, London, on 5 July 1969, headlined by the Rolling Stones. It was their first public concert in over two years and took place two days after the death of Brian Jones.

tokens.name: Lollapalooza
tokens.title: Festival in Grant Park
tokens.description: Lollapalooza is an annual four-day music festival held in Grant Park in Chicago, Illinois. It started as a touring event in 1991 and has been based in Chicago since 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Lacrossewi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Burning Man
tokens.title: City built in the Black Rock Desert
tokens.description: Burning Man is a week-long desert festival focused on community, art, self-expression and self-reliance, held each year in the Black Rock Desert of northwestern Nevada. It ends with the burning of a large wooden effigy called the Man.
tokens.image_credit: BLM Nevada · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Glastonbury Festival
tokens.title: Festival at Worthy Farm
tokens.description: The Glastonbury Festival of Contemporary Performing Arts is a five-day festival of music, dance, comedy, theatre and circus held near Pilton, Somerset, England, in most summers. It has been held on Worthy Farm since 1970.
tokens.image_credit: Raph_PH · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Roskilde Festival
tokens.title: Danish music festival
tokens.description: The Roskilde Festival is a Danish music festival held annually south of Roskilde. Created in 1971, it is one of the largest music festivals in Europe and the largest in the Nordic countries.
tokens.image_credit: Bill Ebbesen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sziget Festival
tokens.title: Festival on an island in Budapest
tokens.description: Sziget Festival is one of the largest music and cultural festivals in Europe. It is held every August on Óbudai-sziget, an island on the Danube in northern Budapest, Hungary.
tokens.image_credit: AAT · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montreux Jazz Festival
tokens.title: Jazz on Lake Geneva
tokens.description: The Montreux Jazz Festival is a music festival held annually in early July in Montreux on the shore of Lake Geneva, Switzerland. It is the second-largest annual jazz festival in the world after the Montreal International Jazz Festival.
tokens.image_credit: Markus Schweizer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fyre Festival
tokens.title: The festival that never was
tokens.description: Fyre Festival was a failed luxury music festival scheduled for April and May 2017 on Great Exuma in the Bahamas. It was organised by Billy McFarland and Ja Rule and never took place as planned.

tokens.name: Love Parade
tokens.title: Techno parade in Berlin
tokens.description: The Love Parade was an electronic dance music festival and techno parade that began in 1989 in West Berlin, Germany. It was held in Berlin until 2006 and in the Ruhr region from 2007 to 2010.
tokens.image_credit: Ago76 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Love Parade disaster
tokens.title: Crowd crush in Duisburg
tokens.description: On 24 July 2010, a crowd crush at the Love Parade festival in Duisburg, Germany, killed 21 people as attendees tried to leave through a tunnel ramp. About 652 people were injured.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima
tokens.title: Photo on Mount Suribachi
tokens.description: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima is a photograph by Joe Rosenthal, taken on 23 February 1945, of US Marines raising the flag on Mount Suribachi during the Battle of Iwo Jima. It was published worldwide and became an icon of the Pacific War.
tokens.image_credit: Joe Rosenthal · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Raising a Flag over the Reichstag
tokens.title: Soviet flag over Berlin
tokens.description: Raising a Flag over the Reichstag is a photograph taken on 2 May 1945 by Yevgeny Khaldei, showing Soviet soldiers planting a flag on the Reichstag building in Berlin. It symbolises the Soviet victory over Nazi Germany.
tokens.image_credit: Yevgeny Khaldei / Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tank Man
tokens.title: Lone man before a tank column
tokens.description: Tank Man is an unidentified man who stood before a column of Type 59 tanks on Chang'an Avenue in Beijing on 5 June 1989, a day after the army cleared Tiananmen Square. The confrontation became one of the most recognised images of the 1989 protests.

tokens.name: Lunch atop a Skyscraper
tokens.title: Workers on a steel beam
tokens.description: Lunch atop a Skyscraper is a photograph taken on 20 September 1932 of eleven ironworkers sitting on a steel beam of the RCA Building during the construction of Rockefeller Center in Manhattan. It was a staged publicity photograph.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Clyde Ebbets · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Migrant Mother
tokens.title: Dorothea Lange photograph
tokens.description: Migrant Mother is a 1936 photograph by Dorothea Lange, taken in Nipomo, California, of a mother with three children during the Great Depression. It became a lasting symbol of the plight of migrant farm workers.
tokens.image_credit: Dorothea Lange · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Terror of War
tokens.title: Photograph at Trảng Bàng
tokens.description: The Terror of War, known as Napalm Girl, is a photograph taken on 8 June 1972 showing children fleeing a South Vietnamese napalm strike that hit Trảng Bàng village. It is one of the most famous images of the Vietnam War.

tokens.name: Saigon Execution
tokens.title: Photograph during the Tet Offensive
tokens.description: Saigon Execution is a 1968 photograph by Associated Press photographer Eddie Adams, taken during the Tet Offensive in Saigon. It won the 1969 Pulitzer Prize for Spot News Photography.

tokens.name: Afghan Girl
tokens.title: National Geographic portrait
tokens.description: Afghan Girl is a 1984 portrait by Steve McCurry of Sharbat Gula, an Afghan refugee, taken near Peshawar in Pakistan. It appeared on the June 1985 cover of National Geographic.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY year and camp location

tokens.name: Le Baiser de l'Hôtel de Ville
tokens.title: Doisneau's Paris kiss
tokens.description: Le Baiser de l'Hôtel de Ville is a 1950 photograph by Robert Doisneau showing a kissing couple in Paris. It became one of the best-known images of romantic love.

tokens.name: Flower Power photograph
tokens.title: Flowers in rifle barrels
tokens.description: Flower Power is a 1967 photograph by Bernie Boston showing a protester placing a carnation into the barrel of a rifle held by a military policeman. It was taken during the March on the Pentagon and was nominated for the 1967 Pulitzer Prize.
tokens.image_credit: By S.Sgt. Albert R. Simpson. Department of Defense. Department of the Army. Office of the Deputy Chief of Staff for Operations. U.S. Army Audiovisual Center. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Earthrise
tokens.title: Earth over the lunar horizon
tokens.description: Earthrise is a photograph of Earth taken from lunar orbit by astronaut William Anders on 24 December 1968 during the Apollo 8 mission. Nature photographer Galen Rowell called it the most influential environmental photograph ever taken.

curation.notes: taken from lunar orbit; coords = Apollo 8 launch site

tokens.image_credit: NASA/Bill Anders · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: View from the Window at Le Gras
tokens.title: Oldest surviving camera photograph
tokens.description: View from the Window at Le Gras is the oldest surviving photograph, made by Nicephore Niepce between June and July 1827 at his estate in Saint-Loup-de-Varennes. It was produced by heliography on a bitumen-coated plate.
tokens.image_credit: Nicéphore Niépce · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Roundhay Garden Scene
tokens.title: Oldest surviving motion picture
tokens.description: Roundhay Garden Scene is a short silent film shot by Louis Le Prince at Oakwood Grange in Roundhay, Leeds, on 14 October 1888. It is believed to be the oldest surviving motion picture.
tokens.image_credit: Louis Le Prince · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory
tokens.title: Early Lumière film in Lyon
tokens.description: An 1895 French silent short directed by Louis Lumière, showing workers leaving the Lumière factory in Lyon. It is often cited as the first real motion picture.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: L'Arrivée d'un train en gare de La Ciotat
tokens.title: Train arriving at La Ciotat
tokens.description: An 1896 French silent documentary short by Auguste and Louis Lumière, showing a train pulling into the La Ciotat station. It was one of the early public film screenings.
tokens.image_credit: w:Auguste and Louis Lumière (Louis d. 1948, Auguste d. 1954) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: A Trip to the Moon
tokens.title: Méliès film made in Montreuil
tokens.description: A 1902 French science-fiction trick film written, directed and produced by Georges Méliès, inspired by Jules Verne. It was made at Méliès's studio in Montreuil.
tokens.image_credit: Georges Méliès · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montparnasse derailment
tokens.title: Locomotive through the station wall
tokens.description: On 22 October 1895 a Granville to Paris express overran the buffer stop and crashed through the wall of Gare Montparnasse in Paris. The locomotive ended up hanging over the station forecourt.
tokens.image_credit: Photo credited to the firm Levy & fils by this site. (It is credited to a photographer "Kuhn" by another publisher [1].) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carnation Revolution
tokens.title: Bloodless coup in Lisbon
tokens.description: The Carnation Revolution was a military coup in Portugal on 25 April 1974 that overthrew the Estado Novo regime of Marcelo Caetano. It was largely bloodless and gave its name to the carnations carried by the crowds.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Singing Revolution
tokens.title: Baltic independence through song
tokens.description: The Singing Revolution was a series of peaceful protests from 1987 to 1991 that restored the independence of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Mass song festivals and demonstrations were central to the movement.

tokens.name: 1981 Spanish coup attempt
tokens.title: Guardia Civil storms parliament
tokens.description: A failed coup in Spain on 23 February 1981, when Civil Guard officers led by Antonio Tejero stormed the Congress of Deputies in Madrid. King Juan Carlos I's public opposition helped defeat it.

tokens.name: Kidnapping and murder of Aldo Moro
tokens.title: Red Brigades seize a statesman
tokens.description: On 16 March 1978 the Red Brigades ambushed the car of former Italian prime minister Aldo Moro in Via Fani, Rome, killing his five bodyguards and kidnapping him. Moro was murdered in May 1978.
tokens.image_credit: a member of the Red Brigades · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: March on Rome
tokens.title: Fascists seize power
tokens.description: The March on Rome was a mass Fascist demonstration in October 1922 that brought Benito Mussolini's National Fascist Party to power in Italy. King Victor Emmanuel III overruled Prime Minister Luigi Facta's plan to declare a state of siege.

tokens.name: Lateran Treaty
tokens.title: Birth of Vatican City State
tokens.description: The Lateran Treaty was one of the Lateran Pacts of 1929, signed by Italy under Benito Mussolini and the Holy See under Pope Pius XI. It recognised Vatican City as an independent state and compensated the Church for the loss of the Papal States.
tokens.image_credit: Istituto Luce · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anschluss
tokens.title: Austria annexed
tokens.description: The Anschluss was the annexation of the Federal State of Austria into Nazi Germany on 12 March 1938. The idea of a united Austria and Germany had grown after the 1871 unification of Germany excluded Austria.
tokens.image_credit: Heinrich Hoffmann · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nazi book burnings
tokens.title: Bonfire at the Opernplatz
tokens.description: The Nazi book burnings were a 1930s campaign by the German Student Union to burn books by Jewish, socialist, communist and other authors opposed to Nazism. One of the burnings took place on 10 May 1933 at the Opernplatz, now Bebelplatz, in Berlin.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2014 Scottish independence referendum
tokens.title: Scotland votes to stay
tokens.description: A referendum on Scottish independence from the United Kingdom was held in Scotland on 18 September 2014. Voters rejected independence, with 55.3% voting No and 44.7% voting Yes.

tokens.name: 2017 Catalan independence referendum
tokens.title: Contested vote in Catalonia
tokens.description: An independence referendum was held on 1 October 2017 in the Spanish autonomous community of Catalonia. Spain's Constitutional Court had declared it unconstitutional and suspended it.

tokens.name: Festival of Britain
tokens.title: South Bank exhibition
tokens.description: The Festival of Britain was a national exhibition and fair held across the United Kingdom in summer 1951. Its main exhibitions were on the South Bank in London, to promote British science, design, architecture and the arts after the Second World War.

tokens.name: Expo 2015
tokens.title: World's fair in Milan
tokens.description: Expo 2015 was a World Expo hosted by Milan, Italy, which opened on 1 May 2015 and closed on 31 October 2015. It was the second time Milan hosted an exposition, after the 1906 Milan International.

tokens.name: Exposition Universelle 1900
tokens.title: Paris world's fair
tokens.description: The Exposition Universelle of 1900 was a world's fair held in Paris from 14 April to 12 November 1900. It was held at Les Invalides, the Champ de Mars, the Trocadero and along the Seine, and drew more than fifty million visitors.
tokens.image_credit: La Librairie Illustrée, editeur · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1964 New York World's Fair
tokens.title: Fair in Flushing Meadows
tokens.description: The 1964 New York World's Fair was an international exposition held at Flushing Meadows-Corona Park in Queens, New York City, in 1964 and 1965. It was presented by 80 nations and 24 U.S. states.
tokens.image_credit: Anthony Conti; scanned and published by PLCjr from Richmond, VA, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Panama-Pacific International Exposition
tokens.title: World's fair in San Francisco
tokens.description: The Panama-Pacific International Exposition was a world's fair held in San Francisco from February to December 1915. It celebrated the completion of the Panama Canal and the city's recovery from the 1906 earthquake.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Louisiana Purchase Exposition
tokens.title: St. Louis World's Fair
tokens.description: The Louisiana Purchase Exposition, also known as the St. Louis World's Fair, was an international exposition held in St. Louis, Missouri, from 30 April to 1 December 1904. It was held in Forest Park.
tokens.image_credit: Alphonse Mucha · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nansen's Fram expedition
tokens.title: Drifting across the Arctic
tokens.description: Nansen's Fram expedition of 1893 to 1896 tried to reach the North Pole by freezing the ship Fram into the Arctic pack ice and drifting with the current. The ship left Christiania, now Oslo, in June 1893.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY departure date; coords = departure

tokens.image_credit: Appears in Fridtjof Nansen's 1897 book, so is PD in the US (published before 1923) and since Nansen died in 1930, it is PD in the UK (life of author plus 70 years) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Discovery Expedition
tokens.title: Scott's first Antarctic expedition
tokens.description: The Discovery Expedition of 1901 to 1904 was the first official British exploration of Antarctica since 1843, led by Robert Falcon Scott. Its base was Discovery Hut at Hut Point on Ross Island.
tokens.image_credit: Robert F. Scott · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Southern Cross Expedition
tokens.title: Hut at Cape Adare
tokens.description: The Southern Cross Expedition of 1898 to 1900, led by Carsten Borchgrevink, was the first to overwinter on the Antarctic mainland. Its hut stood at Cape Adare on the coast of Victoria Land.
tokens.image_credit: William Colbeck [attributed] · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Australasian Antarctic Expedition
tokens.title: Mawson at Cape Denison
tokens.description: The Australasian Antarctic Expedition was a 1911 to 1914 expedition led by Douglas Mawson to explore the Antarctic coast due south of Australia. Its main base was at Cape Denison.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Hurley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition
tokens.title: First overland crossing of Antarctica
tokens.description: The Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition of 1955 to 1958 completed the first overland crossing of Antarctica, via the South Pole. It was led by Vivian Fuchs, with Edmund Hillary leading the Ross Sea support team.

tokens.name: Andrée's Arctic balloon expedition
tokens.title: Balloon launched from Svalbard
tokens.description: Andrée's Arctic balloon expedition of 1897 was a failed Swedish attempt to reach the North Pole by hydrogen balloon. All three members died, and the balloon left from Virgohamna on Danskøya, Svalbard.
tokens.image_credit: Nils Strindberg · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Sunshine
tokens.title: Nautilus under the North Pole
tokens.description: Operation Sunshine was a 1958 US Navy expedition in which USS Nautilus made the first submerged transit under the North Pole. The crossing took place in August 1958 in the Arctic Ocean.

tokens.name: Vega expedition
tokens.title: First Northeast Passage voyage
tokens.description: The Vega expedition of 1878 to 1880, led by Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld, was the first to navigate the Northeast Passage and the first to circumnavigate Eurasia. The ship returned to Stockholm in April 1880.
tokens.image_credit: Robert Haglund · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1954 Italian expedition to K2
tokens.title: First ascent of K2
tokens.description: The 1954 Italian expedition to K2, led by Ardito Desio, made the first ascent of K2 on 31 July 1954. Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli reached the summit, the second-highest mountain in the world.

tokens.name: 1922 British Mount Everest expedition
tokens.title: First attempt on Everest
tokens.description: The 1922 British Mount Everest expedition was the first mountaineering expedition aimed at the first ascent of Everest. It attempted the mountain from the north side in Tibet and was the first to use bottled oxygen on the mountain.
tokens.image_credit: Book author Charles Granville Bruce. Photographer unattributed, probably John Baptist Lucius Noel · PD-US · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2008 K2 disaster
tokens.title: Deadly day on K2
tokens.description: The 2008 K2 disaster on 1 August 2008 killed 11 mountaineers from international expeditions on K2, the second-highest mountain on Earth. It was the worst single episode in the mountain's climbing history.

tokens.name: 2014 Mount Everest ice avalanche
tokens.title: Avalanche in the Khumbu Icefall
tokens.description: On 18 April 2014 ice seracs on the western spur of Mount Everest collapsed in the Khumbu Icefall, killing sixteen climbing Sherpas. It was the deadliest accident on the mountain at that time.

tokens.name: MS Estonia
tokens.title: Ferry sinks in the Baltic
tokens.description: MS Estonia was a car-passenger ferry on the Tallinn to Stockholm route when she sank in the Baltic Sea on 28 September 1994. The disaster killed 852 people and is one of the deadliest peacetime maritime disasters of the 20th century.

tokens.name: MS Herald of Free Enterprise
tokens.title: Ferry capsizes at Zeebrugge
tokens.description: MS Herald of Free Enterprise was a roll-on/roll-off ferry that capsized moments after leaving the port of Zeebrugge on 6 March 1987. The disaster killed 193 passengers and crew.

tokens.name: RMS Empress of Ireland
tokens.title: Liner lost in the St. Lawrence
tokens.description: RMS Empress of Ireland was a British-built ocean liner that sank in the Saint Lawrence River after a collision in fog on 29 May 1914. Of the 1,477 people aboard, 1,012 died, the worst peacetime maritime disaster in Canadian history.

tokens.name: SS Eastland
tokens.title: Capsized on the Chicago River
tokens.description: SS Eastland was a Great Lakes passenger steamship that capsized while moored at a dock in the Chicago River on 24 July 1915. The disaster killed 844 passengers and crew, the largest loss of life from a shipwreck on the Great Lakes.
tokens.image_credit: Bob Satterfield · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: PS General Slocum
tokens.title: Fire on the East River
tokens.description: PS General Slocum was an American sidewheel passenger steamboat built in Brooklyn in 1891. On 15 June 1904 she caught fire and sank in the East River of New York City.
tokens.image_credit: Angelo Agostini · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sultana
tokens.title: Steamboat explosion on the Mississippi
tokens.description: The steamboat Sultana exploded and sank on the Mississippi River on 27 April 1865. About 1,164 people died, the worst maritime disaster in United States history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: HMHS Britannic
tokens.title: Titanic's sister sinks off Kea
tokens.description: HMHS Britannic was the third Olympic-class liner of the White Star Line, used as a hospital ship from 1915. She sank in the Aegean Sea near the Greek island of Kea in November 1916.

tokens.name: Batavia shipwreck
tokens.title: Wreck on the Houtman Abrolhos
tokens.description: Batavia was a Dutch East India Company ship wrecked on the Houtman Abrolhos, a chain of islands off Western Australia, on 4 June 1629. Survivors on the islands later faced mutiny and killings before rescue.

tokens.name: Whydah Gally
tokens.title: Pirate ship wrecked off Cape Cod
tokens.description: Whydah Gally was a ship built as a passenger, cargo and slave vessel that was captured by the pirate Samuel Bellamy in 1717. The ship was lost in a storm off Cape Cod that year, and its wreck was later found off Wellfleet.

tokens.name: Nuestra Señora de Atocha
tokens.title: Treasure galleon off the Keys
tokens.description: Nuestra Señora de Atocha was a Spanish treasure galleon that sank in a hurricane off the Florida Keys in 1622 while sailing from Havana for Spain. The ship carried copper, silver, gold and gems from the New World.

tokens.name: SS Thistlegorm
tokens.title: Wreck in the Red Sea
tokens.description: SS Thistlegorm was a British cargo steamship built in Sunderland in 1940 and sunk by German bombers in the Red Sea in 1941. Her wreck near Ras Muhammad National Park is a well-known diving site.
tokens.image_credit: Woodym555 at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of Prince of Wales and Repulse
tokens.title: Battleships lost off Malaya
tokens.description: The sinking of Prince of Wales and Repulse was a naval engagement on 10 December 1941 in the South China Sea off Malaya. Japanese land-based bombers and torpedo bombers sank both British capital ships of Force Z.

tokens.name: HMS Royal Oak
tokens.title: Sunk at anchor in Scapa Flow
tokens.description: HMS Royal Oak was a Revenge-class battleship of the Royal Navy, completed in 1916 and fought at the Battle of Jutland. She was sunk at her anchorage in Scapa Flow, Orkney, in 1939 with heavy loss of life.

tokens.name: USS Maine explosion
tokens.title: Explosion in Havana Harbor
tokens.description: The explosion and sinking of the United States Navy ship Maine in Havana Harbor on 15 February 1898 contributed to the outbreak of the Spanish-American War. Evidence points to an accident in a coal bunker, although the cause was disputed at the time.

tokens.name: Torrey Canyon oil spill
tokens.title: Tanker on the Seven Stones reef
tokens.description: The Torrey Canyon oil spill followed the grounding of the supertanker SS Torrey Canyon on rocks off south-west England in 1967. An estimated 25 to 36 million gallons of crude oil were spilled, one of the most serious oil spills in the world.

tokens.name: 2021 Suez Canal obstruction
tokens.title: Ever Given blocks the canal
tokens.description: The Ever Given, a 400-metre container ship, ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days from 23 to 29 March 2021. The obstruction halted traffic on one of the world's busiest maritime trade routes.
tokens.image_credit: NASA JSC ISS image library · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
tokens.title: Bridge struck by a container ship
tokens.description: On 26 March 2024 the container ship Dali struck a pier of the Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore, and the main spans collapsed. Six maintenance workers died, and the collapse blocked most shipping to the Port of Baltimore for 11 weeks.
tokens.image_credit: NTSBgov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Titan submersible implosion
tokens.title: Lost on a dive to the Titanic
tokens.description: On 18 June 2023 the OceanGate submersible Titan imploded during a dive to the Titanic wreck in the North Atlantic off Newfoundland. The five people on board were killed.

tokens.name: Antikythera wreck
tokens.title: Ancient ship found by sponge divers
tokens.description: The Antikythera wreck is a Roman-era shipwreck from the first century BC, found by sponge divers off Point Glyphadia on Antikythera in 1900. Its finds include statues, coins and the Antikythera mechanism.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uluburun shipwreck
tokens.title: Bronze Age cargo ship
tokens.description: Uluburun is a Late Bronze Age shipwreck from the late 14th century BC, found in 1982 by sponge diver Mehmed Çakir off Kaş, Turkey. The ship carried over 20 tons of cargo and was excavated from 1984 to 1994.

tokens.name: Exhumation and reburial of Richard III of England
tokens.title: King found under a car park
tokens.description: On 25 August 2012 the remains of Richard III, killed at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485, were found in Leicester at the former Greyfriars Friary. They were reinterred at Leicester Cathedral on 26 March 2015.

tokens.name: Staffordshire Hoard
tokens.title: Largest Anglo-Saxon gold hoard
tokens.description: The Staffordshire Hoard is the largest hoard of Anglo-Saxon gold and silver metalwork yet found, with almost 4,600 items and fragments. It contains about 5.1 kg of gold, 1.4 kg of silver and some 3,500 pieces of garnet cloisonne jewellery.
tokens.image_credit: David Rowan, Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hoxne Hoard
tokens.title: Late Roman treasure
tokens.description: The Hoxne Hoard is the largest hoard of late Roman silver and gold discovered in Britain, with 14,865 coins and about 200 items of tableware and jewellery. It was found with a metal detector at Hoxne, Suffolk, in 1992.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net). · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mildenhall Treasure
tokens.title: Roman silver tableware
tokens.description: The Mildenhall Treasure is a hoard of over thirty pieces of fourth-century Roman silver tableware. It was found at West Row, near Mildenhall, Suffolk, in 1942, and includes the Great Dish, which weighs over 8 kg.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lewis chessmen
tokens.title: Medieval chess pieces
tokens.description: The Lewis chessmen are a group of 12th-century chess pieces, most carved from walrus ivory. They were discovered in 1831 on the Isle of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.
tokens.image_credit: National Museums Scotland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vindolanda tablets
tokens.title: Letters from Hadrian's Wall
tokens.description: The Vindolanda tablets are some of the oldest surviving handwritten documents in Britain. Written on thin wooden leaves, they date to the 1st and 2nd centuries AD and document life on the Roman northern frontier.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net). · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seahenge
tokens.title: Timber circle on a beach
tokens.description: Seahenge, also known as Holme I, was a prehistoric timber circle with an upturned tree root at its centre. It was built in the early Bronze Age, around 2049 BC, at Holme-next-the-Sea in Norfolk.
tokens.image_credit: -JvL- · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amesbury Archer
tokens.title: Rich Bronze Age burial
tokens.description: The Amesbury Archer was an early Bronze Age man who lived around 2340 to 2300 BC. His grave was discovered during excavations at a housing development in Amesbury, near Stonehenge.

tokens.name: Nebra sky disc
tokens.title: Bronze Age star map
tokens.description: The Nebra sky disc is a bronze disc of about 30 cm with gold symbols usually read as the Sun or full moon, a lunar crescent and stars. It was found near Nebra in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, and is shown in the Landesmuseum fur Vorgeschichte in Halle.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Vincentz · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venus of Willendorf
tokens.title: Palaeolithic figurine
tokens.description: The Venus of Willendorf is an 11.1 cm Venus figurine estimated to be about 30,000 years old. It was found in 1908 at a Palaeolithic site near Willendorf in Lower Austria.
tokens.image_credit: User:MatthiasKabel · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venus of Hohle Fels
tokens.title: Oldest known human figurine
tokens.description: The Venus of Hohle Fels is a mammoth ivory figurine dated to about 42,000 to 40,000 years ago, unearthed in 2008. It was found in Hohle Fels cave near Schelklingen, Germany, and is the oldest undisputed depiction of a human being.

tokens.name: Chauvet Cave
tokens.title: Cave paintings rediscovered
tokens.description: The Chauvet-Pont d'Arc Cave in the Ardeche department of France contains some of the best-preserved figurative cave paintings in the world. It was rediscovered on 18 December 1994 and granted UNESCO World Heritage status in 2014.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mask of Agamemnon
tokens.title: Gold mask from Mycenae
tokens.description: The Mask of Agamemnon is a gold funerary mask found at the Bronze Age site of Mycenae in southern Greece by Heinrich Schliemann in 1876. It is displayed in the National Archaeological Museum of Athens.
tokens.image_credit: Gleb Simonov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Priam's Treasure
tokens.title: Schliemann's find at Troy
tokens.description: Priam's Treasure is a cache of gold artifacts found by Frank Calvert and Heinrich Schliemann at Hisarlik in northwestern Turkey in the late 19th century. Schliemann linked the find to the Homeric king Priam, and most of it is now in the Pushkin Museum in Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: sailko · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Riace bronzes
tokens.title: Bronze warriors from the sea
tokens.description: The Riace bronzes are two full-size Greek bronze statues of nude, bearded men, cast by the lost-wax process. They were found in the sea off Riace Marina in Calabria in 1972 and are displayed in Reggio Calabria.
tokens.image_credit: Benjamin Smith · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lady of Elche
tokens.title: Iberian stone bust
tokens.description: The Lady of Elche is a limestone bust discovered in 1897 at La Alcudia, an archaeological site near Elche in Spain. It is generally dated to the 4th century BC and is exhibited in the National Archaeological Museum of Spain in Madrid.
tokens.image_credit: Luis Fernández García · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gundestrup cauldron
tokens.title: Silver vessel from a bog
tokens.description: The Gundestrup cauldron is a richly decorated silver vessel dated to roughly 200 BC to 300 AD, the largest known European Iron Age silver work. It was found dismantled in a peat bog near Gundestrup, Denmark, in 1891.

tokens.name: Oseberg ship
tokens.title: Viking ship burial
tokens.description: The Oseberg ship is a well-preserved Viking Age longship found in a burial mound at Oseberg farm near Tonsberg, Norway, in 1904. It is now displayed at the Viking Ship Museum in Oslo.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tollund Man
tokens.title: Bog body from Jutland
tokens.description: The Tollund Man is a naturally mummified bog body of a man who died between 405 and 384 BCE. He was found in 1950 in a peat bog near Silkeborg in Jutland, Denmark.

tokens.name: Lindow Man
tokens.title: Bog body from Cheshire
tokens.description: Lindow Man is the preserved bog body of a man found on 1 August 1984 by peat cutters at Lindow Moss near Wilmslow in Cheshire, England. The remains are dated to the Iron Age or Roman period.

tokens.name: Peking Man
tokens.title: Fossils at Zhoukoudian
tokens.description: Peking Man is a subspecies of Homo erectus whose fossils were found in a cave at Zhoukoudian, about 50 km southwest of Beijing. The first tooth was found in 1921, and the site has become the most productive H. erectus site in the world.

tokens.name: Java Man
tokens.title: Fossils at Trinil
tokens.description: Java Man is an early human fossil, a skullcap, tooth and thighbone, found in 1891 and 1892 at Trinil on the Solo River in East Java, Indonesia. It is the type specimen for Homo erectus.

tokens.name: Homo floresiensis
tokens.title: The hobbit of Flores
tokens.description: Homo floresiensis is an extinct species of small archaic humans, nicknamed the Hobbit, that lived on Flores, Indonesia, until about 50,000 years ago. Its remains were discovered in 2003 at Liang Bua cave.
tokens.image_credit: Rosino · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Homo naledi
tokens.title: Fossils in the Rising Star Cave
tokens.description: Homo naledi is an extinct species of archaic human discovered in 2013 in the Rising Star Cave system, Gauteng, South Africa, in the Cradle of Humankind. The fossils date to about 335,000 to 236,000 years ago.

tokens.name: Neanderthal 1
tokens.title: Type specimen from the Neander Valley
tokens.description: Neanderthal 1, also called Feldhofer 1, is the roughly 40,000-year-old type specimen of Homo neanderthalensis. It was found in August 1856 in the Kleine Feldhofer Grotte in the Neander Valley near Düsseldorf.

tokens.name: Nag Hammadi library
tokens.title: Codices found in a jar
tokens.description: The Nag Hammadi library is a collection of early Christian and Gnostic texts, twelve papyrus codices in a sealed jar. A farmer and others found it near the Upper Egyptian town of Nag Hammadi in 1945.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cyrus Cylinder
tokens.title: Clay cylinder from Babylon
tokens.description: The Cyrus Cylinder is a broken clay cylinder with an Achaemenid royal inscription in Akkadian cuneiform in the name of Cyrus the Great. It was found in 1879 in the foundations of the Esagila temple at Babylon, now in Iraq, and is held by the British Museum.
tokens.image_credit: Prioryman · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Code of Hammurabi
tokens.title: Law stele found at Susa
tokens.description: The Code of Hammurabi is a Babylonian legal text composed around 1753 BC, inscribed on a basalt stele 2.25 m tall. The primary copy was found at Susa in present-day Iran and is now in the Louvre.
tokens.image_credit: Mbzt · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nefertiti Bust
tokens.title: Bust found at Amarna
tokens.description: The Nefertiti Bust is a painted stucco-coated limestone bust of Nefertiti, the Great Royal Wife of Akhenaten. It was found in the sculpture workshop of Thutmose at Amarna in Egypt and is displayed in the Neues Museum in Berlin.
tokens.image_credit: Giovanni from Firenze, Italy · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Benin Expedition of 1897
tokens.title: Sack of Benin City
tokens.description: The Benin Expedition of 1897 was the British conquest of the Kingdom of Benin after a British party was attacked in January 1897. Benin City was taken and the kingdom was annexed into colonial Nigeria.
tokens.image_credit: Reginald Kerr Granville (d.1912) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coyolxauhqui Stone
tokens.title: Disc that revealed the Templo Mayor
tokens.description: The Coyolxauhqui Stone is a carved circular Aztec relief of the mythical being Coyolxauhqui, dismembered by Huitzilopochtli. It was rediscovered in 1978 at the base of the Templo Mayor in Mexico City.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aztec sun stone
tokens.title: Found in the Zócalo
tokens.description: The Aztec sun stone, also called Piedra del Sol, is a Mexica monolith weighing about 24.6 tonnes. It was found buried in the Zocalo, Mexico City's main square, and is now housed in the National Museum of Anthropology.
tokens.image_credit: Jonathan Cardy · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heinkel He 178
tokens.title: First jet aircraft flight
tokens.description: The Heinkel He 178 was an experimental aircraft that became the first to fly using a turbojet engine. It first flew on 27 August 1939 from the Heinkel airfield at Rostock-Marienehe.

tokens.name: Gloster E.28/39
tokens.title: First British jet flight
tokens.description: The Gloster E.28/39 was the first British turbojet-engined aircraft, built to test Frank Whittle's jet propulsion designs. It first flew in 1941 from RAF Cranwell in Lincolnshire.

tokens.name: Vought-Sikorsky VS-300
tokens.title: Pioneering helicopter
tokens.description: The Vought-Sikorsky VS-300 was a single-rotor helicopter designed by Igor Sikorsky. Its first free flight took place on 13 May 1940 at Sikorsky's works in Stratford, Connecticut.

tokens.name: Zeppelin LZ 1
tokens.title: First Zeppelin flight
tokens.description: The Zeppelin LZ 1 was the first successful experimental rigid airship. It first flew on 2 July 1900 from a floating hangar on Lake Constance near Friedrichshafen, Germany.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Scherer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hughes H-4 Hercules
tokens.title: The Spruce Goose flies once
tokens.description: The Hughes H-4 Hercules, nicknamed the Spruce Goose, was a wooden flying boat built by Howard Hughes. It made its only brief flight over Long Beach harbour, California, on 2 November 1947.

tokens.name: R101
tokens.title: Airship crash near Beauvais
tokens.description: R101 was a British rigid airship, the largest flying craft of its time, that crashed on 5 October 1930 during its first flight to India. The crash at Allonne, near Beauvais, killed 48 people.

tokens.name: MacCready Gossamer Albatross
tokens.title: Pedal-powered Channel crossing
tokens.description: The MacCready Gossamer Albatross, a human-powered aircraft, was pedalled across the English Channel on 12 June 1979. The flight from near Folkestone, England, ended on the beach at Cap Gris-Nez, France.

tokens.name: Concorde first flight
tokens.title: Supersonic airliner first flight
tokens.description: Concorde made its first flight from Toulouse on 2 March 1969. The Anglo-French supersonic airliner was jointly developed by Sud Aviation and the British Aircraft Corporation.
tokens.image_credit: André Cros · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boeing 747 first flight
tokens.title: First flight of the jumbo jet
tokens.description: The Boeing 747 made its first flight on 9 February 1969 from Paine Field in Everett, Washington. The wide-body jumbo jet was designed by Boeing for long-range airline service.

tokens.name: Airbus A380 first flight
tokens.title: First flight of the superjumbo
tokens.description: The Airbus A380 made its maiden flight on 27 April 2005 from Toulouse-Blagnac airport in France. It is the world's largest passenger airliner and the only full-length double-deck jet airliner.

tokens.name: de Havilland Comet first jet airliner
tokens.title: First jet airliner
tokens.description: The de Havilland Comet 1 prototype first flew in 1949, making the Comet the world's first commercial jet airliner. The four-engine aircraft was developed and manufactured by de Havilland in the United Kingdom.

tokens.name: Rainhill trials
tokens.title: Rocket wins the locomotive contest
tokens.description: The Rainhill trials were held from 6 to 14 October 1829 at Rainhill, Lancashire, to choose the locomotive for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway. George Stephenson's Rocket was the only entrant to complete the trials and was declared the winner.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Benz Patent-Motorwagen first automobile patent
tokens.title: The first automobile patent
tokens.description: Carl Benz received German patent DRP 37435 in 1886 for the belt-drive layout of his Patent-Motorwagen. The three-wheeled car with a single-cylinder four-stroke engine is known as the world's first practical production automobile.

tokens.name: First words over the telephone wire
tokens.title: First words over the wire
tokens.description: On 10 March 1876 Alexander Graham Bell transmitted the first intelligible sentence over a telephone wire, from a laboratory at 5 Exeter Place in Boston. The invention was contested by several inventors, including Antonio Meucci, Philipp Reis and Elisha Gray.

tokens.name: Transatlantic telegraph cable
tokens.title: Wire across the ocean
tokens.description: The first transatlantic telegraph cable was laid from Valentia Island, off the west coast of Ireland, to Newfoundland, starting in 1858. The Atlantic Telegraph Company led by Cyrus West Field built the cable, and a successful link followed in 1866.
tokens.image_credit: Robert Charles Dudley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Metropolitan Railway
tokens.title: World's first underground railway
tokens.description: The Metropolitan Railway opened in 1863 as the world's first underground railway, linking the London main-line termini at Paddington, Euston and King's Cross with the City. It was built mainly by cut-and-cover beneath the New Road.
