tokens.description: Lake Tana is the largest lake in Ethiopia and a source of the Blue Nile. It lies in the Amhara Region in the north-western Ethiopian Highlands.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fasil Ghebbi
tokens.description: Fasil Ghebbi is a fortress in Gondar, Amhara Region, Ethiopia, founded in the 17th century by Emperor Fasilides. It was the home of Ethiopian emperors and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dallol
tokens.title: Alien hydrothermal fields
tokens.description: Dallol is a terrestrial hydrothermal system around a cinder cone volcano in the Danakil Depression, northeast of the Erta Ale Range in Ethiopia. It is known for its unearthly colours and some of the most acidic fluids on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sof Omar Caves
tokens.description: Sof Omar Caves is the longest cave in Ethiopia, at 15.1 kilometres long. When surveyed in 1972, it was the longest cave in Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Rod Waddington from Kergunyah, Australia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Abbe
tokens.description: Lake Abbe is a salt lake on the Ethiopia-Djibouti border, the terminal basin of the Awash River in the Afar Triangle. It is one of a chain of six connected lakes.
tokens.image_credit: Jbcombes · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: University of al-Qarawiyyin
tokens.title: Oldest university
tokens.description: The University of al-Qarawiyyin is a university in Fez, Morocco, founded as a mosque by Fatima al-Fihri in 857-859. It became one of the leading spiritual and educational centres of the Islamic Golden Age.
tokens.image_credit: Abdel Hassouni · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Meknes
tokens.description: Meknes is one of the four imperial cities of Morocco, in northern central Morocco. It was founded in the 11th century by the Almoravids and became the capital under Sultan Ismail Ibn Sharif.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Martin from Decatur, Georgia, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dadès Gorges
tokens.description: The Dadès Gorges are a series of rugged wadi gorges carved out by the Dadès River in Morocco. The river rises in the High Atlas and joins the Draa River at the edge of the Sahara.
tokens.image_credit: Holger Uwe Schmitt · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: High Atlas
tokens.description: The High Atlas, also called the Grand Atlas, is a mountain range in central Morocco and the highest part of the Atlas Mountains. It stretches from the Atlantic coast to the Moroccan-Algerian border.
tokens.image_credit: Kobersky (talk · contribs) · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Toubkal
tokens.description: Toubkal is a mountain in central Morocco, located in the Toubkal National Park. At 4,167 m, it is the highest peak in Morocco, the Atlas Mountains, North Africa and the Arab world.
tokens.image_credit: SimonKing74 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Mosque of Kairouan
tokens.description: The Great Mosque of Kairouan, also called the Mosque of Uqba, is a mosque in Kairouan, Tunisia, established in 670-671 CE at the founding of the city. It is one of the largest Islamic monuments in North Africa.
tokens.image_credit: weetoon66 · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dougga
tokens.description: Dougga, also Thugga, was a Berber, Punic and Roman settlement near Teboursouk in northern Tunisia. UNESCO inscribed the site as a World Heritage Site in 1997, as the best-preserved Roman small town in North Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Emna Trabelsi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Djémila
tokens.description: Djémila is a small mountain village in northern Algeria with some of the best preserved Roman ruins in North Africa. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982 for its Roman architecture adapted to a mountain environment.
tokens.image_credit: Alioueche Mokhtar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tipasa
tokens.description: Tipasa is a former Roman colonia on the coast of central Algeria, now called Tipaza. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982, and was on the danger list from 2002 to 2006.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: M'zab
tokens.description: The M'zab is a natural region of the northern Sahara Desert in Ghardaia Province, Algeria, about 600 km south of Algiers. It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Camille Gillet · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hoggar Mountains
tokens.description: The Hoggar Mountains are a highland region in the central Sahara in southern Algeria, covering about 550,000 km2. The Ahaggar Cultural Park covers most of the range, which holds Mount Tahat, the highest peak in Algeria.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sabratha
tokens.description: Sabratha is an ancient Roman city on the Mediterranean coast of western Libya, about 70 km west of Tripoli. It was the westernmost of the three cities of Roman Tripolis, alongside Oea and Leptis Magna.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cyrene, Libya
tokens.description: Cyrene was an ancient Greek colony and Roman city in northeastern Libya, near Shahhat, that gave Cyrenaica its name. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on a ridge of the Jebel Akhdar uplands.
tokens.image_credit: Maher27777 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ghadames
tokens.description: Ghadames is an oasis town in northwestern Libya, known as the pearl of the desert, and one of the oldest pre-Saharan cities. Its Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1986.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Teogomez assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Acacus Mountains
tokens.description: The Acacus Mountains, also called Tadrart Akakus, form a mountain range in the Sahara in western Libya, east of Ghat. The range has a rich array of prehistoric rock art and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Franzfoto · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ubari Sand Sea
tokens.description: The Ubari Sand Sea, also called Idehan Ubari, is an erg of sand dunes in the hyper-arid Fezzan region of southwestern Libya. The area covers about 58,000 square kilometres and has long been home to Tuareg people.
tokens.image_credit: Luca Galuzzi (Lucag) · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tibesti Mountains
tokens.description: The Tibesti Mountains are a mountain range in the central Sahara, mainly in the far north of Chad with a small part in southern Libya. Emi Koussi, the highest peak in the range, is the highest point in Chad and in the Sahara.
tokens.image_credit: michael kerling · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guelta d'Archei
tokens.description: The Guelta d'Archei is a famous rock pool in a sandstone canyon of the Ennedi Plateau in north-eastern Chad. It is home to a small population of West African crocodiles and is part of the Ennedi Massif UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Dario Menasce, I.N.F.N. Italy en:User:Dario Menasce · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lakes of Ounianga
tokens.description: The Lakes of Ounianga are a series of lakes in the Sahara Desert in north-eastern Chad, in a basin between the West Tibesti and Ennedi East mountains. The site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2012.
tokens.image_credit: Jacques Taberlet · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aïr Mountains
tokens.description: The Aïr Mountains, or Aïr Massif, form a triangular massif in northern Niger within the Sahara. They rise above 1,800 metres and cover about 84,000 square kilometres, with a Sahel climate island supporting pastoral and farming communities.
tokens.image_credit: Denvermaxwell at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ténéré
tokens.title: Tree of Ténéré desert
tokens.description: The Ténéré is a desert region in the south central Sahara, a vast plain of sand stretching from north-eastern Niger to western Chad. It covers an area of over 400,000 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Holger Reineccius · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Agadez
tokens.description: Agadez is the fifth largest city in Niger, lying in the Sahara desert and capital of the Agadez Region. Its Historic Centre is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2013.
tokens.image_credit: Dan Lundberg · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Djinguereber Mosque
tokens.description: The Djinguereber Mosque is a famous learning centre in Timbuktu, Mali, built in 1327. It is one of three mosques linked to the historical University of Timbuktu and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988.
tokens.image_credit: upyernoz from Haverford, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sankoré Madrasah
tokens.description: Sankoré Madrasah is one of three medieval mosques and centres of learning in Timbuktu, Mali, founded in the 14th or early 15th century. The three Timbuktu mosques are part of the UNESCO World Heritage property inscribed in 1988.
tokens.image_credit: Anne and David · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bandiagara Escarpment
tokens.title: Land of the Dogons
tokens.description: The Bandiagara Escarpment is a sandstone cliff in the Dogon country of Mali, rising about 500 m above the flats to the south. It runs for about 150 km and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Cliff of Bandiagara (Land of the Dogons).
tokens.image_credit: Timm Guenther · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tomb of Askia
tokens.description: The Tomb of Askia in Gao, Mali, is believed to be the burial place of Askia Muhammad I, emperor of the Songhai Empire. Built at the end of the 15th century, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: David Sessoms from Fribourg, Switzerland · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Niger River
tokens.description: The Niger River is the main river of West Africa, extending about 4,180 kilometres. Its source is in the Guinea Highlands in south-eastern Guinea, near the Sierra Leone border.

tokens.name: Banc d'Arguin National Park
tokens.description: Banc d'Arguin National Park lies on the west coast of Mauritania between Nouakchott and Nouadhibou. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major refuge for migratory and breeding birds, including flamingos and pelicans.
tokens.image_credit: Kokopelado · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chinguetti
tokens.description: Chinguetti is a ksar and medieval trading centre in northern Mauritania, founded in the 13th century on the Adrar Plateau. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata, inscribed in 1996.
tokens.image_credit: François COLIN · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary
tokens.description: The Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary lies on the southeast bank of the Senegal River in northern Senegal. It is a wetland habitat for migrating birds, with almost 400 species recorded, most visibly pelicans and flamingos.
tokens.image_credit: Manu25 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Richard-Molard
tokens.description: Mount Richard-Molard is a mountain on the border of Guinea, Ivory Coast and Liberia in West Africa. Its summit, at 1,752 m, is the highest point of Guinea and Ivory Coast and lies within the Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve.
tokens.image_credit: Guy Debonnet · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taï National Park
tokens.description: Taï National Park is a national park in Ivory Coast that contains one of the last areas of primary rainforest in West Africa. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1982 for the diversity of its flora and fauna.
tokens.image_credit: yakovlev.alexey from Moscow, Russia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
tokens.title: World's largest church
tokens.description: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace is a Catholic minor basilica in Yamoussoukro, the administrative capital of Ivory Coast. Guinness World Records lists it as the largest church in the world, with an area of 30,000 square metres.
tokens.aliases: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace of Yamoussoukro
tokens.image_credit: Didierwiki · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Koutammakou
tokens.description: Koutammakou, the Land of the Batammariba, is a cultural landscape on the border of northern Togo and Benin. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, designated in 2004 and expanded in 2023, known for its traditional mud tower-houses.
tokens.image_credit: Erik Kristensen · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ganvie
tokens.title: Lake stilt village
tokens.description: Ganvie is a lake village on Lake Nokoue near Cotonou in Benin, with around 20,000 residents, probably the largest lake village in Africa. It has not been inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Manu25 at French Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pendjari National Park
tokens.description: Pendjari National Park lies in north-western Benin, adjoining the Arli National Park in Burkina Faso. It is known for its wildlife, including some of the last big game populations in West Africa, and forms part of the W-Arly-Pendjari UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Osun-Osogbo
tokens.description: Osun-Osogbo is a sacred grove along the banks of the Osun River just outside Osogbo in Osun State, Nigeria. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005 as one of the last sacred forests of the Yoruba cities.
tokens.image_credit: ABORISADEADETONA · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dja Faunal Reserve
tokens.description: Dja Faunal Reserve is a protected rainforest area in southeastern Cameroon, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987. It is noted for its species diversity and five threatened mammal species.
tokens.image_credit: Amcaja · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ekom-Nkam Falls
tokens.description: Ekom-Nkam Falls, also called Chutes d'Ekom, is an 80-metre waterfall on the Nkam River in Cameroon. It is known to tourists and lies about 30 kilometres from Bafang.
tokens.image_credit: Ndijose · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Loango National Park
tokens.description: Loango National Park is a national park in western Gabon. It protects part of the Iguéla Lagoon and spans 1,550 square kilometres of savanna, beach, forest and mangroves.

tokens.name: Ivindo National Park
tokens.description: Ivindo National Park is a national park in east-central Gabon, known for the Kongou and Mingouli waterfalls on the Ivindo River. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage natural site in 2021.
tokens.image_credit: Jefe Le Gran · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Odzala-Kokoua National Park
tokens.description: Odzala-Kokoua National Park is a national park in the Republic of the Congo, first protected in 1935. It forms part of the Forest Massif of Odzala-Kokoua, a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2023.

tokens.name: Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park
tokens.description: Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park is a national park in northern Republic of the Congo, established in 1993. It is home to forest elephants, great apes and about 300 bird species, and is part of the Sangha Trinational UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Pico Cão Grande
tokens.description: Pico Cão Grande is a needle-shaped volcanic plug on São Tomé Island, São Tomé and Príncipe. Its summit rises to 663 metres in the Obô de São Tomé natural park.
tokens.image_credit: Philippe Bourachot · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kalandula Falls
tokens.description: Kalandula Falls are waterfalls on the Lucala River in Malanje Province, Angola. They are 105 metres high and 400 metres wide, and among the largest waterfalls by volume in Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Zorglub · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Andasibe-Mantadia National Park
tokens.description: Andasibe-Mantadia National Park is a 155 square kilometre protected area of mainly primary forest, about 150 km east of Antananarivo in eastern Madagascar. Its elevation ranges from 800 to 1260 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Smiley.toerist · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ambohimanga
tokens.description: Ambohimanga is a hill and fortified royal settlement (rova) about 24 km northeast of Antananarivo, Madagascar. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and the best-preserved monument of the precolonial Merina Kingdom.
tokens.image_credit: jm bergougniou · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Masoala National Park
tokens.description: Masoala National Park, in northeast Madagascar, is the largest of the island's protected areas. It protects about 2,300 square kilometres of rainforest and 100 square kilometres of marine park.

tokens.name: Ankarana Special Reserve
tokens.description: Ankarana Special Reserve is a protected area in northern Madagascar, created in 1956. It is a limestone plateau of karst landscape, with caves and underground rivers.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Stooof assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aapravasi Ghat
tokens.description: Aapravasi Ghat is a building complex in Port Louis, Mauritius, the immigration depot where indentured labourers arrived from 1849 to 1923. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Suyash Dwivedi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cidade Velha
tokens.description: Cidade Velha is a town on the island of Santiago, Cape Verde, founded in 1462 and the oldest settlement in the country. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and the former capital.
tokens.image_credit: Cayambe · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bijagós Islands
tokens.description: The Bijagós Islands are a group of about 88 islands and islets in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Guinea-Bissau. The archipelago is also spelled Bijagos, and was formerly known in English as Bissagots.

tokens.name: Thebes, Egypt
tokens.description: Thebes, known to the ancient Egyptians as Waset, was an ancient Egyptian city on the Nile and capital of Egypt in the Middle and New Kingdoms. Its ruins lie within modern Luxor and form the UNESCO site Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis.
tokens.image_credit: Marc Ryckaert · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Memphis, Egypt
tokens.description: Memphis, also called Men-nefer, was the ancient capital of the first nome of Lower Egypt, and its ruins lie near Mit Rahina south of Giza. Memphis and its necropolis, the pyramid fields from Giza to Dahshur, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Neithsabes assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abydos, Egypt
tokens.description: Abydos, also called Abedju, was one of the oldest cities of ancient Egypt and lies in the eighth nome of Upper Egypt. Its ruins are located west of the Nile near the modern towns of El Araba El Madfuna and El Balyana.
tokens.image_credit: Olaf Tausch · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Medinet Habu
tokens.description: Medinet Habu is an archaeological locality on the west bank of the Nile opposite Luxor, known for the mortuary temple of Ramesses III. Its reliefs depict the advent and defeat of the Sea Peoples, and the site lies within the UNESCO property Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ramesseum
tokens.description: The Ramesseum is the memorial temple of Pharaoh Ramesses II, located in the Theban Necropolis on the west bank of the Nile opposite Luxor. It is the second largest temple in Egypt and lies within the UNESCO property Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Deir el-Medina
tokens.description: Deir el-Medina was an ancient Egyptian workmen's village that housed the artisans who worked on the tombs in the Valley of the Kings during the 18th to 20th Dynasties. It forms part of the UNESCO property Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Unfinished obelisk
tokens.description: The Unfinished obelisk is the largest known ancient obelisk, abandoned in the granite quarries of Aswan in northern Egypt. The quarry is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tanis
tokens.description: Tanis, also called San al-Hagar, is an important archaeological site in the northeastern Nile Delta of Egypt. It was the capital of the Egyptian kingdom in its 21st and 22nd Dynasties.
tokens.image_credit: Original uploader was Markh at en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bahariya Oasis
tokens.description: Bahariya Oasis is a depression and naturally rich oasis in the Western Desert of Egypt, about 370 km from Cairo. Its roughly oval valley covers an area of about 2000 km2.
tokens.image_credit: Neil Carey · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Faiyum
tokens.description: Faiyum is a city in Egypt, 100 km southwest of Cairo, and the capital of Faiyum Governorate. It lies in the Faiyum Oasis and is one of Egypt's oldest cities.
tokens.image_credit: Roland Unger · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Qarun
tokens.description: Lake Qarun is a hypersaline lake in the Faiyum Oasis, about 80 km southwest of Cairo. It is what remains of the ancient Lake Moeris, now at a fraction of its former size.

tokens.name: Dakhla Oasis
tokens.description: Dakhla Oasis is one of the seven oases of Egypt's Western Desert. It lies in the New Valley Governorate, between the oases of Farafra and Kharga.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Meidum Pyramid
tokens.description: The Pyramid of Meidum is an archaeological site in Lower Egypt with a large pyramid and several mudbrick mastabas. It was Egypt's first smooth-sided true pyramid, but it partially collapsed in antiquity.
tokens.image_credit: Kurohito · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Red Pyramid
tokens.description: The Red Pyramid is the largest of the pyramids at the Dahshur necropolis in Cairo, Egypt, and the third largest Egyptian pyramid. It is believed to be Egypt's first successful smooth-sided true pyramid.
tokens.image_credit: Olaf Tausch · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pyramid of Khafre
tokens.description: The Pyramid of Khafre is the middle of the three Ancient Egyptian pyramids of Giza, the second tallest and second largest of the group. It is the only one of the three that still has cladding at the top.
tokens.image_credit: M1chu · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pyramid of Menkaure
tokens.description: The Pyramid of Menkaure is the smallest of the three main pyramids of the Giza pyramid complex on the Giza Plateau near Cairo, Egypt. It was built as the tomb of Fourth Dynasty king Menkaure and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Memphis and its Necropolis.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hanging Church
tokens.description: The Hanging Church, officially Saint Virgin Mary's Coptic Orthodox Church, is one of the oldest churches in Egypt, dating to the third century. It belongs to the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria and is in Cairo.
tokens.image_credit: Berthold Werner · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Elephantine
tokens.description: Elephantine is an island on the Nile forming part of the city of Aswan in Upper Egypt. Its archaeological site is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae, inscribed in 1979.

tokens.name: Coricancha
tokens.description: Coricancha was the most important temple in the Inca Empire, located in Cusco, Peru, the empire's capital. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property City of Cuzco, inscribed in 1983.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moray
tokens.description: Moray is an Inca archaeological site in Peru about 50 km northwest of Cusco, on a high plateau near the village of Maras. It consists mostly of circular terraced depressions, the largest about 30 m deep, with an irrigation system.
tokens.image_credit: Draceane · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salt Mines of Maras
tokens.description: The Salt Mines of Maras are one of the largest salt extraction centres of prehispanic origin in Cusco, Peru, at about 3,200 m in the Urubamba Province. The site is on UNESCO's Tentative List but is not a World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Draceane · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Huascarán
tokens.description: Huascarán is a mountain in the Cordillera Blanca of the Peruvian Andes. Its southern summit, at 6,768 m, is the highest point in Peru and in the tropics, and the peak lies within Huascarán National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Pachacamac
tokens.description: Pachacamac is an archaeological site 40 km southeast of Lima, Peru, in the Lurín Valley. It was first settled around AD 200 and flourished for about 1,300 years until the Spanish invasion.
tokens.image_credit: Ingo Mehling · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park
tokens.description: Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park is a national park in the Brazilian state of Goiás, on an ancient plateau estimated at 1.8 billion years old. The park was created in 1961 and listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 2001.
tokens.image_credit: MTur Destinos · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jericoacoara National Park
tokens.description: Jericoacoara National Park is a national park of Brazil in the municipality of Jijoca de Jericoacoara, in the state of Ceará. Famous Jericoacoara Beach lies on its seashore.

tokens.name: Laguna Verde, Bolivia
tokens.description: Laguna Verde is a salt lake in an endorheic basin on the southwestern Altiplano of Bolivia. It lies close to the Chilean border, at the foot of the Licancabur volcano.
tokens.image_credit: Pedro Szekely from USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sucre
tokens.description: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia and the capital of Chuquisaca Department. Its historic centre is listed as the Historic City of Sucre, a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 1991.
tokens.image_credit: Parallelepiped09 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Madidi National Park
tokens.description: Madidi National Park is a national park in the upper Amazon River basin of Bolivia, established in 1995. It covers about 18,958 square kilometres and is part of one of the largest protected areas in the world.

tokens.name: Noel Kempff Mercado National Park
tokens.description: Noel Kempff Mercado National Park is a national park in northeast Santa Cruz Department, Bolivia, on the border with Brazil. The park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: El Fuerte de Samaipata
tokens.description: El Fuerte de Samaipata is a pre-Columbian archaeological site in Santa Cruz Department, Bolivia, served by the nearby town of Samaipata. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Dpasten · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos
tokens.description: The Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos are six former mission settlements in eastern Bolivia's Santa Cruz department, founded by Jesuits in the 17th and 18th centuries. They were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1990.
tokens.image_credit: Daan at Dutch Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sajama National Park
tokens.description: Sajama National Park is a national park in Bolivia's Oruro Department, bordering Lauca National Park in Chile. The park is home to the indigenous Aymara people, whose ancient culture is visible throughout the park.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moai
tokens.description: Moai are monolithic human figures carved from stone by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island between about 1250 and 1500. Nearly half still stand at Rano Raraku, the main quarry, and hundreds were set on stone platforms around the island.
tokens.image_credit: Rivi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Licancabur
tokens.description: Licancabur is a 5,916 metre stratovolcano on the Bolivia-Chile border in the Central Volcanic Zone of the Andes. Its summit crater holds Licancabur Lake, one of the highest lakes in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Albert Backer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ojos del Salado
tokens.title: Highest volcano
tokens.description: Ojos del Salado is a dormant complex volcano in the Andes on the Argentina-Chile border. It is the highest volcano on Earth and the highest peak in Chile.

tokens.name: Lauca National Park
tokens.description: Lauca National Park is in Chile's Norte Grande, within the Andes. It covers 1,379 square kilometres of altiplano and mountains, mainly enormous volcanoes, and neighbours Las Vicuñas National Reserve.
tokens.image_credit: mtchm from - · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cerro Torre
tokens.description: Cerro Torre is one of the mountains of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, on the Argentina-Chile border west of Fitz Roy. At 3,128 metres it is the highest peak of a four-mountain chain.
tokens.image_credit: Gagea · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cape Horn
tokens.description: Cape Horn is the southernmost headland of the Tierra del Fuego archipelago in southern Chile. It marks the northern boundary of the Drake Passage, where the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans meet.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valdés Peninsula
tokens.description: The Valdés Peninsula is a peninsula into the Atlantic Ocean in Chubut Province, Argentina. It is an important nature reserve listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cueva de las Manos
tokens.description: Cueva de las Manos is a cave and rock art complex in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, named for its hundreds of stencilled hand paintings. The art dates from between about 7300 BC and AD 700. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Mariano · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Los Alerces National Park
tokens.description: Los Alerces National Park is located in the Andes in Chubut Province, Argentina, on the Chilean border. Glacial moraines, cirques and clear-water lakes shape its landscape. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 2017.

tokens.name: Nahuel Huapi National Park
tokens.description: Nahuel Huapi National Park is the oldest national park in Argentina, established in 1922. It surrounds Nahuel Huapi Lake in the foothills of the Patagonian Andes and covers about 7,050 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Fernando · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Recoleta Cemetery
tokens.description: La Recoleta Cemetery is a cemetery in the Recoleta neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, Argentina. It holds the graves of Eva Peron, Argentine presidents, Nobel Prize winners and military commanders.
tokens.image_credit: Deensel · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salta Cathedral
tokens.description: Salta Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Salta, Argentina, and the seat of the Archbishop of Salta. It is dedicated to Jesus Christ as the Lord of Miracles and to the Virgin Mary.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iberá Wetlands
tokens.description: The Iberá Wetlands are a mix of swamps, bogs, lakes, lagoons and watercourses in Corrientes Province, Argentina. The article describes them as one of South America's most important freshwater reservoirs and the second-largest wetland in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Evelyn Proimos · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Perito Moreno National Park
tokens.description: Perito Moreno National Park is a national park in western Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, on the border with Chile. It covers 126,830 hectares of mountains and valleys at about 900 metres above sea level.

tokens.name: Cerro de los Siete Colores
tokens.description: Cerro de los Siete Colores is one of the hills bordering the Quebrada de Purmamarca in Jujuy Province, Argentina. Its banded colours come from marine, lake and river sediments lifted by tectonic movement.
tokens.image_credit: Augusto Sarita · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castillo San Felipe de Barajas
tokens.description: The Castillo San Felipe de Barajas is a fortress on Cerro San Lázaro overlooking Cartagena, Colombia, built from 1639. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Cartagena: Port, Fortresses and Group of Monuments.
tokens.image_credit: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sanctuary of Las Lajas
tokens.description: The Basilica of Our Lady of the Holy Rosary of Las Lajas is a Roman Catholic minor basilica in the canyon of the Guáitara River near Ipiales, Colombia. Pope Pius XII granted a papal decree of coronation to its Marian image in 1951.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Agustín Archaeological Park
tokens.description: The San Agustín Archaeological Park is a large archaeological area near the town of San Agustín in Huila Department, Colombia. It holds the largest collection of religious monuments and megalithic sculptures in Latin America and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tierradentro
tokens.description: Tierradentro is a pre-Columbian archaeological site in the Cauca mountains of southwest Colombia, known for its underground tombs (hypogea). The culture flourished from about 200 BC, and the park was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995.
tokens.image_credit: inyucho · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Peñón de Guatapé
tokens.description: El Peñón de Guatapé is a landmark inselberg in the municipality of Guatapé, Antioquia, Colombia. It is also known as El Peñol or La Piedra, and the neighbouring town of El Peñol has also claimed it.
tokens.image_credit: Sebastian Reategui · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nevado del Ruiz
tokens.description: Nevado del Ruiz is a stratovolcano on the border of the Caldas and Tolima departments in Colombia, the highest point of both. It lies about 130 km west of Bogota.
tokens.image_credit: The NASA Expedition 23 crew · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
tokens.description: The Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta is an isolated mountain range in northern Colombia, separate from the Andes. It rises to 5,700 m just 42 km from the Caribbean coast.
tokens.image_credit: Lobocordero5 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Los Nevados National Natural Park
tokens.description: Los Nevados National Natural Park is a national park in the Cordillera Central of the Colombian Andes. It includes the glacier-capped volcanoes Nevado del Ruiz, Nevado del Tolima and Nevado de Santa Isabel.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Mauricioagudelo~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malpelo Island
tokens.description: Malpelo Island is a rocky oceanic island about 500 km west of Colombia's mainland, with a Colombian military post. Its surrounding waters form the Malpelo Fauna and Flora Sanctuary, a UNESCO World Heritage property since 2006.
tokens.image_credit: NOAA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Providencia Island
tokens.description: Providencia is a mountainous Caribbean island in the Colombian archipelago of San Andres, Providencia and Santa Catalina, midway between Costa Rica and Jamaica. Its highest point is 360 m above sea level.

tokens.name: Leticia
tokens.description: Leticia is the southernmost city in Colombia and the capital of the Amazonas department. It is one of the major ports on the Amazon River and a long-standing centre of the aquarium fish trade.

tokens.name: Galápagos National Park
tokens.description: Galápagos National Park was established in 1959 and began operation in 1968. It is Ecuador's first national park and part of the Galápagos Islands UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: putneymark · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Historic Centre of Quito
tokens.description: The Historic Centre of Quito is the old town of Ecuador's capital, in a valley on the eastern slopes of the Pichincha stratovolcano. It is a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: David Adam Kess · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chimborazo
tokens.description: Chimborazo is a stratovolcano in the Cordillera Occidental of the Andes in Ecuador. It is the highest mountain in Ecuador and the 39th-highest peak in the Andes.
tokens.image_credit: Eduardo Navas · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sangay National Park
tokens.description: Sangay National Park is a national park in Ecuador across five provinces. It contains the active volcanoes Sangay and Tungurahua and is a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Albert Backer · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ingapirca
tokens.description: Ingapirca is the largest known Inca ruin site in Ecuador, in Cañar Province. Its most significant building is the Temple of the Sun, an elliptical structure built around a large rock.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Cajas National Park
tokens.description: El Cajas National Park is a national park in the highlands of Ecuador, about 30 km west of Cuenca. Its paramo vegetation covers a jagged landscape of hills and valleys between 3,100 and 4,450 metres.

tokens.name: Auyán-tepui
tokens.description: Auyán-tepui is a tepui in Bolívar state, Venezuela, and one of the largest tepuis of the Guiana Highlands. It lies within Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Christoph Kühnhanss, CH-3011 BERN · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Orinoco
tokens.title: Heavy oil belt of Venezuela
tokens.description: The Orinoco is one of the longest rivers in South America, at 2,140 km. About 65 percent of its basin of roughly 1,000,000 km2 lies in Venezuela and 35 percent in Colombia.
tokens.image_credit: Venecon at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Llanos
tokens.description: The Llanos is a vast tropical grassland plain east of the Andes in Colombia and Venezuela. It is an ecoregion of the tropical and subtropical grasslands, savannas and shrublands biome.

tokens.name: Iwokrama Forest
tokens.description: The Iwokrama Forest is a 3,716 square kilometre nature reserve in central Guyana, in the Guiana Shield. It is bisected by the Georgetown-Lethem Road.

tokens.name: Rupununi
tokens.description: The Rupununi is a region in the south-west of Guyana, bordering the Brazilian Amazon. The Rupununi river, also known as Raponani, flows through the region.

tokens.name: Fort Zeelandia
tokens.description: Fort Zeelandia is a fortress in Paramaribo, Suriname. The French built a wooden fort on the site in 1640, and the Dutch took it in 1667 and renamed it Fort Zeelandia.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Ahsmann · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Central Suriname Nature Reserve
tokens.description: The Central Suriname Nature Reserve is a conservation unit in Suriname that preserves an area of tropical rainforest in pristine condition. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2000.

tokens.name: Brownsberg Nature Park
tokens.description: Brownsberg Nature Park is a nature park in the Brokopondo district of Suriname, about 130 km south of Paramaribo. The 500-metre Brownsberg hill is the central point of the 12,000 ha park.

tokens.name: Paraguay River
tokens.description: The Paraguay River is a major river in south-central South America, running through Brazil and Paraguay. It flows about 2,621 km from its headwaters in Mato Grosso to its confluence with the Paraná River.

tokens.name: La Santísima Trinidad de Paraná
tokens.description: La Santísima Trinidad de Paraná is a former Jesuit reduction in Itapúa Department, Paraguay. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Jesuit Missions of La Santísima Trinidad de Paraná and Jesús de Tavarangue, inscribed in 1993.
tokens.image_credit: ogwen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gran Chaco
tokens.description: The Gran Chaco is a vast semiarid lowland region in central South America, spanning eastern Bolivia, western Paraguay, northern Argentina and parts of Brazil. It is the continent's second-largest forested ecoregion.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY 1.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Atitlán
tokens.description: Lake Atitlán is a large natural lake in the Guatemalan Highlands of the Sierra Madre, in Sololá Department. With a maximum depth of 340 metres, it is the deepest lake in Central America.
tokens.image_credit: Uspn · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Quiriguá
tokens.description: Quiriguá is an ancient Maya archaeological site in the department of Izabal in south-eastern Guatemala. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and was situated at the juncture of several important trade routes in the Classic Period.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Pešula · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Mirador
tokens.description: El Mirador is a large pre-Columbian Maya settlement in the north of the modern department of El Petén, Guatemala. It is considered the most important complex of ancient cities from the Preclassic period.

tokens.name: Semuc Champey
tokens.description: Semuc Champey is a natural enclave in the department of Alta Verapaz, Guatemala. It is a limestone land bridge with stepped turquoise pools, beneath which the Cahabón River runs into a cave system.
tokens.image_credit: Christopher Crouzet · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Acatenango
tokens.description: Acatenango is a stratovolcano in Guatemala, close to the city of Antigua. It is part of the Sierra Madre mountain range and has two peaks, Pico Mayor and Yepocapa.

tokens.name: Volcán de Fuego
tokens.description: Volcán de Fuego is an active stratovolcano in Guatemala, about 16 km west of Antigua. It lies on the borders of Chimaltenango, Escuintla and Sacatepéquez departments in the Sierra Madre.
tokens.image_credit: Murray Foubister · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pacaya
tokens.description: Pacaya is an active complex volcano in Guatemala that began erupting vigorously in 1961 after being dormant for over 70 years. It rises to an elevation of 2,552 metres and has erupted frequently since then.
tokens.image_credit: USGS · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chichicastenango
tokens.description: Chichicastenango is a town and the municipal seat of the same name in El Quiché department, Guatemala, with 71,394 inhabitants at the 2018 census. Set on a high plateau, it historically served as a K'iche' Maya ceremonial and regional center.
tokens.image_credit: Manfredwinslow · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yaxha
tokens.description: Yaxha is a Maya archaeological site in the northeast of the Petén Basin in Guatemala. As a pre-Columbian ceremonial centre it was the third largest city in the region, with its peak in the Early Classic period (c. AD 250-600).
tokens.image_credit: Marie Carianna · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Roatán
tokens.description: Roatán is an island in the Caribbean about 65 kilometres off the northern coast of Honduras. It is the largest of the Bay Islands of Honduras.

tokens.name: Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve
tokens.description: The Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve is a protected area on the Caribbean coast of Honduras, covering 5,250 square kilometres. It holds some of the largest remnants of tropical forest in Central America and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Joya de Cerén
tokens.title: Pompeii of the Americas
tokens.description: Joya de Cerén is an archaeological site in El Salvador containing the remains of a pre-Columbian Maya farming village. Preserved under volcanic ash, it is often called the Pompeii of the Americas, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Duran Ortiz) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santa Ana Volcano
tokens.description: The Santa Ana Volcano, also called Ilamatepec, is a large stratovolcano in the Santa Ana department of El Salvador. At 2,381 metres it is the highest volcano in the country.
tokens.image_credit: Dead.rabbit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Masaya Volcano
tokens.description: Masaya is a caldera and complex volcano in Nicaragua, about 20 km south of the capital Managua. It is Nicaragua's first and largest national park.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Tabla assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ometepe
tokens.description: Ometepe is an island formed by two volcanoes rising out of Lake Nicaragua, in the Rivas Department of Nicaragua. It is the largest island in Lake Nicaragua.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Nicaragua
tokens.description: Lake Nicaragua is a freshwater lake in Nicaragua, covering 8,264 square kilometres. It is the largest freshwater lake in Central America and the tenth largest in the Americas.
tokens.image_credit: Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Granada, Nicaragua
tokens.description: Granada is a city in western Nicaragua and the capital of the Granada Department. It had an estimated population of 105,862 in 2022 and is the ninth most populous city in Nicaragua.
tokens.image_credit: Adalberto.H.Vega · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Corcovado National Park
tokens.description: Corcovado National Park is a national park on the Osa Peninsula in southwestern Costa Rica. Established in 1975, it covers 424 square kilometres and is the largest park in Costa Rica.

tokens.name: Manuel Antonio National Park
tokens.description: Manuel Antonio National Park is a small national park on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica, just south of the city of Quepos. It was established in 1972.
tokens.image_credit: Hanay · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tortuguero National Park
tokens.description: Tortuguero National Park is a national park in Limón Province on the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica. Reachable only by air or boat, it is the third most visited park in Costa Rica.
tokens.image_credit: Leyo · CC BY-SA 2.5 ch · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Poás Volcano
tokens.description: The Poás Volcano is an active 2,697-metre stratovolcano in central Costa Rica, within Poás Volcano National Park. It has erupted about 40 times since 1828.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Andersen · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Irazú Volcano
tokens.description: The Irazú Volcano is an active volcano in the Cordillera Central of Costa Rica, near the city of Cartago. In Costa Rica it is known as El Coloso (the Colossus) because of the disasters it has caused.
tokens.image_credit: Rafael Golan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rincón de la Vieja Volcano
tokens.description: Rincón de la Vieja is an active andesitic complex volcano in northwestern Costa Rica, about 23 km from Liberia in Guanacaste Province. Its national park is part of the Guanacaste Conservation Area, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Panamá Viejo
tokens.description: Panamá Viejo is the ruined original site of Panama City, the former capital destroyed in 1671 by Henry Morgan. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997, as part of the Historic District of Panamá.
tokens.image_credit: Melpanama · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Casco Viejo, Panama
tokens.description: Casco Viejo, also called Casco Antiguo or San Felipe, is the historic district of Panama City. It was built after the original city of Panamá Viejo was destroyed in 1671 and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Garcia.dennis · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Portobelo
tokens.description: Portobelo is a historic port on the Caribbean coast of Panama, with Spanish colonial fortifications that are part of a UNESCO World Heritage property. The town is the seat of Portobelo District in Colón Province.
tokens.image_credit: en:User:Tedder · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Darién National Park
tokens.description: Darién National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Panama and the most extensive national park in the country. It lies about 325 kilometers from Panama City.

tokens.name: San Blas Islands
tokens.description: The San Blas Islands are an archipelago of about 365 islands and cays off Panama's Caribbean coast, of which 49 are inhabited. They form part of the Guna Yala comarca and are home to the Kuna people.
tokens.image_credit: User:Stan Shebs · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coiba National Park
tokens.description: Coiba National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site off the Pacific coast of Veraguas province, Panama. It covers Coiba, the largest island in Central America, with an area of 494 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Volcán Barú
tokens.description: Volcán Barú is an active stratovolcano and the tallest mountain in Panama, at 3,475 metres. It lies about 35 km from the border with Costa Rica.
tokens.image_credit: Sachagriffin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bocas del Toro Archipelago
tokens.description: The Bocas del Toro Archipelago is a group of tropical islands in the Caribbean Sea in north-west Panama, with coral reefs, mangroves and seagrass meadows. Its main island, Colón Island, holds Bocas Town, capital of Bocas del Toro Province.
tokens.image_credit: Dronepicr · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uxmal
tokens.description: Uxmal is an ancient Maya city of the classical period in the Puuc region of the western Yucatan Peninsula, Mexico. It is considered one of the most important archaeological sites of Maya culture.
tokens.image_credit: Adrian Hernandez · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Calakmul
tokens.description: Calakmul is a Maya archaeological site in the Mexican state of Campeche, deep in the jungles of the Peten Basin region. It was one of the largest and most powerful Maya cities.
tokens.image_credit: PashiX · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mitla
tokens.description: Mitla is the second most important archaeological site in the Mexican state of Oaxaca, after Monte Alban. It is the most important site of the Zapotec culture, in the upper Tlacolula Valley.
tokens.image_credit: User:Gengiskanhg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Tajín
tokens.description: El Tajín is a pre-Columbian archaeological site in Veracruz, Mexico, and one of the largest and most important cities of the Classic era of Mesoamerica. It flourished from 600 to 1200 AD.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph: Frank C. Müller, Baden-Baden · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coba
tokens.description: Coba is an ancient Maya city on the Yucatan Peninsula in Quintana Roo, Mexico. The site holds the largest network of stone causeways of the ancient Maya world.
tokens.image_credit: Ken Thomas · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bonampak
tokens.description: Bonampak is an ancient Maya archaeological site in the Mexican state of Chiapas. It is well known for the murals inside its three-roomed Structure 1, the Temple of the Murals.

tokens.name: Yaxchilan
tokens.description: Yaxchilan is an ancient Maya city on the bank of the Usumacinta River in Chiapas, Mexico. In the Late Classic Period it was one of the most powerful Maya states along the river.

tokens.name: Templo Mayor
tokens.description: The Templo Mayor was the main temple of the Mexica people in their capital Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City. It was dedicated to Huitzilopochtli, god of war, and Tlaloc, god of rain.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chapultepec Castle
tokens.description: Chapultepec Castle stands on Chapultepec Hill at the entrance to Chapultepec Park in Mexico City. Its name comes from the Nahuatl for 'on the hill of the grasshopper'.
tokens.image_credit: Sisgeo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zócalo
tokens.description: Zócalo is the common name of the main square in central Mexico City. Before the Spanish conquest it was the main ceremonial centre of the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan.
tokens.image_credit: Comisión Mexicana de Filmaciones from México D. F., México · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
tokens.description: The Palacio de Bellas Artes is a prominent cultural centre in Mexico City that hosts performing arts events and art exhibitions. It is located on the western side of the historic centre, close to Alameda Central park.
tokens.image_credit: Xavier Quetzalcoatl Contreras Castillo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral
tokens.description: The Metropolitan Cathedral is the cathedral church of the Catholic Archdiocese of Mexico. It stands on the northern side of the Zócalo in Mexico City's historic centre, on the former Aztec sacred precinct.
tokens.image_credit: Ulisesmorales · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
tokens.description: The Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe is a Catholic basilica dedicated to the Virgin Mary, at the foot of the Hill of Tepeyac in Mexico City. Some twenty million pilgrims visit it every year.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Xochimilco
tokens.description: Lake Xochimilco is an ancient endorheic lake in the borough of Xochimilco in southern Mexico City. It is the last remaining habitat of the axolotl.
tokens.image_credit: ProtoplasmaKid · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guanajuato
tokens.description: Guanajuato is a municipality in central Mexico and the capital of the state of Guanajuato. Its historic town and adjacent mines have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos ZGZ · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pico de Orizaba
tokens.description: Pico de Orizaba, also called Citlaltépetl, is a volcano on the border of Veracruz and Puebla states. At 5,636 metres it is the highest mountain in Mexico and the highest volcano in North America.
tokens.image_credit: México en Fotos · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parícutin
tokens.description: Parícutin is a cinder cone volcano in Michoacán state, near Uruapan. It surged from a cornfield in 1943 and gave modern science its first chance to document the full life cycle of this type of eruption.
tokens.image_credit: Karla Yannín Alcázar Quintero (photographer) · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Volcán de Colima
tokens.description: Volcán de Colima, also called Volcán de Fuego, is a 4,260 metre stratovolcano and part of the Colima Volcanic Complex. It is one of the most active volcanoes in Mexico and North America.
tokens.image_credit: Jrobertiko · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sumidero Canyon
tokens.description: Sumidero Canyon is a deep natural canyon just north of Chiapa de Corzo in Chiapas, southern Mexico. Its vertical walls reach as high as 1,000 metres, and the Grijalva River runs through the gorge.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Harenburg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ik Kil
tokens.description: Ik Kil is a cenote outside Pisté in Yucatán, Mexico, near Chichén Itzá. It lies in the Ik Kil Archeological Park and is open to the public for swimming.
tokens.image_credit: Dmadeo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sistema Sac Actun
tokens.description: Sistema Sac Actun is an underwater cave system on the Caribbean coast of the Yucatán Peninsula, with passages north and west of Tulum. As of January 2023 it is the second longest underwater cave system in the world.

tokens.name: Cave of the Crystals
tokens.title: Giant selenite crystals
tokens.description: Cave of the Crystals is a chamber connected to the Naica Mine, about 300 metres deep, in Naica, Chihuahua, Mexico. It holds giant selenite crystals, some of the largest natural crystals ever found.
tokens.image_credit: Alexander Van Driessche · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hierve el Agua
tokens.description: Hierve el Agua is a set of natural travertine rock formations in San Lorenzo Albarradas, Oaxaca, Mexico, about 70 km east of Oaxaca City. The white formations look like frozen waterfalls, built up by mineral-rich fresh springs.
tokens.image_credit: Adrián Cerón · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Agua Azul
tokens.description: Agua Azul is a series of waterfalls on the Xanil River in Chiapas, Mexico, in the municipality of Tumbalá, about 69 km from Palenque. The falls form many cataracts one after another.
tokens.image_credit: Own work · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve
tokens.description: The Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the border of Michoacan and the State of Mexico, about 100 km northwest of Mexico City. It contains most of the overwintering sites of the eastern monarch butterfly population.
tokens.image_credit: Charles J. Sharp · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isla Mujeres
tokens.description: Isla Mujeres is an island about 13 km off the Yucatan Peninsula coast in Quintana Roo, Mexico, where the Gulf of Mexico meets the Caribbean Sea. Its namesake town had 12,642 inhabitants in the 2010 census.
tokens.image_credit: dronepicr · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cozumel
tokens.description: Cozumel is an island and municipality in the Caribbean Sea off the eastern coast of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, opposite Playa del Carmen. It is separated from the mainland by the Cozumel Channel.

tokens.name: Revillagigedo Islands
tokens.description: The Revillagigedo Islands are a group of four volcanic islands in the Pacific Ocean, lying south and southwest of Cabo San Lucas, Baja California. The archipelago is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its unique ecosystem.
tokens.image_credit: Lieutenant Debora Barr, NOAA Corps · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isla Holbox
tokens.description: Holbox is an island in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo, off the north coast of the Yucatan Peninsula. It is about 42 km long and is separated from the mainland by a shallow lagoon.
tokens.image_credit: dronepicr · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Chapala
tokens.description: Lake Chapala is Mexico's largest freshwater lake, bordering the states of Jalisco and Michoacan. It has been the country's largest lake since Lake Texcoco dried up in the early 17th century.

tokens.name: Cabo San Lucas
tokens.description: Cabo San Lucas is a resort city on the southern tip of the Baja California peninsula, in the Mexican state of Baja California Sur. The 2020 Census recorded a population of 202,694.
tokens.image_credit: User:Stan Shebs · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Pinacate y Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve
tokens.description: El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Sonoran Desert of northwest Mexico, just south of the Arizona border. It is managed by the Mexican federal government with the state of Sonora and the Tohono O'odham.
tokens.image_credit: Presidencia de la República Mexicana · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sierra Gorda
tokens.description: Sierra Gorda is an ecological region and mountain range in the northern third of the Mexican state of Queretaro, extending into Guanajuato, Hidalgo and San Luis Potosi. The area is rugged, with high steep mountains and deep canyons.
tokens.aliases: Franciscan Missions in the Sierra Gorda
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Diógenes89 assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taxco
tokens.description: Taxco de Alarcon is a small city in the Mexican state of Guerrero, known for silver mining and for its silver jewelry and silverware crafts. It is the administrative centre of Taxco de Alarcon Municipality.
tokens.image_credit: María Quezada Aranda · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Miguel de Allende
tokens.description: San Miguel de Allende is a city in the Bajio region of the Mexican state of Guanajuato, about 274 km from Mexico City. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Protective Town of San Miguel and the Sanctuary of Jesus Nazareno de Atotonilco.
tokens.image_credit: https://www.flickr.com/photos/jiuguangw/ · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Morelia Cathedral
tokens.description: Morelia Cathedral, formally the Metropolitan Cathedral of Morelia, is the seat of the Archdiocese of Morelia in the capital of the Mexican state of Michoacan. It stands on the first square of the city, within the UNESCO Historic Centre of Morelia.
tokens.image_credit: L. Raul Chavez G. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puebla Cathedral
tokens.description: The Basilica Cathedral of Puebla is the episcopal see of the Archdiocese of Puebla de los Angeles in Mexico. Consecrated in 1649, it stands in the historic centre of Puebla, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuicuilco
tokens.description: Cuicuilco is an archaeological site on the southern shore of Lake Texcoco in Mexico City. Its circular pyramid was begun a few centuries BCE, and the site was destroyed by the eruption of Xitle around 245 to 315 CE.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew T. Bradley · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Pyramid of Cholula
tokens.title: Largest pyramid by volume
tokens.description: The Great Pyramid of Cholula, also called Tlachihualtepetl, is in Cholula, Puebla, Mexico. It is the largest pyramid by volume known in the world, and the largest archaeological site of a pyramid in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Xcaret
tokens.description: Xcaret is a Maya archaeological site on the Caribbean coast of the Yucatan Peninsula in Quintana Roo, Mexico. The site functioned as a Maya port and trading centre, and some of its structures lie within the Xcaret Park tourism development.
tokens.image_credit: AMAPO · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Havana Cathedral
tokens.description: Havana Cathedral, formally the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception of Mary, is the seat of the Archdiocese of San Cristobal de la Habana. It stands on Plaza de la Catedral in Old Havana, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: akasenn · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: National Capitol of Cuba
tokens.description: The National Capitol of Cuba, also known as El Capitolio, is a public edifice in Havana, the capital of Cuba. It was built from 1926 to 1929 under the direction of Eugenio Rayneri Piedra.
tokens.image_credit: Yomangani · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castillo de los Tres Reyes Del Morro
tokens.description: The Castillo de los Tres Reyes del Morro, also called Morro Castle, is a fortress guarding the entrance to Havana harbor. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Old Havana and its Fortification System.
tokens.image_credit: National Photo Company Collection · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cienfuegos
tokens.description: Cienfuegos is a city on the southern coast of Cuba and the capital of Cienfuegos Province. Its Urban Historic Centre was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage property in 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Burkhard Mücke · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca
tokens.description: The Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca is a fortress on the coast of Santiago de Cuba, overlooking the bay. UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site in 1997 as the best preserved example of Spanish-American military architecture.
tokens.image_credit: Glogg, Peter, Switzerland · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Desembarco del Granma National Park
tokens.description: Desembarco del Granma National Park is a national park in south-western Cuba, in Granma Province. Named after the yacht Granma that brought Fidel Castro's group to Cuba in 1956, it was listed by UNESCO in 1999 for its uplifted marine terraces and karst.

tokens.name: Sierra Maestra
tokens.description: The Sierra Maestra is a mountain range running westward across the south of south-eastern Cuba, rising abruptly from the coast. It lies mainly within Santiago de Cuba and Granma Provinces.

tokens.name: Jardines de la Reina
tokens.description: Jardines de la Reina is an archipelago of cays and coral reefs in southern Cuba, in Camagüey and Ciego de Ávila provinces. A marine reserve covering a large part of the archipelago was established in 1996.

tokens.name: Blue Mountains, Jamaica
tokens.description: The Blue Mountains are the longest mountain range in Jamaica. They include Blue Mountain Peak, the island's highest point at 2,256 m (7,402 ft).

tokens.name: Dunn's River Falls
tokens.description: Dunn's River Falls is a famous waterfall near Ocho Rios, Jamaica. It is a well-known visitor site on the island.
tokens.image_credit: Breakyunit at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Port Royal
tokens.description: Port Royal is a small town at the end of the Palisadoes, at the mouth of Kingston Harbour, Jamaica. Founded by the Spanish in 1494, it was destroyed by an earthquake in 1692 and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Sans-Souci Palace
tokens.description: Sans-Souci Palace was the principal royal residence of Henri Christophe, King of Haiti, in Milot. The palace and the neighbouring Citadelle were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1982.
tokens.image_credit: Rémi Kaupp · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alcázar de Colón
tokens.description: The Alcázar de Colón is the first fortified European palace built in the Americas, in the colonial area of Santo Domingo. It was built between 1511 and 1514 and forms part of the Ciudad Colonial UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cathedral of Santo Domingo
tokens.description: The Cathedral of Santo Domingo is the oldest existing cathedral in the Americas, begun in 1504 and completed in 1550. It stands in the Colonial City of Santo Domingo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Georg Karl Ell · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pico Duarte
tokens.description: Pico Duarte is the highest peak in the Dominican Republic and in the Caribbean, at 3,101 m above sea level on Hispaniola. It lies about 85 km northeast of Lake Enriquillo, the region's lowest point.

tokens.name: Lake Enriquillo
tokens.description: Lake Enriquillo is a hypersaline lake in southwestern Dominican Republic. It is the largest lake in both the Dominican Republic and the Caribbean, and its waters are shared by the Bahoruco and Independencia provinces.
tokens.image_credit: Juan Alberto Silver · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Yunque National Forest
tokens.description: El Yunque National Forest is a tropical rainforest in the Sierra de Luquillo, northeast of San Juan, Puerto Rico, managed by the U.S. Forest Service since 1903. It is the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. National Forest System.
tokens.image_credit: Harvey Barrison · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Juan National Historic Site
tokens.description: San Juan National Historic Site preserves the Spanish colonial fortification system of San Juan, Puerto Rico, including the San Felipe del Morro and San Cristobal fortresses. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
tokens.image_credit: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Jmoliver · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puerto Mosquito
tokens.title: Brightest bioluminescent bay
tokens.description: Puerto Mosquito, also called Mosquito Bio Bay, is a bay on the island of Vieques, Puerto Rico. It is famous for the bioluminescence produced by the dinoflagellate Pyrodinium bahamense.

tokens.name: Parque Nacional de las Cavernas del Río Camuy
tokens.description: The Parque Nacional de las Cavernas del Río Camuy is a limestone cave system in northwestern Puerto Rico, carved by the Río Camuy. The park lies between the municipalities of Camuy, Hatillo and Lares.
tokens.image_credit: Per Aspera · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gros Piton
tokens.description: Gros Piton is a volcanic plug of about 798 m in Saint Lucia, one of the two Pitons. The Pitons are a UNESCO World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Petit Piton
tokens.description: Petit Piton is a volcanic plug of about 743 m in Saint Lucia, the smaller of the two Pitons. The Pitons are a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Jayen466 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soufrière Hills
tokens.description: The Soufrière Hills is an active stratovolcano with many lava domes on the Caribbean island of Montserrat, a British overseas territory. It erupted from 1995 to 2010 and last erupted in 2013.
tokens.image_credit: CommonismNow · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Soufrière
tokens.description: La Soufrière is an active volcano on the Caribbean island of Saint Vincent and the highest peak on the island. It has had eight recorded eruptions since 1718, the latest in 2020 and 2021.

tokens.name: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park
tokens.description: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park is a well-preserved fortress on a hill on the island of Saint Kitts. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Ukexpat · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boiling Lake
tokens.description: The Boiling Lake is a flooded fumarole in Morne Trois Pitons National Park on the island of Dominica. It is the second-largest hot lake in the world, after Frying Pan Lake in New Zealand.
tokens.image_credit: Bayukjdr · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Morne Trois Pitons National Park
tokens.description: Morne Trois Pitons National Park is a national park in Dominica, established in July 1975 as the first legally established park in the country. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

tokens.name: Nelson's Dockyard
tokens.description: Nelson's Dockyard is a cultural heritage site and marina in English Harbour on the island of Antigua. It is the only continuously working Georgian era dockyard in the world, built in the early 18th century.
tokens.image_credit: David Stanley · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pitch Lake
tokens.title: World's largest natural asphalt lake
tokens.description: The Pitch Lake is the largest natural deposit of bitumen in the world, estimated to contain 10 million tons. It is located in La Brea in southwest Trinidad.
tokens.image_credit: Martina Jackson · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tobago Cays
tokens.description: The Tobago Cays are an archipelago of five small islands and extensive coral reefs in the Southern Grenadines of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. They form the key element of the Tobago Cays Marine Park.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Schäfer, Lich · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Baths
tokens.description: The Baths is a beach area on Virgin Gorda in the British Virgin Islands, known for its granite boulders and white sand beaches. It is part of The Baths National Park managed by the BVI National Parks Trust.
tokens.image_credit: Calyponte · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belize Barrier Reef
tokens.title: Second largest barrier reef
tokens.description: The Belize Barrier Reef is a series of coral reefs along the coast of Belize, the second largest coral reef system in the world after the Great Barrier Reef. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Bernt Rostad · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Caracol
tokens.description: Caracol is a large ancient Maya archaeological site in the Cayo District of Belize. It lies on the Vaca Plateau in the foothills of the Maya Mountains, about 40 km south of Xunantunich.
tokens.image_credit: Pgbk87 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Xunantunich
tokens.description: Xunantunich is an ancient Maya archaeological site in the Cayo District of western Belize, about 110 km west of Belize City. It sits on a ridge above the Mopan River, within sight of the Guatemala border.
tokens.image_credit: Denis Barthel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Altun Ha
tokens.description: Altun Ha is the ruins of an ancient Maya city in the Belize District of Belize, about 50 km north of Belize City. The site came to the attention of archaeologists only in 1963.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Lazarev (Asmadeus) · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Actun Tunichil Muknal
tokens.description: Actun Tunichil Muknal is a cave near San Ignacio in Belize's Cayo District. It is a Maya archaeological site with ceramics and skeletal remains, including the calcified skeleton known as the Crystal Maiden.
tokens.image_credit: Jkolecki · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bermuda
tokens.title: Bermuda Triangle
tokens.description: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is an archipelago of 181 islands, with the main islands joined by bridges.
tokens.image_credit: Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kata Tjuta
tokens.description: Kata Tjuta is a group of large, domed rock formations about 360 km southwest of Alice Springs in central Australia. It is part of the Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Sterry2607 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nitmiluk National Park
tokens.description: Nitmiluk National Park is in the Northern Territory of Australia, about 23 km northeast of Katherine. It is built around a series of gorges on the Katherine River and Edith Falls, and is of great ceremonial significance to the Jawoyn people.

tokens.name: Karijini National Park
tokens.description: Karijini National Park is centred in the Hamersley Ranges of the Pilbara region in north-western Western Australia. It lies about 1,055 km from Perth, the state capital.
tokens.image_credit: Graeme Churchard from Bristol (51.4414, -2.5242), UK · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Purnululu National Park
tokens.title: Bungle Bungle Range
tokens.description: Purnululu National Park is a World Heritage Site in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia. It was declared a World Heritage Site in 2003 and lies about 300 km south of Kununurra.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Kimberley
tokens.description: The Kimberley is the northernmost of the nine regions of Western Australia. It is bordered by the Indian Ocean to the west, the Timor Sea to the north and the Northern Territory to the east.

tokens.name: Shark Bay
tokens.description: Shark Bay is a World Heritage Site in the Gascoyne region of Western Australia, about 800 kilometres north of Perth. It is known for one of the largest and most diverse seagrass beds in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Paul Harrison · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hamelin Pool Marine Nature Reserve
tokens.title: Stromatolites
tokens.description: Hamelin Pool Marine Nature Reserve is a protected marine nature reserve in the Gascoyne region of Western Australia. It lies within the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Shark Bay.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Kraft · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Three Sisters, Australia
tokens.description: The Three Sisters are an unusual rock formation in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia, on the north escarpment of the Jamison Valley. They are located close to the town of Katoomba.
tokens.image_credit: MrActiniuM · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wineglass Bay
tokens.description: Wineglass Bay lies on the Freycinet Peninsula within Freycinet National Park, on the east coast of Tasmania. The park is about 125 kilometres northeast of Hobart.
tokens.image_credit: aussiejeff from Perth, WA, Australia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area
tokens.description: The Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area is a World Heritage Site in Tasmania, Australia. It covers about 15,800 square kilometres, almost 25 per cent of the island, and is one of the last expanses of temperate wilderness in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ball's Pyramid
tokens.description: Ball's Pyramid is an uninhabited islet in the Pacific Ocean about 20 kilometres southeast of Lord Howe Island, between Australia and New Zealand. It is 572 metres high, making it the tallest volcanic stack in the world.
tokens.image_credit: PotMart186 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Willandra Lakes Region
tokens.description: The Willandra Lakes Region is a World Heritage Site in the Far West region of New South Wales, Australia. It is the traditional meeting place of the Muthi Muthi, Ngiyampaa and Paakantyi Aboriginal peoples.

tokens.name: Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre
tokens.description: Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre, known as Lake Eyre, is an endorheic lake in the Far North region of South Australia, about 700 kilometres north of Adelaide. It is the largest ephemeral endorheic lake on the Australian continent.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/STS-35 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Simpson Desert
tokens.description: The Simpson Desert is a large area of dry, red sandy plain and dunes in the Northern Territory, South Australia and Queensland in central Australia. It is the fourth-largest Australian desert, with an area of 176,500 km2.
tokens.image_credit: User:Phanly (talk) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nullarbor Plain
tokens.description: The Nullarbor Plain is a flat, almost treeless, arid to semi-arid region of southern Australia on the Great Australian Bight coast. It is the world's largest single exposure of limestone bedrock.

tokens.name: Great Victoria Desert
tokens.description: The Great Victoria Desert is a sparsely populated desert ecoregion and interim Australian bioregion in Western Australia and South Australia.

tokens.name: Devils Marbles
