It stands in the Old Town, part of the UNESCO-listed Historic Centre of Kraków.
tokens.image_credit: Zygmunt Put · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Main Square, Kraków
tokens.description: The Main Market Square is a historic square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland, dating back to the 13th century. It is the principal urban space at the centre of the city and is part of the UNESCO-listed Historic Centre of Kraków.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Lascar · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kraków Cloth Hall
tokens.description: The Cloth Hall (Sukiennice) is a Renaissance cloth hall in the centre of the Main Market Square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland. It is one of the city's most recognizable monuments and lies within the UNESCO-listed Historic Centre of Kraków.
tokens.image_credit: DESMS · CC BY-SA 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Auschwitz concentration camp
tokens.description: Auschwitz was a complex of over 40 concentration and extermination camps operated by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland during World War II and the Holocaust. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Silar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malbork Castle
tokens.title: Largest castle by land area
tokens.description: Malbork Castle is a Brick Gothic castle complex of the Teutonic Order in the town of Malbork, Poland, built in the 13th century and expanded in the 14th. It is the largest castle in the world by land area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Gregy · CC BY-SA 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wolf's Lair
tokens.description: The Wolf's Lair was Adolf Hitler's first Eastern Front military headquarters in World War II. It lies in the Masurian woods near Gierłoż in present-day Poland and is now a museum open to the public.

tokens.name: Palace of Culture and Science
tokens.description: The Palace of Culture and Science is a 237-metre high-rise building in central Warsaw, Poland. Completed in 1955, it is the second tallest building in Warsaw and in Poland.
tokens.image_credit: Maciurella · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Łazienki Park
tokens.description: Łazienki Park, or the Royal Baths Park, is the largest park in Warsaw, occupying 76 hectares of the city centre. It is a park-and-palace complex on the Royal Route.
tokens.image_credit: Maksym Kozlenko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gdańsk Crane
tokens.description: The Gdańsk Crane is a 15th-century medieval harbour crane on the Motława river in central Gdańsk, Poland. It was the largest port crane in medieval Europe and is a major tourist attraction.
tokens.image_credit: Marek Mróz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wrocław Town Hall
tokens.description: The Old Town Hall of Wrocław is a Gothic town hall from the 13th century at the centre of the city's Market Square. It is one of the main landmarks of Wrocław, Poland.
tokens.image_credit: Szczecinolog · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Centennial Hall
tokens.description: Centennial Hall is a historic multifunctional hall in Wrocław, Poland, designed by Max Berg and built from 1911 to 1913. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2006.
tokens.image_credit: Jar.ciurus · CC BY-SA 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Medieval Town of Toruń
tokens.description: The Medieval Town of Toruń is the oldest historic district of Toruń, Poland, a small medieval trading city with its original street pattern. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Kapitel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zamość
tokens.description: Zamość is a historic city in southeastern Poland, built as a planned Renaissance town. Its Old City was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1992.
tokens.image_credit: Sylwpak · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Slovincian National Park
tokens.description: The Slovincian National Park, also known as Słowiński National Park, lies on the Baltic coast of northern Poland between Łeba and Rowy. Its northern boundary includes 32.5 kilometres of coastline.

tokens.name: Biebrza National Park
tokens.description: Biebrza National Park is a national park in Podlaskie Voivodeship, northeastern Poland, along the Biebrza River. It is the largest of Poland's 23 national parks, created on 9 September 1993.

tokens.name: Bieszczady National Park
tokens.description: Bieszczady National Park is the third-largest national park in Poland, in Subcarpathian Voivodeship in the extreme southeast of the country. In 2021 it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site as an extension of the Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians.

tokens.name: Rysy
tokens.description: Rysy is a mountain in the High Tatras on the border between Poland and Slovakia. Its north-western summit is the highest point of Poland.

tokens.name: Morskie Oko
tokens.description: Morskie Oko is the largest and fourth-deepest lake in the Tatra Mountains, in southern Poland. It lies in Tatra National Park in the High Tatras, at the base of the Mięguszowiecki Summits.
tokens.image_credit: Aneta Pawska · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Masurian Lake District
tokens.description: The Masurian Lake District is a lake district in northeastern Poland within the region of Masuria. It contains more than 2,000 lakes and was one of the 28 finalists of the New 7 Wonders of Nature.

tokens.name: Crooked Forest
tokens.title: Crooked Forest
tokens.description: The Crooked Forest is a grove of oddly shaped Scots pine trees in the village of Nowe Czarnowo near Gryfino, West Pomerania, Poland. It is a protected natural monument, and the grove of about 400 pines was planted around 1930.
tokens.image_credit: Artur Strzelczyk · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sandomierz
tokens.description: Sandomierz is a historic town in south-eastern Poland, on the Vistula River, with 23,863 inhabitants as of 2017. Its preserved Old Town was declared a National Monument of Poland in 2017.
tokens.image_credit: Jakub Hałun · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kalwaria Zebrzydowska
tokens.description: Kalwaria Zebrzydowska is a town in southern Poland, in Lesser Poland. Its Mannerist Architectural and Park Landscape Complex and Pilgrimage Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1999.
tokens.image_credit: image/photo was taken by Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons user Ludwig Schneider. I would appreciate being notified if you use my work outside Wikimedia. Do not copy this image illegally by ignoring the · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treblinka extermination camp
tokens.description: Treblinka was a Nazi German extermination camp in occupied Poland, the second-deadliest after Auschwitz. It operated from 23 July 1942 to 19 October 1943 as part of Operation Reinhard.
tokens.image_credit: Little Savage · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Westerplatte
tokens.description: Westerplatte is a peninsula at the mouth of the Vistula delta in Gdansk, Poland, on the Baltic coast. The first shots of the Second World War were fired at the Battle of Westerplatte on 1 September 1939.
tokens.image_credit: Virtual-Pano · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
tokens.description: The Hungarian Parliament Building is the seat of the National Assembly of Hungary, on the Pest bank of the Danube in Budapest. Designed by Imre Steindl in neo-Gothic style, it opened in 1902.
tokens.image_credit: Kilyann Le Hen · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fisherman's Bastion
tokens.description: Fisherman's Bastion is a neo-Romanesque terrace and lookout near Buda Castle in Budapest, Hungary. It has been designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987 as part of the Buda Castle District.
tokens.image_credit: Brian Adamson · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matthias Church
tokens.description: Matthias Church is a Catholic church in Holy Trinity Square in the Buda Castle District of Budapest, Hungary. The current building is a late Gothic church built in the second half of the 14th century.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Schäfer, Lich · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heroes' Square
tokens.description: Heroes' Square is one of the major squares in Budapest, Hungary. It is noted for the Millennium Monument, with statues of the seven Magyar chieftains and other Hungarian monarchs and national leaders.
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Széchenyi thermal bath
tokens.description: The Széchenyi Medicinal Bath in Budapest, Hungary, is one of the largest spa complexes in Europe. Its water is supplied by two thermal springs at 74 and 77 degrees Celsius.
tokens.image_credit: Marc Ryckaert (MJJR) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gellért Baths
tokens.description: The Gellért Thermal Bath is a bath complex in Buda, Budapest, part of the historic Hotel Gellért. It lies at the foot of Gellért Hill on the Danube bank.
tokens.image_credit: HartOve · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St. Stephen's Basilica
tokens.description: St. Stephen's Basilica is a Roman Catholic basilica in Budapest, Hungary. It is named in honour of Stephen, the first King of Hungary.
tokens.image_credit: Marc Ryckaert (MJJR) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Esztergom Basilica
tokens.description: The Esztergom Basilica, the Primatial Basilica of the Assumption and St Adalbert, is an ecclesiastic basilica in Esztergom, Hungary. It is the largest church in Hungary.
tokens.image_credit: Pudelek · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hortobágy National Park
tokens.description: Hortobágy National Park is an 800 square kilometre national park on the Great Plain in eastern Hungary. It was designated in 1973 as Hungary's first national park and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.

tokens.name: Lake Balaton
tokens.description: Lake Balaton is a freshwater rift lake in the Transdanubian region of Hungary. It is the largest lake in Central Europe and one of the region's foremost tourist destinations.
tokens.image_credit: txd · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tihany Abbey
tokens.description: Tihany Abbey is a Benedictine monastery established in Tihany, Hungary, in 1055. Its patrons are the Virgin Mary and Saint Aignan of Orleans.
tokens.image_credit: Kapeter77 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pannonhalma Archabbey
tokens.description: Pannonhalma Archabbey is a Benedictine abbey founded in 996 on a hill near the town of Pannonhalma, Hungary. It is one of the oldest historical monuments in Hungary and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eger Castle
tokens.description: Eger Castle is a castle in Eger, Hungary. It is known for repelling the Turkish attack in 1552 during the Siege of Eger.

tokens.name: Baradla Cave
tokens.description: Baradla Cave is a large cave system in northern Hungary, part of the Aggtelek Karst, extending more than 25 km. It belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage site Caves of Aggtelek Karst and Slovak Karst.

tokens.name: Hollókő
tokens.description: Hollókő is a village in Nógrád County, northern Hungary, constructed in the 13th century. It is a well-preserved Palóc ethnographic village inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
tokens.image_credit: Kfbs06 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salzburg Cathedral
tokens.description: Salzburg Cathedral is the seventeenth-century Baroque cathedral of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Salzburg, dedicated to Saint Rupert and Saint Vergilius. It lies in the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Sir James assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grossglockner
tokens.description: The Grossglockner is the highest mountain in Austria, at 3,798 metres. It is part of the Glockner Group in the Hohe Tauern range of the Central Eastern Alps.
tokens.image_credit: DennisPeeters · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Krimml Waterfalls
tokens.description: The Krimml Waterfalls, with a total height of 380 metres, are the highest waterfall in Austria. They fall on the Krimmler Ache near the village of Krimml in the High Tauern National Park, Salzburg state.
tokens.image_credit: Andrew Bossi · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hochosterwitz Castle
tokens.description: Hochosterwitz Castle is a medieval castle on a 172-metre dolomite rock near Sankt Georgen am Längsee in Carinthia, Austria. It is one of the state's landmarks and a major tourist attraction.
tokens.image_credit: C.Stadler/Bwag · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ambras Castle
tokens.description: Ambras Castle is a Renaissance castle and palace in the hills above Innsbruck, Austria, built in the 16th century. It is one of the most popular tourist attractions of Tyrol.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Manu25 at French Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Court Church
tokens.description: The Hofkirche, or Court Church, is a Gothic church in the Old Town of Innsbruck, Austria, built in 1553. It holds the cenotaph of Emperor Maximilian I and the tomb of Andreas Hofer.
tokens.image_credit: Bede735c · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Neusiedl
tokens.description: Lake Neusiedl is a saline endorheic lake straddling the Austria and Hungary border, the largest endorheic lake in Central and Western Europe. It covers about 315 square kilometres and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape.

tokens.name: Mauthausen concentration camp
tokens.description: Mauthausen concentration camp was a Nazi concentration camp on a hill above the market town of Mauthausen in Upper Austria, established in 1938. It was the main camp of a group of nearly 100 subcamps across Austria and southern Germany.

tokens.name: Hohenschwangau Castle
tokens.description: Hohenschwangau Castle is a 19th-century palace in southwestern Bavaria, Germany, near the town of Füssen. King Maximilian II of Bavaria built it, and it was the childhood residence of his son, King Ludwig II.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Linderhof Palace
tokens.description: Linderhof Palace is a palace in southwest Bavaria, Germany, about 10 km west of the village of Ettal. It is the smallest of the three palaces built by King Ludwig II of Bavaria, and the only one he completed.
tokens.image_credit: Softeis · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Herrenchiemsee
tokens.description: Herrenchiemsee is a complex of royal buildings on Herreninsel, the largest island in the Chiemsee lake in southern Bavaria, Germany. King Ludwig II of Bavaria bought the island in 1873, and the palaces are part of a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Michimaya · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Berlin Cathedral
tokens.description: Berlin Cathedral is a monumental Protestant church and dynastic tomb of the House of Hohenzollern, at the Lustgarten on Museum Island in central Berlin. The present collegiate church was built from 1894 to 1905 to plans by Julius Raschdorff.
tokens.image_credit: Ansgar Koreng · CC BY 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Charlottenburg Palace
tokens.description: Charlottenburg Palace is a Baroque palace in Berlin, built at the end of the 17th century and greatly expanded in the 18th century, mainly for Frederick the Great. It is among the largest palaces in the world.
tokens.image_credit: abbilder · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
tokens.description: The Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe is a memorial in Berlin to the Jewish victims of the Holocaust, designed by Peter Eisenman. It consists of 2,711 concrete stelae arranged in a grid on a sloping 1.9-hectare site.
tokens.image_credit: NoRud · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Theresienwiese
tokens.title: World's largest beer festival
tokens.description: Theresienwiese is a 42-hectare public space in Munich, best known as the site of the annual Oktoberfest. The grounds also hold a memorial to the victims of the 1980 Oktoberfest bombing.
tokens.image_credit: Usien · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hohenzollern Castle
tokens.description: Hohenzollern Castle is the ancestral seat of the formerly imperial House of Hohenzollern. It is the third hilltop castle built on Mount Hohenzollern, near Hechingen in Baden-Württemberg.
tokens.image_credit: A. Kniesel (= User:-donald-), Lauffen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Speyer Cathedral
tokens.description: Speyer Cathedral, officially the Imperial Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption and St Stephen, is a historical religious building in Speyer, Germany. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Gerd Eichmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trier
tokens.description: Trier is a city on the banks of the Moselle in western Germany, founded by the Romans as Augusta Treverorum. Its Roman monuments, cathedral and Church of Our Lady form a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Wolkenkratzer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Porta Nigra
tokens.description: The Porta Nigra is a large Roman city gate in Trier, Germany. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, as part of the Roman monuments of Trier.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Würzburg Residence
tokens.description: The Würzburg Residence is a Baroque palace in Würzburg, Germany, commissioned in 1720 by the Prince-Bishop of Würzburg and completed in 1744. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site, with its court gardens and residence square.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bamberg
tokens.description: Bamberg is a town in Upper Franconia, Bavaria, on the river Regnitz near its confluence with the Main. Its historic town is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 1993.
tokens.image_credit: Immanuel Giel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Albrechtsburg
tokens.description: The Albrechtsburg is a Late Gothic castle built from 1471 to about 1495. It stands on a hill above the Elbe in the centre of Meissen, Saxony, beside Meissen Cathedral.
tokens.image_credit: Stephan Hoppe · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Holsten Gate
tokens.description: The Holsten Gate (Holstentor) is a 15th-century brick Gothic city gate marking the western boundary of the old centre of Lübeck. It is one of two surviving city gates and a symbol of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Glenn Strong [1] [2] · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moselle
tokens.description: The Moselle is a river that rises in the Vosges mountains and flows through France, Luxembourg and western Germany. It joins the Rhine at Koblenz, at the Deutsches Eck promontory.
tokens.image_credit: Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eltz Castle
tokens.description: Eltz Castle is a medieval castle in the hills above the Moselle between Koblenz and Trier, Germany. It has been owned by a branch of the House of Eltz since the 12th century and has never been destroyed.
tokens.image_credit: kaʁstn Disk/Cat · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hohenneuffen Castle
tokens.description: Hohenneuffen Castle is a large ruined castle in the northern foothills of the Swabian Alb. It stands above the town of Neuffen in the district of Esslingen, Baden-Württemberg.
tokens.image_credit: Dr. Eugen Lehle · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lichtenstein Castle
tokens.description: Lichtenstein Castle is a privately owned Gothic Revival castle in the Swabian Jura, designed by Carl Alexander Heideloff. It overlooks the Echaz valley near Honau, Reutlingen, in Baden-Württemberg, Germany.
tokens.image_credit: -donald- · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saxon Switzerland National Park
tokens.description: Saxon Switzerland National Park is a national park in the German state of Saxony, near Dresden. It covers two areas of 93.5 km2 in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains and adjoins the Bohemian Switzerland National Park in the Czech Republic.

tokens.name: Bastei
tokens.description: The Bastei is a rock formation rising 194 metres above the Elbe River in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains of Germany. It is the major landmark of Saxon Switzerland National Park, near Rathen southeast of Dresden.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Berchtesgaden National Park
tokens.description: Berchtesgaden National Park is in Bavaria on the Austrian border, established in 1978 to protect the Berchtesgaden Alps. It is the only German national park in the Alps and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 1990.

tokens.name: Obersalzberg
tokens.description: Obersalzberg is a mountainside retreat above the market town of Berchtesgaden in Bavaria, Germany. It is best known as the site of Adolf Hitler's former mountain residence, the Berghof, and of the Kehlsteinhaus.

tokens.name: Kehlsteinhaus
tokens.description: The Kehlsteinhaus, known in English as the Eagle's Nest, is a Nazi-era chalet on the Kehlstein above Obersalzberg near Berchtesgaden. It was completed in 1938 and commissioned by Martin Bormann for Adolf Hitler.
tokens.image_credit: Mdavids · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nuremberg Castle
tokens.description: Nuremberg Castle is a group of medieval fortified buildings on a sandstone ridge dominating the historic centre of Nuremberg, Bavaria. Together with the city walls it is considered one of Europe's most formidable medieval fortifications.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was AlterVista at German Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nazi Party rally grounds
tokens.description: The Nazi Party rally grounds is a complex of megastructures and clearings covering about 11 square kilometres southeast of Nuremberg, Germany. Six Nazi Party rallies were held there between 1933 and 1938.
tokens.image_credit: Derzno · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Messel Pit
tokens.description: The Messel Pit is a fossil preservation site in Hesse, Germany, dating from the Eocene epoch, about 47 million years ago. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

tokens.name: Externsteine
tokens.description: The Externsteine are a distinctive sandstone rock formation in the Teutoburg Forest near Horn-Bad Meinberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. The tor's tall rock columns rise abruptly from the wooded hills, and the Hermannsweg trail passes through it.
tokens.image_credit: Tuxyso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hermannsdenkmal
tokens.description: The Hermann Memorial is a monument southwest of Detmold in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It stands on the forested Grotenburg hill in the Teutoburg Forest, inside the remains of a circular rampart.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bavaria statue
tokens.description: Bavaria is a monumental bronze sand-cast statue from the 19th century in Munich, Germany. It is a female personification of the Bavarian homeland and forms an ensemble with the Ruhmeshalle hall of fame and a stairway.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Walhalla
tokens.description: Walhalla is a hall of fame monument in Bavaria, Germany, that honours distinguished people of the German-speaking world. The memorial is named for the Valhalla of Norse paganism.
tokens.image_credit: Wolfgang Pehlemann · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Magdeburg Cathedral
tokens.description: Magdeburg Cathedral, officially the Cathedral of Saints Maurice and Catherine, is a Lutheran cathedral in Magdeburg, Germany. It is the oldest Gothic cathedral in the country and the proto-cathedral of the former Prince-Archbishopric of Magdeburg.
tokens.image_credit: Jjjjjjjjcross · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Naumburg Cathedral
tokens.description: Naumburg Cathedral, officially St Peter and St Paul, is the former cathedral of the Bishopric of Naumburg-Zeitz in Naumburg, Germany. The Wikipedia heritage record lists it as a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Necrophorus at German Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: All Saints' Church, Wittenberg
tokens.description: All Saints' Church, commonly called the Schlosskirche (Castle Church), is a Lutheran church in Wittenberg, Germany. It is the site where, according to Philip Melanchthon, Martin Luther posted the Ninety-five Theses in 1517.
tokens.image_credit: Horst Pomplun · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jungfrau
tokens.description: The Jungfrau is a 4,158 m summit of the Bernese Alps, lying between the cantons of Bern and Valais. Its summit was first reached on 3 August 1811.
tokens.image_credit: Earth explorer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mönch
tokens.description: The Mönch is a 4,110 m mountain in the Bernese Alps, on the border between the cantons of Valais and Bern. It forms a recognisable group with the Eiger and the Jungfrau.
tokens.image_credit: Christian David · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lauterbrunnen Valley
tokens.description: The Lauterbrunnen Valley is a glacial valley in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland. The municipality of Lauterbrunnen includes the villages of Wengen, Mürren, Gimmelwald, Stechelberg and Isenfluh.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trümmelbach Falls
tokens.description: Trümmelbach Falls are a series of ten waterfalls inside a mountain in the Lauterbrunnen Valley of the Bernese Oberland, Switzerland. The stream descends about 140 metres through the mountain.

tokens.name: Pilatus
tokens.description: Pilatus is a mountain massif overlooking Lucerne in central Switzerland. Its highest peak, the Tomlishorn, rises to 2,128.5 m.
tokens.image_credit: Liridon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gotthard Pass
tokens.description: The Gotthard Pass is a mountain pass at 2,106 m in the Swiss Alps, connecting northern and southern Switzerland. It lies between Airolo in Ticino and Andermatt in Uri.

tokens.name: Swiss National Park
tokens.description: The Swiss National Park lies in the Western Rhaetian Alps in the canton of Graubünden, in the Engadin valley. Founded in 1914, it is the oldest national park in the Alps and in Central Europe.

tokens.name: Abbey of Saint Gall
tokens.description: The Abbey of Saint Gall was a monastic abbey from 747 until its dissolution in 1805. Its religious complex in the city of St. Gallen, Switzerland, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Old City of Bern
tokens.description: The Old City is the medieval centre of Bern, Switzerland, built on a narrow hill bordered on three sides by the Aare. Its compact layout has remained essentially unchanged since construction in the 12th to 15th centuries.
tokens.image_credit: Franz Schmid · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zytglogge
tokens.description: The Zytglogge is a medieval clock tower in Bern, Switzerland, built in the early 13th century. It served as a guard tower, prison and clock tower, and is known for its 15th-century astronomical clock.
tokens.image_credit: Mike Lehmann, Mike Switzerland 13:37, 2 July 2006 (UTC) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Basel Minster
tokens.description: Basel Minster is a religious building in Basel, Switzerland, originally a Roman Catholic cathedral and today a Reformed Protestant church. The original cathedral was built between 1019 and 1500 in Romanesque and Gothic styles.
tokens.image_credit: Wladyslaw Sojka · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grossmünster
tokens.description: The Grossmünster is a Romanesque-style Swiss Reformed church in Zurich, Switzerland. It is one of the four major churches of the city, along with the Fraumünster, Predigerkirche and St. Peterskirche.
tokens.image_credit: Roland zh · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castles of Bellinzona
tokens.description: The Castles of Bellinzona are a group of fortifications around the town of Bellinzona, capital of the Swiss canton of Ticino. The group comprises fortified walls and three castles: Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Berger · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Creux du Van
tokens.description: The Creux du Van is a natural rocky cirque about 1,400 metres wide and 150 metres deep, in the Val de Travers district of the Swiss canton of Neuchâtel. It is a well known amphitheatre-shaped attraction in a 15.5 km2 nature reserve.

tokens.name: Contra Dam
tokens.description: The Contra Dam, also known as the Verzasca Dam, is an arch dam on the Verzasca River in Ticino, Switzerland. It was built between 1961 and 1965 and supports the 105 MW Verzasca hydroelectric power station.
tokens.image_credit: Audrix · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Stanley
tokens.title: Highest peak of the Rwenzori
tokens.description: Mount Stanley is a mountain in the Rwenzori range. At 5,109 m it is the highest mountain of both the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, and the fourth-highest in Africa.
tokens.image_credit: El.Sarmiento · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nyamuragira
tokens.description: Nyamuragira, also known as Nyamulagira, is an active shield volcano in the Virunga Mountains of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, about 25 km north of Lake Kivu. It has erupted over 40 times since 1885.
tokens.image_credit: MONUSCO Photos · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ras Dashen
tokens.description: Ras Dashen is the highest mountain in Ethiopia, reaching 4,550 metres. It lies in the Simien Mountains National Park in the Amhara Region.

tokens.name: Church of Saint George, Lalibela
tokens.title: Cross-shaped rock-hewn church
tokens.description: The Church of Saint George is one of eleven rock-hewn monolithic churches in Lalibela, a town in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia. The site is named after King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela of the Zagwe dynasty, who is regarded as a saint.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ruins of Gedi
tokens.description: The Ruins of Gedi are a UNESCO World Heritage site near the Indian Ocean coast of eastern Kenya. They are the remains of a medieval Swahili coastal settlement within the Arabuko-Sokoke Forest.
tokens.image_credit: Mgiganteus · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kahuzi-Biéga National Park
tokens.description: Kahuzi-Biega National Park is a protected area near Bukavu in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, close to the western bank of Lake Kivu. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

tokens.name: Okapi Wildlife Reserve
tokens.description: The Okapi Wildlife Reserve is a wildlife reserve in the Ituri Forest in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, near the borders with South Sudan and Uganda. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.

tokens.name: Boyoma Falls
tokens.description: Boyoma Falls, formerly Stanley Falls, is a series of seven cataracts along more than 100 km of the Lualaba River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. They form the largest waterfall by volume of annual flow in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Ad Meskens · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brandberg Mountain
tokens.description: The Brandberg is Namibia's highest mountain. Its Damara name is Dâures and its Otjiherero name is Omukuruvaro.

tokens.name: Khami
tokens.description: Khami is a ruined city about 22 km west of Bulawayo in Zimbabwe. It was the capital of the Kingdom of Butua under the Torwa dynasty and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.
tokens.image_credit: Digr · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matobo National Park
tokens.description: Matobo National Park forms the core of the Matobo Hills, an area of granite kopjes and wooded valleys about 35 km south of Bulawayo, Zimbabwe. The wider Matobo Hills have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003.

tokens.name: Augrabies Falls
tokens.description: Augrabies Falls is a waterfall about 56 metres high on the Orange River, the largest river in South Africa. The falls have been enclosed by Augrabies Falls National Park since 1966.
tokens.image_credit: Zaian (talk). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castle of Good Hope
tokens.description: The Castle of Good Hope is a 17th century bastion fort in Cape Town, South Africa. It is considered the best preserved example of a Dutch East India Company fort.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lion's Head
tokens.description: Lion's Head is a 669 metre mountain in Cape Town, South Africa, between Table Mountain and Signal Hill. It forms part of Table Mountain National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Hansueli Krapf This file was uploaded with Commonist. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maletsunyane Falls
tokens.description: Maletsunyane Falls is a 192 metre high waterfall in Lesotho, near the town of Semonkong. It falls from a ledge of Triassic-Jurassic basalt on the Maletsunyane River.
tokens.image_credit: BagelBelt · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thabana Ntlenyana
tokens.description: Thabana Ntlenyana is the highest mountain in southern Africa, standing 3,482 metres tall. It lies within the Maloti Mountains that crest Lesotho.

tokens.name: Vallée de Mai
tokens.title: Coco de mer forest
tokens.description: Vallée de Mai is a palm forest nature reserve on Praslin island in the Seychelles, home to the endemic coco de mer. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

tokens.name: Piton des Neiges
tokens.description: Piton des Neiges is a 3,069 m complex volcano on Réunion in the Indian Ocean. It is the highest point on the island and is considered the highest point in the Indian Ocean.
tokens.image_credit: Dunog · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Niokolo-Koba National Park
tokens.description: Niokolo-Koba National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and natural protected area in southeastern Senegal, near the Guinea border. It is served by Niokolo-Koba Airport, an unpaved airstrip.

tokens.name: Larabanga Mosque
tokens.description: The Larabanga Mosque is a mosque built in the Sudanese style in Larabanga village, Savanna Region of Ghana. It is the oldest mosque in the country, first built in 1421 CE and most recently restored in 2023.
tokens.image_credit: Sathyan Velumani · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sukur Cultural Landscape
tokens.description: The Sukur Cultural Landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on a hill above Sukur village in Adamawa State, Nigeria, in the Mandara Mountains near the Cameroon border. Its inscription is based on cultural heritage, material culture and naturally terraced fields.

tokens.name: Ruins of Loropéni
tokens.description: The Ruins of Loropéni are a medieval stone heritage site near the town of Loropéni in southern Burkina Faso. They were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2009 and were the country's first World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Rik Schuiling / TropCrop-TCS · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bunce Island
tokens.description: Bunce Island is an island in the Sierra Leone River, about 32 kilometres upriver from Freetown. It houses a castle built by the Royal Africa Company in about 1670.
tokens.image_credit: Joseph Corry · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ouadane
tokens.description: Ouadane is a small town in the desert of central Mauritania, on the southern edge of the Adrar Plateau. Its old town, now in ruins, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and was a staging post in the trans-Saharan trade.
tokens.image_credit: Clemens Schmillen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kunta Kinteh Island
tokens.description: Kunta Kinteh Island, formerly James Island, lies in the Gambia River near Juffureh and carries the ruins of Fort James. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites, inscribed in 2003.

tokens.name: Tipaza
tokens.description: Tipaza is the capital of Tipaza Province on the Algerian coast, called Tipasa in Roman times. Its Phoenician, Roman and Byzantine ruins form the UNESCO World Heritage Site Tipasa, inscribed in 1982.

tokens.name: Casbah of Algiers
tokens.description: The Casbah of Algiers is the old town, or medina, of Algiers, founded in 944 by the Zirids. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992.

tokens.name: Waw an Namus
tokens.description: Waw an Namus is a volcano in the eastern Fezzan region of Libya, of Pleistocene or Holocene age. The origin of its volcanism, and that of Al Haruj farther north, is not clear.
tokens.image_credit: StFr · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Emi Koussi
tokens.description: Emi Koussi is a high pyroclastic shield volcano at the southeast end of the Tibesti Mountains in northern Chad. It is the highest mountain of the Sahara, rising to 3,447 metres.

tokens.name: Ennedi Plateau
tokens.description: The Ennedi Plateau is a sandstone massif in the northeast of Chad, in the middle of the Sahara, shaped by wind and temperature erosion. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2016 as the Ennedi Massif: Natural and Cultural Landscape.

tokens.name: Old Dongola
tokens.description: Old Dongola is a deserted Nubian town on the east bank of the Nile in Northern State, Sudan. It was the capital of the medieval Makurian state and a departure point for caravans to Darfur and Kordofan.

tokens.name: Suakin
tokens.description: Suakin is a port city on the west coast of the Red Sea in northeastern Sudan, formerly the region's chief port. Its old city, built of coral, is now in ruins, and Port Sudan about 50 km north is the main port.
tokens.image_credit: Bertramz · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kerkouane
tokens.description: Kerkouane is the site of an ancient Punic city near Cape Bon in northeastern Tunisia, probably abandoned during the First Punic War around 250 BC. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site as the Punic Town of Kerkouane and its Necropolis.
tokens.image_credit: CarlesVA on ca.wikipedia or eo.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Todgha Gorge
tokens.description: The Todgha Gorges are limestone river canyons in the eastern High Atlas Mountains of Morocco, near the town of Tinghir. The Todgha and Dades rivers carved their cliff-sided walls, up to 400 metres high, over the last 40 km of their course through the mountains.

tokens.name: Laas Geel
tokens.title: Neolithic cave paintings
tokens.description: Laas Geel is a group of cave formations on the outskirts of Hargeisa in Somaliland, with some of the earliest known cave paintings of domesticated aurochs in the Horn of Africa. The rock art is estimated at about 5,500 to 4,500 years old.

tokens.name: M'banza-Kongo
tokens.description: M'banza-Kongo is the capital of Angola's northwestern Zaire Province, and was the capital of the Kingdom of Kongo from its foundation until the kingdom was abolished in 1915. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017.

tokens.name: Po-i-Kalyan
tokens.description: Po-i-Kalan is an Islamic religious complex in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, made up of the Kalan Mosque, the Kalan Minaret and the Mir-i-Arab Madrasah. The complex is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Historic Centre of Bukhara, inscribed in 1993.
tokens.image_credit: Fulvio Spada from Torino, Italy · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Samanid Mausoleum
tokens.description: The Samanid Mausoleum is a 10th-century mausoleum in northwestern Bukhara, Uzbekistan, built as the resting place of the Samanid dynasty. It is considered one of the iconic examples of early Islamic architecture and the oldest funerary building of Central Asian architecture.
tokens.image_credit: Hylgeriak / Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ulugh Beg Observatory
tokens.description: The Ulugh Beg Observatory is an astronomical observatory in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, built in the 1420s by the Timurid astronomer Ulugh Beg. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Samarkand, Crossroads of Cultures.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Kaindy
tokens.title: Sunken forest lake
tokens.description: Lake Kaindy is a lake in Kazakhstan about 400 metres long, located 129 kilometres east-southeast of Almaty at about 2,000 metres above sea level. It reaches depths of nearly 30 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Jonas Satkauskas · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tanbaly
tokens.description: Tanbaly, also spelled Tamgaly, is a petroglyph site in the Zhetysu region of Kazakhstan, about 170 km by road northwest of Almaty. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004.

tokens.name: Tash Rabat
tokens.title: Silk Road caravanserai
tokens.description: Tash Rabat is a well-preserved stone caravanserai in At-Bashy District, Naryn Province, Kyrgyzstan, at an altitude of 3,200 metres. It is dated to the 10th or 15th century.
tokens.image_credit: Firespeaker · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Burana Tower
tokens.description: Burana Tower is a large minaret in the Chuy Valley of northern Kyrgyzstan, about 80 km east of Bishkek near Tokmok. It is all that remains of the ancient city of Balasagun, founded by the Karakhanids at the end of the 9th century.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lenin Peak
tokens.description: Lenin Peak, also called Ibn Sina Peak, is a mountain in the Trans-Alay Range of the Pamir Mountains on the Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border. At 7,134 metres, it is the second-highest point of both countries.

tokens.name: Sarez Lake
tokens.description: Sarez Lake is a lake in Rushon District of Gorno-Badakhshan province, Tajikistan. It is about 75.8 km long and holds over 16 cubic km of water.

tokens.name: Konye-Urgench
tokens.description: Konye-Urgench is a city in north Turkmenistan, on the Uzbek border. It is the site of the ancient town of Gurganj and the ruins of the capital of Khwarazm, a UNESCO World Heritage property since 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Tim Williams · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves
tokens.description: The Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves are Buddhist cave grottos cut into cliffs of the Mutou Valley in the Flaming Mountains, Xinjiang, China. Most surviving caves date from the West Uyghur kingdom, about the 10th to 13th centuries.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 2.5 es · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Id Kah Mosque
tokens.description: The Id Kah Mosque is a mosque in Kashgar, Xinjiang, China. With room for about 20,000 worshippers inside the mosque and its sahn, it is the largest mosque in China.
tokens.image_credit: N509FZ · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Muztagh Ata
tokens.description: Muztagh Ata is a 7,546 m mountain on the northern edge of the Tibetan Plateau, in Xinjiang, China. It is one of the relatively easier 7,000 m peaks in the world to climb.

tokens.name: Maiden Tower
tokens.description: The Maiden Tower is a 12th-century monument in the Old City of Baku, Azerbaijan, and a national emblem shown on banknotes. It forms a group of historic monuments with the Shirvanshahs' Palace, listed by UNESCO.
tokens.image_credit: Ludvig14 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chiribiquete National Park
tokens.description: Chiribiquete National Natural Park is the largest national park in Colombia and the largest tropical rainforest national park in the world. Established in 1989, it covers about 43,000 km2 of tropical moist forest, savannas and rivers.

tokens.name: Isabela Island
tokens.description: Isabela Island is the largest of the Galápagos Islands, with an area of 4,586 km2, and it straddles the equator. It is part of the Galápagos Islands UNESCO World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Chavín de Huántar
tokens.description: Chavín de Huántar is an archaeological site in the Ancash Region of Peru, with ruins constructed as early as 1200 BC by the Chavín culture. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Apollo⠀ · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Huaca Pucllana
tokens.description: Huaca Pucllana is a large adobe and clay pyramid in the Miraflores district of central Lima, Peru. It was a ceremonial and administrative centre of the Lima culture, which developed between about 200 AD and 700 AD.
tokens.image_credit: McKay Savage · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Illimani
tokens.description: Illimani is a prominent fold mountain in the Cordillera Real of Bolivia, about 82 km southeast of La Paz. At 6,438 metres it is the highest mountain in the Cordillera Real and the second-highest in Bolivia.
tokens.image_credit: Senorhorst Jahnsen · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Churches of Chiloé
tokens.description: The Churches of Chiloé are wooden churches built in native timber and wood shingles on Chile's Chiloé Archipelago, designed to resist its humid oceanic climate. They are a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works
tokens.description: Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works are two former saltpeter refineries in northern Chile. They were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005, as a testament to the history of saltpeter mining.
tokens.image_credit: rewbs.soal · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Robinson Crusoe Island
tokens.description: Robinson Crusoe Island is the second largest of the Juan Fernández Islands, about 670 km west of San Antonio, Chile, in the South Pacific Ocean. Most of its population lives in the town of San Juan Bautista at Cumberland Bay.

tokens.name: San Ignacio Miní
tokens.description: San Ignacio Miní is one of the Jesuit missions founded in 1610 in present-day Misiones Province, Argentina. It is one of four Argentine Jesuit missions designated UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1984.
tokens.image_credit: Fernando · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nahuel Huapi Lake
tokens.description: Nahuel Huapi Lake is an Andean lake in northern Patagonia, between the Argentine provinces of Río Negro and Neuquén. The town of Villa La Angostura lies on its northwestern shore.

tokens.name: Pico da Neblina
tokens.description: Pico da Neblina is the highest mountain in Brazil, at 2,995.30 metres above sea level. It rises in the Serra da Neblina of northwestern Amazonas, near the southern edge of the Guiana Highlands.

tokens.name: Serra da Capivara National Park
tokens.description: Serra da Capivara National Park is in northeastern Brazil and contains many prehistoric paintings. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

tokens.name: Devil's Island
tokens.title: Notorious penal colony
tokens.description: Devil's Island is in the Salvation Islands off French Guiana. It housed the Cayenne penal colony, which operated from 1852 to 1952 and officially closed in 1953.

tokens.name: K'gari
tokens.title: Largest sand island
tokens.description: K'gari, also known as Fraser Island, is a sand island on the south-eastern coast of Queensland, Australia. The island and its surrounding waters are part of a World Heritage listing.

tokens.name: Wilpena Pound
tokens.description: Wilpena Pound is a natural amphitheatre of mountains in the Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park, South Australia. It lies about 429 km north of Adelaide.

tokens.name: Jenolan Caves
tokens.description: The Jenolan Caves are limestone caves in the Jenolan Karst Conservation Reserve in New South Wales, Australia, about 175 km west of Sydney. The article describes them as the oldest known and dated open cave system in the world.

tokens.name: Horizontal Falls
tokens.description: The Horizontal Falls are a natural phenomenon on the Kimberley coast of Western Australia, where tidal flows cause waterfalls on the ebb and flow of each tide. They lie within the Lalang-garram / Horizontal Falls Marine Park.
tokens.image_credit: Reefpix · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Waiotapu
tokens.description: Waiotapu is an active geothermal area in the Taupo Volcanic Zone, 27 km south of Rotorua, New Zealand. It is known for coloured hot springs, the Lady Knox Geyser, the Champagne Pool and boiling mud pools.
tokens.image_credit: Christian Mehlführer, User:Chmehl · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tāne Mahuta
tokens.title: Giant kauri tree
tokens.description: Tāne Mahuta, also called the God of the Forest, is a giant kauri tree in the Waipoua Forest of Northland, New Zealand. It is estimated to be between 1,250 and 2,500 years old and is the largest living kauri known to stand.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rock Islands
tokens.description: The Rock Islands of Palau are several hundred small limestone and coral islands in the Southern Lagoon between Koror and Peleliu. They were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.
tokens.image_credit: Luka Peternel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tavurvur
tokens.description: Tavurvur is an active stratovolcano near Rabaul on the island of New Britain, Papua New Guinea. It is a sub-vent of the Rabaul caldera, and an eruption in 1994 largely destroyed the nearby town of Rabaul.
tokens.image_credit: Taro Taylor · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Levuka
tokens.description: Levuka is a town on the east coast of Ovalau island in Fiji, and was the capital of Fiji before 1877. Its Historical Port Town was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2013.
tokens.image_credit: Anton Leddin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: East Rennell
tokens.description: East Rennell is the southern part of Rennell Island in the Solomon Islands, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Rennell is the largest raised coral atoll in the world, and the area around Lake Tegano has many endemic species.

tokens.name: Niue
tokens.description: Niue is a self-governing island country in the South Pacific Ocean, in Polynesia. It is in free association with New Zealand, and its population is predominantly Polynesian.

tokens.name: Mauna Kea
tokens.title: Astronomy's top mountain
tokens.description: Mauna Kea is a dormant shield volcano on the island of Hawaii. Its peak, 4,207.3 metres above sea level, is the highest point in Hawaii.
tokens.image_credit: Vadim Kurland · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haleakalā
tokens.title: Maui summit observatory
tokens.description: Haleakalā, also called the East Maui Volcano, is a massive active shield volcano that forms more than 75% of the Hawaiian island of Maui. Its tallest peak, Puʻu ʻUlaʻula, rises to 3,055 metres.

tokens.name: ʻIolani Palace
tokens.description: ʻIolani Palace was the royal residence of the rulers of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi from 1845 to 1893. It stands in the capitol district of downtown Honolulu and is a National Historic Landmark.
tokens.image_credit: Gage Skidmore from Surprise, AZ, United States of America · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Norfolk Island
tokens.description: Norfolk Island is an external territory of Australia in the Pacific Ocean, between New Zealand and New Caledonia. At the 2021 census it had 2,188 inhabitants on about 35 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Lake Bosumtwi
tokens.title: Meteorite crater lake
tokens.description: Lake Bosumtwi is the only natural lake in Ghana. It lies in an ancient impact crater about 10.5 kilometres in diameter, roughly 30 km south-east of Kumasi.

tokens.name: Dzanga-Sangha Special Reserve
tokens.description: The Dzanga-Sangha Special Reserve is a protected area of tropical rainforest in southwestern Central African Republic, covering 6,865.54 square kilometres. It is one of three protected areas that form the Sangha Trinational.

tokens.name: Garamba National Park
tokens.description: Garamba National Park is a national park in the north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, covering nearly 5,200 square kilometres. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

tokens.name: Mount Elgon
tokens.description: Mount Elgon is an extinct shield volcano on the border of Uganda and Kenya. Its highest point, Wagagai, lies entirely within Uganda, and it is at least 24 million years old.

tokens.name: Kibale National Park
tokens.description: Kibale National Park is a national park in western Uganda that protects moist evergreen rainforest. It covers 766 km2 and ranges between 1,100 m and 1,600 m in elevation.

tokens.name: Lake Albert
tokens.description: Lake Albert is a lake shared by Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is Africa's sixth-largest lake and the second biggest of Uganda's Great Lakes.

tokens.name: Lake Naivasha
tokens.description: Lake Naivasha is a freshwater lake in Kenya's Great Rift Valley, north west of Nairobi. Its name comes from the Maasai name for bodies of water large enough to have wave action.

tokens.name: Kakamega Forest
tokens.description: Kakamega Forest is a tropical rainforest in western Kenya, near the Ugandan border. It is said to be Kenya's only tropical rainforest and the last remnant of the ancient Guineo-Congolian rainforest.

tokens.name: Kondoa Rock-Art Sites
tokens.description: The Kondoa Rock-Art Sites are ancient paintings on rockshelter walls in central Tanzania. The Kondoa region was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2006 for its rock art.

tokens.name: Yeha
tokens.description: Yeha is a town in the Central Zone of Tigray in northern Ethiopia, with the ruins of a pre-Aksumite temple. It likely served as the capital of the pre-Aksumite kingdom of Dʿmt.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nuri
tokens.description: Nuri is an ancient Nubian necropolis in northern Sudan on the west side of the Nile, near the Fourth Cataract. It dates back to the Napata period.
tokens.image_credit: Hans Birger Nilsen · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Naqa
tokens.description: Naqa is a ruined ancient city of the Kushite Kingdom of Meroe in Sudan. It lies about 170 km north-east of Khartoum, about 50 km east of the Nile.
tokens.image_credit: User:LassiHU · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gilf Kebir
tokens.description: Gilf Kebir is a plateau in the New Valley Governorate in the remote south-west corner of Egypt, extending into south-east Libya. Its name translates as the Great Barrier.

tokens.name: Cave of Swimmers
tokens.description: The Cave of Swimmers is a rock shelter with ancient rock art in the Gilf Kebir plateau of the Libyan Desert. It lies in the New Valley Governorate of south-west Egypt, near the Libyan border.

tokens.name: Faiyum Oasis
tokens.description: The Faiyum Oasis is a depression in the desert immediately west of the Nile, about 62 miles south of Cairo. Its basin floor is irrigated by the Bahr Yussef, a channel of the Nile.

tokens.name: Monastery of Saint Anthony
tokens.description: The Monastery of Saint Anthony is a Coptic Orthodox monastery in an oasis in the Eastern Desert of Egypt, in the Red Sea Mountains. It was established by followers of Anthony the Great, an early Christian monk.
tokens.image_credit: Tentoila (talk) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hasan
tokens.description: The Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hasan is a monumental mosque and madrasa in Salah al-Din Square in historic Cairo, Egypt. It was built between 1356 and 1363 during the Bahri Mamluk period.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Citadel of Qaitbay
tokens.title: Built on the Pharos ruins
tokens.description: The Citadel of Qaitbay is a 15th-century defensive fortress on Pharos Island at the mouth of the port of Alexandria, Egypt. It was built from 1477 to 1479 by Sultan al-Ashraf Sayf al-Din Qaitbay.
tokens.image_credit: Hmkree · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pompey's Pillar
tokens.description: Pompey's Pillar is a Roman triumphal column in Alexandria, Egypt, set up in honour of the emperor Diocletian between 298 and 302 AD. Its name is modern, and it stands beside the ruins of the Serapeum.
tokens.image_credit: Roland Unger · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amarna
tokens.title: Akhenaten's capital
tokens.description: Amarna is an ancient Egyptian archaeological site containing the ruins of Akhetaten, the capital city of the late Eighteenth Dynasty. The city was built at the direction of Akhenaten in 1346 BC and abandoned shortly after his death.
tokens.image_credit: en:User:Markh · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ras Muhammad National Park
tokens.description: Ras Muhammad is a national park in Egypt at the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, overlooking the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba. The park is becoming a centre of eco-tourism in the region.

tokens.name: Qal'at Bani Hammad
tokens.description: Qal'at Bani Hammad is a fortified palatine city in the Hodna Mountains of Algeria, now in ruins. In the 11th century it was the first capital of the Hammadid dynasty, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: R hakka · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Erg Oriental
tokens.description: The Grand Erg Oriental is a large sand sea in the Sahara Desert, covering about 185,000 square kilometres. It lies mostly in the Saharan lowlands of northeast Algeria.

tokens.name: Bulla Regia
tokens.description: Bulla Regia was a Berber, Punic and Roman town near Jendouba, Tunisia. Its ruins are noted for Hadrianic-era semi-subterranean houses built against the heat, and many of its mosaic floors remain in place.
tokens.image_credit: Meryem ATHIMNI · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sbeitla
tokens.description: Sbeitla is a town in west-central Tunisia. Next to it lie the ruins of Sufetula, whose three Capitoline temples are among the best-preserved Roman forum temples in North Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al-Zaytuna Mosque
tokens.description: Al-Zaytuna Mosque is a major mosque at the centre of the historic medina of Tunis, Tunisia. It is the oldest mosque in the city, founded at the end of the 7th century or in the early 8th century.
tokens.image_credit: T A · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ksar Ouled Soltane
tokens.description: Ksar Ouled Soltane is a fortified granary complex in the Tataouine district of southern Tunisia. Built by Berber communities on a hilltop, its two courtyards are lined with multi-story vaulted granary cellars called ghorfas.

tokens.name: Kasbah of the Udayas
tokens.description: The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah, or citadel, in Rabat, Morocco. It stands on a hill at the mouth of the Bou Regreg opposite Salé and is listed as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Rabat.
tokens.image_credit: Davide Cesare Veniani · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bou Inania Madrasa
tokens.description: The Bou Inania Madrasa is a madrasa in Fez, Morocco, built in 1350 to 1355 by the Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris. It is the only madrasa in Morocco that also functioned as a congregational mosque.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
tokens.description: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is an Islamic college in Marrakesh, Morocco, commissioned in 1564 to 1565 by the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib. At its height it was the largest Islamic college in the Maghreb.
tokens.image_credit: Lundeux · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Badi Palace
tokens.description: El Badi Palace is a ruined palace in Marrakesh, Morocco. The Saadian sultan Ahmad al-Mansur commissioned it shortly after his accession in 1578 to showcase the wealth and power of his rule.
tokens.image_credit: C messier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saadian Tombs
tokens.description: The Saadian Tombs are a historic royal necropolis in the Kasbah of Marrakesh, Morocco, from the Saadian dynasty. They are known for their richly decorated interiors, mainly from the reign of Ahmad al-Mansur (1578 to 1603).
tokens.image_credit: C messier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ben Amera
tokens.title: Giant monolith
tokens.description: Ben Amera is a monolith in Mauritania, near the border with Western Sahara, rising 633 metres above the desert floor. It is Africa's largest monolith and the world's second largest after Uluru in Australia.
tokens.image_credit: Les3corbiers · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oualata
tokens.description: Oualata is a small oasis town in southeast Mauritania, once a caravan city on a trans-Saharan trade route in the 13th and 14th centuries. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata.

tokens.name: Senegambian stone circles
tokens.description: The Senegambian stone circles are megalithic stone circles and tumuli in Gambia and Senegal, described as the largest concentration of stone circles in the world. The site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2006.
tokens.image_credit: Niels Broekzitter https://www.flickr.com/people/nbroekzitter86/ · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Mosque of Touba
tokens.description: The Great Mosque of Touba is a mosque in Touba, Senegal, founded by Ahmadou Bamba in 1887 and completed in 1963. Bamba died in 1927 and was interred inside the mosque.

tokens.name: Saint-Louis, Senegal
tokens.description: Saint-Louis is a city near the mouth of the Senegal River in northwest Senegal, about 320 km north of Dakar, and capital of the Saint-Louis Region. The historic island town is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2000.

tokens.name: Gao
tokens.description: Gao is a city in Mali on the River Niger and the capital of the Gao Region. For much of its history it was an important commercial centre in the trans-Saharan trade.

tokens.name: Fouta Djallon
tokens.description: Fouta Djallon is a highland region in the centre of Guinea, West Africa. It roughly corresponds with Middle Guinea.

tokens.name: Benin Moat
tokens.description: The Benin Moat (Edo: Iyanuwo), also known as the Benin City Iya or the Wall of Benin, is a large earthwork within Benin City in Nigeria's Edo state. Part of it formerly encircled the city at the time of the Benin Empire.

tokens.name: Kalambo Falls
tokens.description: The Kalambo Falls on the Kalambo River is a 235-metre single-drop waterfall on the border of Zambia and Tanzania, at the southeast end of Lake Tanganyika. Downstream lies the Kalambo Gorge, about 1 km wide and up to 300 m deep.

tokens.name: Chongoni Rock Art Area
tokens.description: The Chongoni Rock Art Area holds 127 rock art and painting sites on granite hills of the Malawi plateau in Malawi's Central Region. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2006.

tokens.name: Quirimbas Islands
tokens.description: The Quirimbas Islands lie in the Indian Ocean off northeastern Mozambique, close to Pemba. The archipelago consists of about 32 islands, including Ibo, Matemo and Medjumbe.

tokens.name: Chinhoyi Caves
tokens.description: The Chinhoyi Caves, formerly the Sinoia Caves, are a group of limestone and dolomite caves in north central Zimbabwe. The site was designated a National Park in 1955.
tokens.image_credit: Suesen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moremi Game Reserve
tokens.description: Moremi Game Reserve is a protected area on the eastern side of the Okavango Delta in Botswana. It was named after Chief Moremi of the BaTawana tribe and lies within the Okavango Delta World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Waterberg Plateau Park
tokens.description: Waterberg Plateau Park is a national park in central Namibia, on a plateau about 68 km south-east of Otjiwarongo. The park is named after the Waterberg, a prominent table mountain that rises from the plateau.

tokens.name: Epupa Falls
tokens.description: Epupa Falls is a series of large waterfalls formed by the Cunene River on the border of Angola and Namibia, in the Kunene Region. The greatest single drop is 37 metres, and the nearby settlement is also called Epupa.

tokens.name: Dragon's Breath Cave
tokens.title: Vast underground lake
tokens.description: Dragon's Breath Cave is a flooded karst cave in the Otjozondjupa Region of Namibia, on private land and not open to the general public. It was discovered by Roger Ellis during a caving expedition in 1986.

tokens.name: Hoba meteorite
tokens.title: Largest known meteorite
tokens.description: The Hoba meteorite lies on Hoba West farm near Grootfontein in the Otjozondjupa Region of Namibia, where it fell. It has never been moved, and its main mass is estimated at more than 60 tonnes.
tokens.image_credit: Sergio Conti from Montevecchia (LC), Italia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Duwisib Castle
tokens.description: Duwisib Castle is a pseudo-medieval fortress in the hills of the Southern Namib region of Namibia, about 72 km southwest of Maltahohe. It was built in 1909 as the residence of the German officer Hans Heinrich von Wolf and has been government property since 1979.
tokens.image_credit: Bernhard Dunst · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cape Cross
tokens.description: Cape Cross is a headland in the South Atlantic on the Skeleton Coast of western Namibia. The cape is also known by its Afrikaans, German and Portuguese names.

tokens.name: Bourke's Luck Potholes
tokens.description: Bourke's Luck Potholes are sculpted potholes in the Blyde River gorge of Mpumalanga, South Africa, where the Treur River tumbles into the Blyde below. They lie in the Blyde River Canyon Nature Reserve on the Drakensberg escarpment.
tokens.image_credit: ErwinMeier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hluhluwe-Imfolozi Park
tokens.description: Hluhluwe-Imfolozi Park is a nature reserve of about 960 square km in central KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. It is the oldest reserve in Africa and the only state-run park in KwaZulu-Natal where all of the big five game animals occur.

tokens.name: Voortrekker Monument
tokens.description: The Voortrekker Monument is a granite monument on a hilltop just south of Pretoria, South Africa. It commemorates the Voortrekkers who left the Cape Colony between 1835 and 1854 and was designed by the architect Gerard Moerdijk.
tokens.image_credit: John Walker, Images of Africa Taken from de-Wikipedia, where it had been uploaded by Head under the same filename. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Richtersveld
tokens.description: Richtersveld is a desert landscape of rugged kloofs and high mountains in the north-western corner of South Africa's Northern Cape province. The Orange River forms its border with Namibia, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Blombos Cave
tokens.title: Early abstract art cave
tokens.description: Blombos Cave is an archaeological site in the Blombos Private Nature Reserve on the Southern Cape coast of South Africa. It holds Middle Stone Age deposits dated to about 100,000 to 70,000 years ago.

tokens.name: Wonderwerk Cave
tokens.description: Wonderwerk Cave is an archaeological site in the Kuruman Hills between Danielskuil and Kuruman in the Northern Cape, South Africa. It is a National Heritage Site managed as a satellite of the McGregor Museum in Kimberley.

tokens.name: Cape Agulhas
tokens.title: Southernmost tip of Africa
tokens.description: Cape Agulhas is a rocky headland in the Western Cape, South Africa. It is the southernmost point of Africa and the traditional dividing line between the Atlantic and Indian oceans.

tokens.name: Thaba Bosiu
tokens.description: Thaba Bosiu is a sandstone plateau in the Maseru District of Lesotho, about 24 km east of Maseru. It was the stronghold of King Moshoeshoe I and once the capital of Lesotho.

tokens.name: Mafate
tokens.description: Mafate is a volcanic cirque on Réunion, a caldera formed by the collapse of the Piton des Neiges shield volcano. It is part of the UNESCO site Pitons, cirques and remparts of Réunion Island.

tokens.name: Longwood House
tokens.title: Napoleon's last home
tokens.description: Longwood House is a mansion on the island of Saint Helena, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic. It was the final residence of Napoleon Bonaparte during his exile there, until his death in 1821.
tokens.image_credit: Michel Dancoisne-Martineau · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Diana's Peak
tokens.description: Diana's Peak is the highest point of Saint Helena, at 818 metres, in the South Atlantic Ocean. It is of volcanic origin and lies within the island's first national park, proclaimed in 1996.

tokens.name: Gough Island
tokens.description: Gough Island is a rugged volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean, a dependency of Tristan da Cunha. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Gough and Inaccessible Islands.

tokens.name: Garajonay National Park
tokens.description: Garajonay National Park is a protected laurel forest covering the centre and north of La Gomera in the Canary Islands, Spain. It was declared a national park in 1981 and listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

tokens.name: Caldera de Taburiente National Park
tokens.description: Caldera de Taburiente National Park is a national park on La Palma in the Canary Islands, Spain. It protects the Caldera de Taburiente, a large caldera that dominates the north of the island, and was designated a national park in 1954.

tokens.name: Chor Minor
tokens.image_credit: Davide Mauro · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lab-i Hauz
tokens.description: Lab-i Hauz is the area around one of the few surviving hauz pools in Bukhara, Uzbekistan. Its 16th and 17th century madrasas and khanaka surround the pool, and the ensemble is part of the Historic Centre of Bukhara, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Ymblanter · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kaltaminor
tokens.title: Unfinished turquoise minaret
tokens.description: Kaltaminor is a memorial minaret in Khiva, Uzbekistan, on the front of the Muhammad Amin Khan madrasa. It stands inside Itchan Kala, the walled old city of Khiva listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Bgag · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Islamkhodja Madrasah
tokens.description: Islamkhodja Madrasah is an architectural monument in the centre of Khiva, Uzbekistan, built by Islam Khodja, prime minister and father-in-law of Khan Isfandiyar. It stands in Itchan Kala, the walled old city of Khiva, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ustyurt Plateau
tokens.description: The Ustyurt Plateau is a transboundary clay desert shared by Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Its semi-nomadic population raises camels, goats and sheep.

tokens.name: Sawran
tokens.description: Sawran, also spelled Sauran, is an ancient city in southern Kazakhstan, about 43 km north-west of Turkistan. It lies near the Syr Darya river.
tokens.image_credit: Yakov Fedorov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Otrar
tokens.description: Otrar, also called Farab, is an ancient city in southern Kazakhstan on the Silk Road. It was the centre of a major oasis and a key junction linking Kazakhstan with China, Europe, the Middle East and Siberia.
tokens.image_credit: Coopypasted · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arslanbob
tokens.title: Vast wild walnut forest
tokens.description: Arslanbob is a village in the Jalal-Abad Region of Kyrgyzstan, beside a large wild walnut forest. The Arslanbob walnut is recorded as Kyrgyzstan's first known export to Europe.

tokens.name: Sarazm
tokens.description: Sarazm is an archaeological site near Panjakent in north-western Tajikistan, dating to the 4th millennium BC. It was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Bertramz · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nisa, Turkmenistan
tokens.description: Nisa was an ancient Parthian settlement near Ashgabat in Turkmenistan, traditionally seen as the first seat of the Arsacid Empire. Its Parthian fortresses are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Roland Lin · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Panjshir Valley
tokens.description: The Panjshir Valley is a valley in north-eastern Afghanistan, about 150 km north of Kabul, near the Hindu Kush. It is divided by the Panjshir River and is home to more than 100,000 people.

tokens.name: Salang Pass
tokens.description: The Salang Pass is a high mountain pass in the Hindu Kush of Afghanistan, at about 3,878 m. It has long been the main road link between the northern provinces and the rest of the country.

tokens.name: Darul Aman Palace
tokens.description: Darul Aman Palace is a three-storey palace about 16 km south-west of central Kabul, Afghanistan. It was built in the 1920s during the reign of Amanullah Khan and has 150 rooms.
tokens.image_credit: Qasimmirzaie · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uvs Lake
tokens.description: Uvs Lake is a highly saline lake in north-western Mongolia. At about 3,350 km2 it is the largest lake in Mongolia by surface area, with a smaller part in Russia.

tokens.name: Amarbayasgalant Monastery
tokens.description: Amarbayasgalant Monastery is one of the three largest Buddhist monastic centres in Mongolia. It stands in the Iven Valley near the Selenge River, at the foot of Mount Büren-Khaan.
tokens.image_credit: Bogomolov.PL · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yolyn Am
tokens.description: Yolyn Am is a deep and narrow gorge in the Gurvan Saikhan Mountains of southern Mongolia. The valley is named after the lammergeier, called yol in Mongolian.

tokens.name: Kizil Caves
tokens.description: The Kizil Caves are a set of Buddhist rock-cut caves on the northern bank of the Muzat River in Xinjiang, China. They are one of the components of the UNESCO Silk Roads World Heritage serial property.
tokens.image_credit: Rolfmueller · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Loulan
tokens.description: Loulan was an ancient Tocharian kingdom in the Tarim Basin, now consumed by the Lop Desert. It was an oasis city on the Silk Road, known from the 2nd century BCE.

tokens.name: Ananuri
tokens.description: Ananuri is a castle complex on the Aragvi River in Dusheti Municipality, Georgia, about 72 km from Tbilisi. The fortified complex includes churches as well as a fortress.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bagrati Cathedral
tokens.description: Bagrati Cathedral is an 11th-century cathedral in Kutaisi, in the Imereti region of Georgia. It was removed from the UNESCO World Heritage list after controversial conservation works.
tokens.image_credit: Marcin Konsek · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Prometheus Cave Natural Monument
tokens.description: Prometheus Cave Natural Monument is a karst cave in Tsqaltubo Municipality, Imereti region of Georgia. It is also known as Kumistavi Cave.

tokens.name: Katskhi Pillar
tokens.title: Monastery atop a rock pillar
tokens.description: The Katskhi Pillar is a natural limestone monolith about 40 metres high near the village of Katskhi in western Georgia. Church ruins stand on its flat top.
tokens.image_credit: Jaba1977, improvements by Giorgi Balakhadze · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: David Gareji monastery complex
tokens.description: David Gareji monastery complex is a rock-hewn Georgian Orthodox monastery complex in the Kakheti region, on the edge of the Iori Plateau. It has hundreds of cells, churches and chapels cut into the rock face.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi
tokens.description: The Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, known as Sameba, is the main cathedral of the Georgian Orthodox Church. Built between 1995 and 2004, it is the third-tallest Eastern Orthodox cathedral in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Alexxx1979 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sanahin Monastery
tokens.description: Sanahin Monastery is an Armenian monastery founded in the 10th century in Sanahin, Lori Province. It forms a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with the nearby Haghpat Monastery.
tokens.image_credit: Steven C. Price · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Areni-1 cave
tokens.description: The Areni-1 cave complex is an ancient multicomponent site near Areni village in southern Armenia, along the Arpa River. It holds a late Chalcolithic and Early Bronze Age ritual site and settlement.

tokens.name: Carahunge
tokens.description: Carahunge, also known as Zorats Karer, is a prehistoric archaeological site of standing stones near Sisian in Syunik Province, Armenia. Tourists often call it the Armenian Stonehenge.
tokens.image_credit: Aleksey Chalabyan a.k.a Xelgen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matenadaran
tokens.description: The Matenadaran, officially the Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, is a museum, archive and research institution in Yerevan. It holds the most extensive collection of Armenian manuscripts in existence.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khinalug
tokens.description: Khinalug is an ancient mountain village in Quba District, Azerbaijan, with origins in the Caucasian Albanian period. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Cultural Landscape of Khinalig People and Köç Yolu, inscribed in 2023.

tokens.name: Orinoco Delta
tokens.description: The Orinoco Delta is a vast river delta of the Orinoco River in eastern Venezuela. It is where the river spreads into many channels before reaching the Atlantic Ocean.

tokens.name: Pico Cristóbal Colón
tokens.description: Pico Cristóbal Colón is possibly the highest mountain in Colombia, with a reported height of 5,775 metres. It and Pico Simón Bolívar are the two highest peaks in Colombia and almost equal in elevation.

tokens.name: Tatacoa Desert
tokens.description: The Tatacoa Desert is the second largest arid zone in Colombia, after the Guajira Peninsula. It covers more than 330 square kilometres north of Huila Department, near Neiva.

tokens.name: Gorgona Island, Colombia
tokens.description: Gorgona is a Colombian island in the Pacific Ocean, about 28 km off the Colombian Pacific coast. It is 9 km long and is separated from the continent by a 270 m deep underwater depression.

tokens.name: Bartolomé Island
tokens.description: Bartolomé Island is an uninhabited volcanic islet of 1.2 square kilometres in Sullivan Bay, just east of Santiago Island, in the Galápagos Islands. It is named after Sir Bartholomew James Sulivan, a lieutenant aboard HMS Beagle.
tokens.image_credit: Pete from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fernandina Island
