tokens.description: Hraunfossar is a series of waterfalls about 900 metres long, where streams flow out of the Hallmundarhraun lava field into the Hvítá river in western Iceland. The name comes from the Icelandic words for lava and waterfalls.
tokens.image_credit: Reykholt · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kerið
tokens.description: Kerið is a volcanic crater lake in the Grímsnes area of south Iceland, along the Golden Circle route. It is one of several crater lakes there and has one of the most recognisable intact calderas.
tokens.image_credit: Gerd Eichmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grjótagjá
tokens.description: Grjótagjá is a small lava cave near Lake Mývatn in Iceland, with a thermal spring inside. In the early 18th century the outlaw Jón Markússon lived there and used the cave for bathing.
tokens.image_credit: Chris 73 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Silfra
tokens.description: Silfra is a rift formed on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the divergent boundary between the North American and Eurasian plates. It is located in Þingvallavatn lake in Þingvellir National Park, Iceland.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hvítserkur
tokens.description: Hvítserkur is a 15 m high basalt stack on the eastern shore of the Vatnsnes peninsula in northwest Iceland. Two holes at its base give it the look of a dragon drinking.
tokens.image_credit: Árni Gunnarsson · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Látrabjarg
tokens.description: Látrabjarg is a promontory in the Westfjords of Iceland and the westernmost point of the country. Its cliffs are home to millions of seabirds, including puffins, northern gannets, guillemots and razorbills.

tokens.name: Ellesmere Island
tokens.description: Ellesmere Island is Canada's northernmost island and its third largest, and the tenth largest in the world. It lies within the Arctic Archipelago as part of the Queen Elizabeth Islands.

tokens.name: Baffin Island
tokens.description: Baffin Island in Nunavut is the largest island in Canada and the fifth largest in the world. Iqaluit, the capital of Nunavut, lies on Frobisher Bay at its southern tip.

tokens.name: Hongcun
tokens.description: Hongcun is a village in Yi County, Huangshan City, Anhui Province, China, near the southwest slope of Mount Huangshan. Together with Xidi, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000 for its preserved rural village architecture and city plan.
tokens.image_credit: 颐园新居 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jinshanling
tokens.description: Jinshanling is a section of the Great Wall of China in Luanping County, Hebei Province, about 125 km northeast of Beijing. It is part of the Great Wall UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Luka Peternel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mutianyu
tokens.description: Mutianyu is a section of the Great Wall of China in Huairou District, Beijing, about 70 km northeast of the city centre. It is one of the best-preserved parts of the Great Wall and lies within the Great Wall UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Wikibphil · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tashi Lhunpo Monastery
tokens.description: Tashi Lhunpo Monastery is a historically and culturally important monastery in Shigatse, Tibet, founded in 1447 by the 1st Dalai Lama. It is the traditional monastic seat of the Panchen Lama.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Mongol assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon
tokens.description: The Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon is a canyon along the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet Autonomous Region, China. It is described as the deepest canyon in the world, and at 504.6 km it is slightly longer than the Grand Canyon in the United States.

tokens.name: Meili Snow Mountains
tokens.description: Meili Snow Mountains is a mountain range in Yunnan Province, China, near the northwestern boundary of the province. It is a subrange of the Nu Mountains and lies within the Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: 瑞丽江的河水 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
tokens.description: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain is a massif in Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang, Yunnan province, China. Its highest peak, Shanzidou, rises to 5,596 m above sea level.
tokens.image_credit: Brücke-Osteuropa · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Erhai Lake
tokens.description: Erhai is an alpine fault lake in Dali City, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan province, China. In ancient times it was also known as Yeyuze or Kunming Lake.

tokens.name: Yushan, Taiwan
tokens.description: Yushan is the highest mountain in Taiwan, at 3,952 m above sea level. It is the highest point in the western Pacific outside the Kamchatka Peninsula.

tokens.name: Lake Kawaguchi
tokens.description: Lake Kawaguchi is the second largest of the Fuji Five Lakes, in the town of Fujikawaguchiko in Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. It lies at about 800 metres above sea level near Mount Fuji.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oshino Hakkai
tokens.description: Oshino Hakkai are eight springs in Oshino, Yamanashi, Japan, where aquifer water from Mount Fuji rises to the surface. They are a Natural Monument of Japan and part of the Mount Fuji World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: MaedaAkihiko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kamikōchi
tokens.description: Kamikōchi is a remote mountainous highland valley in the Hida Mountains, in western Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is preserved in its natural state within Chūbu-Sangaku National Park.
tokens.image_credit: lumoplank · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route
tokens.description: The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is a mountain sightseeing route between Tateyama, Toyama and Ōmachi, Nagano, Japan. Opened on June 1, 1971, it is 37 kilometres long.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Izumo-taisha
tokens.description: Izumo-taisha, officially Izumo Ōyashiro, is one of the most ancient and important Shinto shrines in Japan. It is located in Izumo, Shimane Prefecture, and hosts two major festivals.
tokens.image_credit: MaedaAkihiko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hikone Castle
tokens.description: Hikone Castle is an Edo-period Japanese castle in the city of Hikone, Shiga Prefecture. It is considered the most significant historical site in Shiga and has been a National Historic Site since 1951.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ritsurin Garden
tokens.description: Ritsurin Garden is a large historic strolling garden in Takamatsu, Kagawa Prefecture, Japan. It was completed in 1745 as a private garden and villa for local feudal lords and opened to the public in 1875.
tokens.image_credit: Leela Soden · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iya Valley
tokens.description: The Iya Valley is a scenic region of mountain valleys in Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. It is known for thatched roof farmhouses and historic Vine Bridges.
tokens.image_credit: Naokijp · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Naruto whirlpools
tokens.description: The Naruto whirlpools are tidal whirlpools in the Naruto Strait, a channel between Naruto in Tokushima and Awaji Island in Hyogo, Japan. The strait links the Pacific Ocean with the Inland Sea.

tokens.name: Takeda Castle
tokens.title: Castle in the clouds
tokens.description: Takeda Castle is a Sengoku period castle ruin in the Wadayama district of Asago, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. Only its foundations and stone walls remain, and it is often called the Machu Picchu of Japan.
tokens.image_credit: Baku13 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kerama Islands
tokens.description: The Kerama Islands are a subtropical island group about 32 km southwest of Okinawa Island in Japan. Tokashiki Island, the largest of the group, is administered from the village of Tokashiki.
tokens.image_credit: Paipateroma · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sanjūsangen-dō
tokens.description: Sanjūsangen-dō is a Buddhist temple of the Tendai sect in the Higashiyama district of Kyoto, Japan. Founded in 1164 by Taira no Kiyomori for the cloistered Emperor Go-Shirakawa, it is officially called Rengeō-in.
tokens.image_credit: Akonnchiroll · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haedong Yonggungsa
tokens.description: Haedong Yonggungsa is a Buddhist temple in Gijang-gun, Busan, South Korea. It is one of the few temple complexes in Korea set on the seaside.
tokens.image_credit: Londenp · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bà Nà Hills
tokens.description: Bà Nà Hills, also called Sun World Ba Na Hills, is a hill station and resort in the Trường Sơn Mountains west of Da Nang, Vietnam. It lies in Hòa Vang district on the South Central Coast.
tokens.image_credit: DvTor8303 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hải Vân Pass
tokens.description: The Hải Vân Pass is a mountain pass about 21 kilometres long on National Route 1 in Vietnam. It crosses a spur of the Annamite Range that juts into the South China Sea, on the border of Đà Nẵng and Huế.

tokens.name: Thiên Mụ Temple
tokens.description: The Thiên Mụ Temple is a historic temple on Hà Khê hill in the city of Huế, Vietnam. Its seven-storey Phước Duyên pagoda is regarded as the unofficial symbol of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Lưu Ly · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ko Lipe
tokens.description: Ko Lipe is a small island in the Adang-Rawi Archipelago of the Strait of Malacca, in Satun Province, southwest Thailand. It lies on the border of Tarutao National Marine Park, close to the Malaysian border.

tokens.name: Wat Chedi Luang
tokens.description: Wat Chedi Luang is a Buddhist temple in the historic centre of Chiang Mai, Thailand. The current temple grounds were originally made up of three temples: Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Ho Tham and Wat Sukmin.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phnom Kulen National Park
tokens.description: Phnom Kulen National Park is a national park in Cambodia, located in the Phnom Kulen mountain massif in Siem Reap Province. It was established in 1993 and covers about 374 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Khone Phapheng Falls
tokens.description: Khone Phapheng Falls is a waterfall on the Mekong River in Champasak Province, southern Laos, near the Cambodian border. Its multiple channels make it the widest waterfall in the world, at 10,783 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Basile Morin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ananda Temple
tokens.description: The Ananda Temple is a Buddhist temple in Bagan, Myanmar, built in 1105 during the reign of King Kyansittha. It has a cruciform layout and houses four standing Buddha statues facing the four cardinal directions.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taman Sari, Yogyakarta
tokens.description: Taman Sari Water Castle is the site of a former royal garden of the Sultanate of Yogyakarta, built in the mid-18th century. It had several functions, including a resting area, a workshop, a meditation area, a defence area and a hiding place.
tokens.image_credit: Crisco 1492 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Goa Gajah
tokens.description: Goa Gajah, meaning The Elephant Cave, is a sanctuary located in Gianyar near Ubud on the island of Bali, Indonesia. It was built in the 9th century.
tokens.image_credit: DerGenaue Allrounder · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gunung Kawi
tokens.description: Gunung Kawi, popularly known as The Valley of the Balinese Kings, is an 11th-century temple and funerary complex in Tampaksiring near Ubud, Bali. It comprises 10 rock-cut shrines carved into a cliff face beside the Pakerisan river.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Derawan Islands
tokens.description: The Derawan Islands are an archipelago of 31 islands in East Kalimantan, Indonesia. The best known islands include Derawan, Kakaban, Maratua and Sangalaki, with numerous submerged reefs and islets.
tokens.image_credit: consigliere ivan from Bontang, Indonesia · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kawasan Falls
tokens.description: Kawasan Falls is a three-stage cascade of clear turquoise water from mountain springs in the jungles of Cebu island. The falls are part of the Kawasan River in Badian, Cebu, Philippines.
tokens.image_credit: A.C.T. Alejandre · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hundred Islands National Park
tokens.description: Hundred Islands National Park is the first national park of the Philippines, located in Alaminos, Pangasinan. About 124 islands at low tide are scattered in Lingayen Gulf, over an area of 16.76 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Elmer nev valenzuela · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Batanes
tokens.description: Batanes is an archipelagic province in the northern Philippines and the smallest province in the country by population and land area. Its capital, Basco, is on Batan Island.

tokens.name: Apo Reef
tokens.description: Apo Reef is a coral reef system in the Mindoro Strait off Occidental Mindoro, Philippines. Covering 34 square kilometres, it is considered the world's second-largest contiguous coral reef system and the largest in the country.
tokens.image_credit: ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bako National Park
tokens.description: Bako National Park is a national park in Kuching District, Sarawak, Malaysia, covering 27.27 square kilometres at the mouth of the Bako and Kuching Rivers. Established in 1957, it is the oldest national park in Sarawak.
tokens.image_credit: Huettepe · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ajloun Castle
tokens.description: Ajloun Castle is a 12th-century Muslim castle on a hilltop in the Mount Ajloun district of northwestern Jordan. From its height it guarded three wadis that descend towards the Jordan Valley.
tokens.image_credit: Hiking in Jordan website and guidebook · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mar Saba
tokens.description: Mar Saba is a Greek Orthodox monastery overlooking the Kidron Valley in the Bethlehem Governorate of the West Bank, halfway between Bethlehem and the Dead Sea. It is considered one of the world's oldest almost continuously inhabited monasteries.
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Beiteddine Palace
tokens.description: Beiteddine Palace is an 18th-century palace in Beiteddine, Lebanon, built by Bashir II. It hosts the annual Beiteddine Festival and the Beiteddine Palace Museum.
tokens.image_credit: Peripitus · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baatara gorge waterfall
tokens.title: Waterfall through three bridges
tokens.description: The Baatara gorge waterfall drops 255 metres into the Balaa Pothole, a cave of Jurassic limestone in the Batroun district of Lebanon. The cave is also known as the Cave of the Three Bridges.
tokens.image_credit: Eli+ · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Church of Saint Simeon Stylites
tokens.description: The Church of Saint Simeon Stylites, founded in the 5th century, is one of the oldest surviving church complexes. It stands about 30 km northwest of Aleppo, Syria, on the site of the pillar of the stylite monk Simeon.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Badab-e Surt
tokens.description: Badab-e Surt is a natural site in Mazandaran Province, northern Iran, with stepped travertine terraces formed by mineral hot springs over thousands of years. It lies about 95 km south-east of the city of Sari.
tokens.image_credit: Samaee · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ali-Sadr Cave
tokens.description: The Ali-Sadr Cave is a water cave in Ali Sadr, Kabudarahang County, about 100 kilometres north of Hamadan in western Iran. It attracts visitors every year.
tokens.image_credit: Nasser-sadeghi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Qal'at al-Bahrain
tokens.description: Qal'at al-Bahrain is an archaeological site in Bahrain, a mound with seven stratified layers of occupation from 2300 BC up to the 18th century. It was once the capital of the Dilmun civilization.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kaçkar Mountains
tokens.description: The Kaçkar Mountains are a range rising above the Black Sea coast in northeastern Turkey. With its highest peak, Kaçkar Dağı, at 3,937 metres, the range is the highest part of the Pontic Mountains.

tokens.name: Uzungöl
tokens.description: Uzungöl is a lake south of the city of Trabzon, in the Çaykara district of Trabzon Province in northeastern Turkey. Its village on the lake coast and the surrounding valley are popular tourist attractions.
tokens.image_credit: İhsan Deniz Kılıçoğlu · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Akdamar Island
tokens.description: Akdamar Island is the second largest of the four main islands in Lake Van in eastern Turkey, about 0.7 square kilometres in size. It lies about 3 kilometres from the shoreline.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kayaköy
tokens.description: Kayaköy is a mostly abandoned neighbourhood of the municipality and district of Fethiye in Muğla Province, Turkey. It is situated 8 kilometres south of Fethiye, and its population was 975 in 2022.
tokens.image_credit: Nikodem Nijaki · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hasankeyf
tokens.description: Hasankeyf is a town along the Tigris in Batman Province, Turkey, declared a natural conservation area in 1981. Its city and archaeological sites were flooded as part of the Ilısu Dam project.
tokens.image_credit: Omer Unlu · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aspendos
tokens.description: Aspendos was an ancient Greco-Roman city in Antalya Province, Turkey, about 40 km east of the modern city of Antalya. It lay on the Eurymedon River, about 16 km inland from the Mediterranean Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Saffron Blaze · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ihlara Valley
tokens.description: The Ihlara Valley is a canyon about 15 km long and up to 150 m deep in southwest Cappadocia, Turkey. It contains around 50 rock-hewn Christian churches and numerous rock-cut buildings.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Morphosis at Turkish Wikipedia. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mesa Arch
tokens.description: Mesa Arch is a natural pothole arch on the eastern edge of the Island in the Sky mesa in Canyonlands National Park, Utah. It sits at the edge of a cliff with views of canyons and the La Sal Mountains.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Landscape Arch
tokens.description: Landscape Arch is a natural rock arch in Arches National Park, Utah, United States. It is among the longest natural rock arches in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rainbow Bridge National Monument
tokens.description: Rainbow Bridge is a natural arch in southern Utah, United States. With a span of 84 m it is one of the largest natural arches in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Jason Hickey · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vermilion Cliffs National Monument
tokens.description: Vermilion Cliffs National Monument is in northern Coconino County, Arizona, next to the Utah border. It protects the Paria Plateau, the Vermilion Cliffs, Coyote Buttes and Paria Canyon.

tokens.name: Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument
tokens.description: Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument is a United States national monument in southern Utah. It protects the Grand Staircase, the Kaiparowits Plateau and the Canyons of the Escalante.

tokens.name: Petrified Forest National Park
tokens.description: Petrified Forest National Park is a national park in northeastern Arizona, United States. Named for its large deposits of petrified wood, it covers about 900 square km of semi-desert and badlands.
tokens.image_credit: Finetooth · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shiprock
tokens.description: Shiprock is a monadnock rising about 482 m above the high-desert plain of the Navajo Nation in San Juan County, New Mexico. Its peak lies at 2,188 m above sea level.
tokens.image_credit: Bowie Snodgrass · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness
tokens.description: The Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness is a 45,000-acre wilderness area of steeply eroded badlands in San Juan County, New Mexico. It was established in 1984 and is managed by the Bureau of Land Management.
tokens.image_credit: John Fowler from Placitas, NM, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zabriskie Point
tokens.description: Zabriskie Point is part of the Amargosa Range east of Death Valley, in Death Valley National Park, California. It is noted for its erosional badlands formed from sediments of an ancient lake.
tokens.image_credit: King of Hearts · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Racetrack Playa
tokens.description: Racetrack Playa, or The Racetrack, is a dry lake feature in California. It is known for sailing stones that inscribe linear "racetrack" imprints across the lake bed.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Mayer (mav) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alabama Hills
tokens.description: The Alabama Hills are a range of hills and rock formations near the eastern slope of the Sierra Nevada. They lie west of Lone Pine in Inyo County, California.
tokens.image_credit: Brian W. Schaller · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest
tokens.description: The Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest is a protected area high in the White Mountains in Inyo County, eastern California. It is named for its ancient bristlecone pines.
tokens.image_credit: Oke (talk · contribs) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: General Sherman Tree
tokens.description: The General Sherman Tree is a giant sequoia in the Giant Forest of Sequoia National Park in Tulare County, California. By volume, it is the largest known living single-stem tree on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: Kimon Berlin · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Hood
tokens.description: Mount Hood is an active stratovolcano in the Cascade Range in Oregon, about 50 miles east-southeast of Portland. It forms part of the Mount Hood National Forest.
tokens.image_credit: Kevin Crosby · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Smith Rock State Park
tokens.description: Smith Rock State Park is a state park in central Oregon's High Desert, near the communities of Redmond and Terrebonne. Its day-use area is open daily from dawn to dusk.
tokens.image_credit: Max Schwarz · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone
tokens.description: The Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone is the first large canyon on the Yellowstone River below Yellowstone Falls, in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming. It is about 39 km long and 240 to 370 m deep.
tokens.image_credit: Brocken Inaglory · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mammoth Hot Springs
tokens.description: Mammoth Hot Springs is a large complex of hot springs on a travertine hill in Yellowstone National Park, next to Fort Yellowstone. Calcium carbonate deposited by the cooling water over thousands of years built its terraces.
tokens.image_credit: I. Reid (User:Reid,iain james) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bass Harbor Head Light
tokens.description: Bass Harbor Head Light is a lighthouse within Acadia National Park on the southwest part of Mount Desert Island, Maine. It marks the entrance to Bass Harbor and Blue Hill Bay.
tokens.image_credit: Mourial · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Exit Glacier
tokens.description: Exit Glacier is a valley glacier derived from the Harding Icefield in the Kenai Mountains of Alaska. It is one of the most accessible valley glaciers in Alaska and lies in Kenai Fjords National Park.

tokens.name: Hubbard Glacier
tokens.description: Hubbard Glacier is a glacier in Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve in eastern Alaska, and in Kluane National Park and Reserve in Yukon, Canada. It is named after Gardiner Hubbard.

tokens.name: Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve
tokens.description: Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve is a United States national park and preserve in south central Alaska. It covers the Wrangell Mountains and a large portion of the Saint Elias Mountains, and is the largest park in the United States.

tokens.name: Lake O'Hara
tokens.description: Lake O'Hara is a lake at an elevation of 2,020 metres in the alpine area of Yoho National Park, British Columbia. The area is known for its scenery and alpine hiking.

tokens.name: Maligne Lake
tokens.description: Maligne Lake is a lake in Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada. It is famed for its azure water, the surrounding peaks and Spirit Island, and lies 44 km south of Jasper town.
tokens.image_credit: Christian Abend from Laufen /, Bayern / Deutschland · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Johnston Canyon
tokens.description: Johnston Creek is a tributary of the Bow River in Canada's Rocky Mountains, in Banff National Park, Alberta. The Johnston Canyon gorge and its waterfalls lie on the creek inside the park.
tokens.image_credit: Armando Davalos · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Robson
tokens.description: Mount Robson is the highest point in the Canadian Rockies and the most prominent mountain in the North American Rocky Mountains. It lies entirely within Mount Robson Provincial Park, British Columbia.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Konen · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Helmcken Falls
tokens.description: Helmcken Falls is a 141 m waterfall on the Murtle River within Wells Gray Provincial Park, British Columbia, Canada. Its protection was one of the reasons for the creation of the park in 1939.
tokens.image_credit: William Redmond · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spotted Lake
tokens.description: Spotted Lake, also called Lake Khiluk, is a saline endorheic alkali lake northwest of Osoyoos in the eastern Similkameen Valley of British Columbia. It is seen from Highway 3, which passes south of the lake.
tokens.image_credit: AndrewEnns · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Butchart Gardens
tokens.description: The Butchart Gardens is a floral display garden in Brentwood Bay, near Victoria on Vancouver Island, British Columbia. The gardens receive over a million visitors each year and are a National Historic Site of Canada.
tokens.image_credit: Marcus · CC BY-SA 1.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ek' Balam
tokens.description: Ek' Balam is a Yucatec-Maya archaeological site in the municipality of Temozón, Yucatán, Mexico. From the Preclassic until the Postclassic period it was the seat of a Mayan kingdom.
tokens.image_credit: Akke · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Islas Marietas National Park
tokens.description: The Islas Marietas are a group of small uninhabited islands a few miles off the coast of Nayarit, Mexico, in the municipality of Bahia de Banderas. Marine life is protected from fishing and hunting, which makes them a popular destination.
tokens.image_credit: Christian Frausto Bernal from Tepic, Nayarit, MEXICO · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shanghai Tower
tokens.title: Twisting supertall of Pudong
tokens.description: The Shanghai Tower is a 128-story, 632 m megatall skyscraper in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai. It is the tallest building in China.
tokens.image_credit: Benjamin Ceci · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ping An Finance Centre
tokens.title: Shenzhen supertall
tokens.description: The Ping An Finance Center is a 115-storey, 599.1-metre supertall skyscraper in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. Completed in 2017, it is the tallest building in Shenzhen and the fifth tallest in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Charlie fong · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shanghai World Financial Center
tokens.title: The bottle opener
tokens.description: The Shanghai World Financial Center is a supertall skyscraper in the Pudong district of Shanghai. It was designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox and developed by the Mori Building Company.
tokens.image_credit: Bechology · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jin Mao Tower
tokens.title: Pagoda-inspired Pudong tower
tokens.description: The Jin Mao Tower is a 420.5-metre, 88-storey landmark skyscraper in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai. It contains a shopping mall, offices and the Grand Hyatt Shanghai hotel.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Canton Tower
tokens.title: Hyperboloid tower of Guangzhou
tokens.description: The Canton Tower is a 600-metre multipurpose observation and broadcast tower in the Haizhu District of Guangzhou, China. It was completed in 2009 and opened in 2010 for the Asian Games.
tokens.image_credit: Chinatravelsavvy · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guangzhou International Finance Center
tokens.description: Guangzhou International Finance Center is a 103-storey, 438.6-metre skyscraper in the Tianhe District of Guangzhou, China. Completed in 2010, it is one half of the Guangzhou Twin Towers.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tianjin CTF Finance Centre
tokens.description: Tianjin CTF Finance Centre is a 530-metre supertall skyscraper in the Binhai New Area of Tianjin, China. Completed in 2019, it has 97 floors and is the tallest building in the world with fewer than 100 floors.
tokens.image_credit: BD2412 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: CCTV Headquarters
tokens.title: The Big Pants
tokens.description: The CCTV Headquarters is a 51-floor skyscraper with two conjoined towers in the Beijing Central Business District. It is the headquarters of China Central Television and was designed by Rem Koolhaas and Ole Scheeren of OMA.
tokens.image_credit: Dayton12345 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 63 Building
tokens.description: The 63 Building is a 249.6-metre skyscraper on Yeouido island overlooking the Han River in Seoul, South Korea. It opened in 1985 and is clad in gold-coloured glass.
tokens.image_credit: Ox1997cow · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Namsan Seoul Tower
tokens.title: Observation tower on Namsan
tokens.description: Namsan Seoul Tower is a communication and observation tower on the summit of Namsan in central Seoul, South Korea. The 236-metre structure was the nation's first tower serving multiple TV and radio broadcasters.
tokens.image_credit: Theskyxcx · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gwangalli Beach
tokens.description: Gwangalli Beach is a half-moon beach of fine sand in the Suyeong District of Busan, South Korea. It lies in a cove spanned by the Gwangan Bridge and is west of Haeundae Beach.
tokens.image_credit: Chelsea Hicks · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haeundae Beach
tokens.title: Busan's famous beach
tokens.description: Haeundae Beach is an urban beach in the Haeundae District of Busan, South Korea. It is one of Busan's most popular tourist attractions and one of South Korea's most popular beaches.
tokens.image_credit: StephNurnberg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Merdeka Maybank
tokens.description: Merdeka Maybank Tower, formerly Merdeka 118, is a 118-story skyscraper in the Merdeka Precinct of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. At 678.9 metres it is the second tallest building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Ahmad Ali Karim · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Landmark 81
tokens.description: Landmark 81 is a supertall skyscraper in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, developed by Vinhomes. It is the tallest building in Vietnam and the second-tallest in Southeast Asia.
tokens.image_credit: Huỳnh Vĩ Nhơn · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bitexco Financial Tower
tokens.description: Bitexco Financial Tower is a 68-floor skyscraper in the Financial District of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. At 262.5 metres it is the second tallest building in the city.
tokens.image_credit: Ngô Trung · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Singapore Flyer
tokens.description: The Singapore Flyer is an observation wheel in the Downtown Core district of Singapore. It opened on 15 April 2008 and has 28 air-conditioned capsules.
tokens.image_credit: DvTor8303 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Orchard Road
tokens.description: Orchard Road is a major 2.5 km road in the Central Area of Singapore. It is an upscale shopping district with department stores, shopping malls, restaurants and coffeehouses.

tokens.name: Raffles Hotel
tokens.title: Colonial icon of Singapore
tokens.description: Raffles Hotel is a historic luxury hotel at 1 Beach Road, Singapore. It was established by the Sarkies Brothers, Armenian hoteliers, in 1887.
tokens.image_credit: Velela. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Roppongi Hills
tokens.description: Roppongi Hills is one of Japan's largest integrated property developments, in the Roppongi district of Minato, Tokyo. Its centrepiece is the 54-storey Roppongi Hills Mori Tower.
tokens.image_credit: 稲妻ノ歯鯨 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abeno Harukas
tokens.description: Abeno Harukas is a 300 m supertall skyscraper and commercial facility in Abeno-ku, Osaka, Japan. It was the tallest building in Japan from 2014 to 2023.
tokens.image_credit: Oilstreet · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yokohama Landmark Tower
tokens.description: The Yokohama Landmark Tower is a 296.3 m office and hotel tower in the Minato Mirai 21 district of Yokohama, Japan. It was Japan's tallest building until Abeno Harukas surpassed it in 2014.
tokens.image_credit: Sunwater~jawiki · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Umeda Sky Building
tokens.description: The Umeda Sky Building is a two-tower mixed-use skyscraper in Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan. The two 40-storey towers are linked at their top by glass bridges across an open atrium.
tokens.image_credit: Kakidai · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Akihabara
tokens.title: Electric Town
tokens.description: Akihabara is a neighbourhood in Chiyoda ward, Tokyo, generally considered to be the area around Akihabara Station. It is nicknamed Akihabara Electric Town.
tokens.image_credit: Jmho · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ginza
tokens.description: Ginza is a district of Chuo, Tokyo, and a popular upscale shopping area. It has numerous internationally renowned department stores, boutiques, restaurants and coffeehouses.
tokens.image_credit: Kakidai · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shinjuku
tokens.title: World's busiest railway station
tokens.description: Shinjuku is one of the 23 special wards of Tokyo and a major commercial and administrative centre. It houses the northern half of Shinjuku Station, the busiest railway station in the world.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Yasuo Osakabe · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Harajuku
tokens.description: Harajuku is a district in Shibuya, Tokyo, spreading from Harajuku Station to Omotesando. Takeshita Street and Cat Street are among its well known backstreets.
tokens.image_credit: Intforce · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gion
tokens.description: Gion is a district of Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, in front of Yasaka Shrine. It grew from a Sengoku period entertainment district and is one of Japan's best known geisha districts.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nishiki Market
tokens.description: Nishiki Market is a marketplace in downtown Kyoto, on Nishikikoji Street near Teramachi Street. It is renowned as a place to buy many of Kyoto's famous foods and goods.
tokens.image_credit: matsuyuki · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tokyo Disneyland
tokens.description: Tokyo Disneyland is a 51 ha theme park at the Tokyo Disney Resort in Urayasu, Chiba Prefecture. It opened on April 15, 1983 as the first Disney park built outside the United States.
tokens.image_credit: LMP 2001 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tokyo DisneySea
tokens.description: Tokyo DisneySea is a theme park at the Tokyo Disney Resort in Urayasu, Chiba Prefecture, next to Tokyo. It opened on 4 September 2001 and is owned by the Oriental Land Company.
tokens.image_credit: CasinoKat · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Universal Studios Japan
tokens.description: Universal Studios Japan is a theme park in Osaka, Japan. It opened on March 31, 2001 and is one of six Universal Studios theme parks worldwide.

tokens.name: Niseko
tokens.title: Powder-snow resort
tokens.description: Niseko is a resort area in Hokkaido, Japan, officially the Niseko Tourism Zone. It consists of Kutchan, Niseko and Rankoshi towns at the foot of Niseko Annupuri.
tokens.image_credit: Wakimasa · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hakuba
tokens.description: Hakuba is a village located in Nagano Prefecture, Japan. The village covers a total area of 189.36 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Hong Kong Disneyland
tokens.description: Hong Kong Disneyland is a theme park on reclaimed land in Penny's Bay, Lantau Island, Hong Kong. It opened on 12 September 2005 as the second Disneyland in Asia, after Tokyo Disneyland.
tokens.image_credit: Ngchikit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ocean Park Hong Kong
tokens.description: Ocean Park Hong Kong is an amusement and animal theme park in Wong Chuk Hang on Hong Kong Island. It opened on 10 January 1977 and combines rides with aquariums and live-animal exhibits.
tokens.image_credit: Exploringlife · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: International Commerce Centre
tokens.description: The International Commerce Centre is a 108-storey, 484 m supertall skyscraper in West Kowloon, Hong Kong. It is the tallest building in Hong Kong and the only building in the city with over 100 storeys.
tokens.image_credit: Ashley Pomeroy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: International Finance Centre, Hong Kong
tokens.description: The International Finance Centre is a commercial complex of two skyscrapers, a shopping mall and a hotel on Victoria Harbour in Central, Hong Kong. Its tower 2 IFC is the second-tallest building in Hong Kong at 412 m.
tokens.image_credit: WiNG · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bank of China Tower, Hong Kong
tokens.description: The Bank of China Tower is a skyscraper in Central, Hong Kong, housing the headquarters of Bank of China (Hong Kong). It is known for its triangular frameworks covered by glass curtain walls.
tokens.image_credit: WiNG · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: HSBC Building, Hong Kong
tokens.description: HSBC Main Building is the headquarters building of The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation in Hong Kong. It stands on the southern side of Statue Square.
tokens.image_credit: WiNG · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Central Plaza, Hong Kong
tokens.description: Central Plaza is a 78-storey, 374 m skyscraper at 18 Harbour Road in Wan Chai, Hong Kong. Completed in 1992, it was the tallest building in Asia from 1992 to 1996.
tokens.image_credit: Baycrest · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Victoria Harbour
tokens.description: Victoria Harbour is a natural harbour separating Hong Kong Island from the Kowloon Peninsula. It is a major trading hub and a tourist attraction, known for its annual fireworks displays.
tokens.image_credit: Bkemaoe HOMA · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tsim Sha Tsui
tokens.description: Tsim Sha Tsui is an area in southern Kowloon, Hong Kong, administratively part of the Yau Tsim Mong District. Tsim Sha Tsui East is land reclaimed from Hung Hom Bay.
tokens.image_credit: Wpcpey · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple Street Night Market
tokens.description: Temple Street is a street in Jordan and Yau Ma Tei in Kowloon, Hong Kong. It is known for its night market, one of the busiest flea markets at night in the territory.
tokens.image_credit: Nick-D · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mong Kok
tokens.description: Mong Kok is an area in Kowloon, Hong Kong, and one of the major shopping areas in the city. The Prince Edward subarea occupies its northern part.

tokens.name: Lan Kwai Fong
tokens.description: Lan Kwai Fong is a small collection of streets and alleys in Central, Hong Kong. The area was dedicated to hawkers before the Second World War and is now a popular expatriate area for drinking, clubbing and dining.
tokens.image_credit: Wiki.lkfa · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Star Ferry
tokens.description: The Star Ferry is a passenger ferry service and tourist attraction in Hong Kong, carrying passengers across Victoria Harbour between Hong Kong Island and Kowloon. The operator was founded in 1888 as the Kowloon Ferry Company.
tokens.image_credit: Baycrest · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peak Tram
tokens.description: The Peak Tram is a funicular railway in Hong Kong that carries tourists and residents from Garden Road in Admiralty to Victoria Peak via the Mid-Levels. Operated since 1888, it was the first funicular railway in Asia.
tokens.image_credit: Samson Ng . D201@EAL · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Macau Tower
tokens.description: Macau Tower is a 338 m tower in Sé, Macau, with an observation deck, restaurants, theatres and shopping malls. Its Skywalk X is a walking tour around the outer rim of the tower.
tokens.image_credit: Yumeto · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jiufen
tokens.description: Jiufen is a historic former gold mining town in Ruifang District, New Taipei City, Taiwan. It is known for Jiufen Old Street, a narrow winding alley of shops and teahouses.
tokens.image_credit: lumoplank · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kenting National Park
tokens.description: Kenting National Park is Taiwan's oldest and southernmost national park, on the Hengchun Peninsula of Pingtung County. Established in 1984, it is known for its tropical climate, beaches and mountain scenery.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dubai Frame
tokens.description: The Dubai Frame is an observatory, museum and monument in Zabeel Park, Dubai. It holds the record for the largest frame in the world, 150.24 metres high.
tokens.image_credit: Sachimo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dubai Mall
tokens.description: Dubai Mall is the largest shopping mall in Dubai. It is part of Downtown Dubai, adjacent to the Burj Khalifa, and includes over 1,200 shops.
tokens.image_credit: EditQ · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ain Dubai
tokens.description: Ain Dubai is a giant Ferris wheel on Bluewaters Island in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. At 250 metres it has been the world's tallest observation wheel since October 2021.
tokens.image_credit: Paasikivi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palm Jumeirah
tokens.title: Palm-shaped artificial island
tokens.description: The Palm Jumeirah is an archipelago of artificial islands on the Persian Gulf in Jumeirah, Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It has a population of over 25,000 as of 2022.
tokens.image_credit: Member of the Expedition 22 crew. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atlantis, The Palm
tokens.description: Atlantis, The Palm is a luxury hotel resort at the apex of the Palm Jumeirah in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It opened on 24 September 2008 and is themed on the myth of Atlantis.
tokens.image_credit: Sergio Boscaino from Busseto, Italy · CC-BY-2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dubai Marina
tokens.description: Dubai Marina is a district in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, built around an artificial canal along a 3 km stretch of the Persian Gulf shoreline. It had a population of 70,550 in 2024.
tokens.image_credit: Norlando Pobre · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Emirates Towers
tokens.description: The Emirates Towers is a building complex in Dubai containing the Emirates Office Tower and the Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel. The two towers rise to 354.6 m (1,163 ft) to the tip.
tokens.image_credit: Mujeebpully · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cayan Tower
tokens.description: Cayan Tower, known as Infinity Tower before it was inaugurated, is a 306 m skyscraper in Dubai. Upon its opening in 2013 it became the world's tallest high-rise building with a twist of 90 degrees.
tokens.image_credit: Guilhem Vellut; cropped by Kestreltail · CC-BY-2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Princess Tower
tokens.description: The Princess Tower is a 101-storey, 413.4 m residential skyscraper in the Marina district of Dubai. It was the tallest residential building in the world from 2012 to 2015.
tokens.image_credit: Saaremees · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marina 101
tokens.description: Marina 101 is a skyscraper in Dubai, located in the Dubai Marina district. Standing 101 stories and 425 m tall, it is the second tallest building in the United Arab Emirates.

tokens.name: Global Village, Dubai
tokens.description: Global Village is a cultural destination in Dubai with pavilions showcasing the culture and traditions of countries around the world. It is also a festive carnival with restaurants and entertainment.
tokens.image_credit: Philosographer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
tokens.description: The Dubai Miracle Garden is a flower garden in the Dubailand district of Dubai, launched in 2013. The article states that it is the world's largest flower garden, covering over 72,000 square metres.
tokens.image_credit: Saaremees · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ski Dubai
tokens.description: Ski Dubai is an indoor ski resort with 22,500 square metres of indoor ski area, kept at about -1 to 2 degrees Celsius year round. It is part of the Mall of the Emirates in Dubai.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Seiplax · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental, Abu Dhabi
tokens.description: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental, Abu Dhabi is a luxury five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. It has been operated by Mandarin Oriental since 1 January 2020.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Down · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Etihad Towers
tokens.description: Etihad Towers is a complex of buildings with five towers in Abu Dhabi, the capital city of the United Arab Emirates. It is a landmark on the city's skyline.
tokens.image_credit: Shaibalahmar · CC-BY-SA-2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yas Island
tokens.description: Yas Island is an artificial island in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, named after the Arabian Bani Yas tribe. It was created through extensive land reclamation and covers about 25 km2.
tokens.image_credit: Dapaan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ferrari World
tokens.description: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a mostly indoors theme park on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. It is the world's first Ferrari-themed park and is the home of the Formula Rossa roller coaster.
tokens.image_credit: Floness · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yas Marina Circuit
tokens.description: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5.281 km motorsport circuit on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. It was designed by Hermann Tilke and has hosted the season-ending Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009.
tokens.image_credit: Pi3.124 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
tokens.description: The Louvre Abu Dhabi is an art museum on Saadiyat Island in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. It is the largest art museum in the Arabian Peninsula and uses the Louvre name under an agreement with France until 2047.
tokens.image_credit: Boubloub · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aspire Tower
tokens.description: Aspire Tower, also known as The Torch Doha, is a 300-metre-tall skyscraper hotel in the Aspire Zone complex in Doha, Qatar. It was the focal point of the 15th Asian Games hosted by Qatar in December 2006.
tokens.image_credit: Jaseem Hamza · CC-BY-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Doha Tower
tokens.description: Doha Tower, also known as Burj Doha, is a 238-metre office tower in West Bay, Doha, Qatar, designed by Jean Nouvel. It received the CTBUH Skyscraper Award for the best tall building worldwide in 2012.
tokens.image_credit: Jaseem Hamza · CC-BY-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Pearl Island
tokens.description: The Pearl Island is an artificial island in Doha, Qatar, covering nearly 4 square kilometres. It was the first land in Qatar available for freehold ownership by foreign nationals.
tokens.image_credit: Planet Labs, Inc · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Souq Waqif
tokens.description: Souq Waqif is a marketplace (souq) in Doha, the capital of Qatar. The souq sells traditional garments, spices, handicrafts, and souvenirs, and is home to restaurants and shisha lounges.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
tokens.description: The Museum of Islamic Art is a museum at one end of the Corniche in Doha, Qatar. Architect I. M. Pei designed it on an artificial peninsula near the traditional dhow harbour.
tokens.image_credit: Ralf Steinberger from Milan, Berlin + Munich, Italy + Germany · CC-BY-2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khalifa International Stadium
tokens.description: Khalifa International Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Al Rayyan, Qatar, about 9 km west of central Doha. It opened in 1976 and is named after Emir Khalifa bin Hamad Al Thani.
tokens.image_credit: Ahmad Dalain · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kingdom Centre
tokens.description: Kingdom Centre, formerly Kingdom Tower, is a 99-storey, 302 m skyscraper in the al-Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. When completed in 2002 it was the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia.
tokens.image_credit: Hamza A. Durrani · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abraj Al Bait
tokens.title: Mecca Royal Clock Tower
tokens.description: The Clock Towers, formerly Abraj Al Bait, is a government-owned hotel complex of seven skyscraper hotels in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. The article ranks its central Mecca Royal Clock Tower as the fourth-tallest building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: King Eliot · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jeddah Tower
tokens.description: Jeddah Tower is a megatall skyscraper under construction in the north of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. It is the centrepiece of the Jeddah Economic City project and is planned to be the world's tallest building.
tokens.image_credit: Xtremez21 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al-Balad, Jeddah
tokens.description: Al-Balad, also called Jeddah Historic District, is the historic centre of Jeddah, the second largest city of Saudi Arabia. It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: User:Jpatokal · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Milad Tower
tokens.description: Milad Tower is a multi-purpose tower in Tehran, Iran, and the tallest tower in the country. The article ranks it as the 24th-tallest freestanding structure in the world.
tokens.image_credit: ZarlokX · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Azadi Tower
tokens.description: The Azadi Tower is a monument at Azadi Square in Tehran, Iran, about 45 metres tall and completely clad in cut marble. Formerly named Shahyad Tower, it is part of the Azadi Cultural Complex.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Bazaar, Tehran
tokens.description: The Grand Bazaar is a bazaar in central Tehran, Iran, split into several corridors over 10 kilometres long, each specialising in different goods. Its main entrance is Sabze Meydan, and it is served by two Tehran Metro stations.

tokens.name: Azrieli Center
tokens.description: Azrieli Center is a complex of three skyscrapers in Tel Aviv, Israel, with a large shopping mall at its base. It was designed by the Israeli-American architect Eli Attia.
tokens.image_credit: Ynhockey · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carmel Market
tokens.description: Carmel Market is an outdoor marketplace in Tel Aviv, Israel. Its Hebrew name is Shuk HaCarmel.

tokens.name: Mahane Yehuda Market
tokens.description: Mahane Yehuda Market, often called The Shuk, is a marketplace in Jerusalem with more than 250 vendors selling fresh produce, baked goods, meat, spices and more. It is popular with locals and tourists alike.
tokens.image_credit: Emilio García from Parla, Spain · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jaffa
tokens.description: Jaffa is an ancient Levantine port city on the Mediterranean coast, now part of Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel. Excavations indicate that the city was settled as early as the Early Bronze Age.
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eilat
tokens.description: Eilat is Israel's southernmost city, a port and resort at the northern tip of the Red Sea. The city has a population of about 56,000.

tokens.name: Rothschild Boulevard
tokens.description: Rothschild Boulevard is one of the principal streets in the centre of Tel Aviv, Israel, running north from Neve Tzedek to Habima Theatre. It is one of the most expensive streets in the city and among its main tourist attractions.

tokens.name: Pigeon Rocks
tokens.description: Pigeon Rocks, also known as the Rock of Raouché, is a natural landmark of two rock formations off the coast of Raouché in Beirut, Lebanon. Raouché is a residential and commercial neighborhood along the Corniche Beirut.
tokens.image_credit: Oussama Tahmaz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khan el-Khalili
tokens.description: Khan el-Khalili is a famous bazaar in the historic centre of Cairo, Egypt. It was established as a centre of trade in the Mamluk era and is named for one of its historic caravanserais.
tokens.image_credit: Heba otefy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tahrir Square
tokens.description: Tahrir Square, also known as Martyr Square, is a public town square in downtown Cairo, Egypt. The 2011 Egyptian revolution and the resignation of President Hosni Mubarak occurred at the square.
tokens.image_credit: Waelmansoory · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zamalek
tokens.description: Zamalek is an affluent district of Cairo, Egypt, on a man-made island in the Nile. The northern third of the district has been developed into a residential area.

tokens.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
tokens.description: The Grand Egyptian Museum is a national archaeological museum in Giza, Egypt, dedicated to Egyptian civilization. It is described as the largest museum in the world for a single civilization.
tokens.image_credit: Mohamed abdelzaher · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sharm El Sheikh
tokens.description: Sharm El Sheikh is an Egyptian city on the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, on the Red Sea coast. It is the administrative hub of South Sinai Governorate.
tokens.image_credit: Tanya Dedyukhina · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurghada
tokens.description: Hurghada is a coastal city on the Red Sea in Egypt, and the largest city and capital of the Red Sea Governorate. It grew from a small fishing village into one of the largest resort destinations along the Red Sea coast.

tokens.name: Blue Hole, Dahab
tokens.description: The Blue Hole is a diving location on the southeast Sinai coast, a few kilometres north of Dahab, Egypt. Its maximum depth is just over 100 m, and a shallow opening called the saddle links it to the sea.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
tokens.description: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina is a major library and cultural centre on the Mediterranean shore in Alexandria, Egypt. It commemorates the ancient Library of Alexandria and was officially inaugurated in 2002.
tokens.image_credit: René Dinkel · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ostankino Tower
tokens.description: The Ostankino Tower is a television and radio tower in Moscow, Russia. Standing 540.1 metres tall, it is the tallest free-standing structure in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Klodklodklod77 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lakhta Center
tokens.description: The Lakhta Center is an 87-storey skyscraper in the Lakhta district of Saint Petersburg, Russia. At 462 metres it is the tallest building in Russia and in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Florstein (Telegram:WikiPhoto.Space) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Federation Tower
tokens.description: The Federation Tower is a complex of two skyscrapers in the Moscow International Business Center, Moscow, Russia. Its taller tower, Vostok, is the second-tallest skyscraper in Europe after the Lakhta Center.
tokens.image_credit: Saiht · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mercury City Tower
tokens.description: Mercury City Tower is a 338.8 m supertall mixed-use skyscraper on plot 14 of the Moscow International Business Center, Russia. It was formerly the tallest building in Russia and in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: AltynAsyr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moscow International Business Center
tokens.description: The Moscow International Business Center, also known as Moscow-City, is a skyscraper business district on the Presnenskaya Embankment of the Moskva River. It lies about 4 km west of Red Square in Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: mos.ru · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Red Square
tokens.title: Heart of Moscow
tokens.description: Red Square is one of the oldest and largest squares in Moscow, Russia, along the eastern walls of the Kremlin. It is part of the Kremlin and Red Square, Moscow UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: mos.ru · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: GUM
tokens.description: GUM is a shopping centre facing Red Square in the Kitai-gorod area of Moscow. The Kremlin and Red Square UNESCO World Heritage property lies on the square it faces.
tokens.image_credit: Josef F. Stuefer · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: VDNKh
tokens.description: VDNKh, the Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy, is a permanent trade show and amusement park in Moscow. Between 1991 and 2014 it was called the All-Russia Exhibition Centre.
tokens.image_credit: Ignat pavlov111 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nevsky Prospect
tokens.description: Nevsky Prospect is the main street of Saint Petersburg, Russia. Its name comes from the Alexander Nevsky Lavra monastery at its eastern end.
tokens.image_credit: Vasilii Martynov · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palace Square
tokens.description: Palace Square is the central city square of Saint Petersburg, Russia, linking Nevsky Prospect with Palace Bridge. Many significant events took place there, including Bloody Sunday and parts of the October Revolution of 1917.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sochi
tokens.description: Sochi is the largest resort city in Russia, on the Black Sea coast in the North Caucasus. The city proper has about 466,000 residents according to its Wikipedia article.
tokens.image_credit: Trace · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Krasnaya Polyana, Sochi
tokens.description: Krasnaya Polyana is an urban-type settlement in the Western Caucasus, under the administration of Sochi in Krasnodar Krai, Russia. It is home to the Rosa Khutor alpine ski resort.
tokens.image_credit: Legioner2016 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Baikal
tokens.description: Lake Baikal is a rift lake in southern Siberia, Russia, and the deepest lake in the world. It is the seventh-largest lake by surface area and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Jacques Descloitres, MODIS Land Rapid Response Team, NASA/GSFC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kamchatka Peninsula
tokens.description: The Kamchatka Peninsula is a 1,250 km long peninsula in the Russian Far East, bounded by the Sea of Okhotsk and the Bering Sea. It covers about 270,000 square km.
tokens.image_credit: Jeff Schmaltz · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trans-Siberian Railway
tokens.description: The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world, about 9,289 km from Moscow in the west to Vladivostok in the east. The token sits at Moscow Yaroslavsky station, its western terminus.
tokens.image_credit: Toen96 · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baikal-Amur Mainline
tokens.description: The Baikal-Amur Mainline is a 4,324 km railway in Eastern Siberia and the Russian Far East, built by the Soviet Union as a strategic alternative to the Trans-Siberian Railway. The token sits at the Severomuysky Tunnel, its longest tunnel.
tokens.image_credit: MOROVICTOR · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khan Shatyr Entertainment Center
tokens.description: Khan Shatyr is a transparent tent-shaped entertainment centre in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan. It was unveiled on 9 December 2006 and is 150 m tall including its spire.
tokens.image_credit: Bgag · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heydar Aliyev Center
tokens.description: The Heydar Aliyev Center is a cultural complex in Baku, Azerbaijan, designed by Zaha Hadid. It is named after Heydar Aliyev, first secretary of Soviet Azerbaijan from 1969 to 1982.
tokens.image_credit: lumoplank · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baku Boulevard
tokens.description: Baku Boulevard is a promenade along the Caspian seafront of Baku, Azerbaijan, established in 1909. It is also known as the National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Khortan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Batumi
tokens.description: Batumi is the second-largest city of Georgia and the capital of the Autonomous Republic of Adjara, on the Black Sea coast. Its economy relies on tourism and gambling, and it is an important seaport.
tokens.image_credit: Matti&Keti, Lorenz.King@geogr.uni-giessen.de · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gudauri
tokens.description: Gudauri is a ski resort in Georgia on the south-facing plateau of the Greater Caucasus, about 120 km north of Tbilisi. It lies at about 2,200 m above sea level in the Kazbegi Municipality.

tokens.name: Yerevan Cascade
tokens.description: The Cascade is a monumental terraced complex of stairs, fountains and sculptures in Yerevan, Armenia, linking the city centre with the Kanaker-Zeytun district. It is one of the symbols of the city and includes exhibition halls.
tokens.image_credit: Textfabrikant · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shilin Night Market
tokens.description: Shilin Night Market is a night market in Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan. It is often considered the largest and most famous night market in Taiwan.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 2.0 tw · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alishan National Scenic Area
tokens.description: Alishan National Scenic Area is a mountain resort and nature reserve located in Alishan Township, Chiayi County, Taiwan. It is a protected mountain landscape in Chiayi County.

tokens.name: Tel Aviv Promenade
tokens.description: Tel Aviv Promenade runs along the Mediterranean seashore in Tel Aviv, Israel. It is commonly referred to in Hebrew simply as the Tayelet.
tokens.image_credit: israeltourism from Israel · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ein Bokek
tokens.description: Ein Bokek is an Israeli seaside resort on the Dead Sea, near Neve Zohar. It is under the jurisdiction of the Tamar Regional Council in the Southern District.
tokens.image_credit: Tiia Monto · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dōtonbori
tokens.title: Neon canal of Osaka
tokens.description: Dōtonbori is a district in Osaka, Japan, along the Dōtonbori canal in the Namba district of Chūō ward. It is one of Osaka's principal tourist and nightlife areas, known for its large illuminated signboards.
tokens.image_credit: Type specimen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Flame Towers
tokens.description: The Flame Towers are a group of three skyscrapers in Baku, Azerbaijan. The tallest tower is 182 m (597 ft) high.
tokens.image_credit: Viceskeeni2 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre
tokens.description: The Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre is a 530-metre mixed-use supertall skyscraper completed in 2016. It is the tallest completed building in Guangzhou and houses offices, apartments, a hotel and a shopping mall.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bridge of Peace
tokens.description: The Bridge of Peace is a bow-shaped pedestrian bridge over the Kura River, linking Rike Park with Old Town in Tbilisi. Opened in 2010, it is illuminated with LEDs and is one of the best-known landmarks of the Georgian capital.
tokens.image_credit: falco · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arbat Street
tokens.description: Arbat Street is a pedestrian street about one kilometre long in the historical centre of Moscow. It has existed since at least the 15th century and forms the heart of the Arbat District.
tokens.image_credit: Raita Futo from Tokyo, Japan · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gorky Park, Moscow
tokens.description: Gorky Central Park of Culture and Leisure is a central park in Moscow, named after the writer Maxim Gorky. Its 90th anniversary was celebrated in 2018, and it was reconstructed in 2011.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tsukiji fish market
tokens.description: Tsukiji Market is a former seafood market and a major tourist attraction in central Tokyo, between the Sumida River and the Ginza shopping district. Before 2018 it was the largest wholesale fish and seafood market in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Kakidai · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khaosan Road
tokens.title: Backpacker street of Bangkok
tokens.description: Khaosan Road is a 410-metre street in central Bangkok, constructed in 1892 during the reign of Rama V. It lies in the Bang Lamphu area of Phra Nakhon District, about 1 km north of the Grand Palace.
tokens.image_credit: Marcin Konsek · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
tokens.description: The Chatuchak Weekend Market, on Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road in Bangkok, is the largest market in Thailand. It has more than 15,000 stalls in 27 sections, selling plants, antiques, electronics, clothing, pets and food.
tokens.image_credit: MikSed · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
tokens.description: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market is a floating market in Ratchaburi province, about 100 km southwest of Bangkok. It has become primarily a tourist attraction and is often considered the most famous floating market.
tokens.image_credit: Ahoerstemeier · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maya Bay
tokens.description: Maya Bay is a beach on Ko Phi Phi Le, an island of the Phi Phi Archipelago in the Andaman Sea, Krabi province, Thailand. It was used as the setting of the 2000 film The Beach.
tokens.image_credit: User:Mikecleggphoto from www.travelanddestinations.com · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phuket
tokens.description: Phuket is one of the southern provinces of Thailand, consisting of the island of Phuket, the country's largest island, and 32 smaller islands. It lies off the west coast of mainland Thailand in the Andaman Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Bennypc · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Patong
tokens.description: Patong is a beach and town on the west coast of Phuket island in Thailand. It is the main tourist resort on Phuket and the centre of the island's nightlife and shopping.
tokens.image_credit: Dvanderven · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pattaya
tokens.description: Pattaya is a city on the east coast of the Gulf of Thailand, about 150 km southeast of Bangkok. It is the largest city in Chonburi province and the eighth-largest city in Thailand.
tokens.image_credit: Sergey S. Dukachev · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Railay Beach
tokens.description: Railay Beach, also known as Rai Leh, is a small peninsula between the city of Krabi and Ao Nang in Thailand. It is reached only by boat and is known for its beaches and for limestone cliffs that attract rock climbers.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baiyoke Tower II
tokens.description: Baiyoke Tower II is an 88-story, 309 m hotel skyscraper in the Ratchathewi district of Bangkok, Thailand. It is the tallest hotel in Southeast Asia and has a public observatory and a revolving roof deck.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: MBK Center
tokens.description: MBK Center is a large shopping mall in the Siam area of Bangkok, Thailand. At eight storeys it contains around 2,000 shops, restaurants and service outlets.
tokens.image_credit: กสิณธร ราชโอรส · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siam Paragon
tokens.description: Siam Paragon is a shopping mall in Bangkok, Thailand, located in front of Siam BTS station. It is one of the largest malls in Thailand and includes a multiplex cinema and the Sea Life Bangkok Ocean World aquarium.
tokens.image_credit: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images, but please mention me as the author and may send me a message. (สามารถใช้ภาพได้อิสระ แต่กรุณาใส่เครดิตผู้ถ่ายและอาจส่งข · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ben Thanh Market
tokens.description: Ben Thanh Market is a covered market in District 1 of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It is one of the earliest surviving structures in the city and a well known destination for visitors.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
tokens.description: Hoan Kiem Lake is a freshwater lake of about 12 hectares in the historic centre of Hanoi, Vietnam. Also called Sword Lake, it is one of the main scenic spots and public gathering places of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Bem photography: · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mui Ne
tokens.description: Mui Ne is a coastal fishing ward of Lam Dong Province, Vietnam, with about 25,000 residents. Since the mid-1990s its coast, stretching about 50 km with Phan Thiet, has developed into a resort destination.

tokens.name: Nha Trang
tokens.description: Nha Trang is a ward of Khanh Hoa province, Vietnam, one of the 65 new wards, communes and special zones formed by the 2025 reorganisation of the province. The ward forms part of the coastal city of Nha Trang.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Lewis · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phu Quoc
tokens.description: Phu Quoc is the largest island of Vietnam and a special zone of An Giang province. The island has a total area of 575 square km and about 179,480 permanent residents in 2020.
tokens.image_credit: [//commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:Trantuonglam Trantuonglam] · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Da Lat
tokens.description: Da Lat is a former city and the former capital of Lam Dong Province, Vietnam, and the largest city of the Central Highlands. It lies about 1,500 m above sea level on the Langbiang Plateau and ceased to exist as a municipal city on 1 July 2025.
tokens.image_credit: qiv · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bukit Bintang
tokens.description: Bukit Bintang is the shopping and entertainment district of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, centred on Jalan Bukit Bintang. It is the city's most prominent retail belt, with many shopping centres, cafes, bars and night markets.
tokens.image_credit: Patrice78500 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Perhentian Islands
tokens.description: The Perhentian Islands are a group of islands off the coast of Besut District, Terengganu, Malaysia. The two main islands are Perhentian Besar and Perhentian Kecil.

tokens.name: Genting Highlands
tokens.description: Genting Highlands is a hill station and integrated resort on Mount Ulu Kali in the Titiwangsa Mountains, about an hour's drive from Kuala Lumpur. The resort was established in 1965 by Lim Goh Tong.
tokens.image_credit: Chongkian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Putrajaya
tokens.description: Putrajaya is the administrative centre of Malaysia, to which the federal government moved from Kuala Lumpur in 1999. Kuala Lumpur remains the constitutional national capital.
tokens.image_credit: Muhammad Faqih · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jalan Alor
tokens.description: Jalan Alor is a street in the Bukit Bintang district of Kuala Lumpur, known for its open-air night food stalls. It is lined with hawker stalls and restaurants serving grilled seafood, satay and other Chinese Malaysian dishes.

tokens.name: Bali
tokens.title: Island of the Gods
tokens.description: Bali is an Indonesian island and province, the westernmost of the Lesser Sunda Islands, east of Java and west of Lombok. The provincial capital is Denpasar.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kuta, Bali
tokens.description: Kuta is a tourist area and urban village in Kuta District, Badung Regency, southern Bali, part of the Denpasar metropolitan area. Originally a fishing village, it became one of the first Balinese towns to see substantial tourism.
tokens.image_credit: Simon_sees from Australia · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ubud
tokens.description: Ubud is a town in Gianyar Regency, Bali, promoted as an arts and culture centre. It has developed a large tourism industry.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gili Islands
tokens.description: The Gili Islands are three small islands, Gili Trawangan, Gili Meno and Gili Air, just off the northwest coast of Lombok, Indonesia. Together they form an administrative village in North Lombok Regency.
tokens.image_credit: Kok Leng Yeo from Singapore, Singapore · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nusa Penida
tokens.description: Nusa Penida is an island near southeastern Bali, forming a district of the same name in Klungkung Regency. The Badung Strait separates it from Bali, and its hilly interior rises to 524 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Indonesia
tokens.description: Grand Indonesia is an integrated shopping mall complex on Thamrin Road in Central Jakarta, Indonesia. The Wikipedia intro describes it as the 4th largest mall in Indonesia.
tokens.image_credit: Baqotun0023 · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jalan Malioboro
tokens.description: Jalan Malioboro is a major shopping street in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, on the north-south line between the Yogyakarta Kraton and Mount Merapi. The name is also used for the surrounding neighbourhood.
tokens.image_credit: Gunawan Kartapranata · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siargao
tokens.description: Siargao is a teardrop-shaped island in the Philippine Sea, about 196 km southeast of Tacloban. It has a land area of approximately 437 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Rizal Park
tokens.description: Rizal Park, also called Luneta, is a historic urban park in Ermita, Manila, Philippines. At 58 hectares it is one of the largest urban parks in the country.
tokens.image_credit: Maynard Rabanal (Greedyplus) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Makati
tokens.description: Makati is a highly urbanized city in the National Capital Region of the Philippines. It is the country's leading centre for finance, commerce and diplomacy, with the largest skyline in the country.
tokens.image_credit: patrickroque01 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Koh Rong
tokens.description: Koh Rong is an island in Preah Sihanouk province, Cambodia, and the second largest island of the country. It is one of the islands within the Koh Rong Marine National Park.

tokens.name: Sihanoukville
tokens.description: Sihanoukville is a coastal port city in Cambodia and the capital of Preah Sihanouk Province, on the Gulf of Thailand. The city has a string of beaches along its coastline.

tokens.name: Vang Vieng
tokens.description: Vang Vieng is a city in Vientiane Province, Laos, on the Nam Song River about 130 km north of Vientiane. It is popular with backpackers for adventure sports and its karst topography.

tokens.name: Si Phan Don
tokens.description: Si Phan Don, meaning 4,000 islands, is a riverine archipelago in the Mekong River in Champasak Province, southern Laos. Many of its islands are half submerged when the river is in flood.

tokens.name: Ngapali Beach
tokens.description: Ngapali Beach is a coastal beach in Rakhine State, western Myanmar, about 7 km from the town of Thandwe. It is considered Myanmar's premier beach destination.
tokens.image_credit: Go-Myanmar.com · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mandalay Hill
tokens.description: Mandalay Hill is a hill with an elevation of 240 m, northeast of the city centre of Mandalay in Myanmar. The city took its name from the hill.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Fussan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thamel
tokens.description: Thamel is a commercial neighborhood in Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal. It has been the centre of the tourist industry in Kathmandu for over four decades.
tokens.image_credit: Saddam Hussain Ansari · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pokhara
tokens.description: Pokhara is a metropolitan city in central Nepal and the capital of Gandaki Province. It is the second largest city in Nepal after Kathmandu, with 600,051 inhabitants at the 2021 census, on the shore of Phewa Lake.
tokens.image_credit: Utsab Raj Giri · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Annapurna Circuit
tokens.description: The Annapurna Circuit is a trek within the mountain ranges of central Nepal. Its length is 160 to 230 km, depending on where motor transport is used, and it encircles the Annapurna Massif.

tokens.name: Everest base camps
tokens.description: There are two base camps on Mount Everest, on opposite sides of the mountain. South Base Camp in Nepal is at 5,364 m, and North Base Camp in Tibet is at 5,150 m.
tokens.image_credit: Nirojsedhai · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thimphu
tokens.description: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan, in the western central part of the country. It replaced Punakha as the capital in 1955, and was officially declared the capital in 1961.

tokens.name: Marine Drive, Mumbai
tokens.description: Marine Drive is a 3-kilometre promenade along the coast of a natural bay in Mumbai, India. Built in 1940 by Pallonji Mistry, it is also known as the Queen's Necklace.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Juhu Beach
tokens.description: Juhu Beach lies on the western coast of Salsette Island, on the Arabian Sea in Mumbai, India. It is the best known feature of Juhu, a coastal suburb of Mumbai.

tokens.name: Dharavi
