tokens.description: The John Hancock Center is a 100-storey, 344-metre skyscraper on North Michigan Avenue in Chicago, Illinois. When it topped out in 1968 it was the second-tallest building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Rycroft from Madison, Wisconsin, United States · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aon Center
tokens.description: The Aon Center is an 83-storey, 346-metre skyscraper at 200 East Randolph Street in the Loop, Chicago. Completed in 1973 as the Standard Oil Building, it is the fourth-tallest building in the city.
tokens.image_credit: MusikAnimal · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trump International Hotel and Tower
tokens.description: A 100-story skyscraper condo-hotel in the Near North Side of downtown Chicago, designed by Adrian Smith of Skidmore, Owings and Merrill. Built between 2005 and 2009, it reaches 423.2 m including its spire.
tokens.image_credit: Basil D Soufi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Magnificent Mile
tokens.description: The Magnificent Mile is the roughly one-mile stretch of Michigan Avenue from the Chicago River to Oak Street on the Near North Side of Chicago. It is the main commercial corridor between the Loop and the Gold Coast.
tokens.image_credit: TonyTheTiger at English Wikipedia (Original text: en:User:TonyTheTiger) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Navy Pier
tokens.description: Navy Pier is a 1,010 m pier on the shoreline of Lake Michigan in the Streeterville neighborhood of Chicago. It holds shops, restaurants, theatres, gardens and exhibition halls, and draws over nine million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Millennium Park
tokens.description: Millennium Park is a 9.9 ha public park in the Loop of Chicago, opened in July 2004 on the northwest part of Grant Park. It features public art, gardens and venues such as the Jay Pritzker Pavilion.
tokens.image_credit: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cloud Gate
tokens.description: Cloud Gate is a public sculpture by Anish Kapoor, built between 2004 and 2006 at Millennium Park in Chicago. Nicknamed The Bean, it is made of 168 welded stainless steel plates with a highly polished surface.

tokens.name: Wrigley Field
tokens.description: Wrigley Field is a ballpark on the North Side of Chicago, first opened in 1914 as Weeghman Park. It is the home ballpark of the Chicago Cubs of Major League Baseball.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soldier Field
tokens.description: Soldier Field is a multi-purpose stadium on the Near South Side of Chicago, opened in 1924. It has been the home of the Chicago Bears of the NFL since 1971 and of Chicago Fire FC since 2020.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shedd Aquarium
tokens.description: Shedd Aquarium is a public aquarium on the Chicago lakefront, opened on May 30, 1930. It holds about 32,000 animals and is one of the oldest continually operating non-governmental aquariums in the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
tokens.description: Lincoln Park Zoo is a 14 ha zoo in Lincoln Park, Chicago, founded in 1868. It is one of the oldest zoos in the United States and one of a small number of zoos with free admission.
tokens.image_credit: Jrbarc! · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Art Institute of Chicago
tokens.description: The Art Institute of Chicago is a private, nonprofit art museum in Grant Park, founded in 1879. It is one of the oldest and largest art museums in the United States.
tokens.image_credit: ajay_suresh · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: One World Trade Center
tokens.description: One World Trade Center, also known as One WTC and the Freedom Tower, is the main building of the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan. It is the tallest building in the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chrysler Building
tokens.description: The Chrysler Building is an Art Deco skyscraper at 42nd Street and Lexington Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 1930, it was the world's tallest building for 11 months.
tokens.image_credit: Ferfive · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Woolworth Building
tokens.description: The Woolworth Building is a Neo-Gothic early skyscraper at 233 Broadway in Tribeca, Lower Manhattan, New York City. It was the tallest building in the world from 1913 to 1930.
tokens.image_credit: Copyright by The Pictorial News Co., N.Y. No. NN 98. {{PD-US}}; cropped by Beyond My Ken (talk) 21:01, 27 September 2011 (UTC) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hearst Tower
tokens.description: The Hearst Tower is a glass skyscraper at 57th Street and Eighth Avenue near Columbus Circle in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It is the world headquarters of the media company Hearst Communications.
tokens.image_credit: Dreamword · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 432 Park Avenue
tokens.description: 432 Park Avenue is a residential skyscraper at 57th Street and Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 2015, it was the tallest residential building in the world at that time.
tokens.image_credit: Epistola8 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Central Park Tower
tokens.description: Central Park Tower is a residential supertall skyscraper at 217 West 57th Street on Billionaires' Row in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 2020, it is the tallest primarily residential building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Percival Kestreltail · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: One Vanderbilt
tokens.description: One Vanderbilt is a 62-story supertall skyscraper at 42nd Street and Vanderbilt Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It opened in 2020 and is the city's fourth-tallest building.
tokens.image_credit: Percival Kestreltail · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hudson Yards
tokens.description: Hudson Yards is a neighborhood on the West Side of Midtown Manhattan, New York City, between 30th and 41st Streets. It is the site of a large-scale redevelopment that extends Midtown westward toward the Hudson River.
tokens.image_credit: King of Hearts · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vessel
tokens.description: Vessel is a 16-story honeycomb-like structure of connected staircases in the Hudson Yards Public Square in Manhattan, New York City. It was designed by Thomas Heatherwick.
tokens.image_credit: Epicgenius · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fifth Avenue
tokens.description: Fifth Avenue is a major thoroughfare in Manhattan, New York City, running from West 143rd Street in Harlem to Washington Square Park. Its Midtown section is one of the most expensive shopping streets in the world.
tokens.image_credit: A. Balet · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Broadway
tokens.description: Broadway is a major thoroughfare running about 21 km from Battery Place in lower Manhattan through the Bronx and into Westchester County, New York. Its Midtown section is home to the Broadway theatre district.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rockefeller Center
tokens.description: Complex of 19 commercial buildings covering 22 acres in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. The 14 original Art Deco buildings were commissioned by the Rockefeller family.
tokens.image_credit: David Shankbone · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yankee Stadium
tokens.description: Baseball stadium in the Bronx, New York City, home field of the New York Yankees of Major League Baseball. It opened in April 2009, one block north of the original Yankee Stadium site.
tokens.image_credit: vtravelled.com · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: High Line
tokens.description: Elevated linear park and greenway on the West Side of Manhattan, New York City, created on a former New York Central Railroad spur. It is 1.45 miles (2.33 km) long.
tokens.image_credit: Wil Fyfordy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chelsea Market
tokens.description: Food hall, shopping mall, office building and television production facility in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. The complex occupies an entire city block.
tokens.image_credit: Beyond My Ken · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coney Island
tokens.description: Neighborhood and entertainment area in the southwestern section of Brooklyn, New York City, on the Coney Island peninsula. The peninsula also includes Sea Gate, Brighton Beach and Manhattan Beach.
tokens.image_credit: OptimumPx · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park
tokens.description: Park of 85 acres (34 ha) on the Brooklyn side of the East River in New York City. It lies along a 1.3-mile (2.1 km) stretch of waterfront from Atlantic Avenue to Jay Street.
tokens.image_credit: Jim.henderson · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bronx Zoo
tokens.description: Zoo within Bronx Park in the Bronx, New York City, covering 265 acres (107 ha) of park lands and naturalistic habitats. It is one of the largest zoos in the United States by area.

tokens.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
tokens.description: Botanical garden in central Brooklyn, New York City, occupying 52 acres (21 ha). It holds over 14,000 taxa of plants and has over 800,000 visitors each year.
tokens.image_credit: Andre Carrotflower · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: New York Botanical Garden
tokens.description: Botanical garden at Bronx Park in the Bronx, New York City, established in 1891 on a 250-acre (100 ha) site. It holds over one million living plants and the Enid A. Haupt Conservatory.
tokens.image_credit: Krzysztof Ziarnek, Kenraiz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Waldorf Astoria New York
tokens.description: Luxury hotel and residential condominium building in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, at 301 Park Avenue. It is a 47-story Art Deco structure completed in 1931.
tokens.image_credit: ajay_suresh · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Plaza Hotel
tokens.description: The Plaza Hotel is a luxury hotel and condominium building on Grand Army Plaza, at the southeastern corner of Central Park in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.
tokens.image_credit: Yarl · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hotel Chelsea
tokens.description: The Hotel Chelsea is a historic hotel at 222 West 23rd Street in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Built in 1883 and 1884, it has been home to many writers, musicians and artists.
tokens.image_credit: Eden, Janine and Jim from New York City · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chinatown, Manhattan
tokens.description: Chinatown is a neighborhood of Lower Manhattan in New York City, home to the highest concentration of Chinese people in the Western Hemisphere. It is one of the oldest Chinese ethnic enclaves.
tokens.image_credit: Famartin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Little Italy, Manhattan
tokens.description: Little Italy is a neighborhood in Lower Manhattan in New York City, known for its Italian American population. It lies between Chinatown, Nolita, SoHo and Tribeca.
tokens.image_credit: Mario A. P. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Greenwich Village
tokens.description: Greenwich Village, or simply the Village, is a neighborhood on the west side of Lower Manhattan in New York City, bounded by 14th Street, Broadway, Houston Street and the Hudson River. Its name comes from the Dutch Groenwijck.
tokens.image_credit: Felix Stahlberg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: SoHo, Manhattan
tokens.description: SoHo, short for South of Houston Street, is a neighborhood in Lower Manhattan, New York City. Since the 1970s it has been home to many artists' lofts and art galleries, and to many shops.
tokens.image_credit: Axel Tschentscher · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Griffith Observatory
tokens.description: Griffith Observatory is a public observatory on the south-facing slope of Mount Hollywood in Griffith Park, Los Angeles, California. It overlooks the Los Angeles Basin and has a close view of the Hollywood Sign.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew Field · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rodeo Drive
tokens.description: Rodeo Drive is a two-mile street in Beverly Hills, California, with its southern segment in the City of Los Angeles. It is known as one of the most expensive streets in the world.
tokens.image_credit: jjron · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sunset Strip
tokens.description: The Sunset Strip is a 1.7-mile stretch of Sunset Boulevard that passes through West Hollywood, California. It is known for its boutiques, restaurants, rock clubs and colorful billboards.
tokens.image_credit: MikeJiroch · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venice, Los Angeles
tokens.description: Venice is a neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, founded by Abbot Kinney in 1905 as a seaside resort town. Its beach and boardwalk, Venice Beach, lie on the Pacific coast.
tokens.image_credit: DanielMichaelPerry · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santa Monica Pier
tokens.description: The Santa Monica Pier is a large pier at the foot of Colorado Avenue in Santa Monica, California. It contains a small amusement park, concession stands and areas for fishing and views.
tokens.image_credit: Jelson25 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malibu, California
tokens.description: Malibu is a beach city in the Santa Monica Mountains region of Los Angeles County, California, about 30 miles west of Los Angeles. It has a strip of Pacific beaches and is known as home to many Hollywood residents.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Tillman at English Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
tokens.title: Universal City backlot
tokens.description: Universal Studios Hollywood is a film studio and theme park in Universal City, California, near Hollywood, Los Angeles. It is owned by NBCUniversal and is one of the oldest Hollywood film studios still in use.
tokens.image_credit: Alec GeoSimonian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Disney California Adventure
tokens.description: Disney California Adventure is a 72-acre theme park at the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, California. It is themed to Disney's interpretation of California and uses Disney Animation, Pixar and Marvel properties.
tokens.image_credit: Craig Conley · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Knott's Berry Farm
tokens.description: Knott's Berry Farm is a 57-acre amusement park in Buena Park, California, owned and operated by Six Flags. It officially opened as Knott's Berry Farm in 1947 and is among the most visited amusement parks in North America.
tokens.image_credit: METRO96 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Six Flags Magic Mountain
tokens.description: Six Flags Magic Mountain is a 209-acre amusement park in unincorporated Los Angeles County, just outside Santa Clarita, California. It opened in 1971 as Magic Mountain and was bought by Six Flags in 1979.
tokens.image_credit: METRO96 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dodger Stadium
tokens.description: Dodger Stadium is a ballpark in the Elysian Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, California. It has been the home of the Los Angeles Dodgers since it opened in 1962.
tokens.image_credit: Carol M. Highsmith · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: SoFi Stadium
tokens.description: SoFi Stadium is a multi-purpose indoor stadium in Inglewood, California, a suburb of Los Angeles. It opened in September 2020 and has a translucent ETFE roof.
tokens.image_credit: Troutfarm27 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rose Bowl Stadium
tokens.description: The Rose Bowl is an outdoor athletic stadium in Pasadena, California. Opened in October 1922, it is a National Historic Landmark.
tokens.image_credit: Ted Eytan · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Crypto.com Arena
tokens.description: Crypto.com Arena, formerly Staples Center, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in downtown Los Angeles, California. It opened in October 1999 and is the home venue of the Los Angeles Lakers and Los Angeles Kings.
tokens.image_credit: Troutfarm27 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
tokens.description: Walt Disney Concert Hall is a concert hall in downtown Los Angeles, California, designed by Frank Gehry and opened in 2003. It is the home of the Los Angeles Philharmonic orchestra.
tokens.image_credit: Carol M. Highsmith · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Getty Center
tokens.description: The Getty Center is a museum campus in Los Angeles, California, run by the Getty Trust and home to the Getty Museum. It opened to the public in 1997 on a hill in the Santa Monica Mountains.
tokens.image_credit: Derbrauni · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Central Market
tokens.description: Grand Central Market is a historic public food market in downtown Los Angeles, California. It opened in 1917 in the Homer Laughlin Building and has operated continuously since then.

tokens.name: Wilshire Grand Center
tokens.description: Wilshire Grand Center is a 335 metre skyscraper in downtown Los Angeles, California, completed in 2017. With its spire it is the tallest building in the United States west of Chicago.
tokens.image_credit: Fredchang931124 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: U.S. Bank Tower
tokens.description: U.S. Bank Tower, formerly the First Interstate Bank World Center, is a 310 metre skyscraper in downtown Los Angeles, California. Completed in 1989, it was designed by Henry N. Cobb of Pei Cobb Freed and Partners.
tokens.image_credit: Selvingarcia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Beverly Hills Hotel
tokens.description: The Beverly Hills Hotel is a landmark hotel on Sunset Boulevard in Beverly Hills, California, known for its pink and green exterior. It has 210 guest rooms and suites and 23 bungalows.
tokens.image_credit: Minnaert · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chateau Marmont
tokens.description: Chateau Marmont is a historic hotel at 8221 Sunset Boulevard in West Hollywood, California. Completed in 1929, it was designed by Arnold A. Weitzman and William Douglas Lee.
tokens.image_credit: Tony Mariotti from Los Angeles, United States · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Los Angeles Zoo
tokens.description: The Los Angeles Zoo and Botanical Gardens is a 133-acre zoo in Griffith Park, Los Angeles, California. It was founded in 1966 and is owned by the City of Los Angeles.

tokens.name: Huntington Library
tokens.description: The Huntington Library, Art Museum and Botanical Gardens is a collections-based institution in San Marino, California, founded by Henry E. and Arabella Huntington. It holds an art collection and about 120 acres of botanical gardens.

tokens.name: San Diego Zoo
tokens.description: The San Diego Zoo is a zoo in Balboa Park, San Diego, California, started from animals left over from the 1915 Panama-California Exposition. It was a pioneer of open-air exhibits without cages.

tokens.name: La Jolla Cove
tokens.description: La Jolla Cove is a small cove with a beach surrounded by cliffs in La Jolla, a community of San Diego, California. The area is protected as a marine reserve and is popular with snorkelers, swimmers and divers.
tokens.image_credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hotel del Coronado
tokens.description: The Hotel del Coronado is a historic beachfront hotel in Coronado, California, across San Diego Bay from San Diego. It is a rare surviving wooden Victorian beach resort and a National Historic Landmark since 1977.
tokens.image_credit: Armandoartist · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Transamerica Pyramid
tokens.description: The Transamerica Pyramid is a 48-story pyramid-shaped modernist skyscraper in San Francisco's Financial District. It was the city's tallest building from 1972 until 2017.
tokens.image_credit: Supercarwaar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salesforce Tower
tokens.description: Salesforce Tower, formerly Transbay Tower, is a 61-story supertall skyscraper in the South of Market district of San Francisco. Its main tenant is the cloud software company Salesforce.
tokens.image_credit: Dead.rabbit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lombard Street, San Francisco
tokens.description: Lombard Street is an east to west street in San Francisco, known for a steep one-block section with eight hairpin turns. Most of its western segment is part of U.S. Route 101.
tokens.image_credit: Érico Andrei · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fisherman's Wharf, San Francisco
tokens.description: Fisherman's Wharf is a neighborhood and tourist area on the northern waterfront of San Francisco. It was a working fishing port until its docks declined in the 1960s and 1970s as tourism took over.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, photographer not specified or unknown · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pier 39
tokens.description: Pier 39 is a shopping center and tourist attraction built on a pier in San Francisco. It has shops, restaurants, an aquarium and a marina where California sea lions haul out on the docks.
tokens.image_credit: jjron · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Painted Ladies, San Francisco
tokens.description: The Painted Ladies are a row of Victorian houses on Steiner Street, facing Alamo Square in San Francisco. The houses are repainted in several colours that accentuate their architectural details.
tokens.image_credit: King of Hearts · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haight-Ashbury
tokens.description: Haight-Ashbury is a district of San Francisco named for the intersection of Haight and Ashbury streets. It is known as one of the main centers of the counterculture of the 1960s.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Schwen · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chinatown, San Francisco
tokens.description: Chinatown in San Francisco, centered on Grant Avenue and Stockton Street, is the oldest Chinatown in North America. Established in the early 1850s, it is one of the largest Chinese enclaves outside Asia.
tokens.image_credit: Christian Mehlführer, User:Chmehl · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Francisco cable car system
tokens.description: The San Francisco cable car system is the world's last manually operated cable car system and an icon of the city. Of the 23 lines built between 1873 and 1890, three remain, serving Union Square, Fisherman's Wharf and California Street.
tokens.image_credit: Pi.1415926535 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alcatraz Island
tokens.description: Alcatraz Island is a small island about 1.25 miles offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay. It hosted a lighthouse and a military fortification before becoming the federal prison Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary in 1934.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Schulenburg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Francisco Ferry Building
tokens.description: The San Francisco Ferry Building is a terminal for ferries across San Francisco Bay, with a food hall and offices. Its 245-foot clock tower can be seen from Market Street.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Lu (User:dllu) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golden Gate Park
tokens.description: Golden Gate Park is an urban park on the west side of San Francisco, covering 1,017 acres. It is the third most visited urban park in the United States, with an estimated 24 million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oracle Park
tokens.description: Oracle Park is a ballpark in the South Beach neighborhood of San Francisco, on the shore of San Francisco Bay. It has been the home of the San Francisco Giants of Major League Baseball since 2000.
tokens.image_credit: Dllu · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Napa Valley
tokens.description: Napa Valley is an American Viticultural Area in Napa County, California, established in 1981 as the nation's second. It is one of the world's premier wine regions, with viticulture dating back to the nineteenth century.
tokens.image_credit: Ebryden at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sonoma Valley
tokens.description: Sonoma Valley is a valley in southeastern Sonoma County, California, in the North Bay of the San Francisco Bay Area. It is known as the birthplace of the California wine industry, with some of the state's earliest vineyards and wineries.
tokens.image_credit: TJM97 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Tahoe
tokens.description: Lake Tahoe is a freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada straddling the California and Nevada border. At 6,225 feet above sea level, it is the largest alpine lake in North America.
tokens.image_credit: Lara Farhadi · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heavenly Mountain Resort
tokens.description: Heavenly Mountain Resort is a ski resort on the California and Nevada border in southeastern Lake Tahoe, in the Sierra Nevada. It opened as Heavenly Valley in 1955 and has 97 runs and 30 lifts.

tokens.name: Palisades Tahoe
tokens.description: Palisades Tahoe is a ski resort in Olympic Valley, California, in the Sierra Nevada. Founded in 1949 as Squaw Valley, it hosted the 1960 Winter Olympics and was renamed in 2021.
tokens.image_credit: 9yz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Jerusalem 1099
tokens.title: First Crusade takes the city
tokens.description: The siege of Jerusalem from 7 June 1099 to 15 July 1099 marked the successful end of the First Crusade, and the founding of the Kingdom of Jerusalem soon afterwards. The siege was carried out by the Christian forces of Western Europe mobilized by Pope Urban II after the Council of Clermont in 1095. The city had been out of Christian control since the Muslim conquest of the Levant in 637 and had been held for a century first by the Seljuk Turks and later by the Egyptian Fatimids.

tokens.name: Siege of Jerusalem 70 CE
tokens.title: Roman forces destroy the Second Temple
tokens.description: The siege of Jerusalem in 70 CE was the decisive event of the First Jewish Revolt against the Roman Empire (66–73 CE). Roman forces led by Titus, son of the emperor Vespasian, besieged Jerusalem, the Jewish capital and the revolt's main stronghold. After months of fighting, they breached the defenses, destroyed the Second Temple, and razed the city.

tokens.name: Third Battle of Panipat
tokens.title: Maratha advance ends
tokens.description: The Third Battle of Panipat took place on 14 January 1761 between the Maratha Empire and the invading army of the Durrani Empire. The battle took place in and around the city of Panipat, approximately 97 kilometres (60 mi) north of Delhi. The Afghans were supported by three key allies in India: Najib-ud-Daula who persuaded the support of the Rohilla chiefs, elements of the declining Mughal Empire, and most prized the Oudh State under Shuja-ud-Daula.
tokens.image_credit: James Wales · Public domain

tokens.name: Warsaw Uprising
tokens.title: Resistance rises against occupation
tokens.description: The Warsaw Uprising (Polish: powstanie warszawskie; German: Warschauer Aufstand), sometimes referred to as the August Uprising (Polish: powstanie sierpniowe), or the Battle of Warsaw,  was a major World War II operation by the Polish underground resistance to liberate Warsaw from German occupation. It occurred in the summer of 1944, and it was led by the Polish resistance Home Army (Polish: Armia Krajowa). The uprising was timed to coincide with the retreat of the German forces from Poland ahead of the Soviet advance.
tokens.image_credit: Drawn by GdrModified by Zocky, Mahahahaneapneap, Julieta39, Claude Zygiel · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Battle of Mosul 2016
tokens.title: Nine-month fight to retake the city
tokens.description:
The Battle of Mosul (Arabic: معركة الموصل, Ma'rakat al-Mawṣil) was a major battle initiated by Iraq and allied forces to retake the city of Mosul from the Islamic State (IS), which had seized the city years prior in June 2014. It was the largest conventional land battle in the world since the capture of Baghdad in 2003. It was also the world's single largest military operation overall since the 2003 invasion of Iraq and was considered the toughest urban battle since World War II.
The operation, which was called Operation "We Are Coming, Nineveh" (قادمون يا نينوى; Qadimun Ya Naynawa), began on 16 October 2016, with forces besieging ISIL-controlled areas in the Nineveh Governorate surrounding Mosul, and continued with Iraqi troops and Peshmerga fighters engaging ISIL on three fronts outside Mosul, going from village to village in the surrounding area in the largest deployment of Iraqi troo

tokens.name: Siege of Lucknow
tokens.title: Residency held for months
tokens.description: The siege of Lucknow was the prolonged defence of the British Residency within the city of Lucknow from rebel sepoys (Indian soldiers in the British East India Company's Army) during the Indian Rebellion of 1857. After two successive relief attempts had reached the city, the defenders and civilians were evacuated from the Residency, which was then abandoned.
tokens.image_credit: Louis Desanges · Public domain

tokens.name: Liberation of Khorramshahr
tokens.title: Iran retakes the port city
tokens.description: The Second Battle of Khorramshahr, also known in Iran as the Liberation of Khorramshahr (Persian: آزادسازی خرمشهر, romanized: Âzâdsâzī-ye Khorramshahr) was the Iranian recapture of the city of Khorramshahr on 24 May 1982, during the Iran–Iraq War. The city had been captured by the Iraqis earlier in the war, on 26 October 1980, shortly after the Iraqi invasion of Iran. The successful retaking of the city was part of Iran's Operation Beit ol-Moqaddas.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain

tokens.name: Battle of Warsaw (1920)
tokens.description:
The Battle of Warsaw (Polish: Bitwa Warszawska; Russian: Варшавская битва, Varshavskaya bitva), also known as the Miracle on the Vistula (Polish: Cud nad Wisłą), was a series of battles that resulted in a decisive Polish victory and complete disintegration of the Red Army in August 1920 during the Polish–Soviet War.
After the Polish Kiev offensive, Soviet forces launched a successful counterattack in summer 1920, forcing the Polish army to retreat westward. The Polish forces seemed on the verge of disintegration and observers predicted a decisive Soviet victory.
tokens.image_credit: Users Lysy, Halibutt on en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Reykjavík Summit
tokens.description: The Reykjavík Summit was a summit meeting between U.S. president Ronald Reagan and Soviet general secretary Mikhail Gorbachev, held in Reykjavík, Iceland, on 11–12 October 1986. The talks collapsed at the last minute, but the progress that had been achieved eventually resulted in the 1987 Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty between the United States and the Soviet Union.

tokens.name: Boston Massacre
tokens.description:
The Boston Massacre, known in Great Britain as the Incident on King Street, was a confrontation on March 5, 1770, in the prelude to the American Revolution in Boston, in what was then the colony of the Province of Massachusetts Bay.
In the confrontation, nine British soldiers shot several in a crowd, estimated between 300 and 400, who were harassing them verbally and throwing various projectiles. Five American colonists were killed.
tokens.image_credit: Boston Gazette newspaper clipping, March 12, 1770, from Library of Congress page · Public domain

tokens.name: 1950 French Annapurna expedition
tokens.title: First 8000-metre summit
tokens.description: The 1950 French Annapurna expedition, led by Maurice Herzog, reached the summit of Annapurna I at 8,091 metres (26,545 ft), the highest peak in the Annapurna Massif. The mountain is in Nepal and the government had given permission for the expedition, the first time it had permitted mountaineering in over a century. After failing to climb Dhaulagiri I at 8,167 metres (26,795 ft), the higher peak nearby to the west, the team attempted Annapurna with Herzog and Louis Lachenal, reaching the summit on 3 June 1950.

tokens.name: Great Baltimore Fire
tokens.title: Downtown Baltimore burns
tokens.description: The Great Baltimore Fire raged in Baltimore, Maryland from Sunday February 7 to Monday February 8, 1904. More than 1,500 buildings were completely leveled, and some 1,000 severely damaged, bringing property loss from the disaster to an estimated $100 million, or $3.6 billion in 2026. 1,231 firefighters helped bring the blaze under control, both professional paid truck and engine companies from the Baltimore City Fire Department (B.C.F.D.) and volunteers from surrounding counties and outlying towns, as well as out-of-state units that arrived on the major railroads.

tokens.name: Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng National Park
tokens.description: Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng (Vietnamese: Vườn quốc gia Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng, Vietnamese pronunciation: [vɯ̀ən kʷǒk.ʑā fɔ̄ŋ.ɲā kɛ̂.ɓàŋ]) is a national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Bố Trạch and Minh Hóa Commune of central Quảng Trị Province in the North Central Coast region of Vietnam, about 500 km south of Hanoi. The park borders the Hin Namno National Park in Khammouane Province, Laos to the west and 42 km east of the East Sea from its borderline point. Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng National Park is in a limestone zone of 2,000 km2 in Vietnamese territory and borders another limestone zone of 2,000 km2 of Hin Namno in Laotian territory.
tokens.aliases: Phong Nha – Ke Bang National Park

tokens.name: Malacca City
tokens.description: Malacca City (Malay: Bandaraya Melaka or Kota Melaka) is the capital city of the Malaysian state of Malacca. It is the oldest Malaysian city on the Strait of Malacca, having become a successful entrepôt in the era of the Malacca Sultanate. The city was founded in 1396 by Parameswara, a Sumatran prince who escaped to the Malay Peninsula when the Srivijaya Empire fell to the Majapahit.
tokens.image_credit: Mahkotamedicalcentre · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Komodo National Park
tokens.title: Home of the Komodo dragon
tokens.description: Komodo National Park (Indonesian: Taman Nasional Komodo) is a national park in Indonesia within the Lesser Sunda Islands in the border region between the provinces of East Nusa Tenggara and West Nusa Tenggara. The park includes the three larger islands—Komodo, Padar and Rinca—and 26 smaller ones, with a total area of 1,733 km2 (669 sq mi), with 603 km2 (233 sq mi) of it land. The park was founded in 1980 to protect the Komodo dragon, the world's largest lizard.
tokens.image_credit: prilfish · CC BY 2.0

tokens.name: Lake Nyos
tokens.title: Deadly gas lake
tokens.description: Lake Nyos ( NEE-ohs) is a crater lake in the Northwest Region of Cameroon, located about 315 km (196 mi) northwest of Yaoundé, the capital. Nyos is a deep lake high on the flank of an inactive volcano in the Oku volcanic plain along the Cameroon line of volcanic activity. A volcanic dam impounds the lake waters.
tokens.image_credit: Pashute · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Land's End, Cabo San Lucas
tokens.description:
The arch of Cabo San Lucas is a distinctive granitic rock formation at the southern tip of Cabo San Lucas, which is itself the extreme southern end of Mexico's Baja California Peninsula.  The arch is locally known as "El Arco," which means "the arch" in Spanish, or "Land's End."
It is here that the Pacific Ocean becomes the Gulf of California.
This area is widely used in hotel advertising in the Los Cabos Corridor.

tokens.name: Franciscan Missions in the Sierra Gorda
tokens.description: The Franciscan missions of the Sierra Gorda of Querétaro are five missions built in Mexico between 1750 and 1760. The foundation of the missions is attributed to Junípero Serra, who also founded the most important missions in California. They were declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 2003.
tokens.image_credit: Tobiascontreras · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Kazan Kremlin
tokens.description: The Kazan Kremlin (Russian: Казанский кремль; Tatar: Казан кирмәне) is the chief historic citadel of Kazan, a city in Russia.  It was built at the behest of Ivan the Terrible on the ruins of the former castle of Kazan khans. It was declared a World Heritage Site in 2000.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Volkov · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Triglav National Park
tokens.description: Triglav National Park (TNP; Slovene: Triglavski narodni park, TNP) is the only national park in Slovenia. It was established in its modern form in 1981 and is located in the northwestern part of the country, respectively the southeastern part of the Alpine massif. Mount Triglav, the highest peak of the Julian Alps, stands almost in the middle of the national park.

tokens.name: Thermopylae
tokens.description: Thermopylae (; Ancient Greek and Katharevousa: Θερμοπύλαι, romanized: Thermopylai; Ancient: [tʰermopýlai], Katharevousa: [θermoˈpile̞]; Demotic Greek (Greek): Θερμοπύλες, romanized: Thermopyles [θermoˈpiles]; "hot gates") is a narrow pass and modern town in Lamia, Phthiotis, Greece. It derives its name from its hot sulphur springs. In Greek mythology the Hot Gates is one of the entrances to Hades.

tokens.name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds
tokens.description:
Waitangi is a locality on the north side of the Waitangi River in the Bay of Islands, 60 kilometres (37 miles) north of Whangārei, on the North Island of New Zealand. Here, two documents pivotal to New Zealand history were signed: the Declaration of Independence of New Zealand, on 28 October 1835, and the Treaty of Waitangi, on 6 February 1840. 
Waitangi is close to the town of Paihia, to which it is connected by a bridge near the mouth of the Waitangi River estuary.
tokens.image_credit: Vanderven · CC BY-SA 2.5

tokens.name: Eyjafjallajökull
tokens.description: Eyjafjallajökull (Icelandic: [ˈeiːjaˌfjatl̥aˌjœːkʏtl̥] ; "glacier of (the mountain) Eyjafjöll"), sometimes referred to by the numeronym E15, is one of the smaller ice caps of Iceland, north of Skógar and west of Mýrdalsjökull. The ice cap covers the caldera of a volcano with a summit elevation of 1,651 metres (5,417 ft). The volcano has erupted relatively frequently since the Last Glacial Period, most recently in 2010, when, although relatively small for a volcanic eruption, it caused enormous disruption to air travel across northern and western Europe for a week.

tokens.name: Tràng An
tokens.description:
Tràng An is a scenic area  located in Ninh Bình Province, near Hoa Lư, Vietnam renowned for its boat cave tours.
On 23 June 2014, at the 38th session of the World Heritage Committee in Doha, the Trang An Scenic Landscape Complex was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Trang An Scenic Landscape Complex includes Hoa Lư and Tam Cốc/Bích Động.
tokens.image_credit: LigerCommon · Public domain

tokens.name: Elephant Trunk Hill
tokens.description: The Elephant Trunk Hill (Chinese: 象鼻山; pinyin: Xiàngbí Shān) is a hill, landmark and tourist attraction in Guilin, Guangxi, China.

tokens.name: Bunaken
tokens.description: Bunaken is an island of 8 km2, part of the Bunaken National Marine Park. Bunaken is located at the northern tip of the island of Sulawesi, Indonesia. It belongs administratively to the municipality of Manado.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Borgx assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain

tokens.name: Kaikoura
tokens.description: Kaikōura (; Māori pronunciation: [kaiˈkoːuɾa] ) is a town on the east coast of the South Island of New Zealand, located on State Highway 1, 180 kilometres (110 mi) north of Christchurch. The town has an estimated permanent resident population of 2,350 as of June 2025. Kaikōura is the seat of the territorial authority of the Kaikōura District, which is part of the Canterbury region.
tokens.image_credit: Graeme A Taylor · CC BY-SA 4.0

tokens.name: Guatapé
tokens.description: Guatapé is a town and municipality in the Department of Antioquia, Colombia. It is a part of the subregion of Eastern Antioquia and is located 79 kilometres (49 mi) from Medellín, the capital of the department. Guatapé is bordered on the north by Alejandría, San Rafael to the east, and Granada and El Peñol to the south.
tokens.image_credit: Gabriel Illescas · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Madrid Rio
tokens.description:
Madrid Río is an urban park in the Spanish capital Madrid, built along an urban stretch of the Manzanares River following the burial of the M-30 bypass road in this area. It is the result of a project led by the architect Ginés Garrido, who won the international ideas competition organised by the Madrid City Council in 2005 to redevelop the area.
The project started with the idea of recovering the banks of the Manzanares River for the use and enjoyment of the citizens.
tokens.image_credit: Diario de Madrid · CC BY 4.0

tokens.name: Mount Teide
tokens.description: Teide (Spanish: El Teide) or Mount Teide (Pico del Teide, pronounced [ˈpiko ðel ˈtejðe]; 'Peak of Teide') is an active stratovolcano on the Spanish island of Tenerife, part of the Canary Islands. Its summit (at 3,715 m (12,188 ft)) is the highest point in Spain and the highest of any island in the Atlantic Ocean. Measured from its base on the ocean floor, Teide reaches a total height of 7,500 m (24,600 ft), making it the third-tallest volcano in the world; UNESCO and NASA also rank it as Earth's third-tallest volcanic structure.

tokens.name: Circuit Zandvoort
tokens.description: The Circuit Zandvoort (Dutch pronunciation: [sɪrˈkʋi ˈzɑntfoːrt]), known for sponsorship reasons as the Mascot Circuit Zandvoort, previously known as the Circuit Park Zandvoort until 2017, is a 4.259 km (2.646 mi) motorsport race track located in the dunes north of Zandvoort, Netherlands, near the North Sea coast line and 35 km (22 mi) west of Amsterdam. It returned to the Formula One calendar in 2021 as the location of the revived Dutch Grand Prix. This partnership with Formula One ended in 2026.

tokens.name: Freedom Tower (Miami)
tokens.description: The Freedom Tower (Spanish: Torre de la Libertad) is a building in Miami, Florida. It was designed by Schultze and Weaver and is currently used as a contemporary art museum and a central office to different disciplines in the arts associated with Miami Dade College. It is located at 600 Biscayne Boulevard on Miami Dade College's Wolfson Campus.
tokens.image_credit: Tom Schaefer, aka Miamitom at en.wikipedia · CC BY 3.0

tokens.name: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
tokens.title: F1 down the Strip
tokens.description: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street circuit around parts of the Las Vegas Strip in Paradise, Nevada, immediately adjacent to Las Vegas, Nevada. It winds through the streets of the city and comprises the Las Vegas Strip, a section of Las Vegas Boulevard that is home to the city's major hotels and casinos. It incorporates some of the most notable landmarks of the city, including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

tokens.name: Suzhou Museum
tokens.title: I. M. Pei's late masterpiece
tokens.description: The Suzhou Museum (Chinese: 蘇州博物館; pinyin: Sūzhōu Bówùguǎn) is a museum of ancient Chinese art, paintings, calligraphy and handmade crafts in Suzhou, Jiangsu, China. It is one of the most visited museums in the world, with more than 2 million visitors in 2018. The Folk Branch of the museum is at the Bei family ancestral temple near Lion Grove Garden.

tokens.name: Indianapolis 500
tokens.title: The Greatest Spectacle in Racing
tokens.description: The Indianapolis 500, commonly shortened to Indy 500, is an automobile race held annually at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway in Speedway, Indiana, United States, an enclave suburb of Indianapolis. The event is traditionally held over Memorial Day weekend, usually the last weekend of May. It is contested as part of the IndyCar Series, which is the top level of American open-wheel car racing, a formula colloquially known as "Indy Car Racing".
tokens.image_credit: The359 · CC BY-SA 2.0

tokens.name: Port of Montreal
tokens.title: St Lawrence river port
tokens.description: The Port of Montreal (French: Port de Montréal, pronounced [pɔʁ də mɔ̃ʁeal]) (ACI Canadian Port Code: 0395, UN/LOCODE: CA MTR) is a cruise and transshipment point. It is located on the St. Lawrence River in Montreal, Québec, Canada.
tokens.image_credit: Maxim Pouska · CC BY-SA 4.0

tokens.name: Port of Buenos Aires
tokens.title: Argentine river port
tokens.description:
The Port of Buenos Aires (Spanish: Puerto de Buenos Aires) is the principal maritime port in Argentina. Operated by the Administración General de Puertos (General Ports Administration), a state enterprise, it is the leading transshipment point for the foreign trade of Argentina.
The current port is located in the city's Retiro ward, and is colloquially known as Puerto Nuevo (New Port).
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC BY 2.5 ar

tokens.name: Grand Central Terminal
tokens.title: New York's Beaux-Arts station
tokens.description: Grand Central Terminal (GCT; also referred to as Grand Central Station or simply as Grand Central) is a commuter rail terminal at 42nd Street and Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Grand Central is the southern terminus of the Metro-North Railroad's Harlem, Hudson and New Haven Lines, serving the northern parts of the New York metropolitan area. It also serves the Long Island Rail Road through Grand Central Madison, a 16-acre (6.5 ha) addition to the station located underneath the Metro-North tracks, built from 2007 to 2023.

tokens.name: Tignes Dam
tokens.title: Alpine arch dam
tokens.description: The Tignes Dam, also known as the Chevril Dam, is an arch dam on the Isère in the municipality of Tignes in the Rhône-Alpes region in south-eastern France. In planning since the 1920s and under the protest of locals, the dam was constructed between 1948 and 1952 with the purpose of hydroelectric power. At the time of its completion, it was the tallest dam in Europe.

tokens.name: Orinoco Belt
tokens.title: Heavy oil belt of Venezuela
tokens.description: The Orinoco Belt is a territory in the southern strip of the eastern Orinoco River basin in Venezuela which overlies the world's largest deposits of petroleum. Its local Spanish name is Faja Petrolífera del Orinoco (Orinoco Petroleum Belt). The Orinoco Belt is located in Guárico and south of the Anzoátegui, Monagas, and Delta Amacuro states, and it follows the line of the river.

tokens.name: BAE Systems
tokens.title: British defence giant
tokens.description: BAE Systems plc is a British multinational aerospace, arms and information security company, based in London. It is the largest manufacturer in Britain as of 2017. It is the largest defence contractor in Europe and the sixth largest in the world based on applicable 2024 revenues.
tokens.image_credit: MAPN · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: City of London
tokens.title: The Square Mile
tokens.description: The City of London (informally known as the City or the Square Mile) is a city, ceremonial county and local government district in England. Established by the Romans around 47 AD as Londinium, it forms the historic centre of the wider London metropolis. Surrounded by the modern ceremonial county of Greater London, the City is a unique local authority area governed by the City of London Corporation, which is led by the Lord Mayor of London.
tokens.image_credit: Ewan-M · CC BY-SA 2.0

tokens.name: Moscow Exchange
tokens.title: Russian stock exchange
tokens.description: The Moscow Exchange (MOEX; Russian: Московская биржа, romanized: Moskovskaya birzha, IPA: [mɐˈskofskəjə ˈbʲirʐə]) is the largest exchange in Russia, operating trading markets in equities, bonds, derivatives, the foreign exchange market, money markets, and precious metals. The Moscow Exchange also operates Russia's central securities depository, the National Settlement Depository (NSD), and the country's largest clearing service provider, the National Clearing Centre. The exchange was formed in 2011 in a merger of the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange and the Russian Trading System.

tokens.name: Tel Aviv Stock Exchange
tokens.title: Israeli stock exchange
tokens.description:
The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE; Hebrew: הַבּוּרְסָה לִנְיָירוֹת עֵרֶךְ בְּתֵל אָבִיב), colloquially known as The Bursa, is the only public stock exchange in Israel and a public company itself, listed on its own exchange since August 1, 2019. It is regulated by the Securities Law (1968) and is under the direct supervision of the Israel Securities Authority (ISA).
The TASE plays a significant role in the Israeli economy, facilitating the trade of securities and the raising of capital and debt for companies and the government on the Israeli capital market.

tokens.name: Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange
tokens.title: Abu Dhabi exchange
tokens.description: Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX; Arabic: سوق أبو ظبي للأوراق المالية) is a stock exchange in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE).

tokens.name: Sandton
tokens.title: Africa's richest square mile
tokens.description: Sandton is a financial, commercial and residential city, located in the northern part of the City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality. Formerly an independent municipality, Sandton's name came from the combination of two of its suburbs, Sandown and Bryanston.
tokens.image_credit: Jeff Attaway · CC BY 2.0

tokens.name: Mauna Kea Observatories
tokens.title: Astronomy's top mountain
tokens.description: The Maunakea Observatories (MKO, also known as Mauna Kea Observatories) are a group of independent astronomical research facilities and large telescope observatories that are located at the summit of Mauna Kea on Hawaiʻi, United States. The facilities are located in a 525-acre (212 ha) special land use zone known as the "Astronomy Precinct", which is located within the 11,228-acre (4,544 ha) Mauna Kea Science Reserve. The Astronomy Precinct was established in 1967 and is located on land protected by the Historical Preservation Act for its significance to Hawaiian culture.

tokens.name: Collège de France
tokens.title: Paris research institution
tokens.description: The Collège de France (French pronunciation: [kɔlɛʒ də fʁɑ̃s] ; formerly known as Collège royal or Collège impérial or Collège des trois langues), founded in 1530 by Francis I of France, is a higher education and research establishment (grand établissement) in France. It is located in Paris near La Sorbonne. The Collège de France has been considered to be France's most prestigious research establishment.

tokens.name: Maralinga
tokens.title: British nuclear test site
tokens.description:
Maralinga is a desert area around 3,300 square kilometres (1,300 sq mi) large located in the west of South Australia, within the Great Victoria Desert. The area is best known for being the location of several British nuclear tests in the 1950s.
In January 1985, in recognition of their native title, freehold title was granted to the Maralinga Tjarutja, a southern Pitjantjatjara Aboriginal Australian people, over some land.

tokens.name: Barolo
tokens.title: King of Italian wines
tokens.description:
Barolo ( bə-ROH-loh, US also  bar-OH-loh, Italian: [baˈrɔːlo]; Piedmontese: bareul [baˈrøl]) is a red denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG) wine produced in the northern Italian region of Piedmont. It is made from the nebbiolo grape and is often described as one of Italy's greatest wines.
The zone of production extends into the communes of Barolo, Castiglione Falletto, Serralunga d'Alba and parts of the communes of Cherasco, Diano d'Alba, Grinzane Cavour, La Morra, Monforte d'Alba, Novello, Roddi, and Verduno, all in the province of Cuneo, south-west of Alba.
tokens.image_credit: Anthony Nicalo · CC BY 2.0

tokens.name: River Thames
tokens.title: London's river
tokens.description:
The River Thames, or simply the Thames (  TEMZ), known alternatively in parts as the River Isis, is a river that flows through southern England including London. At 215 miles (346 km), it is the longest river entirely in England and the second-longest in the United Kingdom, after the River Severn.
The river rises at Thames Head in Gloucestershire and flows into the North Sea near Tilbury, Essex and Gravesend, Kent, via the Thames Estuary.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Clio20 assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Seine
tokens.title: River of Paris
tokens.description: The Seine ( sayn, sen; French: [sɛn] ) is a 777-kilometre-long (483 mi) river in northern France. Its drainage basin is in the Paris Basin (a geological relative lowland) covering most of northern France. It rises at Source-Seine, 30 kilometres (19 mi) northwest of Dijon in northeastern France in the Langres plateau, flowing through Paris and into the English Channel at Le Havre (and Honfleur on the left bank).

tokens.name: Source of the Nile Bridge
tokens.title: Jinja cable-stayed bridge
tokens.description: The Source of the Nile Bridge, also New Jinja Bridge, which was commissioned on 17 October 2018, by the president of Uganda, is a cable-stayed bridge across the Victoria Nile in Uganda. It replaced the Nalubaale Bridge, which was built in 1954.

tokens.name: Baekdu Mountain
tokens.description: Mount Paektu or Mount Baekdu (Korean: 백두산) is an active stratovolcano on the Chinese–North Korean border. In China, it is known as Changbai Mountain (Chinese: 长白山, Chinese Korean: 장백산). At 2,744 m (9,003 ft), it is the tallest mountain in North Korea and Northeast China and the tallest mountain of the Baekdu-daegan and Changbai mountain ranges.

tokens.name: Mount Erebus
tokens.description: Mount Erebus () is the southernmost active volcano on Earth, located on Ross Island in the Ross Dependency in Antarctica. With a summit elevation of 3,792 metres (12,441 ft), it is the second most prominent mountain in Antarctica (after Mount Vinson) and the second-highest volcano in Antarctica (after the dormant Mount Sidley). It is the highest point on Ross Island, which is also home to three inactive volcanoes: Mount Terror, Mount Bird, and Mount Terra Nova.

tokens.name: Île Amsterdam
tokens.description:
Île Amsterdam (French pronunciation: [ilamstɛʁdam]), also known as Amsterdam Island or New Amsterdam (French: Nouvelle-Amsterdam), is an island of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands in the southern Indian Ocean that together with neighbouring Île Saint-Paul 90 kilometres (56 mi) to the south forms one of the five districts of the territory.
The island is roughly equidistant to the land masses of Madagascar, Australia, and Antarctica – as well as the British Indian Ocean Territory and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands (about 3,200 kilometres (2,000 mi) from each). It is the northernmost volcanic island within the Antarctic Plate.
tokens.image_credit: NASA ASTER volcano archive jpl · Public domain

tokens.name: Mount Pelée
tokens.description: Mount Pelée or Mont Pelée ( pə-LAY; French: la montagne Pelée [la mɔ̃taɲ pəle], lit. 'bald mountain' or 'peeled mountain'; Antillean Creole: Montann Pèlé) is an active stratovolcano at the northern end of Martinique, an island and French overseas department in the Lesser Antilles Volcanic Arc of the Caribbean. Its volcanic cone is composed of stratified layers of hardened ash and solidified lava. Its most recent eruption was in 1932.

tokens.name: Hekla
tokens.description: Hekla (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈhɛhkla] ), or Hecla, is an active stratovolcano in the south of Iceland with a height of 1,491 m (4,892 ft). Hekla is one of Iceland's most active volcanoes; over 20 eruptions have occurred in and around the volcano since the year 1210. During the Middle Ages, the Icelandic Norse called the volcano the "Gateway to Hell" and the idea spread over much of Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Patrick Neylan · CC BY-SA 4.0

tokens.name: Vulcano
tokens.description: Vulcano (Sicilian: Vurcanu) or Vulcan is a small volcanic island  belonging to Italy in the Tyrrhenian Sea, about 20 km (12 mi) north of Sicily and located at the southernmost end of the seven Aeolian Islands. The island is known for its volcanic activity and contains several volcanic calderas, including one of the four active volcanoes in Italy that are not submarine.  The English word "volcano" and its equivalents in several European languages derive from the name of this island.

tokens.name: Mount Apo
tokens.description: Mount Apo is the highest mountain peak in the Philippines, with an elevation of 2,954 meters (9,692 ft) above sea level. A large solfataric, dormant stratovolcano, it is part of the Apo-Talomo Mountain Range of Mindanao island. Apo is situated on the tripartite border of Davao City, Davao del Sur, and Cotabato; its peak is visible from Davao City 45 kilometers (28 mi) to the northeast, Digos 25 kilometers (16 mi) to the southeast, and Bansalan 20 kilometers (12 mi) to the west.
tokens.image_credit: markaharper1 · CC BY-SA 2.0

tokens.name: Île Saint-Paul
tokens.description:
Île Saint-Paul (French pronunciation: [il sɛ̃ pɔl], "Saint Paul Island") is an island forming part of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands (French: Terres australes et antarctiques françaises, TAAF) in the Indian Ocean, with an area of 6 km2 (2.3 sq mi; 1,500 acres). The island is located about 90 km (56 mi) south of the larger Île Amsterdam 55 km2 (21 sq mi), 1,300 kilometres (810 mi) northeast of the Kerguelen Islands, and 3,000 km (1,900 mi) southeast of Réunion.
It is an important breeding site for seabirds.

tokens.name: Mount Asama
tokens.description: Mount Asama (浅間山, Asama-yama) is an active stratovolcano in central Honshū, the main island of Japan. The volcano is the most active on Honshū. The Japan Meteorological Agency classifies Mount Asama as rank A. It stands 2,568 metres (8,425 ft) above sea level on the border of Gunma and Nagano prefectures.
tokens.image_credit: Yusuke Shinyama · Public domain

tokens.name: Mount Sinabung
tokens.description: Mount Sinabung (Indonesian: Gunung Sinabung; Batak Karo: ᯑᯩᯞᯩᯰ ᯘᯫᯉᯆᯬᯰ, Deleng Sinabung) is an active stratovolcano consisting of andesite and dacite in the Karo plateau of Karo Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia, 40 kilometres (25 mi) from Lake Toba. Many old lava flows are on its flanks and the last known eruption, before recent times, occurred 1200 years before present, between 740 - 880 CE. Solfataric activities (cracks where steam, gas, and lava are emitted) were last observed at the summit in 1912; recent documented events include an eruption in the early hours of 29 August 2010 and eruptions in September and November 2013, January,  February and October 2014.  The volcano has recently claimed the life of at least 23 people in a number of events since 2014.
tokens.image_credit: Public domain

tokens.name: Grímsvötn
tokens.description: Grímsvötn (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈkrimsˌvœhtn̥] ; vötn = "waters", singular: vatn) is an active volcano with a (partially subglacial) fissure system located in Vatnajökull National Park, Iceland. The central volcano is completely subglacial and located under the northwestern side of the Vatnajökull ice cap. The subglacial caldera is at 64°25′N 17°20′W, at an elevation of 1,725 m (5,659 ft).

tokens.name: Katla
tokens.description: Katla (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈkʰahtla] ) is an active subglacial volcano in southern Iceland. This volcano has been very active historically with at least twenty documented major eruptions since 2920 BC. In its recent history though, Katla has been less active as the last major eruption occurred in 1918. These eruptions have had a Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) of between 4 and 5 on a scale of 0 to 8.

tokens.name: Tungurahua volcano
tokens.description: Tungurahua (; from Quichua language tunguri (throat) and rahua (fire), "Throat of Fire") is an active stratovolcano located in the Cordillera Oriental of Ecuador. The volcano gives its name to the province of Tungurahua. Volcanic activity restarted on August 19, 1999, and is ongoing as of 2023, with several eruptive episodes since then, the most recent lasting from February 26 to March 16, 2016.
tokens.image_credit: Cedancp · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Snæfellsjökull
tokens.description: Snæfellsjökull (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈs(t)naiːˌfɛlsˌjœːkʏtl̥] , snow-fell glacier) is a 700,000-year-old glacier-capped stratovolcano in western Iceland. It is situated on the westernmost part of the Snæfellsnes peninsula. Sometimes it may be seen from the city of Reykjavík over Faxa Bay, at a distance of 120 km (75 mi).

tokens.name: Galeras
tokens.description: Galeras (Urcunina among the 16th-century indigenous people) is an active stratovolcano in the Colombian department of Nariño, near the departmental capital Pasto. Its summit rises 4,276 metres (14,029 ft) above sea level. It has erupted frequently since the Spanish conquest, with its first historical eruption being recorded on December 7, 1580.
tokens.image_credit: DSCN8766.JPG: Josecamilom derivative work: Crisneda2000 (talk) · CC BY-SA 2.5

tokens.name: Beerenberg
tokens.description: Beerenberg is a stratovolcano dominating the northeastern end of the Norwegian island of Jan Mayen. It is 2,277 m (7,470 ft) high and is the world's northernmost subaerial active volcano and the only active volcano in Norway. The volcano is topped by a mostly ice-filled crater about 1 kilometre (0.62 miles) wide, with numerous peaks along its rim, including the highest summit, Haakon VII Toppen, on its western side.

tokens.name: Inaccessible Island
tokens.description: Inaccessible Island is a volcanic island located in the South Atlantic Ocean, 31 km (19 mi) south-west of Tristan da Cunha. Its highest point, Swale's Fell, reaches 581 m (1,906 ft), and the island is 12.65 km2 (4.88 sq mi) in area. The volcano was last active approximately one million years ago and is now extinct.

tokens.name: Copahue
tokens.description: Copahue (Spanish pronunciation: [koˈpawe]) is a stratovolcano in the Andes on the border of Bío Bío Region, Chile and Neuquén Province, Argentina. There are nine volcanic craters along a 2 km (1.2 mi) line, the easternmost of which is historically the most active, and contains a 300 m (1000 ft) wide crater lake with a pH ranging between 0.18 and 0.30.   Eruptions from this crater lake have ejected pyroclastic rocks and chilled liquid sulfur fragments.

tokens.name: Mount Shasta
tokens.description: Mount Shasta ( SHASS-tə; Shasta: Waka-nunee-Tuki-wuki; Karuk: Úytaahkoo) is a potentially active stratovolcano at the southern end of the Cascade Range in Siskiyou County, California. At an elevation of 14,179 ft (4,322 m), it is the second-highest peak in the Cascades and the fifth-highest in the state. Mount Shasta has an estimated volume of 85 cubic miles (350 cubic kilometers), which makes it the most voluminous stratovolcano in the Cascade Volcanic Arc.
tokens.image_credit: boulab · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Mount Karisimbi
tokens.description: Mount Karisimbi is a stratovolcano in the Virunga Mountains on the border between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo. At 4,507 metres (14,787 ft), Karisimbi is the highest of the eight major mountains of the mountain range, which is a part of Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift. Karisimbi is flanked by Mikeno to the north, Bisoke to the east and Nyiragongo to the west, on the other side of the Rift Valley.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Amakuru assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Mount Pico
tokens.description: Mount Pico (Portuguese: Montanha do Pico) is a currently dormant stratovolcano located on Pico Island, in the mid-Atlantic archipelago of the Azores. It is the highest mountain in Portugal, at 2,351 metres (7,713 ft) above sea level, and is one of the highest Atlantic mountains; it is more than twice the elevation of any other peak in the Azores. It has been a designated nature reserve since 1972.

tokens.name: Shiveluch
tokens.description: Shiveluch (Russian: Шивелуч, IPA: [ʂɨˈvʲeɫʊt͡ɕ]), also called Sheveluch, which originates from the name "suelich" which means "smoking mountain" in Itelmen, is the northernmost active volcano in Kamchatka Krai, Russia. It and Karymsky are Kamchatka's largest, most active and most continuously erupting volcanoes, as well as one of the most active on the planet. Shiveluch erupts around 0.015 km3 (0.0036 mi3) of magma per year, which causes frequent and large hot avalanches and lava dome formations at the summit.
tokens.image_credit: MODIS Rapid Response Team, Goddard Space Flight Center, NASA · Public domain

tokens.name: Sangay volcano
tokens.description: Sangay (also known as Macas, Sanagay, or Sangai) is an active stratovolcano in central Ecuador. It exhibits mostly strombolian activity. Geologically, Sangay marks the southern boundary of the Northern Volcanic Zone, and its position straddling two major pieces of crust accounts for its high level of activity.
tokens.image_credit: CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Askja
tokens.description: Askja ([ˈasca] ) is an active volcano situated in a remote part of the central highlands of Iceland. The name Askja refers to a complex of nested calderas within the surrounding Dyngjufjöll [ˈtiɲcʏˌfjœtl̥] mountains, which rise to 1,514 m (4,967 ft), askja meaning box or caldera in Icelandic.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Ryan · Public domain

tokens.name: Mount Baker
tokens.description: Mount Baker, also known as Koma Kulshan or simply Kulshan, is a 10,781-foot (3,286 m) active glacier-covered andesitic stratovolcano in the Cascade Volcanic Arc and the North Cascades of Washington State in the United States. Mount Baker has the second-most thermally active crater in the Cascade Range after Mount St. Helens.
tokens.image_credit: TimBray · CC BY-SA 4.0

tokens.name: Novarupta
tokens.description: Novarupta is a volcano located on the Alaska Peninsula on a slope of Trident Volcano in Katmai National Park and Preserve, about 290 miles (470 km) southwest of Anchorage. Novarupta was formed in 1912, during the largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century, in which it released 30 times the volume of magma of the 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens.
tokens.image_credit: W. A. Hesse · Public domain

tokens.name: Bárðarbunga
tokens.description:
Bárðarbunga (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈpaurðarˌpuŋka] , alternative name Veiðivötn), is an active and productive stratovolcano located under Vatnajökull, which is Iceland's most extensive glacier, in Vatnajökull National Park. The second highest mountain in Iceland, 2,000 metres (6,600 ft) above sea level, Bárðarbunga is also part of the Bárðarbunga-Veiðivötn volcanic system that is approximately 190 kilometres (120 mi) long and 25 kilometres (16 mi) wide.

Bárðarbunga erupted in late August 2014.

tokens.name: Osorno
tokens.description: Osorno Volcano is a 2,652-metre-tall (8,701 ft) conical stratovolcano lying between Osorno Province and Llanquihue Province in the Los Lagos Region of southern Chile. It stands on the southeastern shore of Llanquihue Lake, and also towers over Todos los Santos Lake. Osorno is considered a symbol of the local landscape and, as such, tends to be the referential element of the area in regards to tourism.
tokens.image_credit: Wernerluis · CC BY-SA 4.0

tokens.name: Acotango
tokens.description: Acotango is the central and highest of a group of stratovolcanoes straddling the border of Bolivia and Chile. It is 6,052 metres (19,856 ft) high. The group is known as Kimsa Chata and consists of three mountains: Acotango, Umurata (5,730 metres (18,799 ft)) north of it and Capurata (5,990 metres (19,652 ft)) south of it.
tokens.image_credit: Gerard Prins · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Eldfell
tokens.description: Eldfell is a volcanic cone just over 200 metres (660 ft) high on the Icelandic island of Heimaey in the Westman Islands. It formed in a volcanic eruption that began without warning on the eastern side of Heimaey on 23 January 1973. The name means Hill of Fire in Icelandic.
tokens.image_credit: Hansueli Krapf (User:Simisa) · CC BY-SA 2.5

tokens.name: Vogelsberg
tokens.description:
The Vogelsberg (German pronunciation: [ˈfoːɡl̩sˌbɛʁk] ) is a large volcanic mountain range in the German Central Uplands in the state of Hesse, separated from the Rhön Mountains by the Fulda river valley.
Emerging approximately 19 million years ago, the Vogelsberg is Central Europe's largest basalt formation, consisting of a multitude of layers that descend from their peak in ring-shaped terraces to the base.

The main peaks of the Vogelsberg are the Taufstein, 773.0 metres (2,536.1 ft), and Hoherodskopf, 763 metres (2,503 ft), both now within the High Vogelsberg Nature Park.

tokens.name: Cayambe
tokens.description: Cayambe or Volcán Cayambe is a volcano in Ecuador, in the Cordillera Central, a range of the Ecuadorian Andes. It is located in Pichincha Province, some 70 km (43 mi) northeast of Quito. It is the third-highest mountain in Ecuador, at an elevation of 5,790 m (18,996 ft) above sea level.

tokens.name: Tupungato Volcano
tokens.description: Tupungato, one of the highest mountains in the Americas, is a massive Andean lava dome dating to Pleistocene times. It lies on the Argentina–Chile border, between the Chilean Metropolitan Region (near a major international highway about 80 km or 50 mi east of Santiago) and the Argentine province of Mendoza, about 100 km (60 mi) south of Aconcagua, the highest peak of both the Southern and Western hemispheres. Immediately to its southwest is the active Tupungatito volcano (literally, little Tupungato), which last erupted in 1987.
tokens.image_credit: Gerard Prins · CC BY-SA 3.0

tokens.name: Atlasov Island
tokens.description:
Atlasov Island (sometimes rendered as Atlasova Island, from Russian: Остров Атласова), also known as Alaid Island (Japanese: 阿頼度島, Hepburn: Araido-tō), is the northernmost island of the Kuril Islands, part of the Sakhalin Oblast in Russia. Located on the island is Alaid volcano, the highest volcano of the Kurils and one of the most active.
The island is named after Vladimir Atlasov, a 17th-century Russian explorer who incorporated the nearby Kamchatka Peninsula into Russia.
tokens.image_credit: Public domain

tokens.name: Volcán Tajumulco
tokens.description: Volcán Tajumulco is a large stratovolcano in the department of San Marcos in western Guatemala. It is the highest mountain in Central America at 4,203 metres (13,789 ft). It is part of the mountain range of the Sierra Madre de Chiapas, which begins in Mexico's southernmost state of Chiapas.
tokens.image_credit: CC BY-SA 2.5

tokens.name: Santa María
tokens.description:
Santa María Volcano is a large active volcano in the western highlands of Guatemala, in the Quetzaltenango Department near the city of Quetzaltenango. It is part of the mountain range of the Sierra Madre.
The volcano was known as Gagxanul in the local Kʼicheʼ language, which means "Naked Volcano or Mountain", before the 16th century Spanish conquest of the region.
tokens.image_credit: CC BY-SA 2.5

tokens.name: Öræfajökull
tokens.description:
Öræfajökull (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈœːrˌaiːvaˌjœːkʏtl̥] ; 'Öræfi glacier' or 'wasteland glacier') is an ice-covered volcano in south-east Iceland. The largest active volcano and the highest peak in Iceland at 2,110 metres (6,920 ft), it lies within the Vatnajökull National Park and is covered by part of the glacier.
The original Norse settlers named the volcano Knappafellsjǫkull (Old Norse: [ˈknɑpːɑˌfelːsˌjɔkolː]; Modern Icelandic: Hnappafellsjökull [ˈn̥ahpaˌfɛlsˌjœːkʏtl̥]; 'knobs mountain glacier').

tokens.name: Mount Karthala
tokens.description: Mount Karthala or Karthola (Arabic: القرطالة Al Qirṭālah) is an active shield volcano and the highest point of the Comoros at 2,361 m (7,746 ft) above sea level. It is the southernmost and larger of the two volcanoes forming Grande Comore island, the largest island in the nation of Comoros. The Karthala volcano is very active, having erupted more than 20 times since the 19th century.
tokens.image_credit: alKomor.com · CC BY-SA 2.0

tokens.name: Yellowstone volcano
tokens.description: The Yellowstone Caldera, also known as the Yellowstone Plateau Volcanic Field, is a Quaternary volcanic field, caldera complex, and volcanic plateau spanning parts of Wyoming, Idaho, and Montana. It is driven by the Yellowstone hotspot and lies largely within Yellowstone National Park. The field comprises several overlapping caldera structures, multiple lava domes and resurgent domes, and numerous bimodal lavas and tuffs of basaltic and rhyolitic composition, originally covering about 17,000 km2 (6,600 mi2).
tokens.image_credit: Kelvin Case (talk) · CC BY 3.0

tokens.name: Huaynaputina
tokens.description: Huaynaputina ( WY-nə-puu-TEE-nə; Spanish: [wajnapuˈtina]) is a volcano in a volcanic high plateau in southern Peru. Lying in the Central Volcanic Zone of the Andes, it was formed by the subduction of the oceanic Nazca Plate under the continental South American Plate. Huaynaputina is a large volcanic crater, which lacks an identifiable mountain profile, with an outer stratovolcano and three younger volcanic vents within an amphitheatre-shaped structure that is either a former caldera or a remnant of glacial erosion.

tokens.name: Mount Terror
tokens.description:
Mount Terror is an extinct volcano about 3,230 metres (10,600 ft) high on Ross Island, Antarctica, about 20 nautical miles (37 km; 23 mi) eastward of Mount Erebus.
Mount Terror was named in 1841 by polar explorer James Clark Ross after his second ship, HMS Terror.
tokens.image_credit: John Bortniak, NOAA · Public domain

tokens.name: Mount Hasan
tokens.description: Mount Hasan (Turkish: Hasan Dağı) is a volcano in Anatolia, Turkey. It has two summits, the 3,069 metres (10,069 ft) high eastern Small Hasandağ and the 3,253 metres (10,673 ft) high Big Hasandağ, and rises about 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) above the surrounding terrain. It consists of various volcanic deposits, including several calderas, and its activity has been related to the presence of several faults in the area and to regional tectonics.
tokens.image_credit: LBM1948 · CC BY-SA 4.0

tokens.name: Puyehue-Cordón Caulle
tokens.description: Puyehue (; Spanish pronunciation: [puˈʝewe]) and Cordón Caulle  are two coalesced volcanic edifices that form a major mountain massif in Puyehue National Park in the Andes of Ranco Province, in the South of Chile. In volcanology this group is known as the Puyehue-Cordón Caulle Volcanic Complex (PCCVC). Four volcanoes constitute the volcanic group or complex, the Cordillera Nevada caldera, the Pliocene Mencheca volcano, Cordón Caulle fissure vents and the Puyehue stratovolcano.

tokens.name: Tamu Massif
tokens.description: Tamu Massif is a seamount in the northwest Pacific Ocean, sitting atop a triple junction of mid-ocean ridges. Tamu Massif is located in the Shatsky Rise about 1,600 km (990 mi) east of Japan. The massif covers an area of about 553,000 square kilometres (214,000 mi2).
tokens.image_credit: cropped by User:Seattle Skier · Public domain

tokens.name: Momotombo
tokens.description: Momotombo is a stratovolcano in Nicaragua, located near the city of León. It stands on the shores of Lake Managua. An eruption of the volcano in 1610 forced inhabitants of León, in the Spanish Empire, to relocate about 48 kilometres (30 mi) west.
tokens.image_credit: CC BY-SA 2.5

tokens.name: Pichincha Volcano
tokens.description:
Pichincha is a stratovolcano in Ecuador. The capital Quito wraps around its eastern slopes.
The two highest peaks of the mountain are Wawa Pichincha (Kichwa wawa child, baby / small, Spanish spelling Guagua Pichincha) (4,784 metres (15,696 ft)) and Ruku Pichincha (Kichwa ruku old person, Spanish Rucu Pichincha) (4,698 metres (15,413 ft)).

tokens.name: El Chichón
tokens.description: El Chichón,  also known as Chichonal, is an active stratovolcano in Francisco León, north-western Chiapas, Mexico. El Chichón is part of a geologic zone known as the Chiapanecan Volcanic Arc. El Chichón's cone has a complex of domes with a tuff ring, made of ejected volcanic material, located between the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt and the Central America Volcanic Arc.

tokens.name: Mehetia
tokens.description: Mehetiʻa or Meʻetiʻa is a volcanic island in the Windward Islands, in the east of the Society Islands in French Polynesia. It is a very young active stratovolcano 110 kilometres (68 mi) east of the Taiarapu Peninsula of Tahiti. It is associated with the Teahitiʻa-Mehetia hotspot, and the South Pacific superswell.

tokens.name: Hanish Islands
tokens.description:
The Hanish Islands (Arabic: جزر حنيش, romanized: juzur ḥanīš, Tigrinya: ደሴታት ሓኒሽ, romanized: däsetat ḥaniš) form an archipelago in the Red Sea consisting of a trio of major islands at the centre of an array of smaller islets and rocks. The three major islands are the northern Zuqar Island, the southern Great Anish (Al-anīsh al-Kabīr), and the significantly smaller Little Anish (Al-anīsh al-Ṣaghīr) in between. 
The archipelago is largely under the control of Yemen, with only several small south-western rocks and islets granted to Eritrea by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in 1998 following the Hanish Islands conflict in 1994–1995.

tokens.name: Marapi
tokens.description: The Marapi (Jawi: ماراڤي), or Mount Marapi (Indonesian: Gunung Marapi, Minangkabau: Gunuang Marapi, Jawi: ڬونوواڠ ماراڤي), is a complex volcano in West Sumatra, Indonesia, and is the most active volcano in Sumatra. Like that of its quasi-homonym on Java, its name means "Mountain of Fire". Its elevation is 2,885 metres (9,465.2 ft).
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Hanafiannoy assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain

tokens.name: Llaima
tokens.description: The Llaima Volcano is one of the largest and most active volcanoes in Chile. It is situated 82 km East of Temuco and 663 km South of Santiago, within the borders of Conguillío National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Urbatem2 · CC BY-SA 2.0

tokens.name: Krafla
tokens.description: Krafla (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈkʰrapla] ) is a volcanic caldera of about 10 km (6.2 mi) in diameter with a 90 km (56 mi) long fissure zone. It is located in the north of Iceland in the Mývatn region and is situated on the Iceland hotspot atop the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, which forms the divergent boundary between the North American Plate and the Eurasian Plate. Its highest peak reaches up to 818 m (2,684 ft) and it is 2 km (1.2 mi) in depth.

tokens.name: Puy de Sancy
tokens.description: Puy de Sancy (US: , French: [pɥi d(ə) sɑ̃si]; Auvergnat: Puèi de la Crotz [ˈpœj də lɔ ˈkɾu(ts)], lit. ''Mount of the Cross'') is the highest mountain in the Massif Central, in Puy-de-Dôme departement of south central France. It is part of an ancient stratovolcano which has been inactive for about 220,000 years.

tokens.name: Mount Redoubt
tokens.description: Redoubt Volcano, or Mount Redoubt (Dena'ina: Bentuggezh K’enulgheli), is an active stratovolcano in the largely volcanic Aleutian Range of the U.S. state of Alaska.
